item.title: Abdias Ngateu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084309725 Abdias Ngateu 2226 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640191709405 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013447590109"] Discover Abdias Ngateu (b. 1990, Cameroon), a painter known for witty, colorful social commentary through animal characters. His art humorously highlights Cameroonian life, transport chaos, and issues like corruption, gaining international acclaim. [16571,23179] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdias Ngateu (b. 1990, Douala, Cameroon) is a painter celebrated for his witty social commentary on life in his home country. Through colorful, humorous paintings featuring animal characters, Ngateu sheds light on the everyday struggles of Cameroonians, particularly focusing on the country's chaotic transportation system. His works, while playful, offer deeper insights into issues such as corruption, infrastructure deficiencies, and the resilience of ordinary citizens. \\n \\nNgateu’s artistic journey began at the age of 14, when he studied graphic and decorative arts, later earning a degree in sociology from the University of Douala. His background in sociology deeply informs his art, allowing him to add layers of meaning to his vibrant, detailed works. Beyond the comical animal figures, he includes witty details like slogans on vehicles (“Free Wifi on Board,” “Air-conditioned Taxi”), which challenge viewers to confront the realities behind the humor. \\n \\nOver the years, Ngateu’s talent has gained recognition both locally and internationally. He received accolades such as the Goethe Institute's \"Discovery\" Award in 2015 and third prize in the \"Young Hopes 2017\" National Contest. His work has been showcased at prestigious events, including the DAK'ART Biennale of Contemporary African Art, and his pieces have sold at respected auctions like ArtCurial. Since 2018, Ngateu has been represented by the Out of Africa Gallery, and his career continues to flourish as his unique blend of humor and social critique resonates with global audiences. \\n \\nAnd, as one of his famous taxi slogans warns: “YOU SLEEP, YOUR LIFE SLEEPS!”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013447590109","gid://shopify/Product/9014039478493"]

[19224,19236,19228,19229,19230,19231,19232,19233,19234,19235] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdulla Omer Hamza (b. in Sudan) is a visual artist who delves into social and cultural complexities of his homeland. His recent 2024 series directly confronts the displacement and violence caused by the devastating conflict that erupted in April 2023. While these events deeply inform his practice, Omer's work transcends current crises, aiming to capture the vibrant cultural tapestry of Sudan. \\n \\nHe depicts the diverse relationships and geographical variations with the country, emphasizing unity and resilience. Through his art, Omer strives to \"reshape and bring colour back to life\" in the aftermath of war, envisioning a future marked by peace and inclusivity in Sudan. \\n \\nBorn in Sudan, visual artist Abdullah Omer delves into his homeland's social and cultural landscape. His recent 2024 series powerfully confronts the displacement and violence currently plaguing Sudan, a direct response to the devastating conflict that erupted in April 2023. While this context deeply informs his practice, Omer's work extends beyond current events. \\nHe strives to capture the rich tapestry of Sudanese culture and society, depicting the relationships born from its diversity and the geographical variations within the country. Ultimately, his artistic vision seeks to \"reshape and bring color back to life\" in the aftermath of war and displacement, working towards a more inclusive and peaceful Sudan."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013883273437","gid://shopify/Product/9013884059869","gid://shopify/Product/9013884977373","gid://shopify/Product/9013885796573","gid://shopify/Product/9013886681309","gid://shopify/Product/9013887467741","gid://shopify/Product/9013888418013","gid://shopify/Product/9013889171677","gid://shopify/Product/9013890056413","gid://shopify/Product/9013890777309"]

item.title: Ablade Glover
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085292765 Ablade Glover 1809 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640192233693 Discover Professor Ablade Glover (b. 1934, Ghana), a luminary of modern African art. Explore his vibrant oil paintings depicting Ghanaian life, urban scenes, and the resilience of African women. Educator and founder of Artist Alliance Gallery. [12206,25120,25121,12209,12208,25122,25099,25119,25098,12194,12207,25097] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Professor Ablade Glover, born in 1934 in Accra, Ghana, is one of the most significant figures in modern African art. A celebrated painter, educator, and advocate for African culture, Glover’s vibrant, textured oil paintings are renowned for their depiction of bustling street markets, urban life, and the resilience of African women. His work stands as a powerful expression of Ghana's socio-cultural and political transformations during the 20th and 21st centuries. \\n \\nGrowing up under British colonial rule, Glover’s early life coincided with Ghana's movement towards independence, which deeply influenced his artistic practice. After beginning his education at the College of Art at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi, Glover was awarded a government scholarship to study textile design at London’s School of Art and Design. When he returned to Ghana, the factory where he was meant to work had not yet been built, allowing him to explore his passion for painting. He later earned another scholarship, personally authorized by Ghana’s first president, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, to study Art Education at Newcastle University. Further studies took him to the United States, where he completed a master's degree at Kent State University and earned his doctorate at Ohio University in 1974. \\n \\nUpon returning to Ghana, Glover joined the faculty at KNUST, where he taught for over two decades, eventually becoming Department Head and Dean of the College of Art. Glover was instrumental in shaping Ghana’s modern art scene through his dedication to education and mentorship. After retiring in 1994, he turned to full-time painting and founded the Artist Alliance Gallery in Accra in 1993. This gallery has become a major institution for promoting African contemporary art, showcasing the work of emerging artists from across the continent. \\n \\nGlover’s art is characterized by his dynamic use of color and thick layers of oil paint, applied with palette knives in a \"wet-on-wet\" technique. His paintings, which often require the viewer to step back to fully appreciate their intricate textures, are grouped into categories such as \"Market,\" \"People,\" \"Townscapes,\" and \"Celebrations.\" Glover’s signature approach vividly captures the chaos and energy of Ghanaian life, especially the Makola Market in Accra, which serves as a recurring theme in his work. His respect for women, especially those who sustain Ghana’s informal economy, is a central motif, as seen in his \"Profiles\" series, where women are portrayed with elegance and courage. Through his work, Glover elevates women as symbols of strength and resilience, reclaiming their power from the colonial exploitation of the past. \\nHis contribution to art extends beyond the canvas, as he has played a vital role in bringing international attention to both traditional and contemporary African art. Glover's works are housed in prestigious collections worldwide, including the Imperial Palace of Japan, UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, and Chicago's O'Hare International Airport. He has exhibited extensively in West Africa, Europe, the USA, and Japan, and has received numerous accolades, including the Flagstar Award, the Ghana Order of the Volta, and the Millennium Excellence Award. \\n \\nThroughout his long and distinguished career, Glover’s passion for Ghana, its people, and its culture remains the driving force behind his artistic journey. His paintings are not only a testament to his love for his country but also a powerful celebration of the people who form its backbone, particularly the women of Ghana. Glover's legacy as both an artist and educator continues to inspire future generations of African artists."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014113566941","gid://shopify/Product/9014113665245","gid://shopify/Product/9014113730781","gid://shopify/Product/9014114386141","gid://shopify/Product/9014114418909","gid://shopify/Product/9014114484445","gid://shopify/Product/9014114517213"]

item.title: Abongile Sidzumo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085358301 Abongile Sidzumo 1295 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650685759709 [] Discover Abongile Sidzumo, an award-winning South African artist who uses leather offcuts and repurposed materials to explore themes of healing, coexistence, and memory in post-apartheid South Africa. His work offers a powerful commentary on trauma and restoration. [9018,9019] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abongile Sidzumo, born in 1996 in Cape Town, is an emerging South African artist recognized for his use of leather offcuts and repurposed materials to create thought-provoking works that examine humanity, coexistence, and our connection with nature. A graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Arts (2019), Sidzumo draws inspiration from personal memories, spaces he has inhabited, and the daily lives of marginalized communities. His practice is rooted in the idea of healing trauma, specifically reflecting on the experiences of black communities during and after apartheid in South Africa. \\nSidzumo’s work delves into the symbolic meaning of leather, a material often associated with luxury, wealth, and power. Through his meticulous process of re-stitching and weaving, he encourages viewers to rethink the value of repurposed materials. His practice becomes a metaphor for the healing and restoration of black communities, focusing on the continuous journey of recovery in post-apartheid South Africa. \\n \\n \\nSidzumo works with leather offcuts and repurposed materials to create works that reflect and interrogate humanity, the way we co-exist and our relationship with nature; he re- visits memories and connects them to spaces he has lived in as well as the everyday life of marginalised communities. \\nLeather is often associated with luxury, wealth and power. Through his process of res- tichting and weaving this precious material, Sidzumo is proposing that we start thinking about repurposed materials, connecting it and his process of stitching to notions of heal- ing trauma that has been inflicted on black communities during apartheid, in a sense, his practice also functions as a manner of interrogating the continuous healing of black communities in post-apartheid South Africa. \\nIn 2020, Sidzumo was awarded the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize, which led to his solo exhibition at the Everard Read Gallery in Johannesburg. His work was also featured in \"We’ve come to take you home,\" an exhibition of newly acquired works by the University of Cape Town. The same year, he was a runner-up for the Cassirer Welz Award, hosted by Strauss & Co auctioneers. Sidzumo has participated in several group exhibitions, including \"A Cloud\" and \"The Oasis\" in 2021, curated by Studio Nxumalo Contemporary. His most recent recognition includes the Gerald Sekoto Award as part of the Absa L’Atelier 2021. He continues to live and work in Cape Town."}]}]} []

She holds a BA and BA Honours in Fine Arts from the University of Witswatersrand. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Ada-Ruth Kellow (b. 1957, Bremen, Germany) is a figurative painter residing and working in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her subject matter lies in the uncomfortable and the unspeakable, aligning with Susan Sontag's view that “we can’t be haunted enough”. Kellow continues the tradition of social critique painting, following in the footsteps of artists such as Goya, Gericault, Munch, and Golub. 
 In her work of realistic rendering, Kellow uses metaphors and symbols, incorporating ornamental patterns that provide a sense of consolation. Through her art, she invites viewers to trace the unfolding narrative, blending confrontation with moments of humour. 
 Kellow obtained her BA in Fine Arts from the University of Witswatersrand and completed her BA Honours with distinction in 2022. She has taken classes in painting at Hermann Niebuhr Studio, Johannesburg, and life drawing at Freie Kunstakademie Frankfurt, Germany. She also attended the Pentiment International Summer Academy for Art & Design in Hamburg, Germany. 
 Kellow has participated in several group exhibitions in South Africa, with a solo exhibition at Gordart Gallery in Johannesburg in 2022. In 2024, she was among the top 40 Finalists for the Rust-en-Vrede Portrait Award and attended the Blue Cactus Art Residency in Barcelona, Spain. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9133213581533","gid://shopify/Product/9133213581533","gid://shopify/Product/9132523585757","gid://shopify/Product/9132523585757","gid://shopify/Product/9014057992413","gid://shopify/Product/9014058057949","gid://shopify/Product/9133230915805","gid://shopify/Product/9133230915805","gid://shopify/Product/9134148813021","gid://shopify/Product/9134148813021","gid://shopify/Product/9014033645789","gid://shopify/Product/9014057500893","gid://shopify/Product/9014041477341","gid://shopify/Product/9133230883037","gid://shopify/Product/9133230883037","gid://shopify/Product/9132523421917","gid://shopify/Product/9132523421917","gid://shopify/Product/9014033940701","gid://shopify/Product/9014033711325","gid://shopify/Product/9014033809629","gid://shopify/Product/9014057926877","gid://shopify/Product/9132523028701","gid://shopify/Product/9132523028701","gid://shopify/Product/9014057959645","gid://shopify/Product/9132523389149","gid://shopify/Product/9132523389149","gid://shopify/Product/9133212598493","gid://shopify/Product/9133212598493","gid://shopify/Product/9014057468125","gid://shopify/Product/9132523356381","gid://shopify/Product/9132523356381","gid://shopify/Product/9133230948573","gid://shopify/Product/9133230948573","gid://shopify/Product/9133230981341","gid://shopify/Product/9133230981341","gid://shopify/Product/9132523454685","gid://shopify/Product/9132523454685","gid://shopify/Product/9133212532957","gid://shopify/Product/9133212532957","gid://shopify/Product/9014033875165","gid://shopify/Product/9014033776861","gid://shopify/Product/9134148714717","gid://shopify/Product/9134148714717","gid://shopify/Product/9134148845789","gid://shopify/Product/9134148845789","gid://shopify/Product/9134148747485","gid://shopify/Product/9134148747485","gid://shopify/Product/9132523487453","gid://shopify/Product/9132523487453","gid://shopify/Product/9134146945245","gid://shopify/Product/9134146945245"]

Her work captures the resilience, energy, and diverse communities of the city. [19176,19177] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nigerian photographer Adedolapo Salako embarked on her artistic journey at the age of 25 in 2022, fueled by a passion for self-portraiture and fashion photography. However, her artistic vision soon expanded as she became captivated by the vibrant streets of Lagos, where she now excels in street photography and reportage. \\nAdedolapo's lens acts as a powerful storyteller, documenting the diverse communities that inhabit Lagos. Through her work, she captures their resilience, determination, and the captivating energy that pulsates through the city's street life. Each photograph serves to illuminate the rich tapestry of humanity that thrives in Lagos, providing an intimate glimpse into the lives of its inhabitants. \\n \\nSalako's mission is to amplify the voices of these communities, shedding light on their experiences and stories. Her work not only showcases the beauty and complexity of urban life but also invites viewers to appreciate the depth of human connection found within the bustling streets of Lagos. Through her compelling photography, Adedolapo Salako continues to forge a meaningful narrative that celebrates the spirit of the city and its people."}]}]} []

item.title: Adele Van Heerden
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641086832861 Adele Van Heerden gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193282269 [] Discover Adele van Heerden, a Cape Town-based painter (b. 1989) known for her work in pastel and gouache on drafting film. Her art explores light, reflection, and the relationship between urban landscapes and natural environments, inspired by personal experience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adele van Heerden (b. 1989) is a painter living and working in Cape Town, South Africa. Her artistic practice is characterized by her use of pastel, pencil, and gouache on drafting film, and it is deeply informed by her experiences of specific sites and places. Van Heerden's recent body of work, titled \"Mirror,\" focuses on the careful observation and study of surface, light, reflection, and fluidity, revealing her interest in the relationships between built environments and natural landscapes. \\n \\nIn her artist statement, Van Heerden expresses her interest in the relationships between built environments, natural landscapes, design, and abstraction versus figuration. She aims to capture moments and give shape to experiences, focusing on urban landscapes, waterscapes, and interior spaces. Recently, her work has expanded into a visual exploration of the interplay between water and light, drawing inspiration from her experiences as a swimmer. Water, which refracts and reflects light, serves as a significant theme in her practice. \\n \\nThe autobiographical component of her work reflects an abstracted narration that she translates through her experiences. This exploration began when she was diagnosed with a hip condition that required surgery and extensive rehabilitation, making swimming an embodied experience that facilitates sensory revelations. Through her art, Adele van Heerden continues to connect deeply with the environments she inhabits and portrays. \\n \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Adesola Yusuf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641089061085 Adesola Yusuf gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193315037 [] Discover Abdulrahman Adesola Yusuf (Arclight) (b. 1997), a multidimensional artist exploring connection through liminal processes. His portraits blend abstraction and recognition, embodying "optimistic nihilism" and examining reality through emotive figures. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdulrahman Adesola Yusuf (Arclight) (b.1997) is a multidimensional artist deeply fascinated by connection, whose philosophy of creation centers the process rather than the destination. For Adesola, the true meaning of art lies in the labour of creation—an iterative journey of overthinking minute details and embracing the art of collage, layering materials through trail and error, and learning from irrevocable mistakes. His creative process is heavily rooted in the liminal. \\n \\nAdesola focuses on painting the intricate interplay of colour, form, and human expression to create silhouettes that teeter between abstraction and recognition. These figures are both present and elusive, reflecting his profound fascination with the transient nature of identity and the fluidity of the human form. He describes his compelling portraits as embodying \"optimistic nihilism\". \\nThrough his work, Adesola deconstructs his perception of the experiences that shape his world, revealing the subtle threads of connection between transcendent ideas and economic conditions. \\n \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Adrian Kohler
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641093222621 Adrian Kohler 2492 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195182813 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015754461"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/134184763613 Unknown Discover Adrian Kohler, co-founder of Handspring Puppet Company and a world-leading puppetry expert. His acclaimed puppets, blending artistry and engineering, are exhibited internationally and held in major collections. [22394] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Adrian Kohler (b. 1957) is widely recognized as one of the word's foremost experts in puppetry, serving as the esteemed Co-founder and Artistic Director of the renowned Handspring Puppet Company. 

 Kohler's foundation passion for creating moving figures was nurtured from a young age; his mother; an amateur puppeteer, alongside his father, a yacht builder and cabinetmaker, instilled in him a deep understanding of woodwork and kinetic artistry. He further honed his artistic skills, earning a BA in Fine Art from the University of Cape Town. His early career included significant stints at The Space Theatre in Cape Town, the city's sole non-racial venue at the time, and a year in the U.K. at the Canon Hills Arts Centre and Weld Community Arts Centre in Birmingham. Kohler then dedicated three years to running the National Popular Theatre Program in Botswana. 

 His groundbreaking puppets for Handspring Puppet Company have garnered widespread international acclaim and extensive exhibition. Kohler has been honored with a solo retrospective at the National Gallery in South Africa, and selections of his works have been showcased at prestigious venues globally, including The Barbican Art Gallery in London and The Museum for African Art in New York. His exceptional puppets are part of significant public and private collections, notably including the Constitutional Court in South Africa, the Munich Stadt Museum in Germany, and the Old Mutual Art Collection. 
 In recognition of his profound contributions to the arts, Kohler received the Michaelis Prize, a lifetime achievement award from Tshwane University in 2006, and an honorary doctorate in literature from the University of Cape Town in 2012. 
"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015754461"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641095450845 Agnes Waruguru 2231 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195707101 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062474461"] Discover the work of Agnes Waruguru, a Kenyan contemporary artist exploring identity and home through multi-sensory painting, installation, and textile art. [18430] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Agnes Waruguru (b.1994) is Kenyan whose work delves into the intimate realms of everyday life, home and personal histories. Through a dedicated and repetitive practice of material experimentation, she create multi-sensory experiences that transform painting, drawing, printmaking, and needlework into immersive installations. \\nWaruguru’s art is deeply connected to her surrounding, yet it weaves in multiple histories and identities, inviting viewers into meticulously crafted environments. By engaging the senses with elements like scent, organic materials, light, and water, she constructs spaces that suspend time, encouraging moments of care, slowness, and contemplation. \\nA graduate of the Savannah College of Art and Design (BFA), Waruguru has gained significant international recognition. She has participated in the inaugural Stellenbosch Triennale (2020) and completed a prestigious residency at the Rijksakademie in Amsterdam (2021-2023). Her work has been exhibited across the globe, in Kenya, South Africa, France and the United States. Following her first solo show, 'Small things to Consider', at Circle Art Gallery in 2020, she was nominated for the esteemed Volkskrant Beeldende Kunst Prijs in 2022. Waruguru continues to live and work in Amsterdam, Netherlands."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062474461"]

item.title: Ajarb Bernard Ategwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641097908445 Ajarb Bernard Ategwa 2227 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640196755677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066439389"] Discover the vibrant paintings of Ajarb Bernard Ategwa, a leading Cameroonian artist capturing moments of peace within the chaotic energy of urban street life. [18915,18931,16575,18932,18933,16574,18934] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ajarb Bernard Ategwa (b. 1988) is a self-taught Cameroonian visual artist who has risen to international prominence from his home base in Douala, Cameroon. His artistic journey began in 1998 with illustrations on plywood, but his perspective was transformed in 2001 after witnessing the work of artists like Hako Hankson, which inspired him to explore new dimensions of painting. \\nAtegwa's work is an intimate reflection of the bustling street life of Douala. He captures the \"plural, hard-working, noisy and eclectic\" energy of the city, yet his focus is on the moments of quiet respite found within the urban chaos. In a style influenced by Pop Art and the colour profusion of Jackson Pollock, he depicts characters in moments of pause—a \"ceasefire\" that creates a pocket of poetry amidst the disorder. \\nRepresented by leading galleries such as Jack Bell Gallery (London), Peres Projects (Berlin), and Fredric Snitzer Gallery (Miami), Ategwa's work has been showcased at prestigious international art fairs including Art Basel, FIAC, and Frieze. His paintings are held in notable public collections, including the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM), the Chazen Museum of Art, and the Zuzeum Art Centre."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066439389"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098399965 Akintunde Disu 2511 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640197279965 [] Explore the work of Akintunde Disu, a Nigerian mixed-media artist and screen printer whose layered art delves into personal and Nigerian history. [19996,19999,19994,19995,19993,19998] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Akintunde Disu is a distinguished Nigerian mixed-media artist and screen printer whose work intricately navigate his personal history and the broader history of Nigeria. First gaining prominence as a runner-up in the 1986 BP National Portrait competition, Disu has built a career defined by intellectual depth and technical skill. \\n \\nHis artistic language is a rich tapestry woven from diverse influences, including Surrealism, Pop Art, and the masterful printmaking of fellow Nigerian artist Bruce Onobrakpeya, alongside Islamic and classic European art traditions. \\n \\nThrough the deliberate process of screen printing and layering, Disu creates immersive \"conversations on canvas,\" inviting viewers to look beyond the surface and uncover underlying narratives. His art, which often employs repetition and motif reminiscent of tribal art, serves as a tangible exploration of history and identity. Disu has exhibited extensively both in Nigeria and internationally, with notable shows at the National Museum in Lagos, a solo exhibition at the Didi Museum, and participation in exhibitions in the United Kingdom. He continues to challenge perceptions and create sensational, original work that dialogues with the very essence and fluidity of art. \\n \\n Disu draws inspiration from various sources including Surrealism, the Pop-art movement, and notably, the Nigerian print master Bruce Onobrakpeya. \\n \\nHis notable exhibitions span both national and international stages, showcasing his depth and versatility. Highlights include participation in the Society of Nigerian Artists group exhibition at the National Museum in Onikan, Lagos, a solo exhibition at Didi Museum in Lagos in November 2014, and contributions to group shows such as Pecha Kucha at the Goethe Institute in Lagos, and \"What is the Point?\" at the Federation of British Artists' Threadneedle Space, Mall Gallery, in the United Kingdom. \\n \\nDisu is committed to creating immersive art that serves as a conversation on canvas, offering fresh perspectives on the essence of art. He leverages screen printing to delve into the history of his people, aiming to create a magical, tangible experience. His work is a testament to the power of collaboration and the liberating effect of intentional methodology. Through layering, Disu invites audiences to look beyond the surface, challenging them to uncover the underlying narratives. \\n \\nHe masters his craft by engaging with significant, substantive subjects and cites a broad array of influences from Islamic and tribal art to classic landscape artists like Turner and environmental artists like Christo and Jeanne-Claude. His art speaks a language of repetition and motif inherent in tribal art, while also drawing contemporary influences from artists such as Rene Magritte, Salvador Dali, Sol Lewitt, and Andy Warhol. Disu's art is not only a reflection of his rich heritage and diverse influences but also a dialogue on the democratization and fluidity of art, emphasizing its originality and sensational impact."}]}]} []

item.title: Akshar Maganbeharie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098531037 Akshar Maganbeharie 1874 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640197345501 gid://shopify/Metaobject/169542516957 Cape Town ZA Discover the art of Akshar Maganbeharie, a South African artist using pop culture icons to critique capitalism, colonialism, and identity in his vibrant work. [22784,22783,22785] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Akshar Maganbeharie is a Cape Town-based, multi-disciplinary artist whose work offers a sharp and witty critique of contemporary culture.A 2017 Fine Art graduate from the University of the Witwatersrand, Maganbeharie moves fluidly between painting, drawing, and installation to explore how identity is shaped by pop culture and social media. \r\n Citing Britney Spears, Starbucks, and Kylie Jenner as primary inspirations, he employs a semi-abstract, impressionistic style that appears carefree on the surface. However, beneath this veneer of \"unserious\" subject matter lies a pointed commentary on complex issues such as cultural imperialism, neo-colonialism, and capitalism. As a member of the Kutti Collective, a group of South African Indian artists, and selected as one of Design Indaba's Emerging Creatives in 2022, Maganbeharie has established himself as a significant voice. His works, held in private collections locally and internationally, challenge viewers to reconsider the profound impact of popular culture on the modern world. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014025486557","gid://shopify/Product/9013289648349"]

[4186,4189,4190,4194,4191,4187,4195,4193,4188,4185,4192,4374] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Alastair Whitton is a prominent South African photographic artist whose work thoughtfully explores the mechanisms of memory and the passage of time. His practice is centered on what he terms ‘the architecture of time and the poetics and politics of place,’ seeking to illuminate the 'space between moments.' Through his lens, Whitton elevates the seemingly commonplace, creating monuments to overlooked or dislocated scenes and objects, thereby capturing their quiet significance. \r\n Whitton has an extensive international exhibition history, with five solo shows and inclusion in numerous curated group exhibitions at prestigious institutions such as the Fotomuseum, Antwerp; Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, Lisbon; Johannesburg Art Gallery; and the IZIKO South African National Gallery. His work has been featured at major art fairs, including multiple editions of the Investec Cape Town Art Fair. \r\n Beyond his personal practice, Whitton is a key figure in the Cape Town art scene as the director of These Four Walls gallery, where he curates and presents the work of other contemporary artists. His photographs are held in significant public and private collections, including the Durban Art Museum, the Jack Ginsberg Collection, and the National Museum of Mali. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013291319517","gid://shopify/Product/9013291417821","gid://shopify/Product/9013291450589","gid://shopify/Product/9013291614429","gid://shopify/Product/9013291483357","gid://shopify/Product/9013291352285","gid://shopify/Product/9013291548893","gid://shopify/Product/9013291385053","gid://shopify/Product/9013291253981","gid://shopify/Product/9013291516125"]

item.title: Aldo Balding
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098989789 Aldo Balding 1833 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640198590685 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013420785885"] Discover the evocative, narrative paintings of English artist Aldo Balding. Inspired by John Singer Sargent, his work captures moments of intrigue and emotion. [19024,15267,12356,12362,12358,15268,15269,12361,12368,12357,12367,12366,12359,12365,12364,15270,15272,12360,19022,15271] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aldo Balding (b. 1960) is a celebrated English artist known for his evocative and narrative-driven figurative paintings. After beginning his career as an illustrator in London, he transitioned to become a full-time artist based in the South of France. A pivotal moment in his youth—an encounter with the work of John Singer Sargent—ignited his artistic direction. \\nBalding was captivated by Sargent's ability to create a stunning illusion of reality with loose, expressive brushwork that resolves into realism only from a distance. This principle remains central to Balding's own technique. He masterfully balances detailed realism with painterly strokes, creating contemporary scenes rich with atmosphere and intrigue. Unity of colour is paramount in his work, lending harmony and balance to his compositions. More than just a technician, Balding is a storyteller who uses body language, light, and the arrangement of figures to create a sense of anticipation, inviting viewers to interpret the unspoken narratives within each piece."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013420785885"]

[25478,25477,25476,25475] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Aleruchi Kinika (b.1997) is a visual artist living in Port Harcourt, Nigeria. Her mediums include photography, writing and pen on paper drawing. She started photography in order to preserve her culture and understand her identity. Her works explore individual storytelling through an intersection of surrealism and chiaroscuro. She aims to express deep seated emotions and cultural values through storytelling in effective and exciting ways. \r\n Kinika’s work also highlights femininity, beauty and fashion and is deeply inspired by cinema and baroque techniques which involves the play of light and shadows to further dramatize her subjects and drive her story. She expresses her personal struggles, passion and joy as well as those found around her in her daily life with the use of photographs. \r\n Kinika has showcased her work in both local and international group exhibitions such as Polaroid x Magnum Real Life is not Black & White, Paris Photo Fair and Divergence, 1952 Africa, Lagos Nigeria. Kinika has participated in two art residencies which are Divergence, 1952 Art Accelerator Programme. Lagos, Nigeria and Alternative Heritage by StoryMi x French Embassy in Nigeria x The Republic Magazine. Ibadan, Nigeria. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9133234323677","gid://shopify/Product/9133234323677","gid://shopify/Product/9133234225373","gid://shopify/Product/9133234225373","gid://shopify/Product/9133233144029","gid://shopify/Product/9133233144029","gid://shopify/Product/9133230555357","gid://shopify/Product/9133230555357"]

[7819,7818,7816,12269,12268,12271] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Alex Ayivi is a French contemporary visual artist of Togolese heritage whose work delves into themes of family, pan-Africanism, and Afrotopia. A 2018 graduate in printmaking from the prestigious ENSAV La Cambre in Brussels, Ayivi combines his technical skill with a deeply personal narrative. As a second-generation immigrant, he navigates the complexities of identity and belonging through a vibrant and multifaceted practice that includes painting and printmaking. \r\n In 2019, Ayivi was awarded the inaugural residency by the Foundation Culture & Diversité at the Cité Internationale des Arts, where he presented his celebrated project La MUA. His paintings are notable for their vibrant hues and the palpable intimacy he creates. He often depicts characters in moments of serene repose, seemingly exhausted by their daily lives yet radiating a communicative sense of peace. Through this \"uninterrupted technical wander,\" Ayivi builds a visual dialogue around the intimate and the political, crafting a unique space of reflection and connection. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013322186973","gid://shopify/Product/9013367701725","gid://shopify/Product/9013322088669","gid://shopify/Product/9013367668957","gid://shopify/Product/9013367800029"]

[21922,21923,21924,21925] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexandra Dickson (b. 2000)is an innovative artist, illustrator, and printmaker based in Cape Town, South Africa. A graduate of the Stellenbosch Academy of Design and Photography, Alexandra's work is deeply influenced by themes of memory, the body, womanhood, and the self. Her preferred mediums—film photography, print-making, and oil painting—serve as vessels for her exploration of these profound subjects. \\nHer artistic journey is marked by a passion for visual storytelling and a keen eye for detail. Alexandra's creative process is centered on making meaning through her art, whether it's capturing the fleeting moments of memory, exploring the intricacies of the human form, or delving into the multifaceted experiences of womanhood. \\nAs a Visual Communication Honours graduate of 2022, Alexandra has developed a broad range of skills that enhance her artistic practice. Her proficiency in graphic and illustration design, social media marketing, education, photography, fashion design, content curation and creation, digital art, and print-making allows her to create visually compelling work that resonates with her audience. Her style is adaptable, meeting the diverse needs of her clients while maintaining her unique artistic voice. \\nAlexandra's work as a clothing and surface designer is notable, particularly her clothing collection, The Lavender Project. Her collaborations with brands featured in We are Egg and Storytellers in the V&A Waterfront highlight her versatility and creativity. Alexandra's dedication to blending storytelling with visual art creates pieces that are not only visually striking but also emotionally impactful."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452104974557","gid://shopify/Product/9452105040093","gid://shopify/Product/9452105072861","gid://shopify/Product/9452105105629"]

item.title: Alexandra Naledi Holtman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641100005597 Alexandra Naledi Holtman 1998 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640202784989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013397127389", "gid://shopify/Product/9013429698781"] Discover the work of Alexandra Naledi Holtman, a Cape Town interdisciplinary artist exploring communication and technology through sound and installation art. [15576,15706,14025,15575] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexandra Naledi Holtman is a Cape Town-based interdisciplinary artist and a graduate of the University of Cape Town's Michaelis School of Fine Art. Her practice, which often incorporates sound, sculpture, and interactive installation, is a thoughtful investigation into the nature of communication, connection, and perception. \\nDrawing on both academic theory and playful, tangible experiences, Holtman's work explores how we relate to one another across space and technology. A key example is her interactive sound installation based on Roy Ascott's concept of \"telematics.\" In this piece, she uses lo-fi materials like parabolic receivers and cup-and-string telephones to create an intimate, private communication channel between two people. By grounding a high-tech theory in a simple, physical experience, she encourages participants to reflect on the fundamentals of connection in a digitally saturated world. Through her work, Holtman consistently creates spaces that challenge our awareness and highlight the delicate pathways of human interaction."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013397127389","gid://shopify/Product/9013427208413","gid://shopify/Product/9013427241181","gid://shopify/Product/9013429698781"]

item.title: Alfred Thoba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641103544541 Alfred Thoba 1010 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640214778077 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126077149","gid://shopify/Product/9452126109917"] Discover the powerful work of Alfred Thoba, a key figure in South Africa's resistance art movement. Explore his politically charged paintings that document the struggles of apartheid and the social challenges of post-apartheid life in Johannesburg's townships. [23901,23899] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alfred Thoba (b. 1951, Johannesburg) is a prominent self-taught artist who is renowned for his politically charged and socially conscious artworks. As an active member of the resistance art movement during apartheid, Thoba used his paintbrush as a powerful tool for protest. His work not only condemned the violence of the state but also unflinchingly depicted the internal conflicts and societal damage inflicted upon the Black population by the oppressive system. \\n \\n \\nIn the post-apartheid era, Thoba’s focus shifted but his profound connection to the struggles of his community remained. He became deeply moved by the plight of people in Black townships, exploring the complex effects of urbanization and Westernization on traditional values. His canvases often feature narratives of survival, highlighting the harsh realities faced by children forced into stealing, prostitution, and violence on the streets. Drawing inspiration from human relationships, personal suffering, and current events sourced from newspaper articles, Thoba frequently accompanies his finished paintings with a handwritten letter, adding another layer of narrative to his visual commentary. \\nThoba’s significant contributions to South African art have been recognized both critically and commercially. His seminal piece, 1976 Riots, set a world record for the artist in June 2012, selling for R913,480 at a Strauss & Co auction. This was followed by another major sale in May 2013, with Fruits of Life achieving R818,496. In 2018, the Wits Art Museum hosted a major retrospective of his work titled Alfred Thoba: A Step Becomes a Statement, solidifying his status as a key figure in South African art history. He continues to live and work in his hometown of Johannesburg. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126077149","gid://shopify/Product/9452126109917"]

[23406,23407] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alka Dass (b. 1992, KwaZulu-Natal) is a South African contemporary artist whose practice centres on the exploration of identity, memory, and folklore. After studying Fine Art at the Durban University of Technology, she/they received the prestigious Young Female Residency Award from The Bag Factory and 'Project Space' in Johannesburg in 2017. This recognition marked a significant step in their career, leading to the accomplishment of three international residencies and two solo exhibitions. \\n \\nWorking across diverse mediums including thread, cyanotypes, collage, and sculpture, Dass delves into personal and collective histories by drawing from archival family photographs, anecdotes, and dreamwork. A central tenet of her/their practice is the re-contextualization of techniques often dismissed as 'ladies' handicrafts.' By elevating these methods, Dass intentionally challenges and disregards the conventional hierarchies within contemporary fine art, creating a deeply personal and subversive visual language."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452193022173","gid://shopify/Product/9452193054941","gid://shopify/Product/9452193087709","gid://shopify/Product/9452193153245","gid://shopify/Product/9452193186013","gid://shopify/Product/9452193251549"]

item.title: Alon Skuy
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106100445 Alon Skuy 2664 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640218480861 Explore the impactful photojournalism of Alon Skuy, a renowned South African photographer based in Miami. His work captures issues of inequality, conflict, and resilience. Buy prints and books online to experience his powerful visual storytelling. [22167,22165,22161,22162,22166,22168,22169,22164,22163] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alon Skuy is a distinguished photojournalist born in Johannesburg, South Africa, and currently based in Miami, Florida. After studying photography at The Market Photo Workship, Skuy embarked on a career that lead him to become the Chief Photographer for the Sunday Times and The Times in South Africa. His work focuses on issues of inequality, conflict, resilience, and life on the fringes of society. \\nSkuy's career is defined by his depth and range as a news and documentary photographer. He is especially noted for his coverage of the 2012 Marikana Massacre, the most lethal use of force by South African security forces against civilians since the Sharpeville Massacre of 1960. His long-term work includes documenting xenophobic violence and intimate portrayals of subcultures. \\nHe has received numerous accolades, including recognition from the World Press Photo Foundation and multiple awards from the Picture of the Year International (POYI). Notably, he won first place in the News category of the POYI awards in 2015 for his work on the unrest at the Marikana Mine, and was awarded Photographer of the Year, Local in POYI in 2020. Skuy has also been honored with 9 Standard Bank Sikuvile Awards and multiple Vodacom Journalist of the Year Awards in photography. \\nIn addition to his photojournalistic achievements, Skuy was awarded the Ruth First Fellowship for Photojournalism at the University of the Witwatersrand for his photographic essay \"Living Inside A Bridge\" (2008). He has mentored young photographers and conducted workshops in collaboration with World Press Photo. \\nHis work has been featured in public collections and he has published notable books, including [BR]OTHER (2021), which received an Award of Excellence at the 80th Pictures of the Year International Awards, and MARiKANA 2012/2022, commemorating a decade since the Marikana Massacre."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014011199709","gid://shopify/Product/9014011232477","gid://shopify/Product/9014011265245","gid://shopify/Product/9014011298013","gid://shopify/Product/9014011330781","gid://shopify/Product/9014011363549","gid://shopify/Product/9014011396317","gid://shopify/Product/9014011461853"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106395357 Amalie von Maltitz gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640219005149 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452136956125","gid://shopify/Product/9452137021661","gid://shopify/Product/9452137939165","gid://shopify/Product/9452138070237"] Discover the work of Amalie von Maltitz, a South African sculptor, art historian, and licensed pilot. Explore her unique sculptures that blend figurative and abstract forms and delve into a career that combines artistic production with academic research on South African art history. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amalie von Maltitz is a distinguished South African sculptor whose work thoughtfully navigates the space between figuration and abstraction. Her art explores profound themes of form, identity, and transformation, reflecting a career deeply rooted in both artistic creation and intellectual inquiry. \\nVon Maltitz laid the foundation for her career at the prestigious Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, graduating in 1962. She further honed her craft in Germany at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart. Her extensive career is marked not only by decades of artistic production but also by significant contributions as an educator and curator. She held positions at the Rand Afrikaans University (now the University of Johannesburg), where she also earned a Master of Arts in History of Art with distinction. \\nHer sculptural language is characterized by a modernist simplification of form, combined with a nuanced sensitivity to gesture and material. Von Maltitz has exhibited extensively in both solo and group exhibitions since the 1970s, including shows alongside other notable South African artists like Deborah Bell. Her academic pursuits include important contributions to the documentation of South African art history, notably through her work on a publication about the sculptor Edoardo Villa. \\nAdding a unique dimension to her creative practice, von Maltitz is also a licensed commercial pilot and aviation advocate, embodying a rare blend of artistic sensibility and technical precision."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452136956125","gid://shopify/Product/9452137021661","gid://shopify/Product/9452137939165","gid://shopify/Product/9452138070237"]

item.title: Amber Alcock
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107017949 Amber Alcock gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640225067229 [] Discover the surrealist art of Amber Alcock, a graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art and recipient of the Simon Gerson and Judy Steinberg awards. Her paintings challenge apathy by exploring themes of care, the human-animal connection, and ecological consciousness through a unique blend of fantasy and unsettling beauty. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Surrealist painter Amber Alcock, a 2022 graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art, is redefining the narrative of 'care' through her evocative and unsettling artworks. An award-winning artist, Alcock received both the prestigious Simon Gerson and Judy Steinberg awards for her distinctive painting style upon her graduation. \\nIn a world often marked by apathy, Alcock’s work champions the concepts of fragility, tenderness, and conscientiousness as potent tools of preservation. Her surreal compositions are a battleground where horror and charm, humour and menace, awareness and ignorance converge. Through these juxtapositions, she aims to provoke a \"new wariness and awareness\" in the viewer. \\nAlcock's art delves into the complex and often fraught relationship between humanity, nature, and the animal kingdom. Drawing inspiration from art history and her own sense of personal power and helplessness, she uses the lens of fantasy and surrealism to cast a light on pressing ethical, personal, humanitarian, and ecological concerns. Her work does not seek to provide answers but rather to make evident the profound consequences of a collective lack of genuine care. \\n\"Alcock is fascinated by the inexplicably large galaxy of relational modes, transfused mythologies and histories that govern our attending of the relationship between humanity, the animal and nature,\" states a release about her work. Her paintings serve as a visual exploration of these intricate dynamics, prompting a re-evaluation of our place within the natural world. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Amira Shariff
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107050717 Amira Shariff 2005 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640225460445 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399355613", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399421149", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399486685"] Explore the work of Amira Shariff, a multidisciplinary artist, photographer, and art director from Johannesburg. Discover her layered photographic style that unpacks themes of self, identity, and connection, exhibited at major platforms like the FNB Art Fair. [14461,14465,14466,14467,14083,14084,14085,14086] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist Amira Shariff (b. 1999) utilizes photography as her primary medium to navigate the complexities of identity and connection in the contemporary world. Currently completing her degree in strategic brand communications at Vega, Shariff seamlessly merges her artistic pursuits with her professional roles as an art director, set designer, strategist, and cultural curator, where she serves as an art director and creative strategist for an agency and events. \\nShariff's formal photographic education began at the renowned Market Photo Workshop in 2019, followed by her involvement with the Through the Lens Collective in 2020. Her distinct approach to photography, which often involves layering images to create evocative and questioning narratives, has gained significant recognition. Her work has been showcased at prominent platforms including the FNB Art Fair (2022), the Through The Lens Collective Portrait Show (2020), and the Advanced Student Show at Berman Contemporary (2021). \\nInspired by her late uncle, Abdul Shariff, her photographic journey began at the age of thirteen. Today, her practice is a deeply personal exploration of her relationship with herself and the world around her. She poetically investigates how the very elements that are meant to connect individuals can also be the source of their disconnection, inviting viewers to question their own perceptions and the realities presented before them."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845","gid://shopify/Product/9013399355613","gid://shopify/Product/9013399421149","gid://shopify/Product/9013399486685","gid://shopify/Product/9013403255005","gid://shopify/Product/9013403418845","gid://shopify/Product/9013403451613","gid://shopify/Product/9013403549917"]

item.title: Amy Ayanda Lester
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107607773 Amy Ayanda Lester 2493 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640226148573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013939962077", "gid://shopify/Product/9013940420829", "gid://shopify/Product/9013940945117", "gid://shopify/Product/9013941567709"] Discover the work of Amy Ayanda Lester, a Cape Town-based artist with an Honours degree from Michaelis School of Fine Art. Her abstract art engages with themes of memory, loss, and the South African landscape, particularly fynbos and proteas, influenced by her family's history with Apartheid forced removals. [19813,19989,19853,23325,23328,19876] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Ayanda Lester (b.1992) is a Cape Town-based artist and musician whose vibrant, abstract works explore the intricate relationship between memory, loss, and the striking natural beauty of the South African landscape. A graduate of The Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, where she earned an Honours degree in Painting, Lester's work is deeply inspired by her surroundings, particularly the region's unique flora, colours, and people. \\nHer art, which spans paintings, prints, and collaborative vessels, often features iconic elements like proteas, fynbos, and the silhouette of Table Mountain. These motifs are not merely decorative but are imbued with personal and historical weight, stemming from her family's profound connection to the land and the trauma of their forced removal from their flower farm during Apartheid. This poignant contradiction—between the land's stunning beauty and the painful memories it holds—reverberates through her work. \\nLester's style is characterized by a loose, wandering quality, guided by an intuitive and spontaneous use of colour. She describes her application of colour as being dedicated to a specific feeling or moment, capturing its immediate, abstract, and playful essence. \\nThroughout her career, Lester has been a notable participant in numerous group exhibitions and has exhibited independently. In March 2024, she collaborated with printmaker Roxy Kaczmarek at the prestigious David Krut Workshop. Her recent projects also include a series of vessels with Natasha Human and a new body of nine original works on canvas prepared for a solo presentation at the Latitudes Art Fair in May 2024."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013939568861","gid://shopify/Product/9013939962077","gid://shopify/Product/9013940420829","gid://shopify/Product/9013940945117","gid://shopify/Product/9013941567709","gid://shopify/Product/9014041772253","gid://shopify/Product/9014041805021"]

item.title: Amy-Leigh Braaf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107280093 Amy-Leigh Braaf gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650693001437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452061982941","gid://shopify/Product/9452062015709","gid://shopify/Product/9452062081245"] Discover the work of Hakopike (Amy-Leigh Braaf), a South African painter and illustrator exploring mixed heritage and identity. Through vibrant art, she tells the untold stories of her Indonesian, Japanese, and Cape Malay ancestors in post-Apartheid South Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hakopike, the professional name of Johannesburg-born artist Amy-Leigh Braaf, is a South African painter, illustrator, and photographer with eight years of professional experience. Specializing in vibrant acrylic paintings and digital pieces, Hakopike embarks on a deeply personal exploration of her mixed heritage, drawing from travels and ancestral ties to Indonesia, Japan, and South Africa. \\nBorn into the complexities of post-Apartheid South Africa, Braaf was confronted with labels from a young age. This experience ignited a profound interest in the oral histories and ancestry within her family, leading her to question the nature of history documented primarily through storytelling. This inquiry became the catalyst for her powerful series, \"Celestial Deities.\" Through this body of work, she channels and explores the lives of \"those who came before,\" giving form to the ancestors who gifted her a rich and diverse lineage. \\nAfter learning of her great-grandmother's Indonesian and Japanese roots, combined with her \"Cape Malay\" heritage, Braaf began to investigate the meaning of being racially ambiguous in South Africa. Her art seeks to showcase the unique mixed culture of Coloured people in the nation, celebrating everything from local culinary traditions to the psychological resilience developed in response to the trauma of Apartheid. \\nThrough a compelling use of symbolism, vibrant colour, and narrative, \"Celestial Deities\" depicts characters that fuse her knowledge of the past with the reality of their descendants today. Hakopike's work aims to illuminate the rich, untold stories of those who were denied a voice, bringing their powerful histories to the forefront."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452061982941","gid://shopify/Product/9452062015709","gid://shopify/Product/9452062081245"]

item.title: Amy Rusch
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108295901 Amy Rusch 1737 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640226443485 Discover the work of Amy Rusch, a South African interdisciplinary artist who uses stitched thread on found plastic bags to explore themes of deep time, archaeology, and sensory experience. Her unique mark-making bridges contemporary culture with elemental time. [25459,25458,25460,25455,25456,25457] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Rusch is an artist working across disciplines and mediums. She’s been exploring a vibrational expression of mark-making, using stitched thread into layers of found plastic bags. \\n”Cutting, stitching, heating, pulling, binding, gathering, layering – these practices demand their own rhythm, by turns slow and meticulous then quick, fast interventions. The motions enacted in making provide a retrospective link to the embodied experiences, transmuted in the process. The machine stitching into plastic is not about replicating an experience, an object, or anything formally understood. The process is about sitting with the remnants of man-made materials; human time in contrast to the elemental and deep time.” \\nRecent exhibitions include presentations at the Investec Cape Town Art Fair 2025 and FNB Art Joburg 2024 with Suburbia Contemporary. Amy presented a solo body of work with SMAC gallery in 2022 titled Seeing with a Listening Ear, a culmination of 3 years of making. She exhibited at the Norval Foundation as part of the Norval Sovereign African Art Prize 2023 finalists exhibition. She has shown work at the Pretoria Art Museum, Iziko South African National Gallery as well as the Zeitz MOCAA. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9132522602717","gid://shopify/Product/9133224001757","gid://shopify/Product/9133224067293","gid://shopify/Product/9133224198365","gid://shopify/Product/9133224100061","gid://shopify/Product/9133233045725"]

[25402,25404,11421] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anastasia Pather s a Johannesburg-based artist distinguished by her unique practice of finger painting. Her work is a dynamic exploration of value, rejection, and production, delving into the intricate connections between surface, gender, and perceived worth. Pather masterfully employs ambiguity and innuendo, creating layered narratives that invite deeper contemplation. \\nHer paintings navigate the complex and often overlapping territories of exoticism, eroticism, and history. Through this lens, Pather examines her own-conflicted feelings surrounding culture, inheritance, and love. The tactile and immediate nature of finger painting allows for a direct and visceral expression of these multifaceted themes, resulting in works that are as intellectually provocative as they are visually compelling. She challenges viewers to confront their own preconceptions and explore the subtle nuances that define our understanding of identity and relationships."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359247581"]

item.title: Andiswa Bhungane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108754653 Andiswa Bhungane 1654 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650695229661 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013353054429", "gid://shopify/Product/9013376286941", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394899165", "gid://shopify/Product/9013449490653"] Discover the work of Andiswa, a Johannesburg luxury artist creating 3D sculpted paintings with resin, plaster, and gold. Her collections are inspired by dance, joy, and finding art in the everyday. [13901,16656,10740,21601,12974,21602] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andiswa Bhungane is a Johannesburg-based mixed media artist whose work is a vibrant celebration of life's euphoric pleasures. Despite holding a Bachelor of Commerce from the Univ. of KwaZulu-Natal, her creative path was inevitable. Born in KwaZulu-Natal to a family of creatives—her mother a dressmaker and pastry chef, and her sister an event planner and restaurateur—Andiswa's love for art was nurtured from a young age, allowing her to hone the distinctive skills she employs today. \\nIn her practice, Andiswa masterfully combines luxurious and tactile materials, including resin, plaster, oil paint, acrylic, and various forms of gold. She launched her art career just two years ago, making an immediate impact with two collections: “Tempt the fates once more” and “Darling, might we dance?” Inspired by the liberating feeling of dance, these works capture moments of simple, profound joy. This theme of movement and celebration continued into her latest collection, “Invitation to the dance,” which features dynamic 3D sculpted pieces on canvas, beaming with rich colour and texture. \\nGuided by her personal motto, \"Find art in the everyday,\" Andiswa's work translates the energy of social connection and personal delight into tangible, opulent forms. Her art is an invitation to embrace the sentiment expressed by Agnes De Mille: “To dance is to be out of yourself, larger, more beautiful, more powerful…this is power. It is glory on Earth and it is yours for thetaking.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013353054429","gid://shopify/Product/9013376286941","gid://shopify/Product/9013394899165","gid://shopify/Product/9013449490653","gid://shopify/Product/9014000222429","gid://shopify/Product/9014000255197"]

item.title: Andrea Burgener
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108984029 Andrea Burgener 2466 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650697392349 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013989408989"] Discover Andrea Burgener, a Johannesburg-based artist who explores the politics of food through various media. Learn about her work, exhibitions, and her connection to sustainable ethical food production. [19465,19466,23316,21242,19468,23320,19469,19470,19471,23315,19767,19473,19474,19486,21243,23318] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrea Burgener graduated with an MAFA (cum laude) from Wits University and resides in Johannesburg. Her artistic practice is closely linked to her long-standing support of sustainable ethical food production. Burgener's work, which spans her roles as an artist, chef, and food writer, explores the politics of food using various media, including paint, pen, fast food boxes, coffee filters, and birthday cakes. \\n \\nHer work is characterized by distinctive wit and a cynical sensibility, creating a nexus of motifs and notations. The European high-hat toque, symbolic of hierarchical, military-style kitchen brigades, frequently appears in her pieces that explore the links between agricultural processes and warfare. In her series 'The Phosphorus Trail,' she uses phosphorescent paint on objects to trace the devastation caused by this chemical in historical conflicts and its common use in fertilizer. Rats appear regularly in her work as markers of how globalized systems dictate ethics, rendering them permissible collateral damage. \\n \\nTitles like 'Soil Erosion - the Musical' and 'Battle Hymn of the Crop Sprayers' delve into the disconnect in domestic consumption and Burgener's own conflicted culpability. By highlighting the 'invisibility' of labor, food chains, and chemicals like phosphorus and nitrogen in our food, Burgener questions how visual fields made for observation can engage the divide between urban consumers and industrial agriculture."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013934489821","gid://shopify/Product/9013934522589","gid://shopify/Product/9013934588125","gid://shopify/Product/9013934620893","gid://shopify/Product/9013934653661","gid://shopify/Product/9013934686429","gid://shopify/Product/9013934784733","gid://shopify/Product/9013934850269","gid://shopify/Product/9013938815197","gid://shopify/Product/9013989408989","gid://shopify/Product/9013289648349","gid://shopify/Product/9014041510109","gid://shopify/Product/9014041575645","gid://shopify/Product/9014041608413","gid://shopify/Product/9013297578205","gid://shopify/Product/9014041673949"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109049565 Andrew Kayser 2333 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650698146013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014045573341", "gid://shopify/Product/9014045638877"] Explore the psycho-geographical paintings of Andrew Kayser, a South African artist whose works delve into the complexities of suburban life. [23441,23915,23440,23439,23916,14590] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Kayser (b. 1975) is a psycho-geographical painter whose works explore the complexities and contradictions of suburban life, a middle-class ideal fraught with struggles to maintain comfort. Utilizing oil paint, Kayser;s art reflects a collision of inner and outer realities, inviting various interpretations without imposing a singular viewpoint. His paintings delve into themes of doubt, ambiguity, and contradiction, capturing a poignant, melancholic, and beautiful essence. \\nBorn in East London, South Africa, Kayser graduated from the Koninklijke Academie van Beeldende Kunsten (Royal Academy of Art) in Den Haag, Netherlands, in 2001. After several exhibitions in the Netherlands, he returned to South Africa in 2005. Following a battle with alcoholism, he resumed his professional art practice in 2014. His solo exhibitions include 'At Home After Dark' (2017) and 'Fragments of Longer Stories' (2023) at Graham Contemporary, Johannesburg. His work has been showcased at numerous international art fairs and is collected both nationally and internationally. Kayser lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013406007517","gid://shopify/Product/9013406138589","gid://shopify/Product/9014045573341","gid://shopify/Product/9014045638877","gid://shopify/Product/9014063136989"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641112064221 Anico Mostert 2229 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650708861149 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452132663517", "gid://shopify/Product/9452132696285", "gid://shopify/Product/9452132729053", "gid://shopify/Product/9452132794589", "gid://shopify/Product/9452132892893"] Discover Anico Mostert, a Cape Town artist and printmaker. Her multi-disciplinary work transforms quiet, everyday moments into surreal and colourful still lifes that are both familiar and unexpected. [24355,24356,24357,24358,24359,24360] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anico Mostert (b.1995) is a multi-disciplinary artist and printmaker from Cape Town. She graduated from Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2017, where she majored in printmaking. \\nAnico’s work speaks to the quiet moments of the everyday. Her approach to making is versatile, seeing her producing across ceramics, textile design, animation and painting. She allows her practice to be intuitive and exist as a process of learning and discovery, creating the space for vivid colours and coltish figures to find their place in paintings and prints. \\nAnico uses reference images from social media to imagine still lifes of ordinary scenes, observing the elements of the medium for the artwork to determine itself. Each piece’s name occurs as Anico imagines what it would say if it could speak. The works upend familiarity, reminiscent of home spaces, yet offering a surreal swing of imagery, where rooms are unpeopled and yet full of life and pictures of people are empty of objects. \\nHer works exude a calm quietness, illustrating unexpected details and unassuming scenarios that verge on the mundane but are illuminated through her attention and careful colour choices. Anico’s work depicts still lifes, interactions and scenes that feel familiar and comforting but are also somewhat inverted and distorted to feel fresh and unexpected."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452132663517","gid://shopify/Product/9452132696285","gid://shopify/Product/9452132729053","gid://shopify/Product/9452132794589","gid://shopify/Product/9452132892893","gid://shopify/Product/9452132925661"]

item.title: Ann Gollifer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641114030301 Ann Gollifer 2373 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640228704477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452132565213","gid://shopify/Product/9452132597981","gid://shopify/Product/9452132630749"] Explore the work of Ann Gollifer, a Botswana-based visual artist specializing in painting, printmaking, writing, and photography. Discover how her experiences and collaborations have shaped her unique artistic vision. [23599,24354,24352,24353,23600,24446,18786,24445,24447,19985,19980,19983,19977] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ann Mary Gollifer is a multifaceted visual artist whose practice spans painting, printmaking, writing, and photography. A permanent resident of Botswana since 1985, her artistic journey is deeply intertwined with the country's vibrant cultural landscape. Gollifer's academic foundation was laid at Edinburgh University, where she earned a Master's degree in History of Art in 1983. \\nHer professional career began at the National Museum and Art Gallery in Gaborone, where she served as a Senior Technical Officer under the visionary leadership of Alec Campbell. Her significant contributions include her decade-long involvement with the Thapong Triangle International Artist’s workshops, where she facilitated global artistic exchange and helped establish the Thapong Visual Arts Centre. \\nThese workshops, initiated by Veryan Edwards and Robert Loder, connected her with a diverse network of artists from Africa, Europe, and beyond. Residencies and workshops at venues like the Bag Factory, Greatmore Studios, and Gas Works further enriched her practice. Encounters with artists like Goddy Leye, David Koloane, and Vanessa Jackson profoundly shaped her artistic perspective. \\nGollifer’s work is driven by a belief in art's capacity to foster dialogue and celebrate diversity. She continues her studio practice in Gaborone, exploring the intersections of various artistic disciplines and cultural influences."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452132565213","gid://shopify/Product/9452132597981","gid://shopify/Product/9452132630749"]
