item.title: Anna van der Ploeg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641113506013 Anna van der Ploeg gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650710139101 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452043895005","gid://shopify/Product/9452044222685"] Discover Anna van der Ploeg, a South African artist creating poetic paintings, carved plywood sculptures, woodblock prints, and immersive video work. Known for her storytelling, Mokuhanga mastery, beekeeping motifs, and shows like Visitor and Omens in Hot Bacon Contradiction. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anna van der Ploeg (b. 1992) is a contemporary South African artist whose multi-disciplinary practice encompasses painting, printmaking, sculpture, and video. She has held several solo exhibitions, shown in galleries locally and abroad, and participated in artist residencies in Japan, India, and France. Her work is held in private and public collections, including the South African National Art Bank. She is currently pursuing a Master of Fine Arts at the KASK Royal Conservatory of Art in Belgium. \\n \\nHer artistic practice is built on a foundation of technical dexterity and intellectual curiosity. A pivotal influence is her hands-on experience as a beekeeper, which began after a dramatic encounter with a swarm of bees. This has become a central motif in her work, where the figure of the beekeeper serves as a recurring protagonist and the societal structure of the hive becomes a metaphor for human communities. This theme defines her distinctive palette of warm ochres and wood blue. \\n \\nVan der Ploeg’s process is labour-intensive and deeply engaged with materiality. Her background as a printmaker led her to train in Mokuhanga (traditional Japanese woodblock printing), an experience that inspired her recent carved and painted woodblocks which merge the disciplines of print, painting, and sculpture. This focus on craft is paralleled by a sharp interest in language and literature; her titles often precede the artwork, acting as prompts for fictions in which she can probe at truth. \\n \\nAs a figurative artist, van der Ploeg seeks new metaphors to understand social assemblies and instigate dialogue. Her work offers nuanced reflections that hint at surrealism before charting their own singular path. She views the role of the contemporary South African artist as that of a cultural practitioner responsible for navigating the ruptures of our time, using art as a vital space to lay common ground and imagine things differently. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452043895005","gid://shopify/Product/9452044222685"]

item.title: Annamieke Engelbrecht
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641113211101 Annamieke Engelbrecht 627 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650710270173 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452112511197"] Explore Annamieke Engelbrecht’s cosmic-themed oil and steel works. From masked self-portraits addressing social media identity to exhibitions like Between Worlds, her art invites reflection on our place in the universe. [22871,22875,22870,22869,20869,22868,22874,20867,22867,22866,22860,22865,22879,22864,22876,22851,22863,22881,22882,22883,22877,22862,22880,22873,22878,22968] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Annamieke Engelbrecht iss is a Cape Town-based artist providing a critical commentary on internet culture and the impact of modern technology on contemporary life. Working primarily in oil paint, she intentionally juxtaposes the slow, labour-intensive process of painting with the frenetic, instant-gratification pace of the digital world. Her layered paintings, often disguised self-portraits, are inspired by the aesthetics of pixelated, low-resolution YouTube videos, critiquing a culture of quick clicks and superficial engagement. \\n \\nIn addition to her paintings, Engelbrecht's practice includes performance art where she transforms her own body into a canvas. She creates striking costumes that embody personal traits typically reserved for her closest circles, allowing the self-proclaimed introvert to express herself with a bold confidence in a \"caterpillar-to-butterfly\" metamorphosis. Esteemed art critic Llody Pollak praised her work for its depth, stating, “Annamieke teaches us something far more profound than the mere act of glancing. She teaches us how to behold.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452112511197"]

item.title: Anton Kannemeyer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641128972509 Anton Kannemeyer 1239 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640229097693 [] Discover Anton Kannemeyer, creator of Bitterkomix and Joe Dog. Known for his satirical, thought?provoking comics and graphic works critiquing race, politics, and post?apartheid society. Exhibited globally and featured in MoMA, SFMOMA, Jack Shainman Gallery, and more. [8512] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anton Kannemeyer (b. 1967) is known, revered and also berated for his work in Bitterkomix – a subversive and biting satirical publication started in 1992 with fellow student Conrad Botes. But over the years, while Kannemeyer’s provocative take on South African politics, sex and race has continued to attract critical acclaim, a sleeper project of sorts has been quietly establishing itself in the background of his practice. It’s the documentation of alien, weatherbeaten and deformed pine trees on Table Mountain; a project that originates from his enduring visual interest in the forms and abstract marks found in the landscape – keenly observed and described in the artist’s signature, masterful use of line. \\nThe mangled shapes of the trees themselves seem to stand as forms drawn by cross-currents of time and place – the results of decades of the unrelenting South Easter wind. But, echoing the thoughts of writer JM Coetzee*, the disfigured forms also make spectacular profiles, what Coetzee calls “emblems of distinction”. Kannemeyer has held numerous solo and group exhibitions both locally and abroad, including two solo shows in New York and group shows in Canada, Switzerland, Denmark, USA, Australia, Germany, DRC and The Netherlands. He has published a number of books including Pappa in Afrika (2010) which won the 2015 prize for best foreign graphic novel at Amadoras International Comic Festival in Portugal. \\n*Attwell, D 1993, J.M. Coetzee: South Africa and the Politics of Writing, University of California Press, California."}]}]} []

item.title: Anushka Kempken
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641130447069 Anushka Kempken 337 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640230015197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452043141341","gid://shopify/Product/9452043272413"] Discover Anushka Kempken’s contemporary art practice on Latitudes Online. Explore her latest works, exhibitions, and creative approach within the South African art scene. [11472,4132,4133,11473] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Astrologers often describe the planets as weaving their dances around the sky. This concept became particularly interesting to Kempken when she considered how humans weave their lives around each other too. Kempken began weaving three years ago, fascinated by chaos versus order. She found herself moved by the meditative space she entered into by repeating the familiar ‘over, under, over, under’ movement of the strands of paper she weaved. \\nOver the past three years, her weavings have continued to take her to a quiet and still place, offering time to listen to thoughts and feelings, uninterrupted. It is in that space that Kempken developed and strengthened her relationship to the divine, to intuition and to her sense of purpose in the world: \\nWe are weaving the direction we are taking for our future. We are co-creating with the universe our new reality, each thought, feeling, interaction and conversation is adding to the future we have in store for ourselves and the world. It is with every one of these thoughts that we can make a choice to create a beautiful world or not. In every single moment, we can create a pathway for our collective Well-Being. Thoughts become things. By weaving our energy intentionally, with grace and love we create more intentional grace and love in the world. We create a world where love can be seen in all areas of our lives, we live in harmony with nature and harmoniously co-create with the universe. We are the true alchemists, we are all The Rain Makers. \\nKempken has, with deliberate intention, chosen to shape and create works by first destroying them - cutting them up - only to recreate them into something new. This process of intention, creation, destruction and recreation is again a representation of the internal journey the artist experiences. Each work has been made in order to shift something within the artist's own consciousness and in turn the universal collective consciousness, expanding her awareness of internal and external existences. The titles are often inspired by affirmations, gentle reminders, concepts or ideas that moved the artist deeply. \\nInhaling, expanding. Exhaling, releasing. Gently and easily. Weaving."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452043141341","gid://shopify/Product/9452043272413"]

item.title: Arno Morland

A South African MFA-trained artist whose work—like I ride lions and Unscared Womin—bridges storytelling and silent wonder. [19748,19750,19751,19752] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Arno Morland is a South African artist based near Cape Town whose practice spans painting and bronze sculpture. Beginning his creative journey after studying Psychology, Philosophy, Theology, and later earning an MFA in Johannesburg, he has lived and worked across the US and UK before returning to South Africa \\nMorland describes himself as a “restless experimenter,” embracing early failures to forge a distinctive visual language. His paintings—often on canvas board—feature serene figures and contemplative landscapes with poetic titles like \"I ride lions\" and “A wave does not fear the oshen” \\nHis bronze sculptures, often editioned and mounted on stone, use childlike forms and angelic motifs to explore themes of humility, wonder, and human resilience. Notable works include “The way it is supposed to be and the way it is” (2018), “Big Dreams” (2019), and recent editions like “Unscared Womin” and “Nobody understand gawd” (2023) \\nMorland’s work has been exhibited internationally—he’s had several solo shows—and is represented by galleries such as Melrose Gallery, Johannesburg, and Muse Gallery Franschhoek \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452084756701","gid://shopify/Product/9452084789469","gid://shopify/Product/9452084822237","gid://shopify/Product/9452084855005"]

[9831,15026,15025,7343,18200,22794,9022] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Asha Zero was born in Johannesburg, South Africa in 1975, and currently lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nAsha Zero received his National Diploma in Fine Arts from the Tshwane University of Technology (TUT), Pretoria, South Africa in 1997. He went on to present his first solo exhibition, Winner in Hawaii, in Pretoria, South Africa in 2004. Following this, Zero presented numerous solo exhibitions, including: err_evvz in 2016 at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town, South Africa; Untitled at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town in 2015; forget about the goohexx: send in the du_plicann, in Cape Town in 2013; numberrs at Pertwee, Anderson & Gold, in London, UK in 2012; Micro Cluster Picnic at Rooke Gallery, in Johannesburg, South Africa in 2011; Macro Soda Text Hits in 2009 and Say For Me in 2008, both at 34FineArt in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nZero’s work has formed part of numerous group exhibitions and art fair presentations, both locally and abroad. His work is included in multiple collections, most notably: the Matthais & Gervanne Leridon Collection; the Jack Ginsberg Collection; the Sanlam Art Collection, and the Campbell Smith Art Collection."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452042453213","gid://shopify/Product/9452051267805","gid://shopify/Product/9452051333341","gid://shopify/Product/9452111003869","gid://shopify/Product/9452266619101"]

item.title: Asanda Kupa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641133265117 Asanda Kupa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640235127005 [] Explore the work of Asanda Kupa, a South African artist known for his expressive paintings and sculptures that delve into themes of collective identity and socio-political struggles. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"B. 1981, Molteno, Eastern Cape, South Africa. \\nAsanda Kupa’s (b.1981) work is grounded by the experiences of those forced to the periph- ery of ‘The New South Africa’; despite its great re-birth. Born in Molteno – a semi-rural village in South Africa’s poorest province, the Eastern Cape – Kupa’s scenes depict the chaos and energy of life for many of South Africa’s subjugated black population, a life that is defined by struggle and by lack of access to basic resources. \\nKupa is concerned with how the new political regime has failed its people – the very people who brought it to power through their own sacrifice – whilst also celebrating the self-de-termining spirit that marks a long history of civic action. Protest, spurred by grass-roots community frustration, is a central theme of his work. His series of striking crowd scenes, inspired by the Marikana mine-worker massacre of 2012, shows militant action not only as an expression of fury, but also a place of refuge and hope in post-apartheid South Africa. \\n"}]}]} []

Shop vibrant, expressive pieces exploring identity, culture, and everyday life. [19788,19793,19789,19798,15208,19791,19320,19795,19792,20765,19790] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Atang Tshikare (b. 1980, Bloemfontein, South Africa) is a self-taught multidisciplinary artist whose work bridges the worlds of street art, sculptural furniture, functional art, and fine art sculpture. From his early influences through the visual storytelling of his father, an anti-Apartheid activist and illustrator, Tshikare developed a distinctive style that critiques political corruption and social inequalities. \\nIn 2010, he founded Zabalazaa Designs, collaborating with local artists and working on notable commissions such as Chimurenga Magazine, Adidas Originals, BMW, MTV Base, Belvedere Vodka, and Nando’s. His work has been extensively exhibited by Southern Guild gallery (2012-2020) and has featured at prominent international events, including Design Miami/Basel with Dior and the Metropolitan Museum in New York. \\nHis exhibitions include the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa, PAD London, and Design Days Dubai. Tshikare's art emerges from dynamic negotiations between urban contemporary art and traditional Southern African cultural heritage, deeply rooted in personal experiences and an intuitive understanding of primal matter. His recent works reflect a growing engagement with global art discourse, exemplified by his 2021 show dedicated to his firstborn son, Peo. \\n \\nWith a practice that embraces a visionary African identity within a global contemporary art language, Tshikare continues to shape and influence the contemporary art and design landscape. His accolades and international recognition mark him as one of South Africa's leading contemporary artists."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452085444829","gid://shopify/Product/9452085477597","gid://shopify/Product/9452085510365","gid://shopify/Product/9452085543133","gid://shopify/Product/9452085575901","gid://shopify/Product/9452085674205","gid://shopify/Product/9452085739741","gid://shopify/Product/9452085772509","gid://shopify/Product/9452090163421"]

Shop vibrant florals, playful still lifes, and joyful compositions celebrating color and form. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As a self-taught artist, Austen Gordon practice explores illustrative realism, naïve art, and aestheticism. While their primary medium is paint, they also enjoy extending their visual expressions to ceramics. Looking forward, they are eager to delve into mixed media on larger canvases, seeking to work more expansively and freely across a variety of mediums."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452267012317"]

item.title: Awanle Ayiboro Hawa Ali
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641139294429 Awanle Ayiboro Hawa Ali gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640242204893 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045435101"] Explore and collect original paintings by Awanle Ayiboro Hawa Ali on Latitudes Online. Shop vibrant portraits and cultural narratives that delve into identity, migration, and West African heritage. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Awanle Ayiboro Hawa Ali (Ghanaian, b. 1997) is a visual artist focused on creating art based on the experiences of the African woman in a patriarchal society. Born into a strict muslim family as the first female child of her nuclear family, there had always been unrealistic societal expectations and pressure on her concerning ‘settling down’ and having children. However, Awanle, does not believe in the institution of marriage and its limitation to a woman’s worth; she paints with the intent of defying the standards set for women like her. \\nHawa aims to achieve her goals of becoming an artist who will be known for generations to come. She has always been interested in the visual arts, but could not grow her skills due to lack of interest from her parents who influenced her to follow a career in General Arts and the Humanities. However, various instances where she unknowingly gravitated towards the visual art scene and artist mentors caused her to rebel and decide on pursuing a career as an artist and defying standards that were not hers to begin with. Hawa is determined to portray these experiences through her art and as a result inspire many women to break free from societal limitations. She currently works with Artemartis, an art collective in Accra, where she spends time researching, experimenting and painting."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045435101"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641140408541 Ayanfe Olarinde 2463 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640243024093 Explore and collect original artworks by Ayanfe Olarinde on Latitudes Online. Shop vibrant mixed-media pieces and conceptual photography that delve into identity, mental health, and Yoruba folklore. [20143,20144] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1996, Ayanfe Olarinde is a self-trained visual artist from Nigeria currently employing scribbling techniques as well as photography in creating intricately detailed and multi-layered images. In 2018, Olarinde graduated from the University of Lagos with a BSc in Microbiology and has since then been dedicating her full time to art, creating works from her studio based in Lagos. \\nHer journey into art emanated from her love for scribbling, an art form bore out of imperfection on her quest for acceptance. Through this she is able to unpack her emotions in thought-provoking ways. Ayanfe’s artistic dynamism connects enthusiasts in more perspectives than one as she exploits her use of several medium including ink, paint, wire, fabric and discarded objects in creating scribbles, doodles, sculptures, paintings, digital art, upcycled artworks, and textures for her scribbles whilst speaking on broader issues of self-exploration. As an evocative artist influenced by her passage through life, her oeuvre has evolved from mixed media works on canvas to include works in photography and digital art. \\nShe is particularly interested in exploring conceptual photography as a tool for understanding the psychology of her subjects. In the past couple of years, Olarinde has participated in several group exhibitions in Nigeria and abroad including: Dis Lagos Life (2020) at SMO Contemporary Arts in Lagos, Say My Name (2020) at Signature African Art Gallery in the London, Unusual Suspects (2021) at the African Artists Foundation in Lagos, Black Voices- Friends Of My Mind at the Ross-Sutton Gallery in New York City, and Real Life Is Fragile (2021) at Thinkspace Projects in Los Angeles to name a few. \\nSome of her career highlights from the ongoing year 2021 include winning the Artist In Focus grand for Guest Projects Digital offered by the Gas Foundation in Nigeria, and receiving the Raise Our Voice grant from Voice HQ, an NFT platform for emerging artists. In 2020, Olarinde won the Creative Industry award awarded by AWIEF AWARD in South Africa. In the previous years, other achievements include being shortlisted for the GTBank \\nDays of Dorcas photography contest (2018), being nominated at 23 for the Future Awards prize for arts (2019), and winning the First Bank Magic 125 Creative Contest (2019). Olarinde’s internationally recognised series “Dem Bobo”, has been featured in several local and international publications including Reuters News, CNN, NowThisNews, Vogue, Konbini, MSN, Premium Times, NTA, and RADR Africa. In 2020, Olarinde was listed amongst the 100 Most Inspiring Women in Nigeria by Leading Women Africa."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013944942813","gid://shopify/Product/9013945041117"]

item.title: Azeezah Muhammad
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641141948637 Azeezah Muhammad 2562 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640243646685 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452093800669","gid://shopify/Product/9452093866205","gid://shopify/Product/9452093898973"] Explore and collect original artworks by Azeezah Muhammad on Latitudes Online. Shop minimalist compositions and architectural-inspired pieces that delve into form, function, and emotional resonance. [20940,20939] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 2001, in Johannesburg South Africa. Azeezah draws inspiration from varying sources and the media. Drawn to rich compositions and plays on scale and distortion of perspective. She loves the interplay of colour and rich texture in work, created by layers of colour, depth or richness of line. She dreamed of being a curator, but life had other plans for her. She still practise on the side and stays enamoured in her work. Often trying to remain authentic, her work centres around introspection, the interrogation of self, the analysis of mind scapes, perception of self and merely existing in this odd world. Azeezah’s works are simple in medium and subject matter but speak to larger and intangible concepts such as ‘emotion’ discovering art through the lens of personal experience. \\nHer works are not necessarily representational, and they are not set or situated in any particular manner or context, the viewer is able to create their own story through the visceral experience of shape, line and colour. This season of her work is situated in black inks with rich abstract forms and lines that are intended to draw the viewer in and interrogate their confusion and be taken on an experience or form one on their own, this leaves every person that engages her work to have an entirely different experience that is free from any preconceived notions or critical theories. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452093800669","gid://shopify/Product/9452093866205","gid://shopify/Product/9452093898973"]

item.title: Azola Kingston
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641142407389 Azola Kingston 2953 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640243908829 Discover Azola Kingston, an emerging South African contemporary artist featured in the Sasol New Signatures "Enduring Signatures" exhibition (2025). Known for vibrant mixed-media works that explore identity, resilience, and cultural narratives. [25426] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Azola Kingston is a self-taught visual artist born in 1994 in Philadelphia, USA, and raised in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her work is a bold celebration of Blackness. Through vibrant colour and layered composition, she honours the richness of African life - its people, its traditions, its spirit. \\nHer current range explores the idea of a seat at the table: not as invitation, but as affirmation. Her work insists that African art, stories, and voices are central to the cultural conversation, not because they echo others, but because they carry their own undeniable weight. She draws beauty from community: shared meals, everyday rituals, generational wisdom, unspoken knowing. Her work brings light to the untold narratives of Black and African contribution, ones that deserve not only to be acknowledged, but celebrated. \\nEach piece tells a story that’s been waiting to be seen: a story of pride, presence and power. It doesn’t whisper. It doesn’t wait. It arrives. Vivid, vital, and impossible to ignore."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9133216104669"]

item.title: Azuka Muoh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641142669533 Azuka Muoh 1817 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640243941597 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452057821405","gid://shopify/Product/9452170510557","gid://shopify/Product/9452181061853","gid://shopify/Product/9452278350045","gid://shopify/Product/9452278382813"] Explore the evocative works of Azuka Muoh, a Lagos-born artist whose digital surrealist paintings and films confront masculinity, memory, and societal narratives. Her acclaimed exhibitions include "Harmattan Has Come" and "Store in a Cool Dry Place" at Christopher Moller Gallery. [12410,25569,16697,16700,16701,21671,20566,16702,12409,21673,12407,12257,16693,16695,16694,12489,12415,16696,20548,12413,23957,12411,23958] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Azuka Muoh (b. 2000) is a multidisciplinary artist born and raised in Lagos, Nigeria. Her work explores the intricate relationship between memory, identity, and place, using visual storytelling to challenge the narratives that shape collective and personal histories. Drawing from her own lived experiences, Muoh reimagines cultural memory, interrogating how shared pasts influence the present. \\nHer creative process is deeply rooted in design and film, a foundation that allows her to wield colour, form, and composition with striking intentionality, seamlessly merging technical precision with raw emotional depth. The result is a body of work that is both visually compelling and conceptually rich—works that carry weighty introspections on nostalgia, and kinship. At the heart of Muoh’s practice is a desire to question long-held societal norms and disrupt conventional perspectives. As a Nigerian woman navigating a deeply complex society, she uses her art to confront the interplay between tradition, modernity, and autonomy. \\nHer pieces often serve as a commentary on generational shifts, highlighting the tension between inherited cultural values and the evolving realities of younger generations. Muoh sees art as both a mirror and a megaphone—a way to reflect lived realities while amplifying new possibilities. As she merges indigenous patterns with contemporary forms to question how identity evolves across borders, Muoh calls her peers to change—making for a common goal; to study the generations before them, so that they can better shape the world for themselves."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452057821405","gid://shopify/Product/9452170510557","gid://shopify/Product/9452181061853","gid://shopify/Product/9452278350045","gid://shopify/Product/9452278382813"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641145061597 Bahati Simoens 1963 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640245350621 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013398077661","gid://shopify/Product/9013398175965"] Explore the vibrant figurative paintings of Belgian-Congolese visual artist Bahati Simoens, based in Johannesburg. Discover and buy original art pieces that reflect cultural heritage and personal narratives, available online for collectors worldwide. [14053,9392,9396,9393,9394,9395,14054] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bahati Simoens (b. 1992) is a Belgian-Congolese visual artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Bahati embarked on her journey as an artist in 2021, crafting a unique style deeply embedded in her cultural heritage and personal narrative. She describes her work as a \"love letter to the Black body,\" encapsulating the beauty and strength of Black identities through vibrant figurative paintings that evoke warmth, softness, and a serene yet assertive presence. \\nBahati's artistry stems from a deeply personal place—her practice began as a form of self-therapy, a journey to find a sense of belong and home. This introspective beginning has since expanded into a reflective exploration of the Black experience, using art as a medium to inspire viewers to see themselves through a lens of compassion and strength. Her work is suffused with memories and elements of everyday life, articulated through dynamic compositions and a palette that harmonizes brightness and shadow, embodying a \"daydream under the midday sun.\" \\nHer career took off with her participation in a group exhibition at Botho Project Space in Johannesburg, soon followed by a solo exhibition at Medium Tings in New York. Since then, she has exhibited internationally at notable venues, including La Causa Galeria in Madrid, and participated in events such as the Investec Cape Town Art Fair and collaborations with Selfridges & Co and Nataal Media. Her pieces have been featured in group exhibitions across Berlin, Los Angeles, and Johannesburg, marking her presence on the global art scene. \\nThrough her practice, Bahati aims to affirm and celebrate Black identities, offering viewers a mirror through which they might recognize a sense of self and presence they hadn't known they were missing."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013398077661","gid://shopify/Product/9013398175965"]

[22084,22078,24361,24362,24363,14596,22086,22067,22066,20083,20091,22068,22148,22082,22069,22085,22075,14591,20093,20092,22070,22079,22071,22080,22072,22295,22083,11399,22073,22074,22090,3517,25615] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Balekane Legoabe (b. 1995) is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. With a formal educational background in graphic design and illustration, Legoabe holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Visual Communication with a specialization in Illustration and a Bachelor of Arts degree in Film Arts with a specialization in Motion Design, both from the Open Window Institute. \\nLegoabe's artistic practice spans mixed media, digital collages, animations, and gestural ink drawings. Her work is marked by a deep exploration of the interdependent relationships between humanity and the natural world. By using organic objects like plants, animals, and human figures, she creates pieces that resonate on a visceral level, encouraging viewers to tap into the complexity and obscurity of their emotions. Her art often delves into themes of liminality, emotional states, and the parallel experiences that characterize human and natural interactions. \\nHer creative process involves working in both digital and traditional media, often resulting in intricate compositions that blend visual storytelling with abstract representations. Legoabe’s work is known for its dynamic use of color and form, creating a powerful narrative that speaks to both personal and collective experiences. \\nLegoabe has exhibited her work in numerous group exhibitions and art fairs across South Africa, including the Turbine Art Fair and the StateoftheART Gallery Award Finalists Exhibition, where she won the prize in 2019. Her work is also part of public collections at the William Humphreys Gallery in Kimberley, South Africa, and the Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe in Hamburg, Germany. \\nIn addition to her artistic practice, Legoabe teaches extramural art lessons and has over four years of experience in arts management and curation. She currently serves as the Curator and Marketing Liaison for Latitudes Online."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013358526685","gid://shopify/Product/9013291483357","gid://shopify/Product/9013406236893","gid://shopify/Product/9013942616285","gid://shopify/Product/9013942649053","gid://shopify/Product/9013942681821","gid://shopify/Product/9013942747357","gid://shopify/Product/9014009200861","gid://shopify/Product/9014009331933","gid://shopify/Product/9014009430237","gid://shopify/Product/9014009463005","gid://shopify/Product/9014009659613","gid://shopify/Product/9014009725149","gid://shopify/Product/9014009757917","gid://shopify/Product/9014009790685","gid://shopify/Product/9014009823453","gid://shopify/Product/9014009856221","gid://shopify/Product/9014009888989","gid://shopify/Product/9014009921757","gid://shopify/Product/9014009954525","gid://shopify/Product/9014009987293","gid://shopify/Product/9014010118365","gid://shopify/Product/9014011166941","gid://shopify/Product/9014084763869","gid://shopify/Product/9014084796637","gid://shopify/Product/9014084829405","gid://shopify/Product/9133235077341"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641145815261 Balnura Nussipova 2262 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640246169821 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452105597149","gid://shopify/Product/9452105629917","gid://shopify/Product/9452105662685","gid://shopify/Product/9452170608861"] Explore the works of Balnura Nussipova, a multimedia artist and film photographer from Kazakhstan, on Latitudes Online. Her art delves into themes of equality, social justice, and LGBTQ+ awareness, reflecting her cultural heritage and personal experiences. [21973,21974,21975,21972] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Balnura Nussipova is a multimedia artist and film photographer based in Almaty, Kazakhstan. Born in 1998, Nussipova grew up in Astana and Almaty, and spent significant time in the Jambyl region (Taraz). Balnura has collaborated on various projects with FMT.Jetlag, Qara Production, the United Nations Development Programme, and Red Bull. She has also held roles as a production designer and exhibited in various spaces, including the National Museum of Kazakhstan in Astana, TEDx Astana, and ARTBATFEST in Almaty. \\nA strong advocate for human rights, Nussipova’s Contemporary practice focuses on themes such as equality, social justice, LGBTQ+ awareness, and education in Central Asia. Nussipova’s works are informed by her experience with different mediums such as animation, music, painting, collage, video, and photography, which she uses to narrate her impressions of the world around her. As a femme artist who draws from her childhood experiences in the village, Nussipova’s works are both nostalgic yet anticipatory, and as such, exist as not only a reflection of her national culture, traditions, and memories, but also her relationship with the environment. Above all, Nussipova’s practice extends beyond the analogue lens, as she also tackles themes of social inequality. Regardless of gender, race, nationality, religion, or sexual orientation, Nussipova advocates for the equal rights of all. Oyan Qazaq is another seminal work by Nussipova that further explores her experience of the industrialization of Kazakhstan, in which she highlights themes of collectivization and repression. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452105597149","gid://shopify/Product/9452105629917","gid://shopify/Product/9452105662685","gid://shopify/Product/9452170608861"]

item.title: Bambo Sibiya
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641146601693 Bambo Sibiya 559 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640246497501 [] Discover Bambo Sibiya's art, marked by rich detail and textures. His linocuts and lithographs explore masculine identity and community in Johannesburg. A finalist in the ABSA L’Atelier top ten awards and winner of the Gerard Sekoto Award, Sibiya's work is held in esteemed collections like the Bibliothèque Nationale de France. [24117,24116,24118] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bambo Sibiya was born in KwaThema, Springs, near Johannesburg. He trained and worked at the Artist Proof Studio (APS) Gallery, where he has collaborated on large-scale linocuts for several prominent artists, including William Kentridge, Diane Victor, Norman Catherine, and Colbert Mashile. Sibiya’s linocuts, drypoint, and lithographic works are marked by rich stylistic detail and textures, offering insight into masculine identity and community on the streets of Johannesburg. \\nDuring apartheid, men from the rural areas journeyed to cities in search of work. They often brought stylish suits to impress families back home and practiced looking sharp for friends and neighbours. This evolved into “the Swenkas”, where working-class South Africans held competitions to showcase the best outfits and moves. The men valued physical cleanliness, sobriety, and above all, self-respect. \\nIn recent years, Sibiya has excelled in South African art competitions. In 2012, he was a finalist in the ABSA L’Atelier top ten awards and won the prestigious Gerard Sekoto Award, which facilitated his completion of two residencies in 2013 at Atelier le Grand Village (Angouleme, France) and Cité Internationale des Arts (Paris, France). Bambo’s works are held in the Bibliothèque Nationale de France (the national collection of prints), among other collections. \\nSelect Exhibitions \\n \\n2018 ‘Izikhali ze Mpilo’: Solo Exhibition, Jack Bell Gallery, London \\n2018 ‘Rassemblement, Jack Bell Gallery, London \\n2018 1:54 Art Fair, Jack Bell Gallery, London \\n2018 1:54 Art Fair, Jack Bell Gallery, New York \\n2017 ‘Ubuntu Ngabantu’: Solo Exhibition, Jack Bell Gallery, London \\n2017 ‘Tales of Migration’: Solo Exhibition, Red Room Gallery, Cape Town \\n2017 1:54 Art Fair, Jack Bell Gallery, London \\n2017: 10th Print Triennial, Chamalières, France \\n2016: Douro Print Biennial, Portugal \\n2016 Art Exchange: Querètaro, Galeria Municipal and Taller Tamayo, Oaxaca, Mexico \\n2015: 7th International Lithographic Symposium, Tidaholm, Sweden \\n2013 ‘Khumbula Ekhaya (Home Sick)’, Gallery 2, Johannesburg \\n2013 ‘Human Spirit’, ABSA Art Gallery, Johannesburg \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Banele Khoza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641146896605 Banele Khoza 509 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640246857949 Discover the evocative works of Banele Khoza, a South African-based visual artist renowned for his expressive paintings and digital art. His work delves into themes of love, masculinity, and human connection, characterized by vibrant colours and fluid forms. [3553,3554,18585,18583,18582,18584,3550,18587,18586,3552] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Banele Khoza was born Eswatini and is a South African-based visual artist. He holds a BTech in Fine Arts from Tshwane University of Technology, Pretoria. He started his studies at the London International School of Fashion in Johannesburg but soon realised his passion was drawing and transferred to study Fine Arts. On completion of his degree, he taught Drawing as well as Art Theory at the University of Technology, Pretoria. In 2018 he decided to stop teaching to work as a full-time artist and to launch a multi-purpose studio and gallery called BKhz in Johannesburg. \\nBanele Khoza has had a solo show at Zeitz MOCAA, has the 2017 Gerard Sekoto Foundation award under his belt and a fleet of taxi’s covered in his work (as the result of him winning the SA Taxi Foundation Art Award). In 2019 he was named as one of the Mail and Guardian's 200 Young South Africans. \\nKhoza’s lithographs, demonstrate his skill and dexterity. Khoza’s ability to embrace the unknown and to immerse himself in the technical possibilities of what lithography has to offer combined with the skills of Master Printer Mark Attwood have resulted in prints that reveal the artist’s gifts. \\nIn 2017 he won the prestigious Gerard Sekoto Award and with it a three-month residency at the CitéInternationale des Arts in Paris. His solo exhibitions include Temporary Feelings at the Pretoria Art Museum (2016); Lonely Nights at Lizamore Gallery (2017) LOVE? at Smith Studio in Cape Town (2018). Khoza also headlined the solo exhibition titled LGBTQI+: Banele Khoza as part of the Curatorial Lab at Zeitz MOCAA (2018). \\nIn 2018 he curated A Letter to my 22 Year Old Self, a group show presented to launch his fundraising activities which will give grants to art students dealing with economic hardship at SA universities. In 2019 Khoza opened Seeking Love; a museum touring show around South Africa and has been awarded the M&G 200 Young South Africans. \\nKhoza is also the co-curator with Nicole Siegenthaler of Art Joburg: Gallery Lab."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013843591389","gid://shopify/Product/9013843624157","gid://shopify/Product/9013843656925","gid://shopify/Product/9013843722461","gid://shopify/Product/9013843755229","gid://shopify/Product/9013843787997"]

item.title: Bastiaan van Stenis
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641151516893 Bastiaan van Stenis gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640250233053 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013465219293","gid://shopify/Product/9452175425757","gid://shopify/Product/9452175458525"] Discover the evocative works of Bastiaan van Stenis, a self-taught South African artist renowned for his mixed-media paintings and sculptures. Drawing inspiration from his heritage and life experiences, his art delves into themes of identity, memory, and the human condition. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bastiaan van Stenis (b. 1981) lives and works near Cape Town, South Africa. He is of half Dutch, half South African descent and grew up in Cape Town. He is a descendant of the renowned 19th Century English painter Thomas Baines. \\nVan Stenis is primarily a self-taught artist but he received private art tutoring and guidance from a young age. After his schooling in 2000, he dedicated himself to painting full-time. It is said that a good painter is good at solving problems on the canvas – a challenge that Van Stenis enjoys. He veers toward the unexpected then carefully steers it back to somewhere slightly more sensible. The result leaves the viewer intrigued and with a sense of adventure. The manner in which he weaves his mediums together represents the stitching together of the self in a dreamlike portrayal of reality. \\nThe childlike brutality refers to a narrative of growing up and surviving as an individual amidst the complexities of social codes, expectations and definitions of being. “We carry memories like marks that define us. We collect emotions and they shape our form,” he says. Bastiaan van Stenis works mainly with oil paint on canvas but on occasion uses acrylic paint, glue and found objects in his paintings. Other projects include taxidermy and sculpture."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013465219293","gid://shopify/Product/9452175425757","gid://shopify/Product/9452175458525"]

item.title: Bau Kaashe (Kuru Art Project Collective)
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641151779037 Bau Kaashe (Kuru Art Project Collective) gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640250364125 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131385565"] Discover Bau Kaashe, a collaborative art collective under the Kuru Art Project, showcasing innovative contemporary African artworks rooted in cultural dialogue and creative exploration. View exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Kuru Art Project is located in the village of D'kar, Western Botswana. The project was established in 1991 as part of the larger Kuru Development Trust. The artists are Naro and Dcui San, who have lived in and around D'kar since the early 1960's. Formally a nomadic people, hunting and food gathering from the veld remain significant cultural activities, but increasing westernisation means that this is not a sustainable lifestyle anymore. Myths, legends and events of a bygone era are readily told by elders, but the less fortunate can only try to imagine life as it once was. Yet they all converge on a theme characterised by a mythical connection with animals and objects of their ancient past, while continuing their lives in a world that demands completely different skills to survive. \\nToday, there are 18 artists actively participating in the project. The artists work in a variety of media and techniques, which include oil on canvas, different printmaking techniques, and embroidery. \\nThey draw inspiration from stories told by their ancestors, and their expansive knowledge about the plants and animals from the Kalahari. For them, their art is a way to convey their identity and unique ways of life to the rest of the world. The Kuru artists’ work is known for its spontaneity. Often, the process is preferred over the product—their love for making and creating forms an intricate part of their culture. Bright colours and naive animal and plant forms signify the work of these artists. Their body of work is internationally acclaimed and has been exhibited in over fifteen countries abroad and in Africa over the years. \\nBau was born in D’kar (b.1985) and attended D’kar Primary school. She later attended Rethuseng Junior Secondary School in Charles Hill. \\nShe was first introduced to embroidery at a workshop in D’kar that was hosted by embroiderers from the Keiskamma Art Project in the Eastern Cape. She was excited about the workshop and hoped that learning a new skill will help her to be able to earn some income in the future. Bau loves making all kinds of craft and being creative. The plants and animals from the Kalahari are very important to the people from her culture and therefore she loves to depict it in things she embroiders. \\nBau was born in D’kar and attended D’kar Primary school. She later attended Rethuseng Junior Secondary School in Charles Hill. \\nShe was first introduced to embroidery at a workshop in D’kar that was hosted by embroiderers from the Keiskamma Art Project in the Eastern Cape. She was excited about the workshop and hoped that learning a new skill will help her to be able to earn some income in the future. Bau loves making all kinds of craft and being creative. The plants and animals from the Kalahari are very important to the people from her culture and therefore she loves to depict it in things she embroiders. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131385565"]

item.title: Beau Disundi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641151910109 Beau Disundi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640250790109 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452168413405"] Explore the evocative works of Beau Disundi Nzazi, a Congolese-born visual artist renowned for his expressive paintings and installations. His work delves into themes of identity, colonial history, and cultural exchange, characterized by vibrant colours and symbolic materials. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Beau Disundi obtained his degree in interior design from the Kinshasa Academy of Fine Arts in 2016. During his studies, Disundi questioned his identity and how other cultures influence his own, which gave rise to his artistic practice. His explorations, in particular of cultural roots in Belgium, led him to the guiding principle of not only relating the history of the Congo, but of all peoples influenced or dominated by external cultures. “We no longer belong to a single time or place. We straddle different times and places” – Beau Disundi. Beau Disundi's works perform artistic and literary means of expression to create forms that go beyond these disciplines, blurring the boundaries between sculpture, architecture, and image. Through his creations, Beau Disundi refers to subjects that inhabit multicultural spaces. \\nHis work reveals multiple co-existing spaces, inviting the world to travel within them in order to experience other points of view. From a complementary perspective, Disundi’s work aims to convey the perception of a person in this liminal space. A person prey to acculturation and alienation. Achieving this representation enables the artist to deconstruct and step back from the confusion of identity that reigns in these spaces. So, to better understand his experience, Disundi materializes the links between his identity, historical events and global dynamics. What happens when two diametrically opposed points of view become homogeneous? How does a living being evolving in space A, while adapting to culture B, perceive the world? All these questions have led Disundi to the concept of troubled identity and appropriation, reflected in the vagueness and gaps that he creates in his work."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452168413405"]

item.title: Bekezela Mabena
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641153024221 Bekezela Mabena 2190 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650714398941 Discover the compelling works of Bekezela Mabena, a South African-based visual artist born in 1996. His mixed-media paintings and prints explore themes of identity, migration, and belonging—drawing from his Zimbabwean roots and South African experience. [23608,23607] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bekezela Mabena (born 1996) is a South African-based visual artist originally from Zimbabwe. Now living and working in Tembisa, Johannesburg, Mabena’s practice explores complex themes of migration, identity, and belonging. His work draws on his personal experience of crossing borders—both physical and cultural—navigating life between his Zimbabwean heritage and South African reality. \\nWorking primarily in mixed media, Bekezela combines screen printing, drawing, painting, and collage. His layered surfaces often integrate found materials, archival images, and text, reflecting how identities can be built from fragments of personal and collective memory. Through recurring motifs—such as maps, barbed wire, and stylized figures—he invites viewers to question notions of home, place, and dislocation. \\nA graduate of Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, Mabena is considered part of a new generation of young African artists redefining contemporary printmaking. His work has been shown in local exhibitions, and he continues to expand his practice through residencies and collaborative projects that engage with community and social justice issues."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014051897565","gid://shopify/Product/9014051930333"]

[22918,22922,22919] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ben Agbee (b. 1966 in Accra, Ghana) is a seasoned painter and portraitist known for his bold and colourful work that reflects the vitality and convivial nature of his locality. His playful poetic abstractions illuminate the balance between individuality and the wider community sphere. Full name Benjamin Agbenyega, Agbee was the first of three children born to Emmanuel Agbenyega. \\nDuring his school days, he found that creativity and art came naturally to him, becoming his easiest form of expression. Graduating with a major in art in 1989, Agbee initially worked in advertising and design. However, the harsh realities of life led him to augment his earnings by painting, quickly realizing his innate talent. \\nComing from a family of great artists, notably his uncle Victor Ameyibor, a professional artist in the Volta region of Ghana, Agbee has participated in numerous collective exhibitions in Ghana and abroad. His solo exhibitions include shows in the USA (Washington, Chicago, Detroit), Canada, and Holland. Agbee's work is celebrated for its vibrant and informative exploration of individuality and community."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014030500061","gid://shopify/Product/9014030565597","gid://shopify/Product/9014030598365"]

item.title: Ben Orkin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641160528093 Ben Orkin 2451 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640254165213 [] Ben Orkin (b.?1998, Cape Town) creates hand-coiled ceramic sculptures exploring queer intimacy, body-awareness, and emotional vulnerability. A Michaelis graduate with award-winning solo shows at WHATIFTHEWORLD and works acquired by the A4 Foundation, his evocative vessels reimagine protection and connection. [19356] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ben Orkin is a sculptor based in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nHis ceramic vessels reflect queer intimacy, oscillating between moments of nourishment and dependency, validation and resistance, love and separation.Their textured finish is evidence of the hand-builder’s careful touch, imbuing the sculptures with a sense of the tactile and, at times, the erotic. Orkin graduated in 2020 with a BFA from Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town, South Africa. Since 2019, he has held three solo exhibitions with WHATIFTHEWORLD Cape Town, namely You told me… (2019), Extra Safe (2021) and Backrooms, Bookstores, Balconies, Meatracks and Tearooms (2023). He was awarded the Simon Gerson prize in 2021. His work has been recently acquired by the A4 Foundation. In 2022 Orkin participated in the OÖ AIR artist in residence program at OÖ Landes-Kultur GmbH Museumstraße. \\nHis art work is part of the public collection OÖ Landes-Kultur GmbH, Austria. Orkin has participated in various art fairs locally and Internationally, including Investec Cape Town Art Fair (2023), Art Joburg (2022), 1-54 London (2022), Miart Milan (2022), FNB Art Joburg (2023), NOMAD Capri 2023 and Investec Cape Town Art Fair (2023)."}]}]} []

[14048,20783,14050] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Benjamin Salvatore is a multidisciplinary artist working in painting, sculpture, photography and video. \\nHis work has been featured in prestigious group shows at The Fourth Gallery in Cape Town and Candice Berman Gallery in Johannesburg. In his 2020 solo exhibition „Everybody stand still“ with Worldart Gallery he showed a selection of paintings from his Gitter series for which he is best known. \\nSalvatore remains heavily engaged with the subjects of systematic restrictions of individual freedom. Whether these restrictions are self-imposed or implicitly understood to be a societal or political norm. Conceptual influences by Maurizio Cattelan as well as Marcel Duchamp occasionally find their way into his work paired with a visibly exhausting contention about the benefits and drawbacks of systems in general. \\nHe is bored by the corporate pursuit of money, appreciates bravery to fail in a personal capacity and prefers winter over summer. \\nBenjamin Salvatore (b. 1987 in Germany) \\nbased in Cape Town, South Africa"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013397749981","gid://shopify/Product/9013397913821","gid://shopify/Product/9013964439773"]

item.title: Bev Butkow
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641162428637 Bev Butkow 625 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640262684893 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452172476637","gid://shopify/Product/9452172509405","gid://shopify/Product/9452172542173"] Explore the artistic work of Bev Butkow on Latitudes Online. Discover her unique illustrations and contemporary art practice. Stay updated on exhibitions and new artworks. [24489,24487,24488] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bev Butkow started making art in her mid-40s and is now a full time artist grounded in the seriousness of her responsibility as an artist, maker, communicator and social actor. Deeply committed to social engagement and education, she co-founded a library in Limpopo and sits on the board of 11 schools. Born and living in Johannesburg with her husband and four children, her creative home is the Bag Factory Artist Studios, blocks away from where her grandfather sold eggs at the Fresh Produce Market in the 1960s. \\nButkow uses processes of making like weaving and painting to knot and entangle, creating networks of connections that maintain a fragile equilibrium between holding together and unravelling. These entanglements give texture to the experiences that lie sedimented in her artist body, like tension experienced from taking on conflicting roles of career and mothering. \\nInvestigating socially-encoded expectations of women, women’s labour and a deep exploration of materiality, Butkow creates abstracted woven, stitched, printed and mixed media works. A slow immersion in the in-out meditation of weaving embodies a rebellion from structured control and then being contained again. Enmeshed materials, creative-making processes and personal narrative come together to make meaning of issues around gendered labour and the experiences that become written into female bodies. The female body is foregrounded as a sedimentary site of knowledge, accumulated through the micro-events of the day-to-day. With their coded surfaces, Butkow’s objects are layered stories and a mapping of contemporary life. \\nButkow is currently pursuing a Master of Fine Arts at Wits University on a scholarship from the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation Governing Intimacies project. \\nRecent exhibitions include The Art of Lithography, Wits Art Museum (2019) and 1:54 Contemporary African Art Fair in London (2019). \\nSolo exhibitions \\n2015, m/other, Lizamore & Associates, Johannesburg \\nSelect group exhibitions and fairs \\n2020 Dakar Biennele \\n2020 Investec Cape Town Art Fair \\n2019 1:54 Contemporary African Art Fair, London \\n2019 Latitudes Art Fair, Johannesburg \\n2019 Conversations in Texture, Berman Contemporary, Johannesburg \\n2018 The Art of Lithography: a collaborative expression of LL Editions, Wits Art Museum, Johannesburg \\n2018 Sister Sister, National Arts Festival, Makhanda \\n2018 Imposed, Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2018 Turbine Art Fair, Johannesburg \\n2017 Joburg Art Fair \\n2016 Contemporary showcase, Gains & Rain, Johannesburg \\n2016 Cape Town Art Fair \\n2016 Untitled 2.99 and 3.99, 99 Loop Gallery, Cape Town \\n2016 Young Collectors II, Fried Contemporary, Pretoria \\n2016 Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards Top 100, Johannesburg"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452172476637","gid://shopify/Product/9452172509405","gid://shopify/Product/9452172542173"]

Learn about his exhibitions, awards, and artistic practice. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Bevan de Wet (b. 1985) is an artist and printmaker based in Johannesburg. He graduated with a BFA with a distinction from Rhodes University in 2008. From 2011 to 2016, de Wet worked at the Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg as a professional print technician, collaborator, and academic facilitator. In 2016, he founded his own print studio, Eleven Editions, where he collaborates with artists and publishes various projects. \\n \\nDe Wet regularly works with Phumani Archive Mill, a paper-making research unit at the University of Johannesburg, where he produces his handmade paper work. His practice centers around our increase sense of alienation from the natural environment and the spaces we inhabit, highlighting the fragmented nature of our current engagement with the world. Concerns around displacement and belonging have led to a fascination with boundaries, both biological and geographical, which are never fixed but rather permeable and shifting. De Wet explores tensions between the organic and constructed world, engaging primarily with paper to push the boundaries of the surface through etching, relief printing, paper-making, drawing, and installation. \\nDe Wet has exhibited extensively both locally and internationally, holding five solo exhibitions including \\n The Other Landscape (Lizamore Gallery, 2019), \\n Drawing on Entropy (Hazard Gallery, 2018), \\n New Forms: A Study of Broken Parallels (Candice Berman Gallery, 2017) and was also included in \\n Origins & Trajectories (Paris, 2016), \\n the International Printmaking Alliance Exhibition (China 2016-17) amongst others. \\n He has exhibited numerously in the Turbine Art Fair, FNB Joburg Art Fair and the Cape Town Art Fair. His work is included in collections such as the Wits Art Museum, Nirox Foundation, South African Embassy in Washington DC, and the Ahmanson Foundation in Los Angeles. \\n \\nHis awards include the Ampersand Foundation Fellowship (New York residency, 2013), the Thami Mnyele Art on Paper Award (2013), the ABSA L'Atelier Merit Award (2014, Sylt Foundation residency, Germany), and the ImpAct Award for Visual Art from the Arts and Culture Trust (2014). He also attended the Cill Rialaig Artists Residency in Ireland (2017). \\n \\nAwards & Affiliations \\n \\n 2014 - L’Atelier Merit Award Winner \\n 2015 - Sylt Foundation Residency (Germany) \\n 2014 - ImpACT Award for Young Professionals \\n Visual Arts Winner, Arts and Culture Trust (JHB) \\n Ampersand Foundation Fellowship & Residency (New York) \\n 2012 Thami Mnyela Art on Paper Merit Award (JHB) \\n \\nResidencies \\n \\n Cill Rialaig Art Residency (Ireland) \\n Sylt Foundation Residency (Germany) \\n Bag Factory Artist Residency (Johannesburg) \\n Bag Factory Artist Residency (Johannesburg) \\n Ampersand Fellowship Residency (New York) \\n \\nSelect solo Exhibitions \\n \\n 2019 - item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641163182301 Bianca Batlle Nguema 2131 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640264519901 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452055953629"] Discover Bianca Batlle Nguema’s contemporary artworks on Latitudes Online. Explore her unique artistic style and stay updated on exhibitions and new collections. [16028,16094,16025,16033,16093,16024] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The talented Spanish-Guinean artist is Catalan-born (1980) and based in Barcelona. Bianca Batlle Nguema is a prolific painter and mixed media artist with a gift for capturing the human form and its expression in her portraits and figurative paintings. The artist's work is closely informed by her Black and African maternal roots and cultural identity. \\n`The first woman I have reference to is my great-grandmother, Emilia. She was a seamstress in Equatorial Guinea, a very modern woman, she sewed the clothes of the Spanish colonizers. Her daughter (my grandmother Marina) was a very good student and she sent her to study in Barcelona, Spain, where she studied teaching. But since she was a woman, she had to go back to town to get married. \\nShe had seven children in total, but she did not leave her vocation behind and she became a relevant character in both Guinea and Barcelona, even traveling to the United States, to New York, to teach. Following her instincts, she opened the doors for her three daughters to be educated and independent women. \\nMy grandmother had a very strong character and was unafraid. I am shaped and inspired by her, still. \\nMy mother, Marina, who was really like an older sister, who at the age of 12 years old was the first to set foot on Spanish soil, and she never returned to her homeland on the African continent. She studied and worked in Barcelona, and Andorra.When she was 25 years old I arrived in the world and from her womb. She fought many hidden things troubling her within for a long, long time in solitude and silence - all her life in fact. For reasons still only known to her and which have left this world with her, she never wanted to talk to me about her past. In 2010 she died, at that moment I decided to start my journey as a professional artist'. Bianca Batlle Nguema."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452055953629","gid://shopify/Product/9452055986397","gid://shopify/Product/9452155568349"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641163968733 Billy Monk 1216 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640265535709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452033409245", "gid://shopify/Product/9452033442013", "gid://shopify/Product/9452033835229", "gid://shopify/Product/9452033900765", "gid://shopify/Product/9452033933533", "gid://shopify/Product/9452033999069", "gid://shopify/Product/9452034654429", "gid://shopify/Product/9452034687197", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151144669", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151242973", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151308509", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151374045", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151439581", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151472349", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151505117", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151537885", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151570653", "gid://shopify/Product/9452151668957", "gid://shopify/Product/9452152160477", "gid://shopify/Product/9452162121949", "gid://shopify/Product/9452162154717", "gid://shopify/Product/9452162187485", "gid://shopify/Product/9452162253021", "gid://shopify/Product/9452162318557"] Billy Monk, Billy Monk photographer, South African photography, 1960s Cape Town, black and white photography, Latitudes Online artists, iconic photographers, original photographic prints, online art gallery [7504,6759,7482,7483,6760,7572,7573,6758,7568,7569,6755,6766,6761,6756,6769,6770,6754,6767,6768,6750,6765,6751,6753,6763,6764,6757,7486,7487,7542,7507,7508,7501,7502,7480,7546,7570,7511,7512,7558,7503,7488,6934,6939,6936,6937,6949,6952,6953,6933,6940,6946,6941,6947,6935,6945,6951,6948,6950,6942,6944,6943,6938,6954,6336,6337,6374,6396,6375,6398,6400,6402,6399,6401] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in South Africa in 1937, Billy Monk worked as a bouncer in 1960s Cape Town. Armed with a camera, he also managed to photograph inside night clubs like The Catacombs. Housing revellers of all creeds and colours, this dockside spot illustrated both forms of the word 'underground'. His access to this cross-section of society allowed him to photograph scenes of uncensored joy, passion and debauchery not often associated with apartheid-era South Africa. \\nA decade later, Paul Gordon, who had once shared a studio space with Monk, handed the meticulously labelled negatives to photographer Jac de Villiers. Intrigued by what he saw and with David Goldblatt on board too, an exhibition was staged at The Market Gallery in Johannesburg in 1982, with Monk's blessing. The show was a critical success and Billy Monk took leave from his job as a diamond diver in the north of the country's shoreline, to attend. A pit-stop in Cape Town along the way, however, proved to be the full stop in Monk's story. He was shot dead in a drunken argument. His photographs, though, live on and continue to give the world a rare glimpse into this period in Cape Town's history."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452033409245","gid://shopify/Product/9452033442013","gid://shopify/Product/9452033835229","gid://shopify/Product/9452033900765","gid://shopify/Product/9452033933533","gid://shopify/Product/9452033999069","gid://shopify/Product/9452034654429","gid://shopify/Product/9452034687197","gid://shopify/Product/9452151144669","gid://shopify/Product/9452151177437","gid://shopify/Product/9452151210205","gid://shopify/Product/9452151242973","gid://shopify/Product/9452151308509","gid://shopify/Product/9452151341277","gid://shopify/Product/9452151374045","gid://shopify/Product/9452151406813","gid://shopify/Product/9452151439581","gid://shopify/Product/9452151472349","gid://shopify/Product/9452151505117","gid://shopify/Product/9452151537885","gid://shopify/Product/9452151570653","gid://shopify/Product/9452151603421","gid://shopify/Product/9452151636189","gid://shopify/Product/9452151668957","gid://shopify/Product/9452151701725","gid://shopify/Product/9452151734493","gid://shopify/Product/9452152160477","gid://shopify/Product/9452154323165","gid://shopify/Product/9452154355933","gid://shopify/Product/9452154388701","gid://shopify/Product/9452154421469","gid://shopify/Product/9452154454237","gid://shopify/Product/9452154487005","gid://shopify/Product/9452162121949","gid://shopify/Product/9452162154717","gid://shopify/Product/9452162187485","gid://shopify/Product/9452162253021","gid://shopify/Product/9452162318557"]

item.title: Birhane Worede
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641164656861 Birhane Worede 2398 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640268845277 [] Learn about Birhane Worede, the pioneering Ethiopian environmentalist and scientist, featured on Latitudes Online. Discover his impactful work in sustainable agriculture and conservation. [24285,20174,18989,18988] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Birhane Worede’s captivated figures inhabit timeless, formless and spaceless worlds which engage only with colour, gesture and surface. Worede’s loose, washy works are reductive - exploring colour and emotion to allow his gestural hand to take centre stage, effortlessly shifting between figuration and abstraction. His figures often appear captivated by the devices they hold, navigating online social spaces rather than physical ones - a concept which is reflected in the voids they occupy. Worede ruminates on these figures disconnect from their environment as a result of being tied to their phone, leaving the spaces they occupy somewhat un-rendered. Working with oil paint on canvas, \\nWorede’s works are somewhat improvised, shifting and transforming as the artist engages with space, surface and colour. Reducing his composition to simply colour and shape, Worede sees his process as one akin to abstraction, only adding line and form at the end when he decides to pick out a figure from the rich, lush swathes of colour he has laid down. Worede’s works play with mood, oscillating between cool and warm palettes which are always punctuated by marks in the opposite hue. Worede grew up in Addis Ababa and was inspired by the frantic nature of the world famous Merkato - often sketching figures, ideas and colours inspired by his experiences at the market. Worede often uses these rapid sketches as launchpads for larger works on canvas, which prefer to push the parameters of the paint itself. \\nBirhane Worede (b. 1998, Ethiopia) lives and works in Addis Ababa. Worede graduated from the Alle School of Fine Art and Design, Addis Ababa University in 2021. Worede has previously shown with Urevbu Contemporary, Memphis, TN and as part of ‘One One’ at Moa Anbessa, Ethiopia."}]}]} []

[24289,21035,24127,24293,21032,24126,24282,24284,24128,24123] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Birhanu Manaye was born in 1998 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. His artistic journey began during his teenage years, significantly shaped by the inspiration of his older brother. With a passion for drawing ignited early on, Manaye pursued formal art education at Ale School of Fine Arts and Design (ASFAD), where he earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts with the highest honors. \\nManaye’s work explores profound and abstract concepts, delving into themes such as the subconscious, the ethereal nature of the universe, and the intricate relationships between patterns, textures, and memory. His art serves as a reflection on the complexity of existence, seeking to capture and express the intangible essence of the world around us. \\nA versatile artist, Manaye employs a wide range of media in his creative practice. His explorations span painting, woodcut, linocut, dry point print, photography, and most notably, silkscreen printing. His approach to art is characterized by a spirit of experimentation and innovation, as he continually seeks new techniques and methods to enrich his work. Manaye’s artistic practice is marked by a dedication to learning and growth, driven by a desire to push the boundaries of traditional art forms and uncover new avenues for creative expression."}]}]} []

[21985,23133,23242,23978,21986,23977,21987,21984] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Blessing Blaai (b. 1994) is a South African artist whose work is deeply influenced by his upbringing in Troyeville, a suburb of Johannesburg. He began his serious art journey at 32 Flavors Art Studio, where he honed his skills in painting, drawing, and printmaking before further mastering printmaking at Artist Proof Studio for over three years. Blaai primarily explores various media, including paint, watercolours, ink, and mixed media, often infusing his pieces with conceptual depth. \\nIn addition to his studio work, he is an accomplished muralist, completing both public and private commissions, and has contributed to numerous community mural projects commissioned by the city. \\nHis artistic contributions extend beyond individual works; he participated in the group exhibition African Mobilities: This is Not a Refugee Camp and facilitated art programs at the Windybrow Theatre for children in Hillbrow, Johannesburg through the Market Foundation. \\nBlessing Blaai's work has gained recognition, with exhibitions in notable galleries, including Gallery 2 in Johannesburg. His pieces have been offered at auction multiple times, such as his artwork MONK, which sold for $68 USD at Stephan Welz & Co. in 2022. Blaai continues to engage with the vibrant art community, creating works that reflect his unique perspective and experiences."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014007267549","gid://shopify/Product/9013395259613","gid://shopify/Product/9014007333085","gid://shopify/Product/9014007398621","gid://shopify/Product/9014037446877","gid://shopify/Product/9014040002781"]
