Layo Bright lives and works in New York, NY, US."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452085379293"]

item.title: Lawrence Lemaoana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641650082013 Lawrence Lemaoana 2406 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640735264989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086690013"] [19863,20115] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lawrence Lemaoana is an artist with a Bachelor of Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg. He currently lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. He is currently reading for a master’s degree at the University of South Africa’s Art History, Visual Arts & Musicology Department, where he is also a junior lecturer in Visual Art. His body of work has, as its departure, a fascination with the role of the mass media in present-day South Africa. Seeing the relationship between media and the 'people' as inherently problematic, he identifies and repurposes existing control apparatuses, questioning modes of control within representation; specifically, who gets to represent those in control. The power of the media to act as didactic tool or propagandistic weapon, to reveal and shape the psyche, or group consciousness. Lemaoana's embroidered text works are emblazoned with appropriated political dictums woven in kanga fabric - a material with its own complex ancestry. \\nHere, Lemaoana wages criticism on the agency of local media, and its ability to shape social consciousness: the result turns didactic and propagandistic tools on their head. He regularly exhibits in France, most notably in the context of memorable exhibitions at Foundation Louis Vuitton, La Maison \\nRouge – Antoine de Galbert Foundation, MAC-VAL, Les abattoirs, Toulouse but also in the United States, Norway, Italy, and of course, in South Africa, at the IZIKO South African National Gallery and Wits Art Museum, Johannesburg, South Africa. His work features in prominent local and international collections, including Sindika Dokolo Fondation, Luanda, IZIKO South African National Gallery, Cape Town, Louis Vuitton Fondation, Paris, and Lafayette Anticipation, Paris. Lemaoana is co-founder of the Occupying the Gallery a project that aims to transform gallery spaces into makeshift open studios for mentorship and artistic development."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086690013"]

item.title: Layziehound Coka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641651917021 Layziehound Coka 257 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640737362141 [] [289,23975,24153,23976,23973,24310,24311,24312,23974] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Layziehound Coka was born in Bilanyoni situated in Northern KwaZulu Natal in 1982. His early years were determined by the South African apartheid system that separated people of different race, and permitted very limited educational choices for people of colour. The 80s were characterized by turmoil, violence and the uprising of young, black people protesting against the regime. \\nHe attended a local primary school at Bilanyoni, before he moved to Inkamana, a Catholic High School in Vryheid in 1995. Coka matriculated at Sinethemba Agricultural and Technical Boys School. He moved to Gauteng in 2001 and started studying engineering in 2003 at Pretoria Technikon. He gave up engineering for fine art in 2005 when he started studying print making at Newtown’s Artist Proof Studio (APS). He has been working as a professional artist since graduating from APS in 2007 and predominantly works with acrylic and charcoal on paper or canvas."}]}]} []

item.title: Lazi Mathebula
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641651982557 Lazi Mathebula 323 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640737394909 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014088401117", "gid://shopify/Product/9014122971357", "gid://shopify/Product/9014123659485"] [25200,25201,22401,24433] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lazi Mathebula (b. 1989 – Johannesburg, SA) is an award-winning illustrator and independent designer who believes that real creativity involves transforming the ordinary and in a sense, turning realism on its head. He currently lives and works in Johannesburg. \\n \\nMathebula’s work reflects a recognisable fixation on fine detailing, the intricacies of the purely African stories and a tasteful use of luminous colour to create long-lasting visual impressions. His instantly recognizable textures and patterns are as distinctive as they are delicate. \\n \\nCrafted from the artist’s early experiences making drawings, paintings and digital illustration, his current artistic practice occupies a space that is concurrently post-digital, post-street and post-apartheid. Reflecting an interest in the relationships between different sectors of South African society, the history of indigenous communities and the relationship between fashion and ritual. Mathebula’s practice investigates the people and the textures that seem to define the urban reality of Johannesburg. In this new body of work, sculptural forms take centre stage, with each character referencing a different narrative, unique in our diverse social landscape. \\n \\nSelected Solo Exhibitions \\n2020 Shadows of My Freedom – Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg, SA \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions & Projects \\n2016 FIERCE.NOW – Afrovibes Festival, Amsterdam, NLD \\n2014 Drawing the Line – Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg, SA \\n2014 RIOT – Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg, SA \\n2013 The Path Less Deconstructed – .M Contemporary, AUS \\n2013 Illustrators Show – Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg, SA \\n \\nArt Fairs \\nInvestec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, SA (2020) \\nBasha Uhuru Festival, Constitutional Hill, Johannesburg, SA (2013 – 2019) \\nDesign Indaba Expo 2013: Emerging Creatives, Cape Town, SA (2013)"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015983837","gid://shopify/Product/9014088401117","gid://shopify/Product/9014122971357","gid://shopify/Product/9014123659485"]

item.title: Lea Colombo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641652965597 Lea Colombo 1760 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640737493213 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045205725","gid://shopify/Product/9452045238493","gid://shopify/Product/9452045271261"] [11680,11679,11678] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"A self-taught artist born in 1993 in Cape Town, South Africa, Lea Colombo is a creative nomad. Her commercial work as a photographer and director has cemented her place among the most influential global fashion names, whilst her profile as a fine artist rapidly gains clout. Recognised for her bold and saturated style, Colombo examines the values and connections between colour, light and emotion. Her art reflects her personality – she is unafraid to push boundaries. \\n Colombo’s practice is spontaneous and intuitive, unguarded and intimate. Her artworks reflect \\nhow she views both herself and the world. She channels her mediums to explore individuation and to connect with her surroundings. Colombo combines unconventional approaches to create balance – balance that is expressed through the masculine and feminine, shadow and light, colour and desaturated, yin and yang. As a multidisciplinary artist, Colombo works with a range of mediums such as print, photography, painting, and sculpture. Her highly recognizable dark room prints express fluidity and intimacy that engage the viewer on a deeply personal plane. Her \\nexploration of colour through diverse mediums reveals the multiplicity of our connections to a higher consciousness. According to Numéro Art’s editor in chief, Thibaut Wychowanok, “the work of Lea Colombo has become more complex and denser but has always preserved its heart: the colour, omnipresent, frontal and explosive, like a boxer punching the viewer's eye to reach their whole body.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045205725","gid://shopify/Product/9452045238493","gid://shopify/Product/9452045271261"]

item.title: Leanie Barnard
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641652375773 Leanie Barnard 1766 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640738705629 [11753,13644] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Leanie Barnard Mentz, was born in Pretoria and graduated from the Open Window Art Academy in 2004. She studied visual communication and is a multi-disciplinary artist. She is the owner of a floral design company that specializes in corporate events and weddings, creating large scale installations with her flowers. \\n \\nExploring boundaries and traces, she creates large scale paintings and drawings with layers of thick paint and charcoal. She is interested in how multiple realities exist together and how everything is in constant flux. Her works are neither documentation nor fiction. They depict human life, and more importantly the human condition. Ambiguity and multiplicity of possible meanings are a driving force in her work. \\n \\nMany of her pieces explore the human form, body language, imperfections, and movement, and are often characterized by spontaneous and gestural brushstrokes. She often leaves imperfections, “search marks” or “traces” in her works. The layering creates movement and emotion. Traces of a former self will always remain. This also plays on the idea that we are confronted by a perfect world on social media every day, so we have to choose carefully what to reveal or conceal to the outside world. \\n \\nShe is drawn to the raw expressive qualities of charcoal and oil paint as her chosen media."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013362983133","gid://shopify/Product/9013389295837"]

item.title: Leah Rachel Hawker
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641652343005 Leah Rachel Hawker 2568 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640738672861 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013980397789", "gid://shopify/Product/9013980430557", "gid://shopify/Product/9013980627165", "gid://shopify/Product/9013981348061"] [21127,21125,21030,21131,21126,21132] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Leah Rachel Hawker (b.1983) is a South African artist. She completed a post-graduate diploma (with distinction) in fine art at the University of Cape Town in 2023 which took an intimate look at the lives and subsequent identities of GenZ women. She completed her initial studies at Ruth Prowse School of Art (with distinction) in 2005 with a body of work that dealt with female stereotyping. Her passion for image making evolved from a fascination with gender roles in society and our shared human condition. \\nBy working with thousands of individuals in all contexts and environments over the last 20 years she has gained immense knowledge and understanding of human behavior. It is in both the public and private domain that she has made these observations, those of our fears and vanities: this is what she brings to her work. She published her documentary art book Breastfeeding 101 (ISBN: 978-1-928440-29-1) in 2019. Leah has placed three times, as a finalist, in both the Sasol New Signatures Competition (2009, 2018, current - 2024) and Vuleka Awards (2006, 2022). She was a finalist in the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts, 2021. More recently she has exhibited at the Voortrekker Monument in Pretoria, the University of Johannesburg and the KKNK \\nLeah has initiated and worked on a number of curatorial projects, lectured at City Varsity, Western Cape Government seminars and Ruth Prowse Art School. She’s created photo essays for women’s upliftment projects and organizations in South Africa, Tanzania and Sri Lanka to date. She is currently working towards her first solo as well as on a yearlong documentary photo story funded by the National Arts Council on the Madeiran community of Woodstock for exhibition in 2025."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013978562781","gid://shopify/Product/9013980397789","gid://shopify/Product/9013980430557","gid://shopify/Product/9013980627165","gid://shopify/Product/9013981348061","gid://shopify/Product/9013985345757","gid://shopify/Product/9013985411293","gid://shopify/Product/9013985542365","gid://shopify/Product/9013985673437","gid://shopify/Product/9013985738973"]

item.title: Lebo Kekana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641653194973 Lebo Kekana 2213 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640738803933 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452056936669","gid://shopify/Product/9452056969437","gid://shopify/Product/9013459321053","gid://shopify/Product/9013465120989"] [17413,17082,16268,16267] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lebo Kekana (b. 2000, South Africa) is the founder, director and curator of FEDE Arthouse. Practicing as a self-taught artist himself, Kekana makes figurative paintings depicting love and estrangement set along the Cape’s shoreline. \\nWith the intention to create the spaces he seeks to see his work exist in, Lebo started FEDE because of an age-old frustration. “I really wanted to get into the art scene in Cape Town, but I wasn’t very familiar with the channels or which doors to knock on,” he said in an interview in 2021 ,one year after Fede's inception. Rather than nurture resentment at the art world’s strange codes and habits, FEDE sets out to create alternative exhibition experiences which dismiss the commercial and clinical approach to exhibition-making for more of a curious and community-based one."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452056936669","gid://shopify/Product/9452056969437","gid://shopify/Product/9013459321053","gid://shopify/Product/9013465120989"]

item.title: Lebo Thoka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641653358813 Lebo Thoka 585 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640738836701 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013358133469","gid://shopify/Product/9013359411421"] [11429,11382] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lebo Thoka (b.1996) is a photographer and artist who was born and raised in Johannesburg, South Africa. She attended primary and high schools in Midrand and later studied at the Open Window Institute and graduated with a BA in Visual Communication cum laude, majoring in photography. During her final year of study, in which she was mostly studying commercial photography, she stumbled across fine art photography and created her first art series. \\n \\nShe has since had a solo exhibition and hosted a talk with David Krut Gallery. In 2018 she won a Loerie Award. She has been a part of the Addis Foto Fest based in Ethiopia, and has had her work featured in the Washington Post and The New York times online platforms. Her work is mainly influenced by being a Feminist and covers topics such as femicide in South Africa, navigating South Africa as a black woman, as well as the black female existence in proximity to topics such as religion, history vs present day etc."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013358133469","gid://shopify/Product/9013359411421"]

item.title: Lebohang Motaung
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641653162205 Lebohang Motaung 698 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640738935005 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052258013", "gid://shopify/Product/9014052290781", "gid://shopify/Product/9014052356317", "gid://shopify/Product/9014058680541"] Discover the art of Lebohang Motaung, a South African artist who explores the politics of Black hair through her unique use of synthetic hair. Drawing from personal experiences, Motaung’s work celebrates women’s identity and promotes confidence, beauty, and the freedom to express individuality in the face of societal judgment. [2494,2495,23792,2491,23614,2496,2492,2493,23615,2489,24544,2497,24543,2488] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lebogang Motaung, a talented fine artist from Sebokeng in the Vaal, holds a BTech in Fine Arts with a major in printmaking from the Vaal University of Technology. She has established herself as a prominent figure in the art world. In 2015, she earned a certificate of excellence in printmaking from Artist Proof Studios, which accelerated her art career and opened door to both local and international opportunities. \\nThat same year, Motaung participated in a four-month residency at The School of Museum of Fine Arts in Boston, USA, where she learned advanced intaglio techniques and contributed as an assistant teacher to the program. \\nIn 2018, she spent eight months at The Project Space, where she had the privilege of being mentored by the legendary Benon Lutaaya. These experiences, along with exposure to established artist mentorship, have greatly shaped her unique artistic style. \\nMotaung’s art explores the politics of hair, specifically focusing on the identity preservation of women. She uses synthetic hair as her medium to champion women’s right to wear their hair as they choose, free from judgment. As a Black woman, Motaung draws from her own experiences with hair, navigating the pressures and traditions that shape perceptions of Black hair. Despite tackling these societal challenges, her work exudes youthful playfulness, beauty, and the confidence of her subjects."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052258013","gid://shopify/Product/9014052290781","gid://shopify/Product/9014052356317","gid://shopify/Product/9014058680541","gid://shopify/Product/9014094397661","gid://shopify/Product/9014094430429"]

item.title: Lee-Ann Olwage
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641654046941 Lee-Ann Olwage gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640742179037 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013978988765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013979021533", "gid://shopify/Product/9013979054301"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lee-Ann Olwage is a visual storyteller from South Africa who uses collaborative storytelling to explore themes relating to gender and identity. She is interested in using the medium of photography as a mode of celebration and aims to create a space where people she collaborates with can play an active part in the creation of images, they feel tells their stories in a way that is affirming and celebratory. \\nHer journey in photography began unexpectedly after studying film directing and scriptwriting. Following her education, she spent nine years working as a set decorator in the film industry, an experience that profoundly shaped her approach to narrative and visual composition. Through this background, Olwage developed a keen eye for capturing not just imagery but also narratives. She is particularly interested in reflecting on the way in which different cultures and communities interpret mental health and stories about education. Through her art, Olwage fosters a sense of community and creates vivid narratives filled with possibility. \\nThe Right To Play creates a powerful narrative that sheds light on the challenges faced by millions of girls globally in their pursuit of an education. Every day, girls face barriers to education caused by poverty, cultural norms and practices, poor infrastructure and violence. The project poses the question - What do girls dream of? And what happens when a supportive environment is created where girls are empowered and given the opportunity to learn and dream? What does that world look like? \\nThe result is a poignant exploration of the dreams and aspirations of young girls, challenging societal expectations that limit their potential. By creating a playful world where girls are not confined by poverty, cultural norms, or violence and instead, is shown through a lens that paints a vivid picture of the possibilities that arise when girls are given the opportunity to learn and dream freely. The Right To Play merges storytelling with an imagined playful world where girls are the shown in an empowered and affirming way blooming as the heroines of their own stories and overcoming the many barriers to getting an education. \\nHer work has been featured in National Geographic, Vogue, The British Journal of Photography, Foam magazine, Geo, The Guardian, Atmos, Vanity Fair Italy, Dazed, Wired, Musee Magazine and IMA Magazine. Notable awards include a World Press Photo Award, 2020, 2023 & 2024, Sony World Photography Awards, 2023, International Women in Photo Award Laurette 2023, Winner of This Is Gender, 2021, Pride Photo Award, 2021, CAP Prize winner, 2022, Marilyn Stafford Fotoreportage Award shortlist, 2021+2022, International Photography Awards Honourable Mention, 2020 and selected for The New York Times Portfolio Review 2022."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013978628317","gid://shopify/Product/9013978661085","gid://shopify/Product/9013978693853","gid://shopify/Product/9013978726621","gid://shopify/Product/9013978759389","gid://shopify/Product/9013978792157","gid://shopify/Product/9013978824925","gid://shopify/Product/9013978857693","gid://shopify/Product/9013978923229","gid://shopify/Product/9013978988765","gid://shopify/Product/9013979021533","gid://shopify/Product/9013979054301","gid://shopify/Product/9013841297629","gid://shopify/Product/9013994225885","gid://shopify/Product/9013994258653","gid://shopify/Product/9013994291421","gid://shopify/Product/9013994324189","gid://shopify/Product/9013994389725","gid://shopify/Product/9013994422493","gid://shopify/Product/9013994455261","gid://shopify/Product/9013994488029","gid://shopify/Product/9013994553565","gid://shopify/Product/9013293023453","gid://shopify/Product/9013994651869","gid://shopify/Product/9013994684637","gid://shopify/Product/9013994750173","gid://shopify/Product/9013994782941"]

item.title: LegakwanaLeo Makgekgenene
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641654407389 LegakwanaLeo Makgekgenene gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640742244573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169822429","gid://shopify/Product/9452169887965"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"LegakwanaLeo Makgekgenene b. 1995 Gaborone, Botswana holds a BAFA (Hon.)(New Media) from the University of Cape Town. LegakwanaLeo’s work is a determined effort to bypass cultural censorship and to counteract the restrictions of toxic traditionalism, producing an elusive critique of state machinery and sociological constructions. Makgekgenene is currently studying towards their Master of Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Fine Art; tracking the evolutions of Botswana’s women’s movements while exploring specifically for black women-alternative points of access to critical and radical pedagogies. Makgekgenene is a co-founder of The Botswana Pavilion and was selected for the Thapong Arts Centre and British Council’s collaborative initiative Echoes of (Un)silenced Voices (2019). \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169822429","gid://shopify/Product/9452169887965"]

item.title: Lehlogonolo Mashaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641654472925 Lehlogonolo Mashaba 459 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640742473949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013935407325","gid://shopify/Product/9013935440093"] [19516,19517] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lehlogonolo Mashaba (b.1983 Kwa-Thema, Johannesburg) is a South African artist with an extensive background in printmaking. After obtaining a certificate in design and printmaking in 2004 from the Artist Proof Studio, South Africa, he went on to work collaboratively there. Specialising in intaglio, relief, monotype and silkscreen he has assisted in printmaking for top established artists in South Africa. \\n \\nMashaba won the Standard Bank Grahamstown Festival's Picasso in Africa mural competition in 2006. Other public artwork includes a painting completed for Pick n Pay at Maponya Mall which was later enlarged and placed on a billboard in Soweto. \\n \\nLehlogonolo Mashaba’s work is centered on text. One of the running motifs in Mashaba’s work is his continuous use of cell phone texts. He uses texts from people’s text (sms) messages. \\n \\n\"I have always felt learning has been laboursome and slow process to grasp on hence I use text to construct/deconstruct my figures(myself). In that case I combine different information and words from different texts source most especially the Bible as it is to me the ultimate source of knowledge yet the most ambiguous. I swop around the body and text, having text on the body and using text to create bodiesfigures\". \\n \\nMashaba not only draws from his personal archive, he also draws influence from the media by extracting texts from newspaper articles. \\n \\n\"My artwork plays on the tools of communication merging imagery and text. The interest in theology, technology, books/reading, and Biology set a base for my art making process. We as human beings are a product of what we eat (food/words)\" \\n \\n \\n \\nSelected exhibitions, awards and residencies \\n \\n2017 \\nSummer Exhibition, Group show at Everard Read, London, UK \\n \\n2014 \\nMarking the Map at Lizamore & Associates Gallery, Johannesburg \\nNo Man’s Art Pop-up Gallery, Cape Town. \\nNr.10 of Top 25 South African Artists You Should Know Now, House & Leisure \\n \\n2013 \\nNoise at Lizamore & Associates Gallery, Johannesburg. \\nSouth African Voices: A New Generation Of Printmakers at Washington Printmakers Gallery, Washington D.C. USA. \\nWorks on Paper at Gallery MoMo, Johannesburg. \\n \\n2010 \\nResidency at the Rendezvous Art Project, Elisabeth Pons Studio, Paris (France) \\n \\n2009 \\nTop 76 Artists for the Thami Myele Fine Art Award. \\n \\n2008 \\nResidency at Experimental Printmaking Institute, Lafayette College, Easton, PA (USA) \\nArtist Image Resource, Pittsburg, PA (USA) \\n \\n2006 \\nGrahamstown festival, Picasso in Africa Mural Competition (First Prize) \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013935407325","gid://shopify/Product/9013935440093"]

item.title: LEILA ABRAHAMS
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641654538461 LEILA ABRAHAMS gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640729661661 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013442085085"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"LEILA ABRAHAMS (b. 1999) is an interdisciplinary artist from Cape Town, South Africa. Her practice weaves together aspects of her personal histories drawing from her experiences with grief, mental health and chronic illness. Her decade-long journey with the condition of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus is foundational to her artistic inquiries. Using materials ubiquitous within the medical practice; gel capsules and blister packs, Abrahams gestures at a new vocabulary to approach difficult conversations around invisible ailments. At the heart of her deeply intimate and embodied practice, is a yearning to find ways to navigate her own illness while also creating space for less stigma and more compassion. Through an abstract and minimalist language emphasised by the careful placement of materials, Abrahams creates beauty, harmony and order —which in turn become subtle acts of resistance. She reflects; “My work speaks to the overwhelming nature of chronic medication and the waves of emotion that accompany the experience. I came to accept my medication as something I take daily but that no longer has power over me.” \\n \\nAbrahams obtained a BA(FA) from the Michaelis School of Fine Art (University of Cape Town) in 2021. In 2022, she participated in the group exhibition; Within the Fold at Smac Gallery in Johannesburg. Abrahams is the inaugural artist in residence with The Ramp Residency in Cape Town (2022)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013442085085"]

item.title: Leon Chauke
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641657258205 Leon Chauke 1313 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640742867165 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154814685"] [12508,12509] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Leon Chauke is a self-taught photographer and collage artist that lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. He started his career in advertising as a graphic designer in 2017. In his personal work, he focuses on telling authentic South African stories that are relatable and familiar. His work strives to inspire South Africa and Africa to tell their own stories. \\nHis childhood and upbringing have had a huge influence on his work, he describes growing up in Tembisa as magical and gave him a sense of richness and beauty of the small daily victories and challenges that made his community. \\nEverybody has a story to tell that is worth capturing and this has shaped my work. Interacting with people through his work gave him a new language to express his emotions - pain, joy, sadness, forgiveness - without having to necessarily articulate those emotions in words. \\nHe is drawn to unearthing the soulfulness in the stories and the opportunity he gets to tell them. He creates work that has a nostalgic feeling, a relatable feeling, a sense of newness and familiarity, striving to create work that allows the viewer to relive moments they have shared with friends, loved ones, and their community."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154814685"]

item.title: Lerato Lodi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641657946333 Lerato Lodi 1296 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640743456989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013399879901","gid://shopify/Product/9013399945437","gid://shopify/Product/9013400010973","gid://shopify/Product/9452095307997","gid://shopify/Product/9452163170525"] [14105,14102,21071,14104,14103,9145] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"B. 1996, - Pretoria, South Africa \\n \\nLerato Lodi was born in 1996, in Ga-Rankuwa, Pretoria, South Africa. Lodi is currently study- ing towards an M-Tech Fine Arts Degree at the Tshwane University of Technology in her hometown. \\nLodi’s artistic practice explores themes centred around her spirituality. She uses acrylic paint on canvas as well as beads and cloth to interrogate ideas and ideals of African spirituality and Christianity as it manifests in her own life and the lives of those she encounters. Lodi exam- ines the different ways in which people worship and pray as she explores shrines, temples and materials brought into those sites as offerings. \\n \\nLodi has participated in the following group exhibitions: Initiative: Blessing Ngobeni Studio Art Award at Room Gallery; Genesis X’Ibition at Pretoria Art Museum (2018); Emergence: A group exhibition at mm-Arthouse Gallery; Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize Group Exhibition at Aspire Art Auctions; The Aesthetics of time: in space of time at Polokwane Art Museum and Genesis Group Exhibition at Bkhz Gallery (2019) to name a few. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013399879901","gid://shopify/Product/9013399945437","gid://shopify/Product/9013400010973","gid://shopify/Product/9452095307997","gid://shopify/Product/9452163170525"]

item.title: Lerato Motaung
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641658241245 Lerato Motaung 2730 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640744243421 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014042329309","gid://shopify/Product/9014042394845","gid://shopify/Product/9014042427613","gid://shopify/Product/9014042460381"] Explore the art of Lerato Motaung, a Johannesburg-based visual artist whose work delves into memory, selfhood, and collective narratives. His expressive color palettes and layered compositions reflect the emotional weight of memory and the complexities of human experience. Discover his global exhibitions and accolades. [23355,23352,23353,23354] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lerato Motaung (b. 1991, South Africa) is a Johannesburg-based visual artist whose multidisciplinary practice delves into the interplay between memory, selfhood, and collective narratives. He examines how personal and cultural histories shape the human experience, employing various mediums to capture the tension between memory's fragility and persistence. \\nThrough expressive colour palettes and layered compositions, Motaung creates a visual language that reflects the emotional weight of memory and the complexities of experience, from joy and sorrow to transformation and resilience. He holds a National Diploma in Fine Art from Tshwane University of Technology, Pretoria. His impact extends beyond the canvas, with global participations and exhibitions. In 2021, he was a finalist in the Sasol New Signature Awards at the Pretoria Art Museum. His international exposure includes the \"Our Africa, Our Future\" residency in Senegal (2022) hosted by the African Union. Motaung's group exhibitions include prestigious venues such as the Pretoria Art Museum, Haart Gallery in London, THK Gallery in Cologne, and Boschendal in Cape Town. He won The Emergence Art Prize in 2020 and completed a two-month residency in Cologne, Germany, in 2022. \\nMotaung's artwork is featured in collections worldwide, including Foundation H in Paris and Madagascar, and a planned museum in Cardiff, Wales. His artistic journey is marked by a commitment to exploring cultural identity, leaving a significant mark on the global art scene."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014042329309","gid://shopify/Product/9014042394845","gid://shopify/Product/9014042427613","gid://shopify/Product/9014042460381"]

item.title: Lerato Ntili
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641658667229 Lerato Ntili 2912 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640744440029 [] Lerato Ntili (b.?2001, Bloemfontein) is a Johannesburg-based fine arts photographer whose black?and?white self?portraiture interrogates cultural narratives around body image, identity, and belonging within a South African context. [24808,25502,25500,25503,24807,24806,25501] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lerato Ntili (b. 2001) is a South African artist born and raised in Bloemfontein, Free State currently based in Johannesburg. She completed her BA (Honours) in Fine Arts at the University of Pretoria in 2023. \\nNtili’s artistic journey began with an intimate exploration of her own body and its relationship to beauty standards through self-portraiture. A departure from this personal focus, has driven a desire to understand the deeper origins of her lifelong struggle with body image. Starting with the seemingly harmless childhood nickname 'motsetserepa' – a Sesotho word for skinny – which stood in stark contrast to her internal perception, Ntili investigates the powerful role of cultural discourse in shaping body image within the South African context, aiming to articulate the pervasive influence of familial and societal observations on body and figure, revealing the intricate ways in which these cultural dynamics contribute to the formation of body image. \\nThe early experience of being labeled, regardless of the intention, can contribute to a lifelong preoccupation with body size and shape. Exploring the visual and textual representations of body image within culture, analyzing their aesthetic qualities and their impact on individual experience. Exploring the cultural values and beliefs that underpin this open commentary on bodies. Bringing forward questions, are there specific gendered aspects to this? How does it intersect with notions of health, beauty and social status within different South African communities? \\nNtili's artistic practice delves into the complex and often challenging formation of body image within cultural contexts. Her work examines the pervasive influence of societal and familial commentary on the body, exploring how these dynamics shape individual self-perception from a young age. A formative experience of being given a childhood nickname related to her physique – a label that contrasted with her internal sense of self – serves as a crucial point of departure for this inquiry. Ntili's practice articulates the enduring impact of constant observations on physique, regardless of whether one is perceived as thin or large, revealing the complex ways in which cultural discourse molds one's sense of self. \\nThrough her artistic lens, she investigates the aesthetics and phenomenology of these cultural environments, analyzing the language, visual cues and implicit judgments that constitute the ongoing dialogue about bodies. Ultimately, Ntili's work illuminates the cultural roots of body image concerns, offering a broader commentary on the shared experiences of navigating body perception within diverse societal frameworks."}]}]} []

item.title: Lerato Nkosi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641658339549 Lerato Nkosi 1464 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640744374493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013354463453","gid://shopify/Product/9013354561757","gid://shopify/Product/9013354594525","gid://shopify/Product/9013354627293","gid://shopify/Product/9013354692829","gid://shopify/Product/9013371175133","gid://shopify/Product/9013371240669","gid://shopify/Product/9013372715229","gid://shopify/Product/9013408170205","gid://shopify/Product/9013408235741","gid://shopify/Product/9013408301277","gid://shopify/Product/9013408334045","gid://shopify/Product/9013408399581","gid://shopify/Product/9013408465117","gid://shopify/Product/9013408497885","gid://shopify/Product/9013408530653","gid://shopify/Product/9013408596189","gid://shopify/Product/9013408628957","gid://shopify/Product/9013408694493","gid://shopify/Product/9013408727261","gid://shopify/Product/9013408792797","gid://shopify/Product/9013408858333","gid://shopify/Product/9013408923869","gid://shopify/Product/9013408989405","gid://shopify/Product/9013409054941","gid://shopify/Product/9013409186013","gid://shopify/Product/9013409251549","gid://shopify/Product/9013409284317","gid://shopify/Product/9013409317085","gid://shopify/Product/9013409349853","gid://shopify/Product/9013409415389","gid://shopify/Product/9013409480925","gid://shopify/Product/9013409513693","gid://shopify/Product/9013409546461","gid://shopify/Product/9013409611997","gid://shopify/Product/9013409677533","gid://shopify/Product/9013409710301","gid://shopify/Product/9013409808605"] [12707,14707,14708,14709,10946,14710,14711,14712,14713,12435,14714,14715,14716,14717,14719,10950,10949,14720,14722,14721,14723,14724,14725,10948,14726,12436,14727,14728,14729,14730,14731,10947,14701,14702,14703,14704,14705,14706] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lerato Nkosi ( b. 1993, Mpumalanga, South Africa; lives and works in Johannesburg ). \\nDrawing from her experiences as a young girl growing up in a sheltered world that was created for her by her predecessors, she has developed a dynamic practice that examines the intricacies of existing in the world as a woman with the awareness that the teachings are impacting and affecting her existence. \\nHer work employs ink and stamps as a vital, organic, multifaceted material. For Nkosi ink and stamps are mediums that stain and certify with their contact on any surface, these materials arethose that never leave a surface the same after being in contact with it. The stamp and ink is always used to verify and ordain documents of importance which grants the holder automatic approval to the decision of others, this process is always handled by an individual of authority. \\nThe teachings of parents onto the girl child is embedded in and never leaves her the same as she previously was, with the ideas that whatsoever has been stamped and inked upon her is approved. The medium tempers heavier subjects that are faced in societies regarding the expectations of a woman. Investigating the medium allows Nkosi to overcome her daily conundrums and escape the victim mentality \\nLerato Nkosi is the winner of the inaugural ANNA Award. The aim of the award is to discover, recognise and nurture a new generation of women-identifying artists from the African continent and the diaspora."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013354463453","gid://shopify/Product/9013354561757","gid://shopify/Product/9013354594525","gid://shopify/Product/9013354627293","gid://shopify/Product/9013354692829","gid://shopify/Product/9013371175133","gid://shopify/Product/9013371240669","gid://shopify/Product/9013372715229","gid://shopify/Product/9013408170205","gid://shopify/Product/9013408235741","gid://shopify/Product/9013408301277","gid://shopify/Product/9013408334045","gid://shopify/Product/9013408399581","gid://shopify/Product/9013408465117","gid://shopify/Product/9013408497885","gid://shopify/Product/9013408530653","gid://shopify/Product/9013408596189","gid://shopify/Product/9013408628957","gid://shopify/Product/9013408694493","gid://shopify/Product/9013408727261","gid://shopify/Product/9013408792797","gid://shopify/Product/9013408858333","gid://shopify/Product/9013408923869","gid://shopify/Product/9013408989405","gid://shopify/Product/9013409054941","gid://shopify/Product/9013409186013","gid://shopify/Product/9013409251549","gid://shopify/Product/9013409284317","gid://shopify/Product/9013409317085","gid://shopify/Product/9013409349853","gid://shopify/Product/9013409415389","gid://shopify/Product/9013409480925","gid://shopify/Product/9013409513693","gid://shopify/Product/9013409546461","gid://shopify/Product/9013409611997","gid://shopify/Product/9013409677533","gid://shopify/Product/9013409710301","gid://shopify/Product/9013409808605"]

[24631] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lesedi Modupi, 22, hails from Johannesburg. As a child he spent hours sketching portraits of those close to him. In high school he began to consider art as a career when he received his first payment for drawing a portrait of his teacher’s daughter. Fuelled by determination Modupi embarked on a self-taught path, honing his skills through hours of practice and experimentation in his home studio. \\nDrawing inspiration from his surroundings and the beauty of Black children, his art is a fusion of traditional techniques and modern aesthetics. While proficient in various artistic mediums, his preferred medium is the ballpen, which he uses to create compositions on Fabriano paper. item.title: Lesedi Ramushu

His bold and colorful artworks celebrate African culture and heritage. Purchase original art online and experience the beauty and diversity of Africa through his unique prints. [25421,25422,25651,25650] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lesedi Ramushu (b. 1994) is a self-taught artist from Mpumalanga, specializing in the intricate art of linocut printmaking. Inspired by the rich culture and heritage of his homeland, Lesedi's work celebrates the beauty and diversity of Africa. Through his bold prints, he aims to share the unique stories and experiences of his people with the world, while also inspiring others to explore and appreciate the many different cultures that make up our planet. \\nLinocut printmaking is a labor-intensive process that involves carving designs into blocks of linoleum, inking them up, and then printing them onto paper or fabric. This process requires immense patience, skill, and attention to detail. However, the results are undeniably worth it, as each print carries a piece of the artist’s soul. \\nLesedi's work is characterized by bold colors and patterns, which reflect the vibrant energy of Africa. He draws inspiration from traditional motifs and symbols, as well as scenes from everyday life, infusing his work with authenticity and cultural richness. His prints have garnered international recognition, being exhibited and collected around the world in both private and public collections. \\nIn addition to his artistic practice, Lesedi is also an educator, working with students of all ages to help them discover their own creative potential. His ability to capture the essence of African culture and translate it into visually stunning prints sets him apart as a truly remarkable artist. Whether you are a seasoned art collector or just beginning your journey into the world of art, exploring Lesedi Ramushu’s prints is an experience not to be missed. His unique perspective and dedication to celebrating African culture make his work both captivating and enlightening."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452174868701","gid://shopify/Product/9452192301277","gid://shopify/Product/9452214386909","gid://shopify/Product/9452214485213","gid://shopify/Product/9452214550749","gid://shopify/Product/9452275368157","gid://shopify/Product/9452275433693","gid://shopify/Product/9452275499229","gid://shopify/Product/9452275564765","gid://shopify/Product/9452275630301","gid://shopify/Product/9452275695837","gid://shopify/Product/9452275761373","gid://shopify/Product/9452275826909","gid://shopify/Product/9452275957981","gid://shopify/Product/9452276056285","gid://shopify/Product/9452276187357","gid://shopify/Product/9452276285661"]

item.title: Lesego Seoketsa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641672986845 Lesego Seoketsa 1921 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640748634333 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046614749","gid://shopify/Product/9452046680285","gid://shopify/Product/9452046713053"] [13572,13571,13569] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lesego Seoketsa is an artist who lives and works in Springs, South Africa. She has a Bachelor of Arts in Fashion from Stadio (formerly known as Lisof). Her practice consists of photography, painting, and garment construction. Through her artistic work and practice, she engages her own critical thinking on postmodernist theory, and what living in a postmodernist world really means for equality and liberation among Africans, particularly black women. She considers feminism, black liberation and identity, as she makes work that directly addresses those themes, both from a theoretical perspective and a deeply personal one too. Raised in the post-apartheid era, she is influenced by Western traditional artists. But importantly, through her art, she is able to use these artists as reference points to distinguish the visual language of her own art as an African. \\n \\n \\nLesego's work and persona have been featured in publications such as Visi, Vogue, Sunday Times, House & Garden, Glamour Magazine and many more. In January 2021 she was a guest on the Expresso Show on national television where she discussed the details of her debut solo exhibition through the Orms Circle Mentorship Programme 2020 - titled 'Uthethathethwano' - to which she was the recipient of mentorship and a grant to produce the show. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046614749","gid://shopify/Product/9452046680285","gid://shopify/Product/9452046713053"]

item.title: Letso Leipego
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641676099805 Letso Leipego 2312 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640749158621 [] Explore the photography of Letso Leipego, a Botswana-based artist who captures rural life through a unique manipulation of light and shadow. His work highlights the overlooked stories of people living beyond urban society [17782,17783,17784,17785] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Letso Leipego (b. 1991, Gaborone, Botswana) is a photographer whose work explores rural life in Botswana, driven by a deep-seated curiosity inherited from his grandfather, who frequently features in his photographs. Fascinated by light, Letso's work emphasizes contrast and the stylized manipulation of light and shadow, bringing attention to overlooked details. \\nHis subjects, usually captured in rural settings, reflects his interest in the lives of people beyond mainstream urban society, whose stories and histories often remain in the shadows. \\nOver several years, Letso has photographed his subjects in their environments, both at home and at work. His background in fashion and commercial photography is evident in his images, which are layered with hidden qualities and references. Letso's work is central to the notion of revelation, using tricks of light and innovative composition strategies to bring a revelatory tone to ethnographic photography."}]}]} []

item.title: Levy Pooe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641676198109 Levy Pooe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640749224157 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452101304541","gid://shopify/Product/9452101337309","gid://shopify/Product/9452101402845","gid://shopify/Product/9452101435613","gid://shopify/Product/9452101468381","gid://shopify/Product/9452256100573"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Levy Pooe (b. 1994) is a Johannesburg-based South African visual artist born during the country's transition to democracy. He is the recipient of the 2020 Cassirer Welz award in partnership with Strauss & Co Auctioneers, which culminated in a solo exhibition at the Bag Factory Artist Studios. Pooe works with and explores different mediums of expression ranging from painting, drawing, murals and printmaking. He is invested in telling stories and creating narratives, describing his work as a public social diary. Through figurative paintings, Pooe aims to make visible intimate and public scenes, conversations, daily rituals and routines in everyday South Africa. He recently joined the global JP Morgan Chase Art Collection, a collection by contemporary black South African artists."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452101304541","gid://shopify/Product/9452101337309","gid://shopify/Product/9452101402845","gid://shopify/Product/9452101435613","gid://shopify/Product/9452101468381","gid://shopify/Product/9452256100573"]

item.title: Liam Van Der Heever
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641679245533 Liam Van Der Heever gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640749650141 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Liam Van Der Heever (b. 2000) is a Cape Town based artist, whose explorative nature with consistency in stylistic preference, allows for an open-to-interpretation approach in regard to the symbolisms he incorporates within his work. \\n \\nVan Der Heever enjoys the idea that his artworks actually ‘see’ those who interact with them, creating an essence of acknowledgment for shared experience and an empathetic exchange. He creates these paintings to cultivate a relatability towards individual struggles and experiences we endure, whilst searching for a conducive understanding of who we are. This exploration showcases the journey of individuality and connectivity we maintain, through various human experiences portrayed in each artwork. This evidently holds a conversation connected to the search to be whole in both the body and self, with particular regard to the various interactions that affect our individual balance in the search for authenticity. The underlying focus is directed toward how individuals interact with idealistic social constructs produced via societal beliefs; often seen through reoccurrences in the paintings, such as the bird, use of tears and inherent iconography. The use of eye contact and lack thereof also play an important role in exclaiming the internal feelings of each character to the viewer. This eye contact is used in a direct manner to provide the understanding of ‘self’ within each piece, cultivating a wider connective interaction. On the scale of stylistic repetition, these characters remain within their own scenarios. They all have a unique perception, which is relayed between the viewer and the characters. With these artworks there is a duality in focus, where it either enlightens the authentic self and allows one to be whole in their being or prevents individuals from being whole, as it restricts an individual’s acceptance of self. \\n \\nVan Der Heever has created a visual space for reflection to be embraced, an interaction that feels your experience, shares its own and allows for inherent understandings to be felt by those who are never truly seen."}]}]} []

item.title: Linathi Makanda
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641683734749 Linathi Makanda 1368 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640754860253 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013328314589", "gid://shopify/Product/9013328380125", "gid://shopify/Product/9013328543965"] [8365,9787,9786,8350,8351] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Linathi Makanda is a multidisciplinary artist based in South Africa. \\nAs an emerging artist born in the small town of Mthatha, Eastern Cape, a large part of Linathi’s creative story explores the intersections of impossibility, passion, and the making of everything possible out of nothing. Venturing out into art has been a calling she has followed blindly and she remains committed to the way she sees the world and her desire to share this perspective through her art. \\nAt the heart of Makanda's photography are stories the world has heard, but not enough about. Her specialties include Portraiture, Still Life, and Fine Art photography. Makanda's work also embodies a strong sense of vulnerability, and through each story she tells, she strives to find ways to make others feel and reflect. \\nMakanda is a member of the global Black Women Photographers community started by Polly Irungu, and her photographic works have been internationally recognized by publications such as Vogue Italia, Color Bloc Magazine as well as Michigan’s Saginaw Valley State University art journal, Cardinal Sins. Additionally, her visual, Seasons, which blends elements of art direction, poetry, and videography has been featured in New Plains Review, a platform by the College of Liberal Arts at the University Of Central Oklahoma. This body of work was also selected to screen at the Lift-Off Online Film Festival in the UK, under Short Films. Linathi Makanda's work was recently included in the Photo for Non-Majors (Part 2) online group exhibition, curated by Roula Seikaly and Jon Feinstein for the Humble Arts Foundation. \\nShe is also the author of the poetry collection When No One Is Watching, published by the Australian publishing house, Odyssey Books."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013328314589","gid://shopify/Product/9013328380125","gid://shopify/Product/9013328543965","gid://shopify/Product/9013344698589","gid://shopify/Product/9013344731357"]

item.title: Lindeka Qampi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641685864669 Lindeka Qampi 2195 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640756990173 [] [16039,16037,16042] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Award-winning photographer and visual activist Lindeka Qampi (b.1969) began taking photographs in 2006, when she met members of the Iliso Labantu a community-based photo collective. Her gift for capturing the lives of women and communities has ensured that Qampi's works reside in museums and private collections worldwide. She began her career as a street photographer photographing weddings, events, and portraits but moved on to exploring her community in different ways including a project on street culture shown here. A recent film, Life Framed, has been made about Lindeka Qampi's extraordinary talent, her life, and her work."}]}]} []

item.title: Lindo Zwane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641690124509 Lindo Zwane 465 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640757907677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013935505629", "gid://shopify/Product/9014037807325", "gid://shopify/Product/9014037840093"] [23143,19690,19520,23140,23142,23141] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lindokuhle Zwane was born in 1992 in Newcastle, South Africa. He works predominantly in paintings and charcoal drawings as well as printmaking mediums. He studied printmaking at Artist Proof Studio, where he also worked as a drawing facilitator for 3 years. In 2017, Zwane won an award in one of the country prestigious art competition the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards, he took the 2nd prize (the Ekurhuleni prize). Another achievement for Zwane was winning a painting merit award in the 2019 Thami Mnyele Arts Award. Zwane’s work is focused around feelings of nostalgia and the process of catharsis. He is interested in everyday life and where it is headed, but also in how the past inextricably weaves itself into the present. The memory and influence of the past, and the reality of the present often pose deep psychological challenges that he expresses through the work. The challenges come from the difficulty of being able to accept the past and acknowledge the present, particularly the chasm that can exist between those two realities."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013935505629","gid://shopify/Product/9013937668317","gid://shopify/Product/9014037807325","gid://shopify/Product/9014037840093"]

item.title: Lindokuhle Tshabalala

He feels enlightened, invigorated, and a live when he immerses himself in the Art realm. His work unpacks layers and nuances of African history in African Art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013459648733","gid://shopify/Product/9013459681501","gid://shopify/Product/9013459714269","gid://shopify/Product/9013459812573","gid://shopify/Product/9452124831965","gid://shopify/Product/9452214943965","gid://shopify/Product/9452215075037","gid://shopify/Product/9452215173341"]

item.title: Lindokuhle Sobekwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641689993437 Lindokuhle Sobekwa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640758104285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452238962909"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lindokuhle Sobekwa is a South African photographer born in Katlehong, Johannesburg. He was introduced to photography in 2012 through his participation in the Of Soul and Joy Project – a photography project in Thokoza, a township in the southeast of Johannesburg. During this time, he studied with photographers Bieke Depoorter, Cyprien Clément-Delmas, Thabiso Sekgala, Tjorven Bruyneel and Kutlwano Moagi. \\n \\n \\n \\nSobekwa began exhibiting his work in 2013 as part of a group show in Thokoza, organised by the Rubis Mécénat foundation. His photo essay, Nyaope, was published in the Mail & Guardian (South Africa) in 2014. Nyaope was also published in Vice magazine’s annual Photo Issue and the De Standaard (Belgium) in the same year and exhibited at the Turbine Art Fair as part of their new artist feature exhibition. In 2015, Sobekwa was awarded a scholarship to study at the Market Photo Workshop where he completed his Foundation Course. Nyaope was exhibited in the ensuing group show, Free from My Happiness, organised by Rubis Mécénat for the International Photo Festival of Ghent (Belgium); the exhibition toured to additional sites in Belgium and South Africa. A publication, edited by Tjorven Bruyneel, included a selection of the works. \\n \\n \\n \\nIn 2017 Sobekwa was selected by the Magnum Foundation for Photography and Social Justice, New York, to develop the project I carry Her photo of Me. He received the Magnum Foundation Fund to continue with his long-term project, Nyaope, in 2018. Sobekwa’s work has been exhibited in South Africa, Iran, Norway and the USA, and was presented by several galleries at the 2019 edition of Paris Photo. His hand-made photobook, I carry Her photo with Me was included in African Cosmologies at the FotoFest Biennial Houston, curated by Mark Sealy. He joined Magnum Photos in 2018 and became an associate member in 2020."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452238962909"]

item.title: Lionel Davis
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641692778717 Lionel Davis 2454 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640759283933 [] [19354,19349,19355] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"A former political prisoner, Lionel Davis’ name features prominently in the history of the Community Arts Project, Vakalisa Art Associates, Thupelo Workshop and Greatmore Artists Studios. \\nDrawing, painting, and printing, and often combining these media, Davis works in visual modes that range from the realist to the abstract. His themes include everyday scenes as well as reflections on black and African identity. \\nIn 2024, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from the University of Cape Town (UCT), South Africa."}]}]} []

item.title: Lionel Mbayiwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641693925597 Lionel Mbayiwa 1144 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640759349469 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037669085","gid://shopify/Product/9452037701853"] Explore the works of Lionel Tazvitya Mbayiwa, a talented Zimbabwean artist mentored by his brother and fellow artists. Discover his exhibitions at Gallery Delta and the Zimbabwe National Gallery. [23391,23962,20860,20862,23963,23395,23392,5993,23393,23394,5994,20859] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lionel Mbayiwa, born in 1982, is an artist hailing from the Shona tribe in Zimbabwe. Growing \\nup on his family farm in the Mhondoro, Mabira, Chegutu District, Mbayiwa experienced the \\nstrong bond and close-knit community that characterised the rural area. In Shona culture, \\nthe connection between the land and the people holds deep significance, as it is not merely \\nseen as a physical space but as an integral part of their identity, history, spirituality, and way \\nof life. \\nMbayiwa's artwork explores the sacred nature of the land in Shona culture, portraying \\nit as a vessel of spiritual energy and the dwelling place of ancestral spirits. The artist depicts \\nthe profound respect that the Shona people have for the land, viewing it as the physical \\nmanifestation of the ancestral realm, with their ancestors guiding and protecting them. Within \\nMbayiwa's artistic expression, oral storytelling assumes immense importance. It serves as a \\npowerful tool in preserving history, passing down knowledge, and connecting generations \\nwithin Shona culture. For centuries, the tradition of oral storytelling has played a significant \\nrole in shaping the cultural identity of the Shona people. \\nThrough stories, myths, legends, and folktales, the Shona community maintains a collective memory of their past, allowing each generation to understand and appreciate their cultural roots. Mbayiwa's work serves as a bridge between the present and the past, facilitating an understanding and appreciation of cultural heritage. It not only preserves history but also transmits knowledge, strengthens community bonds, and celebrates creativity. By embracing and drawing upon their cultural value systems, individuals can navigate the moral ambiguity and ethical dilemmas prevalent in today's world, making informed choices aligned with their personal values and contributing to the greater good. \\nMbayiwa's artwork acts as a reminder of the profound impact cultural heritage can have on shaping identity and fostering positive change in society. Unfortunately, due to economic and political hardships in Zimbabwe, Mbayiwa and his family were compelled to relocate to Cape Town, South Africa. This experience highlights the global issue of immigration, where individuals often face the challenge of preserving their heritage and value systems in a foreign environment. \\nMbayiwa's work emphasises the importance of embracing one's culture, as it provides a guiding compass in a world where moral ambiguity prevails. By drawing upon their cultural heritage, individuals can find strength, make informed choices, and contribute to a more harmonious society. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037669085","gid://shopify/Product/9452037701853"]

item.title: Lionel Smit
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641694810333 Lionel Smit 2139 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640759415005 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013421211869","gid://shopify/Product/9013423931613","gid://shopify/Product/9013423964381","gid://shopify/Product/9013424029917"] [15265,15285,15427,15426,15425] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lionel Smit was born in 1982 in Pretoria, South Africa. Smit has had several solo exhibitions. He has been exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London, receiving the Visitors' Choice - BP Portrait Award in 2013. His work can be found in many collections, such as the Standard Chartered Bank and Laurence Graff Art Collection. A painting of Smit has been featured on the cover of Christie’s Auction Catalogue. \\nSmit is one of South Africa’s most prolific and exalted artists. His artistic diversity is pursued through various mediums, and he is best known for his contemporary portraiture. His art is defined by a deeply rooted symbiotic relationship between sculpture and painting. Today, each of Smit’s works offers us an entry point into the variety and richness beneath every face we encounter, whether applied in bronze or paint. The blending of techniques across genres displays Smit’s work in multiple media, all with visible and tangible overlap."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013421211869","gid://shopify/Product/9013423931613","gid://shopify/Product/9013423964381","gid://shopify/Product/9013424029917"]

item.title: Lionel Tazvitya Mbayiwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641697136861 Lionel Tazvitya Mbayiwa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640759513309 [] Lionel Tazvitya Mbayiwa is a dynamic Zimbabwean artist whose work explores themes of identity, culture, and social issues. Through his powerful and expressive artworks, Mbayiwa captures the complexities of African experiences, offering viewers a profound reflection on contemporary life, history, and personal narratives. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lionel Tazvitya Mbayiwa is a self-taught artist whose practice spans painting, drawing, sculpture, and photography. Born in Mhondoro, Mubaira, Zimbabwe, Mbayiwa relocated to Cape Town, South Africa, in 2009, where he has since integrated his cultural heritage and personal beliefs into his artistic expressions. Influenced by his elder brother, Hugh Hatitye Mbayiwa, an art teacher, as well as mentorship from established artists such as James Jali and Nhavira Tendai, Mbayiwa draws deeply from the narratives and fables that resonate with his life experiences. \\n \\nMbayiwa has participated in numerous group exhibitions and art fairs, including “Extensive Landscapes” at The Cape Gallery in 2020 and the artHARARE online fair in the same year. His recent projects include “Kutsvaga (Searching)” at Spin Street Gallery and the performance intervention “Beitbridge Polite Force,” showcased at the Beitbridge Border and the 2022 Cape Town Art Fair. Mbayiwa’s installation, “Kudzivirira Mheni,” was featured in the Spier Light Art festival in 2022. His solo exhibitions, “Kura Uwone/Grow Up and See” at AVA Gallery (2022) and “Takambosvika Sei Pano?” at Sisonke Gallery (2023), further reflect his evolving artistic journey. “My beliefs and cultural values shape the way I conceptualize my work. Growing up in the countryside, I was surrounded by stories and experiences that deeply inform my artistic practice. I entertain myself with memories of hide and seek, river swimming, cattle herding, and the folk tales shared by my parents. These childhood experiences are woven into my art, where I often employ animals —particularly cows, birds, and f ish — as metaphorical characters. Ultimately, my work seeks to bridge the gap between my rural upbringing and the contemporary narratives that shape our world, capturing the essence of my journey and the stories that continue to guide me.\""}]}]} []

item.title: Lisette Forsyth
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641703100637 Lisette Forsyth 685 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640761708765 [2433,2442,2435,2436,2437,2438,2434,2443,2432,2439,2441,4475,2440] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Namibia when it was still South West Africa, Lisette Forsyth attended Jan van Riebeek Primary School, which was burnt down during the struggle. She then switched to Camps Bay High School - which was like a holiday camp compared to the constraints of the Afrikaner system. \\nAt Camps Bay she was able to model part-time from the age of 14 and managed to matriculate just before calculators were permitted in Maths in 1986. She travelled and worked in Europe as a model from 1987 until 1989. It was a huge hindrance to travel on a South African passport at this time. \\nShe returned to South Africa and studied Graphic Design at the Cape Technikon and graduated in 1999 - majoring in Printmaking and Photography. Only to find it all go digital the very next year. \\nForsyth worked in Europe in 1992. She completed an apprenticeship in Mechanical Graphics at the Bayerische Rundfunk (German Television Station) and returned to South Africa with her infant son permanently in 1994."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452160286941"]

item.title: Lisolomzi Pikoli

His work aims to interpret the mechanics of the modern world and our inherited wisdom through the human figure and its relationship to line, shape, form, movement and time. The main disciplines in his artistic practice revolve around painting, drawing, mural, installation and public art as a catalyst for social change, understanding and healing. Drawing and painting from his early childhood, he has gathered a wealth of both commercial and fine art experience. \\n \\nLisolomzi has shown work individually and in group shows in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Berlin, London, Tokyo and Amsterdam. He has also been hosted as an artist-in-residence by the Trinity Sessions, Soul City movement and the Keleketla! Library in Johannesburg. In August 2017, he was selected as one of Mzansi’s (South Africa’s) Top 100 Young Independents."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014029648093","gid://shopify/Product/9014029811933","gid://shopify/Product/9014030008541","gid://shopify/Product/9014030041309","gid://shopify/Product/9014030074077"]

item.title: Liza Grobler
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641703493853 Liza Grobler 544 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640762298589 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452042846429"] [11455,25373,24095] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Liza Grobler is a contemporary artist whose work explores the tangible qualities of materials and the connections between people, artworks and the world around us. Her work, largely process driven, blurs the traditions of craft and fine art. The viewer is encouraged to travel with her into an imaginary world where fact and fiction become one, everything is in flux, and anything is possible. \\n \\nIn 2016, she was a recipient of the Africa Centre Award and IZIKO Museum commissioned her to create a site-specific work for the National Gallery. Other career highlights include: a solo project for Cape Town International Art Fair (2017), a commissioned public artwork for Cape Town International Design Capital (2015) and the screening of her video work at the ADDIS International Video Arts Festival (Ethiopia) and at MOFO for Forever Now (Tasmania and Deep Space, 2015). She was short-listed for the Commonwealth Arts and Craft Award (2006). Grobler attended residencies in Norway, Finland, Switzerland, Belgium, France, Mexico, India, the United States (ARTOMI and Residency Unlimited) and initiated an international residency and exhibition ‘Smokey Signals from the Groot Karoo’ in South Africa (2017). Her beaded work in collaboration Qaqambile Bead Studio was showcased at 1:54 Art Fair (2015) and at Context Art Miami Fair in December 2019. She is represented by Everard Read Galleries (Cape Town, Johannesburg, London)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452042846429"]

item.title: Lloyd Maluleke
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641706115293 Lloyd Maluleke 2186 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640762855645 [] [23795] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lloyd Maluleke is a Limpopo-born, Johannesburg-based professional printer and artist exploring the theme of absent parentage from an unexpectedly positive and whimsical perspective. His practice delves into the emotional complexity of growing up without a father, but instead of approaching it from a standpoint of victimhood, Maluleke’s work invites viewers to see the world through the eyes of a child who, despite the absence, holds an idealized view of the missing parent. \\nMaluleke's personal experience as one of many South African children raised without a father due to the pressures of migration for work, particularly to the city, forms the foundation of his artistic approach. His mother, who explained this situation to him in a nurturing and non-bitter way, greatly influenced his understanding of absent parentage. She taught him that the community plays an integral role in shaping who a child becomes, a theme which Maluleke explores in his art. \\nHis prints often depict children wearing brightly colored hardhats or carrying shovels. These symbols are not to be understood as signs of child labor, but rather as visual representations of a child’s perception of a father figure who is off to the city to build a better life for his family. The vibrant yellow hardhats contrast with the muted tones of the figures and backgrounds, highlighting the larger-than-life image a child might hold of an absent parent. This whimsical approach captures the imagination of a child who idealizes his father’s role as a provider, while simultaneously acknowledging the significant role mothers and guardians play in shaping a child’s worldview. \\nIn contrast, Maluleke uses similar imagery of hardhats and shovels when depicting women in his prints, but here the symbolism shifts. The women, who are often left behind to shoulder the daily responsibilities of supporting the family, embody a more grounded, realistic interpretation of strength. The hardhats and shovels now represent the heavy, literal burden that these women carry, giving the work a deeper emotional resonance. \\nMaluleke’s work is a powerful reminder of how the narratives we grow up with, especially those shaped by caregivers, can profoundly affect how we perceive absence, strength, and resilience. His art speaks to the importance of community, the power of positivity, and the strength of the human spirit, all while addressing the complex issue of fatherlessness with both empathy and lightheartedness."}]}]} []

She combines this with her artistic practice, making art to express her personal experiences, with this sculpture part of a larger body of work."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452258525405"]

item.title: Lorraine Marcus
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641709457629 Lorraine Marcus 1357 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640764035293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013844607197","gid://shopify/Product/9013844639965","gid://shopify/Product/9013844672733","gid://shopify/Product/9013844705501","gid://shopify/Product/9013844738269","gid://shopify/Product/9013844771037","gid://shopify/Product/9013844803805","gid://shopify/Product/9013837955293"] [18637,18640,18642,18639,18641,18635,18643,18644,18638,18636] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lorraine Marcus is a South African Fine Artist who has been producing work prolifically for over 30 years. Her work is expressionist in style and her abstract, figurative practice is pure and refined. Marcus is known for her emotionally deep yet whimsical artworks that express her vivid interpretation of the world as she experiences it - with a poignant acknowledgement of sadness expressed through humour and absurdity - brought together in a catalogue of multi- textured artworks that both prompt and stimulate discussion. \\nMarcus's work embodies a commitment to delivering art that is true to her stories, experiences and world-view. Having had a long-term interest in art, Marcus has cultivated her artistic practice under the mentorship of South Africa's leading art teachers and artists including Lynda Ballen and Phillipa Kotzen. She spent her formative years working with Gail Mechanic and has since spent many years since painting and developing her style. She is currently working closely with Ricky Burnett. Lorraine’s portfolio consists of vibrant Pastel works, while her current focus is oil on canvas with some mixed media and collage. \\nMarcus has presented her work in a number of group exhibitions, and a collection of her curated work is currently on display at Life on Iris, as a part of the Light and Knight collection. \\nMarcus is a woman, a mother, a wife and a widow. She understands that women have a lot to say, and feels a need to embrace this. As such, she shares her experiences through her art. The images depicted are predominantly personal and sometimes abstractly imagined. Her experience of loss has shaped the ideas that she portrays in her art. The expressionist and abstract style of her work presents a rich exploration of texture, as she reveals her experience of colours and movement. Marcus’ portraiture seeks to convey the expressiveness of a face, through its form and character, gestures, movements and emotions. By painting abstractly, she highlights the ‘realness’ of human experiences and feelings. \\nSome of the themes she has explored in her work include family and maternity, popular culture, and the spaces she has navigated during her travels locally and abroad. Marcus has been significantly influenced by her travels in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Europe, Indonesia and Australia. She found that each of these spaces held their own charm, which evoked emotions in her that she felt driven to share through her art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013844607197","gid://shopify/Product/9013844639965","gid://shopify/Product/9013844672733","gid://shopify/Product/9013844705501","gid://shopify/Product/9013844738269","gid://shopify/Product/9013844771037","gid://shopify/Product/9013844803805","gid://shopify/Product/9013837955293"]

item.title: Louise VA
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641713029341 Louise VA gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640764494045 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"TCAG member artist Louise A, originally from the Philippines, has lived in Nigeria with her family since 2019. Louise began her artistic journey via painting in 2021. Considering her paintings a hobby and a passion, she’ll often give her paintings as birthday gifts to family and friends. \\n \\nLouise’s pieces contain layers of harmonious elements, bearing weight on her meticulous style when it comes to craftsmanship. With a natural flow in compositions, her paintings lead the eye on a specific and smooth journey through each piece. Louise ensures intention with each step of her creating process, particularly by using interesting elements and tools to paint with, such as leaves; nature scenery providing inspiration for her subject matter via multiple channels. This adds subtle, yet significant touches to her paintings. \\n \\nLouise’s paintings are performative in nature; she systematically records the entire painting process from beginning to end, creating an engaging time lapse where each piece comes to life. These combined elements provide an immersive experience, bringing her landscapes and subject matter to life."}]}]} []

item.title: LUCA EVANS
