Explore their artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"(b. 1994 Cape Town, South Africa ) Luca Evans is a Cape Town-based artist who works with wood and text. In 2018 they completed a BA Honours in Linguistics at the University of Cape Town. After six years studying and working with language, they made a shift towards tactile art-making, completing a BA in Contemporary Art at the Cape Town Creative Academy in 2022. In 2022 they co-founded Under Projects, an artist-run experimental project space where they work as a curator and programmer. They also lecture part-time in Conceptual and Curatorial practice. \\nThey currently work from a studio in Paarden Eiland, where they utilise a hit-and-miss experimental approach to carpentry and marquetry. Their pop-ish work plays with ideas around language, failure, mishap and humour. Since graduating in 2022, they have participated in a number of group exhibitions locally and internationally, as well as a Cubicle show at Everard Read Cape Town in January 2024. This is their first solo exhibition with the gallery. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129124573"]

item.title: Lucky Sibiya
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641716469981 Lucky Sibiya 556 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640765509853 [] [24600,24595] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lucky Sibiya was born in Vryheid, South Africa in 1942, Lucky Sibiya was internationally renowned for his abstract paintings and sculptural carvings. \\n \\nThe artist's fascination with the abstract began in his childhood, partly due to his presence at his father's consultations as a Sangoma. Here strange and beautiful artefacts were used to assist in diagnostic and traditional healing medicine. \\n \\nThe destruction of the colourful neighbourhood of Sophiatown during the Fifties resulted in the Sibiya family relocating to Soweto. During his school years he was sent away to Hammanskraal where the young boy experimented with woodcarvings. Shortly before completing his school education at St. Peter's Seminary, Lucky introduced himself to Cecil Skotnes, armed with some of his painted 'found' objects. Skotnes was at this time one of South Africa's foremost contemporary artists. He was head of the Polly Street Art Centre in Johannesburg and he promoted young talent. Skotnes was enthusiastic to accept Sibiya as a private pupil. His mentor's engraved paintings were influential in Sibiya's decision to paint on carved wood. \\n \\nSibiya took folk art to its most expressive and sophisticated levels. By rubbing powdered pigments into richly engraved images, Sibiya's compositions progressed from purely decorative to a conceptually abstract vision. As the artist matured, his leaning to carve, rather than to engrave, presented what would emerge as Sibiya's unique signature. The most distinctive features of his style are his use of organic shapes which are connected with flowing, rhythmic lines, juxtaposed on a background of complex carved and painted relief and intaglio spaces. \\n \\nFor the last thirty years of his life his work moved towards more deeply carved studies on a two dimensional plane and working the wood into an almost three dimensional art form. Compounding this form was his addition of intricately worked found objects. These include clothing, steel, leather and richly rusted metals. Over the years he devised a language of abstract symbols; unique and instantly recognizable. \\n \\nThe physical demand of Sibiya's technique was matched only by the harmonious, spiritual feeling experienced when transported into his world of ritual. Key elements of his figurative work include ancient tribal traditions and rites of passage. \\n \\nIn addition to his contribution to the visual arts, Sibiya also contributed to the performing arts with his portfolio illustrations of classic drama. His work, inspired by Welcome Msomi's adaptation of \"Macbeth\" was highly acclaimed at that time and travelled to the Royal Ceasaria Theatre in Israel and the Old Vic Theatre in London. This Umbatha portfolio was well received in Australia where it featured at the South African Exhibition in Canberra. \\n \\nLucky Sibiya tragically passed away in a road accident on 24 January 1999."}]}]} []

item.title: Lugra Ilunga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641718567133 Lugra Ilunga 2731 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640766591197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014026928349","gid://shopify/Product/9014026961117","gid://shopify/Product/9014027026653","gid://shopify/Product/9014027059421"] Explore the bold and dynamic works of Lugra Ilunga, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Ilunga’s art blends vivid color, abstract forms, and rich cultural themes to create powerful visual stories that engage with identity, heritage, and societal issues. [22848,22847,22850,22849] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lugra Israel Ilunga (b. 1995, Lubumbashi, DRC) is a Congolese-born, Johannesburg based mixed media artist who interrogates the complexities of masculinity in modern society. Shaped by his experiences an immigrant in one of Africa's most dynamic urban centers, Lugra brings a unique perspective to his work. He trained as a mixed-media artist at the Little Artist School Project and as a printmaker at Artist Proof Studios. \\nLugra's art combines techniques such as drawing with ink and charcoal, collage, and oil pastels. He challenges traditional narratives while celebrating the diverse dimensions of masculinity. Central to his practice is the concept of \"the outside world\"—both a physical and metaphorical space. Historically seen as a male-dominated sphere of provision and growth, the outside world also represents a space of temptation, corruption, and moral challenge. Lugra explores this duality, depicting masculinity as both evolving and under pressure in a rapidly changing world. \\nLugra has exhibited in group exhibitions with Little Artist School Project Annual art exhibition presented by Deutsche Bank at JSE Sandton, the Society for Animal in Distress presented by JSE Deutsche Bank at Graham's Fine Art, both in Johannesburg, South Africa. Johannesburg plays a significant role in his current body of work, symbolizing ambition, cultural diversity, and the pursuit of wealth. Using cityscapes, iconic landmarks, and masculine objects, Lugra crafts visual narratives that explore the struggles, principles, and societal expectations imposed on men. \\nLugra's work questions and redefines constructs of masculinity in South African society, across Africa, and globally, opening conversations about its celebration, critique, and transformation. In addition to his artistic pursuits, Lugra holds a law degree from the University of Johannesburg and is passionate about human rights—a theme that informs some of his current and future works. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014026928349","gid://shopify/Product/9014026961117","gid://shopify/Product/9014027026653","gid://shopify/Product/9014027059421"]

item.title: Luís Damião
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641732395229 Luís Damião gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640769769693 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066668765","gid://shopify/Product/9452066701533","gid://shopify/Product/9452066734301"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Luís Damião (b. 1978, Luanda, Angola) is best known for his photography work, which integrates a strong component of research and experimentation. Namely, the artist focuses on developing unconventional production and presentation methods, integrating a generation of emerging artists whose new perspectives around traditional compositions are highly influenced by the age of digital technology and image manipulation. \\n \\nAesthetically, his constructions often refer to the universe of documentary photography, but simultaneously to an elaborate staging of the images. This performative aspect of his work results in the recurring fading of the border between what is real - documental - and what is fiction and is often used to emphasize proposals for reflection on the social and political experiences of Luanda’s urban context. \\n \\nLuís Damião was born into a family with strong artistic roots, his father Paulino Damião (Kota 50) being a photographer and photojournalist, and his brother Lino Damião, also an artist. Influenced and incentivized by his family, he was early involved in the art world as an autodidact. Later on, he attended the Visual Arts course at the former Barracão, organized by the Swedish Embassy in Angola, and in 2002, presented himself publicly for the first time. Since then, he has been exhibiting and collaborating on cultural projects regularly. \\n \\nIn 2020, his work “Coronavírus” was awarded the special prize of photography and the Alliance Française Prize – Ensa Arte 2020, in Luanda. As part of this award, Damião took part in an artistic residency in Paris in 2021, funded by the Embassy of France. In the same year, he completed two other artistic residencies: in Lisbon, supported by THIS IS NOT A WHITE CUBE Art Gallery, and in Porto, by d’O INSTITUTO. Furthermore, in the context of AKKA – Art & Design Fair 2021, the book “À rebrousse-temps” - which includes an essay devoted to Damião’s artistic production by the curator Dénètem Touam - was launched."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066668765","gid://shopify/Product/9452066701533","gid://shopify/Product/9452066734301"]

item.title: Lulu Mhlana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641722171613 Lulu Mhlana 2194 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640767344861 [] [16018,16019,16020] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Biography \\nSouth African-born visual artist, activist and photographer Lulu Mhlana (Nolubabalo) (b.1993) is from the Eastern Cape and currently works and lives in Cape Town. \\nMhlana is one of the country's foremost young photographers exploring representations of gender identity and non-binary bodies. They became as a self-trained lens-based artist after her Diploma in Business Communications from the Tshwane University of Technology (2014). She was awarded the Zanele Muholi Scholarship in Technical Photography at Cape Town School of Photography (2018). \\nMhlana centres her practice around the intimacy of black bodies and black existence in rewriting the current and historical narratives of blackness. The folds of memory in the quiet moments of skin and culture layers the sensitivity and poise in her work. \\nThrough Documentary Photography Mhlana forged a unique position as woman in documenting the intricate and sacred custom of male initiation through the partnership and guidance of her mother’s organisation Ubuntu Care and Development that prepares young men with skillsets into adulthood ahead of their initiation, amongst other social issues. In this regard the body in relation to cultural identity as a subject through sacredness is introduced in her work. \\nSwitching in between the mediums of Documentary Photography and Self-Portraiture, under the tutelage of Lindeka Qampi and Zanele Muholi, her flagship project, Ubumnyama Bam was realised in 2019. \\nHer work is a personal and shared archive of blackness, and continues to contribute to the lack of representation of the black body in mainstream media."}]}]} []

[22421,22674,21096,20117,21093,21098,11434,11389] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lungile Ngcobo is a visual artist from Johannesburg. She also took part in Season 2 of \"Occupying the Gallery\" at SMAC Gallery. \\nUnder the mentorship of Tatenda Chidora during the 2023 Incubator Programme at the Market Photo Workshop, she won first prize in the 2024 Sanlam Group and Youth Content Collective exhibition titled \"Roots Unveiled.\" In 2024, she exhibited in a pop-up show with Stevenson Gallery Group titled \"Kiki\" and was part of the Zine launched at the opening of Fouad Asfour's PhD exhibition at Wits Art Museum. \\nLungile's storytelling prowess shines through her exploration of the themes of \"home\" and \\n“identity” in her work. item.title: Lwando Dlamini
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641733771485 Lwando Dlamini 261 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640772391133 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013378220253","gid://shopify/Product/9452102648029"] [21610,13097] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lwando Dlamini, born in Eastern Cape, is a South African artist based between Cape Town and Johannesburg. Using oil paints and mixed media, his work explores the fragility of the human body, memory loss, and the complexities of black joy. His signature style features thick, textured brushstrokes and distorted figures that challenge conventional ideas of beauty. Inspired by lived experiences and social imagery, Dlamini's art delves into themes of resilience, discomfort, and liberation. \\n \\nA graduate of the Ruth Prowse School of Art, Dlamini has exhibited at major art fairs, including FNB Art Joburg, Intersect Chicago, Investec Cape Town Art Fair, and African Galleries Now. His first solo exhibition, ‘Triumph’, debuted at EBONY/CURATED in 2020, followed by ‘Learning How to Be Less Afraid Brave’ in 2022. Among his accolades, he received the 2018 David Koloane Award, was a finalist in the Absa L'Atelier Art Competition, and won the August House Emerging Residency Artist Award in 2022. Committed to supporting emerging Black artists, he established an art prize at the Ruth Prowse School of Art. \\n \\nSolo Exhibitions: \\n \\n2022 LEARNING HOW TO BE LESS AFRAID BRAVE, EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2020 Triumph, EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions \\n \\n2022 Investec Cape Town Art Fair, EBONY/CURATED Main Booth B3, South Africa \\n2021 Everything Was Beautiful and Nothing Hurt, Open City, Keyes Art Mile, Rosebank, \\nJohannesburg, South Africa \\n \\n8X8, EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa \\nInvestec Cape Town Art Fair Digital Event \\nEBONY/CURATED booth, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\n1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair, New York, United States of America \\n \\n‘In [the] Loop, EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\n‘In his work, Dlamini layers paint thickly onto the surface so that brushstrokes and palette knife marks are visible. This has become a distinct feature of his oeuvre. Dlamini highlights his commitment to testing the boundaries of his working mediums....... we are confronted with discomfort - images and figures that are curved and distorted, with certain features (eyes and lips in particular) exaggerated and others (nose and ears) minimised. These are extraordinary images not concerned with simple ideas of beauty — but rather, they are an investigation of fragility and the strangeness of life’. - Nkgopoleng Moloi"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013378220253","gid://shopify/Product/9452102648029"]

item.title: Lynette Musukubili
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641737441501 Lynette Musukubili 1990 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640774652125 [] [25011,25012,25014,25010,25024,25016,25017,25013,25009] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lynette Musukubili (b. 1995, Windhoek) earned a Diploma in Visual Arts from the University of Namibia in 2022. She has participated in group shows in Namibia, and her work was shown by the NJE Collective at the Investec Cape Town Art Fair in 2022. Musukubili is a recipient of the Africa Prime Initiative (API) Grant, which aims to equip African creatives with funding to develop their skills and to showcase their work and talent. Of the ‘born free’ generation in a newly independent country, Musukubili navigates the challenges of being a young woman in Namibia, often commenting on social issues, including the overwhelmingly high incidence of violence against women and girls. Elements of her Caprivian (Zambezi) heritage are deeply embedded in her recent work. She held her first solo exhibition at the Project Room Namibia in March 2023."}]}]} []

item.title: Lyra Ouattara
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641740226781 Lyra Ouattara 2464 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640776093917 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082299101"] Lyra Ouattara [19424] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Lyra Akissi Ouattara is an Ivorian sculptor and curator based in Abidjan. Her practice is rooted in her sense of culture, spirituality, and aesthetics developed during her childhood in Cote d’Ivoire. It explores the links between traditional codes, modern problematics and identity. Her preferred medium is clay, defining herself as an artist and healer, she creates objects of spiritual healing, shaping pathways through sculptural artefacts as portals. Currently, the forms she creates earth-side are coming to her through mediation as she believes these forms to be sent by Women ancestors, as tools to serve for reclaiming of Women sacred bodies and spirits. After training in Arts Administration and Communication at the University of Ottawa, she returned to Abidjan, where she began her career as a sculptor in 2023."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082299101"]

Upon leaving art school, Madeleine followed a career in the advertising and publishing industry for two decades, and also ran a small gallery before finally getting the opportunity to start working as a full time artist herself. She currently works from her home studio in Cape Town, doing mainly painting and experimental prints. \\nShe uses her personal experiences as reference and tries to recreate the atmosphere of each experience in her work, rather than focussing on the exact details. Current recurring themes include landscapes, cityscapes and domestic situations. The latter sometimes include the use of animals as a symbolic reference, carrying a message that is sometimes dark and disturbing and at other times tongue in cheek."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452051136733","gid://shopify/Product/9013458403549","gid://shopify/Product/9013458469085","gid://shopify/Product/9013458534621","gid://shopify/Product/9013458567389","gid://shopify/Product/9013458600157","gid://shopify/Product/9013458632925","gid://shopify/Product/9013458698461","gid://shopify/Product/9013459157213","gid://shopify/Product/9013459189981","gid://shopify/Product/9013459255517","gid://shopify/Product/9013459484893","gid://shopify/Product/9452150030557","gid://shopify/Product/9452258590941","gid://shopify/Product/9452258656477","gid://shopify/Product/9452258689245"]

item.title: Madikotsi "Mummy" Khumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641743339741 Madikotsi "Mummy" Khumalo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640783139037 [] Gauteng artist Madikotsi "Mummy" Khumalo (b.1988) uses bright colours & vivid imagery to explore complex themes of war, control, spirituality & the divine feminine beneath a deceptive surface. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Madikotsi \"Mummy\" Khumalo (b. 1988, Sebokeng, Gauteng) is a contemporary South African artist known for her distinctive visual language. Her work immediately engages viewers with bright colours and vivid imagery, often creating an initial impression of lightness and happiness. However, close inspection reveals a deeper layer of commentary and exploration. \\n \\nBeneath the vibrant surface, Khumalo tackles complex and challenging themes, including representations of war, the concept of control over the human soul, and the profound presence—or sometimes absence—of spirituality. A significant and recurring element in her art is the divine feminine energy, often manifested as a powerful Goddess figure, symbolizing the mother of all existence. Through this juxtaposition of aesthetics and subject matter, Khumalo prompts viewers to look beyond the surface and contemplate intricate aspects of the human condition and spiritual life."}]}]} []

item.title: Maingaila Muvundika
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641750221021 Maingaila Muvundika 2543 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640787693789 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014032138461"] Maingaila Muvundika [22960] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maingaila Muvundika (b.1999) is a Zambian visual artist and photographer whose work explores how different demographic elements of a community inform how people interact and navigate within the wider community. Through costuming and the production of sets, Maingaila produces staged photographs that are deeply personal and observant. His practice probes aspects of individuality, fashion, beauty standards, spirituality and belonging as a discovery into how identity and sense of self is shaped. \\nGrowing up, Maingaila was always fascinated with his family’s photo album. This is where his fascination with the medium began. In his teens, he started \\nan Instagram account that became a repository of many photographs of his immediate surroundings and observations, from foggy mornings on his way to \\nschool or plant matter in his home. \\nAs his practice developed, he began to incorporate his love for fashion and editorials with self portraiture which he is now known for. \\nWhile pursuing a Banking and Finance degree at Mulungushi University, he turned the camera on his friends. Deeping his practice to not only encompass \\nfashion and self-portraiture but to also investigate different sociological issues of class, familial structures and the establishment with a focus on how the \\nshape who we become and when we become. In recent years, his practice has expanded to printmaking and collage further exploring his dissection of \\nwhat it means to be."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014032138461"]

item.title: MAKANO
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641754317021 MAKANO gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640776913117 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452094783709"] MAKANO {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Makano (b. 2000, Bukavu) is a Congolese visual artist based in Kampala, Uganda, with a multifaceted practice in which writing plays a central role. His work is influenced by his native country, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), a nation marked by conflict. The DRC has endured decades of political instability and armed conflicts, resulting in the demise of countless individuals, including Makano’s parents. In 2018, his life was irrevocably altered by the tragic loss of his parents during the civil war in the Democratic Republic of Congo. This heart-wrenching event plunged him into a vortex of grief, depression, and frustration. The weight of his past, coupled with an uncertain future, drove him to confront a present filled with rebellion and despair, even pushing him to the brink of suicide. However, from this abyss of darkness, Makano unearthed unexpected strength and purpose. He transformed from a grieving son to an empowered artist. Makano’s work is a testament to the human spirit’s capacity to find meaning and voice amid chaos. His art serves as a therapeutic outlet, a poignant reflection of his internal struggles, and a response to the ceaseless dialogue of society. His works are not unadorned expressions of personal anguish but eloquent contributions to the collective narrative, inviting viewers to engage in a communal exchange of ideas and emotions. He channels tumultuous thought processes into superimposed pieces of abstract poetry that sometimes contract into the form of a manic third-eye alter ego, grinning the artist’s name “Makano.” \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452094783709"]

item.title: Manuela Pimentel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641768210653 Manuela Pimentel 2408 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794378461 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066767069","gid://shopify/Product/9452066799837","gid://shopify/Product/9452066832605"] [19054,19056,19055] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Manuela Pimentel (b. 1979, Portugal) ingeniously fuses together references to the traditional handicraft art of painted mural tiles with the aesthetics of street billboards and their cumulative layers of ripped and lacerated advertising posters. Bearing in mind post-war artists of the New Realism movement such as Mimmo Rotella, Raymond Hains or Jacques Villeglé, Pimentel incorporates fragments of street posters she takes off herself or uses them as supports for her painted interventions. \\n \\nUsing acrylic colours, the artist accurately reproduces traditional figures and scenes taken from the visual culture of the Portuguese tiles (azulejos). By integrating the tiles’ conventional chromaticism, iconography and naif-style rendering into specific wall-mounted artworks, and by merging all of it with torn street posters, adding resins, rough mortar and neon lights, the artist reconfigures the place of the tile as a popular and decorative expression that used to belong to local collective memory to inscribe it in the space of global artistic creation."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452066767069","gid://shopify/Product/9452066799837","gid://shopify/Product/9452066832605"]

item.title: Marguerite Roux
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641777025245 Marguerite Roux 622 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640797098205 [] [3190,3191,3193,3192] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marguerite Roux was born in 1991 in the Karoo town of Beaufort West. She grew up in Wellington in the Cape Winelands and matriculated from La Rochelle Girls’ High School in Paarl. In 2018 Roux obtained her MA Visual Arts degree from the University of Stellenbosch, prior to which she completed a BAVA (Fine Arts) degree from the same institution in 2014. In 2014, Roux was awarded the Keith Dietrich Award for students who pass their final year with a distinction as well as the Timo Smuts prize for top academic achiever in Fine Arts. Marguerite Roux is a three time top 100 finalist in the Sasol New Signatures Award competition. \\n \\nSince graduating in 2014 Roux has taken part in a number of group exhibitions, including Greatest Hits: The Domestic Odyssey presented by the AVA Gallery in 2015 and Hinterlands: The Keith Dietrich Award Exhibition at GUS in the same year. Most notably Roux’s work has been shown at the 4th Istanbul Design Biennial, in Turkey as part of Emelie Röndahl’s project Google Weaving Stop-Time in 2018 and at the Also Known as Africa (AKAA) Art Fair in Paris, France with Dyman Gallery in 2019."}]}]} []

item.title: Marie Aimée Fattouche
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641785872605 Marie Aimée Fattouche gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640798605533 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013979283677", "gid://shopify/Product/9013979349213", "gid://shopify/Product/9013979447517"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1991,Marie Aimée Fattouche lives and works in Seine-Saint-Denis, France. Marie draws inspiration from her fascination with mechanics, whether mental, bodily, or environmental. From simple disruptions to breakdowns, from initial impulses to the ultimate fluidity of movement, her art navigates the space between repair and sublimation, exploring areas of uncertainty where contradictory possibilities converge. For her, each fracture, whether tangible or abstract, serves as a catalyst for profound transformation. \\nImbued with her Egyptian roots, her perspective on the organization of bodies reflects Eastern perceptions of space. Through her work, she actively interrogates collective narratives and femininity while scrutinizing mechanisms of power and belief systems. Her artistic compositions offer a multitude of perspectives, both spatial and temporal, inviting the viewer to immerse themselves in a construction perpetually in motion, transcending mere representation. \\nFollowing her final MA Fine Art exhibition in 2016 (Chelsea College of Arts, London), M.A Fattouche was awarded the Mercers’ Arts Award. In 2017, as the winner of the Red Mansion Art Prize, she was invited to spend a month of residency in Beijing. In 2019, she had the honor of being among the eight artists shortlisted for the Mark Tanner Sculpture Award at Standpoint Gallery in London (the UK’s most prestigious prize for emerging artists working in sculpture). Her work has been exhibited in various institutions, including the Hock-ney Gallery (2018), and more recently at the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MAMC+) in Saint-Étienne as part of the GLOBALISTO exhibition (June to October 2022). In January 2024, she has presented her solo exhibition NOUS INFINIR MON AMOUR at Galerie du Haut-Pavé in Paris."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013977383133","gid://shopify/Product/9013977579741","gid://shopify/Product/9013979283677","gid://shopify/Product/9013979349213","gid://shopify/Product/9013979447517"]

item.title: Marie Kenny
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641786724573 Marie Kenny 2750 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640798867677 Discover Marie Kenny, a self-taught lens-based artist from Lyon, France, who uses photography to explore identity, cultural heritage, and neurodivergence. Her work merges documentary style with painterly qualities, inviting viewers into a contemplative space. [23005] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marie Kenny (b. 1984), a self-taught contemporary lens-based artist from Lyon, France, has been passionate about art from a young age. After studying the cello at the Conservatoire de Lyon, she moved to the UK and Ireland in her early twenties to further her studies in music, language, art history, and literature. \\nMotherhood, particularly raising neurodivergent children, deepened her commitment to photography, which she uses as a tool to navigate and understand the world, and explore her own neurodivergence. Radical acceptance and mindfulness are central to her practice. \\nMarie’s work merges documentary style with painterly qualities, using light, movement, and framing to create images that feel both immediate and timeless. Her art explores themes such as identity, cultural and familial heritage, and neurodivergence, inviting viewers into a contemplative space where fleeting, nuanced moments are celebrated. \\nMarie draws inspiration from her experiences and has been a mentee of the Through the Lens Collective."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014034366685"]

item.title: Marie-Lorraine Kalassa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641783644381 Marie-Lorraine Kalassa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640799260893 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013927051485", "gid://shopify/Product/9013927117021", "gid://shopify/Product/9013927149789"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Through an autoethnographic practice; that is the primary use of personal reflexive writing to craft narratives related to wider social and cultural experiences, Lorraine Kalassa explores themes revolving around her experiences of ‘otherness’. \\nHer main focus lies in trying to make sense of notions of home as a person born in South Africa with ancestry rooted in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Lorraine is fascinated with her family photo archive as well as the archive existing within her mother’s mind. She is also intrigued by how relationship with land and place influences the development of identity and culture. Returning to her ancestral archives have become important sites of exploration and excavation for her work as this act becomes a form of pilgrimage and time travel to her place of origin. By using a range of media and thinking through cracks in identity, landscape and policies, Lorraine ultimately tethers ancestral fragments as a means to remember and heal. \\nLorraine’s obtained a degree in Fine Arts from the Michaelis School of Fine Arts and an Honours degree in Landscape Architecture from the University of Cape Town. Lorraine is a member of The Photographic Collective(TPC) and has been featured in the following exhibitions and publications: \\nUnder Projects, Cape Town: JIVE Exhibition, 2023 ,Goethe-Institut, Johannesburg: JIVE Exhibition, 2023, Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg: We are Culture Exhibition, Sept-Oct 2022 ArtThrob: Family Albums, September 2021, 99 Loop Gallery, Cape Town: 12 Hours of Breathing (group show), July 2021 Group exhibition with TPC, London: 1-54, Contemporary African Art Fair, 2021 In conversation with The Photographic Collective (TPC): In Conversation with Lorraine Kalassa, May 2020"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013927051485","gid://shopify/Product/9013927117021","gid://shopify/Product/9013927149789","gid://shopify/Product/9013944713437"]

item.title: Marilú Mapengo Námoda
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641792917725 Marilú Mapengo Námoda gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640800407773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452048253149","gid://shopify/Product/9452048285917","gid://shopify/Product/9452048318685","gid://shopify/Product/9452048351453"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marilú Mapengo Námoda is an artist that engages with the politics of giving birth to the futureS. Her research explores the possibility of a love politics for healing colonial wounds in its multiple expressions of racism, machismo, classism, etc. Through hybrid formats, their practice weaves languages from performance art, animist astrology, storytelling, Bantu writing symbols, healing rituals, and post-activist provocateur prompts. Her work has been exhibited at the Santarcangelo Festival (Italy, 2022), Spielart Festival (Germany, 2021), Kaserne Basel (Switzerland, 2021), and Entretodos Human Rights Festival, ( Brazil, 2019), among others. \\nNámoda holds a MA degree in Art Praxis from the Dutch Art Institute, Arnhem 2022; A BA in Sociology from the Eduardo Mondlane University - Maputo, 2013; and a Post-Graduation Degree in Gender Studies from the University of Iceland /UNU GEST Program – Reykjavik, 2016. In 2022 the Artist was nominated for two international awards: The Berry Koedam Award by Kunstinstituut Melly, Netherlands, and The Paulo Cunha e Silva award by the Municipality of Porto, Portugal."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452048253149","gid://shopify/Product/9452048285917","gid://shopify/Product/9452048318685","gid://shopify/Product/9452048351453"]

item.title: Marion Boehm
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641795375325 Marion Boehm 636 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640801554653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062867677","gid://shopify/Product/9452062933213","gid://shopify/Product/9452115165405","gid://shopify/Product/9452115296477","gid://shopify/Product/9452168577245"] [23180,18484,16614,23181,16610,16613,16609,16603,16612,16604,16608,16605,18489] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marion Boehm worked as Interior Architect in Europe before moving to South Africa in 2010. Being engaged in a private community project in Kliptown, she began her artistic career in Johannesburg creating her unique, magnificent collages. The artist addresses and examines the interfaces and relationships between African and Western cultures in history until nowadays. Her themes relate to personal experiences and are reflected in her different series focusing on socio-economic and cultural matters. Her work is an impressive combination of artistic integrity, conceptual vision and aesthetic beauty. \\n \\n2020 \\n- Solo Show - OOA Gallery - Barcelona, Spain \\n- Art X Lagos Art Fair - OOA Gallery - Lagos, Nigeria \\n- 1-54 New York Online Art Fair - OOA Gallery - New York, USA \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n2019 \\n- “On paper” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n- Cape Town Art fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- Expo Chicago – ARTCO Gallery – Chicago, USA \\n- “Filam(a)nt Exhibition – Fondation Blachère – Apt, France \\n- “Spaces in Between” Exhibition – This is Not a White Cube Gallery - Lisbon, Portugal \\n- AKAA ART Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- Paper Positions Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Berlin, Germany \\n- Latitudes Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Gallery Michel Giraud – Paris, France - Luxembourg Art Week – Gallery Michel Giraud – Luxembourg, Grand-Dûché de Luxembourg \\n2018 \\n- “Background Africa” - SOART Gallery – Casablanca, Morocco \\n- AKAA Art Fair - ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- 1-54 London Art Fair (solo show) – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Black Paris” (solo show) – Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- “Unfolding fibre” - Pretoria Art Museum – Pretoria, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- London Art Fair (solo show) – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n2017 \\n- “Hairitage” - AKAA Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- “Stitched” (solo show) – Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- “Rituale” - Afrikahaus Aachen – Aachen, Germany \\n2016 \\n- “Maskerade” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n- AKAA Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- That Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- “Targets” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n2015 \\n- Start Art Fair Saatchi Gallery – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n- Art Vilnius – ARTCO Gallery – Vilnius, Lithuania \\n- “Swenkas” (solo show) – In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Ubuntu Reflections” (solo show) – Alliance Française – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – Cape Town, South Africa \\n2014 \\n- Group exhibition – Youngblood Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Silent beauty” (solo show) – Saxon Hotel – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Silent beauty” (solo show) – Alliance Française – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Gold rush” - In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2013 \\n- Joburg Fringe Art Fair – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Group Exhibition - The German Weeks – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Patched” (solo show) – In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2012 \\n- Grand Hyatt Hotel Rosebank – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\nHer newest series “Legacy” interprets a new African identity based on traditional roots facing the confusion of a globalized world. “In my series„ Legacy, I want to point out that the African continent has a rich cultural background to build on” says Marion. Her mixed media collages with traditional African masks, beads, cawrie shells and fabrics highlight the beauty, loyalty and positive energy of the African women. \\n \\nThe traditional African masks that Marion Boehm integrates in her artworks were used in traditional and social events to represent the spirits of ancestors or to control the good and evil forces in the community. They come to life, possessed by their spirit in the performance of the dance and are enhanced by the music and atmosphere of the occasion. Some masks combine human and animal features to unite man with his natural environment. This bond with nature is of great importance to the African and, through the ages, masks have always been used to express this relationship. \\n \\n“I use African masks in my work to relate to the beauty and spiritual power of them in the context of a culturally impoverished and spiritually distressed modern world. But do they still have their original meaning? What do they represent to the generation of today? Can they be a point of reference and still offer a kind of orientation? What do the traditions mean for today’s life and what do they teach us for the future?” In order to underline her message, Marion’s statement is always printed in the faces of her characters. \\n \\nMarion Boehm ?s work has been collected internationally. Her artwork was presented during shows and art fairs in South Africa, Germany, France, UK, Lithuania, Morocco, Portugal, Luxemburg, Switzerland, USA. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062867677","gid://shopify/Product/9452062933213","gid://shopify/Product/9452115165405","gid://shopify/Product/9452115296477","gid://shopify/Product/9452168577245"]

item.title: Marisa Maré
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798193373 Marisa Maré gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640802603229 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marisa Maré is an artist and educator from the Western Cape who investigates the pressing issues related to climate change. \\nAs a leader in the arts education space she has actively developed her students' awareness of climate change issues through various educational initiatives. This included participation in the Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Programme, collaboration with the WWF, and planning and presenting a webinar titled Drought in South Africa: Resilience in the Face of Climate Change. Marisa has won the Bow Seat global Educator Innovation Award for two years. \\nMore recently, she has turned her focus to her visual arts practice completing a Master's degree in Visual Arts at the University of Johannesburg with distinction. Her dissertation and exhibition titled Making and Unmaking: Plastic Matters explored themes such as grieving ecological loss, and developing empathy with nonhumans. In her exploration of the creative and destructive potential of plastic, Maré has developed bioplastic from natural and agricultural waste materials, utilising them as art materials for her experimental works. She documents the degradation of these bioplastic sculptures through photographic and microscopic imaging to raise questions about the possibility of 'touching the Earth lightly'. Through her creative process, she aims to uncover how her choice of medium is entangled with an extensive web of environmental factors. To some extent, her sculptures and the microbesaiding in their decay are ‘performers’ with agency beyond the artist’s control that render the entangled materiality visible. \\nIn earlier bodies of work, she has been concerned with the impermanence and transience of her art materials. In an exhibition titled Symptoms, she created an installation that included sculptural works with hand-made paper, gauze, rust and salt which pointed to 'symptoms' that are indexical of broader societal concerns."}]}]} []

item.title: Mark Modimola
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798258909 Mark Modimola 1593 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640803127517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013371961565", "gid://shopify/Product/9013371994333"] [21597,21599,12510,12511,9606] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I am an African Visual Artist, born in Pretoria. Originally a graphic designer, I consider myself a versatile creator, with a portfolio that explores the cadences of African identity and spirituality, often through the cultural aesthetics of portraiture and surrealism. I aim to emphasize the experience of blackness through my work. I believe in sharing positive representation to and for the black community while translating the complexity we bring to the world through vivid imagery. I am highly inspired by nature, it’s authenticity, unending originality and innovation. As such, my passions are tied in with Africa; its land and its people, this can be seen in my work. \\nOver recent years, I have been involved in a range of international projects. My work features on several articles by The Kraal who have published: The Guide to African Spirituality. Volume 0, in which my artwork of Ma’at is featured. I worked on a South African history graphic novel called “All Rise ; Resistance and Rebellion “. My work will appear in an upcoming American book called Black Joy Project. In 2021, I worked on a campaign for #Giveheracrown, an initiative raising funds for young female Africa designers in association with Jaguar, in which my work was donated and exhibited. \\nMy work has been exhibited in Art it is Gallery as well as Stargazer gallery among other. group shows in Johannesburg. Having participated in an Online art Residency known as BLVCK BLOCK I have explored natural themes and materials in a search for a deeper connection between contemporary Africans and nature. Recently I showcased my new clay and acrylic paintings at Solo restaurant in Sandton, as well as Troyeville house in Johannesburg with The Culture Review."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013371961565","gid://shopify/Product/9013371994333","gid://shopify/Product/9014000156893","gid://shopify/Product/9014000189661"]

item.title: Marsi van de Heuvel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641804681437 Marsi van de Heuvel gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640807256285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452081414365"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marsi van de Heuvel is a Cape Town-based artist. \\nHer current work deals with visibly, using paint to explore the act of fading as part of the artist’s broader interest in what it means to belong to a place, to a family and to a particular culture. \\nThe artist deals with this erasure through family photographs that record their experiences before forced removals in Upington and Graaff Reinet during this period in South Africa’s history: I use the mediation of these photographs to bridge past to present, to feel out what resonates, what I connect with, what’s worth keeping and to preserve what needs to be re-imagined, reframed, restored, and repaired – van de Heuvel"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452081414365"]

item.title: Mary Sibande
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641807728861 Mary Sibande gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640808829149 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013991276765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013991309533", "gid://shopify/Product/9013991342301", "gid://shopify/Product/9013991440605", "gid://shopify/Product/9013991473373", "gid://shopify/Product/9013991571677", "gid://shopify/Product/9014052389085", "gid://shopify/Product/9014088433885"] Mary Sibande, a South African sculptor and visual artist, explores identity and the black female body through her alter-ego, Sophie. Her innovative work blends sculpture, photography, and installation, and has earned her numerous awards, including the Smithsonian African Artist Award. Sibande's art is exhibited globally, reflecting post-colonial and post-apartheid themes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mary Sibande (b. 1982, Barberton, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist renowned for her compelling explorations of identity, the black female body, and the socio-political landscape of post-colonial and post apartheid South Africa. She received her Diploma in Fine Arts from the Witwaterand Technical College and her Honours degree from the University of Johannesburg in 2007. \\nSibande's practice combines sculpture, photography, and installation, often centered around her alter-ego, Sophie. This sculptural figure, modeled after herself and inspired by the women in her family, serves as a powerful symbol of femininity, labour, and the intersection of personal and collective histories. Sophie's attire, blending domestic worker uniforms with extravagant Victorian dress, subverts traditional power structures and challenges historical narratives. \\nHer work addresses sensitive topics such as gender-based violence, ensuring dignity and respect for the women she represents. Sibande's art has evolved through phases marked by distinct colors—Blue, Purple, and currently Red—each reflecting a shift in focus and narrative depth. \\nSibande's notable achievements include the Helgaard Steyn Prize for Sculpture (2021), the Smithsonian African Artist Award (2017), and the Standard Bank Young Artist Award for Visual Arts (2013). She has exhibited widely, including at the 54th Venice Biennale (2011), the 12th Biennale of Contemporary Art in Lyon (2013), and recent solo shows such as \"Unhand Me, Demon!\" at Kavi Gupta Gallery in Chicago (2021) and \"The Red Ventriloquist\" at Musée d’art Contemporain de Lyon (2022). \\nAs co-founder of Occupying the Gallery, Sibande transforms gallery spaces into open studios for mentorship and artistic development. Her work continues to evolve, now focusing on future-oriented themes and the transformative power of imagination and storytelling. \\nSibande resides in Johannesburg, where she remains deeply connected to the society and culture that inspire her art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013943795933","gid://shopify/Product/9013991276765","gid://shopify/Product/9013991309533","gid://shopify/Product/9013991342301","gid://shopify/Product/9013991440605","gid://shopify/Product/9013991473373","gid://shopify/Product/9013991571677","gid://shopify/Product/9014016737501","gid://shopify/Product/9014052389085","gid://shopify/Product/9014067822813","gid://shopify/Product/9014067855581","gid://shopify/Product/9014067921117","gid://shopify/Product/9014088433885","gid://shopify/Product/9014115369181"]

item.title: Mashir Kresenshun
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641808679133 Mashir Kresenshun 1237 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640809976029 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452135416029","gid://shopify/Product/9452172574941","gid://shopify/Product/9452172607709"] Discover the art of Mashir Kresenshun, a South African artist based in Johannesburg. His work explores human identity through cardboard, combining drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. [23796,24502,24504,24501] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mashir Kresenshun (b. 1999, South Africa) is a dynamic and evolving artist based in Johannesburg. From a young age, he developed a deep connection with creativity, and upon graduating high school, he made a conscious decision to pursue a career that combined both passion and purpose. His artistic journey led him to explore various mediums, ultimately finding a distinctive voice in the world of visual arts. \\n \\nKresenshun works across multiple discipline, with a particular focus on drawing, printmaking, and sculpture. Central to his practice is the use of cardboard, which he has chosen not only as a medium but also a metaphor. Through this, Kresenshun questions the essence of humanity, exploring ideas of fragility, impermanence, and identity. The cardboard itself—an often discarded material—becomes a powerful tool for reflection on the value and significance of life, challenging the traditional understanding of what makes us human. \\nHis approach to printmaking on cardboard sets him apart. This innovative method allows him to create unique textures and surfaces, while his sculptural additions add a dimensional quality to the works, inviting viewers to engage with the art on multiple levels. The layered use of materials and techniques within his practice reflects his ongoing exploration of the boundaries between two-dimensional and three-dimensional art. \\nKresenshun's formal education began at the University of Johannesburg, where he hone his skills and deepened his understanding of art theory and practice. He is currently studying at Artist Proof Studios, further refining his techniques. His artistic endeavors are centered at his studio in August House. \\nKresenshun's work has earned him significant recognition. In 2019, he was selected as one of the Top 20 artists in Thami Mnyele and was also named among the Top 100 artists in Sasol New Signatures. Looking ahead, Kresenshun is preparing for a highly anticipated exhibition in London later this year. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452135416029","gid://shopify/Product/9452172574941","gid://shopify/Product/9452172607709"]

item.title: Mashudu Nevhutalu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641809465565 Mashudu Nevhutalu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640810238173 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mashudu Nevhutalu was born in Auckland Park, Johannesburg in 1992. Although he did not receive much art training at a primary or high school level, he has always had a keen interest in art. Mashudu’s first artistic influence was the graffiti and street murals he saw that decorated dilapidated buildings, almost bringing them to life with their colours. This love for graffiti urged Mashudu to pursue art at a tertiary level where he received an Honours in Fine and Applied Arts in 2014 at the Tshwane University of Technology. As an artist that year, Mashudu felt as if his foot was in the door and that he had found his voice as he was selected to participate in the Sasol New Signatures Competition. As his work developed each year, he went on to take part in a number of small group shows and other competitions such as the SA Taxi Foundation Art Award in which he participated in both 2016 and 2017. \\n \\nMashudu seeks to bring about feelings of nostalgia in the viewer looking at his work. He believes these feelings occur from anything such as a dress worn by one’s mother, or a bumper sticker that reminds one of their parents', or their own, first car. Mashudu is interested in photography and works from old family photographs in his paintings. Though these images are personal to him, he believes that we have all had similar experiences and moments captured in photographs. In his works, Mashudu’s figures are simplified and often made to look hazy and blurry, this depiction emphasizes the notion of memory being a vague and elusive thing. This effect also removes the identity of the person from the original photograph, making the work universal and the figure representative of anyone the viewer wishes them to be from their own memories. Mashudu’s use of bright, vivid colours is his way of reliving those memories and creating them anew."}]}]} []

His work has been featured in group exhibitions with the Moleskine Foundation, Asisebenze Art Atelier, Denzil’s and Jo, Saint Lorient Gallery, and Keyes Art Mile."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452101501149","gid://shopify/Product/9452101533917","gid://shopify/Product/9452101599453","gid://shopify/Product/9452101632221","gid://shopify/Product/9452101664989","gid://shopify/Product/9452102123741","gid://shopify/Product/9452170248413"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641810415837 Masonwabe Ntloko 2622 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640810598621 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452123193565", "gid://shopify/Product/9452123226333", "gid://shopify/Product/9452158615773", "gid://shopify/Product/9452170281181", "gid://shopify/Product/9452170346717", "gid://shopify/Product/9452170379485", "gid://shopify/Product/9452170412253", "gid://shopify/Product/9452172312797", "gid://shopify/Product/9452172345565", "gid://shopify/Product/9452172378333", "gid://shopify/Product/9452172411101", "gid://shopify/Product/9452189843677"] [21568,21567,21565,25688,21564,25690,23745,24190,24192,24193,24195,25691,21566,25689,21563,23746] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Masonwabe Ntloko (b. 1996) is a South African visual artist, illustrator, and textile design graduate known for his modern heritage style that blends cultural richness with contemporary expression. Originally from Engwane, a village that greatly influences his work, Masonwabe grew up in a small town of Dutywa. His art is deeply rooted in Xhosa culture, South African heritage, and personal experiences, which he intricately weaves into his visual narratives. Ntloko's art serves as a storyteller, offering a bridge between past traditions and modern life, with particular focus on the everyday experiences of ordinary Black people. \\n \\nHis work is characterized by its simplicity and cultural influence, often exploring themes of spirituality, rites of passage, and the role of matriarchs within the Xhosa community. Through these stories, Masonwabe celebrates not just the Xhosa people but the diversity of South African culture as a whole. His pieces, which include illustration, painting, textile, and rug design, have been featured in museums and exhibitions across South Africa, allowing him to showcase his unique interpretation of South African heritage."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452123193565","gid://shopify/Product/9452123226333","gid://shopify/Product/9452158615773","gid://shopify/Product/9452170281181","gid://shopify/Product/9452170346717","gid://shopify/Product/9452170379485","gid://shopify/Product/9452170412253","gid://shopify/Product/9452172312797","gid://shopify/Product/9452172345565","gid://shopify/Product/9452172378333","gid://shopify/Product/9452172411101","gid://shopify/Product/9452189843677","gid://shopify/Product/9452189941981"]

item.title: Matthew Eguavoen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641810546909 Matthew Eguavoen 2239 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640812826845 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452058443997", "gid://shopify/Product/9452058542301"] [16736,16735] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Matthew Eguavoen (born 1988), is a rising contemporary artist from Edo State, currently living in the city of Lagos, Nigeria. He attended the University of Port Harcourt , where he attained a Bachelors in Engineering for Civil Engineering and Structures. In his final year at the university of Port Harcourt, Matthew decided to pursue his passion for creating art through self-study, where he continued his artistic development. \\n \\nMatthew is a full-time contemporary painter, he depicts his figurative and portrait subjects using a combination of oil paint, acrylic paint, charcoal, and graphite pencils to document stories that encompass the emotions and demeanor of his muse to the viewer of his work. \\n \\nMatthew uses his work to address the societal, economic, and political views across the complex intersectionality that Nigerians face in different facets of life. The constraint of societal ideology about life, on human existence and survival. \\n \\nHis work addresses the impact of Slavery on the Africa and its people, the extinction of African traditional values and the growing sensation of religion in Africa, importation of western moral and cultural values to Africa and exiling Africa’s own cultural values as a people, with Africans abandoning Africa for relative greener pastures in western countries. \\n \\nMatthews works are featured in collections across West Africa, USA, Europe, and North America. \\n \\nArtist statement \\n\"As an artist I am deeply concerned about the impact of my work on my immediate environment and the world at large and that is why themes of my art centers around the societal, political and economic imbalance taking over humanity happiness, swamping over the essence of society. \\n \\nI am fascinated by people’s reaction to their immediate environment, and how it affects their demeanor and in turn affects their reaction to life. That is what I find really interesting. I see people trying to re-write their past, I see violence, I see the effect of corruption and slavery on the lives of nations citizens, I see people trying to find a way to have fun and survive. \\n \\nFrom my work you can notice a strong striking focus from each of my models, this bold unwavering stare is my way of using my works to project identity formation, mental health, gender construct, societies and government’s impact on both the common man and the affluent. I have a need for facial representation and I am fascinated by its power to evoke an emotional response from my viewers. \\n \\nIf you look at my work from a distance, it looks realistic but when you come close you start to notice my brush strokes, the strokes are a representation of the subjects’ experience, and how they are affected by it. \\n \\nI want people to see the good and the bad times I see. I want to make the unseen other-self tangible, to feel a connection to something larger and feel the magic of transformation, in so doing, inviting my viewers to look in. I appreciate mystery in a painting; uncertainty about what you are seeing is desirable for me, why and how the subject(s) has been affected.\""}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452058443997","gid://shopify/Product/9452058509533","gid://shopify/Product/9452058542301"]

item.title: Mavis Tauzeni
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641814020317 Mavis Tauzeni 471 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640814727389 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088688861","gid://shopify/Product/9452088754397","gid://shopify/Product/9452088787165","gid://shopify/Product/9452088852701","gid://shopify/Product/9452088885469","gid://shopify/Product/9452088918237"] [20443,20404,20431,20433,20441,20444] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mavis Tauzeni is a subtle talent. Her work in print and mixed media moves one to mediation and reflection of one’s inner self, in the same way as Tauzeni herself reflects on her inner world. Speaking unapologetically from a woman’s perspective, she constantly reflects on the mutable relationship between a woman, her potential and her actual in daily life, and through the life cycle. \\n \\n“I feel that women in particular relate the physical with the spiritual and emotional in a uniquely powerful way, being the givers of life and the nurtures of others. The physical strength is integral to the spiritual importance.” With quiet confidence and gentle poetry, Tauzeni asserts the right of the new generation of women in Zimbabwe to claim a place in their society on their own terms. \\n \\nTauzeni represented First Floor Gallery Harare at 1-54 contemporary African art fair in London, 2013 and at Berliner Liste 2013. She lives and works in Harare, Zimbabwe. \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088688861","gid://shopify/Product/9452088754397","gid://shopify/Product/9452088787165","gid://shopify/Product/9452088852701","gid://shopify/Product/9452088885469","gid://shopify/Product/9452088918237"]

item.title: Mbali Nqobile Mdikane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641814479069 Mbali Nqobile Mdikane gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640819151069 [] Mbali Nqobile Mdikane {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mbali Nqobile Mdikane (b. 2001) is a visual artist based in Johannesburg. Hailing from Mthatha/East London in the Eastern Cape, Mdikane has been actively involved in the art world since a young age. Her works concentrate on the development of fantastical characters that seemingly transcend human anatomy. These characters serve the purpose of presenting solutions to human problems and highlight the simplicity of life, diverging from its complexities. embracing afrofuturism/africanism, Mdikane intriguingly explores how black individuals can be perceived. By challenging the conventional depictions of the black body through the use of organic shapes and unconventional approaches to color, materiality, and form, Mdikane aims to shift the narrative surrounding black people and ensure their representation in the forefront of ideas."}]}]} []

item.title: Mbali Shabane

Her work is the observation and the aim to reflect the female; journey, transmutation, experience and the relationship it has with itself. After featuring in the 2013 Sasol New Signatures, she primarily participated in group exhibitions and in 2017 ventured to the administrative and curatorial side of the arts thereafter launched her first independent curatorial project in 2019, Change Room, which is a collaborative visual arts conversation through an interactive discourse aimed at bringing womxn together through an engagement of shared experiences. \\n \\nMost recently her work is part of the Durban: A Curatorial Journey (2024) exhibition at The Pencil Club, Durban."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013848277213","gid://shopify/Product/9013959688413","gid://shopify/Product/9013959786717"]

item.title: Mbali Tshabalala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641818607837 Mbali Tshabalala 523 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640820920541 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013372027101", "gid://shopify/Product/9013372092637", "gid://shopify/Product/9013850374365"] [14407,23012,23015,23018,23020,23939,14415,12591,18953,12592,16082,16144] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mbali Tshabalala is a South African multidisciplinary artist, curator, and creative entrepreneur. She was born in East London, in the Eastern Cape. She holds a Bachelor's Degree in Fine and Applied Arts from Tshwane University of Technology. Tshabalala honed her skills with studies in printmaking at the Artist Proof Studio, complementing her background in Graphic Design and Darkroom photography. \\nHer artistic journey began in 2019, transitioning from a career in curatorial and art administration spanning over seven years. This background enriches her artwork, often described as embracing a \"curator as artist\" approach. \\nPrior to focusing entirely on her art, Tshabalala held prominent roles including assistant curator at the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA). Her curatorial credits include leading initiatives like The Joburg Fringe under the Young Capital banner. Driven by an entrepreneurial spirit, Tshabalala founded Collective UNTITLD and Anecdotes Gallery, contributing to South Africa's art scene. Her talent has garnered recognition, with features in prestigious collections such as Rand Merchants Bank, JP Morgan Chase, William Humphreys Gallery, Art Bank South Africa, and Spier Art Trust. Her work has also been showcased at esteemed institutions like Pretoria Art Association, Constitution Hill, Johannesburg Art Gallery, and prominent auction houses including Strauss & Co. and Aspire Art Auction. \\nTshabalala's practice encompasses collage, painting, printmaking, drawing, and photography, exploring the intersectionality of black women's experiences. Mbali's work challenges dominant narratives around mental health, femininity, and African spirituality. \\nCentral to her artistic expression is her own identity, particularly within the context of a post-colonial African city. I critique the collision between indigenous culture and a Eurocentric urban landscape, highlighting the neglect and its impact on mental health. Tshabalala's artwork intertwines ancient African knowledge systems with contemporary lived experiences through storytelling that reflects this cultural collision and its consequences."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013372027101","gid://shopify/Product/9013372092637","gid://shopify/Product/9013403091165","gid://shopify/Product/9013436940509","gid://shopify/Product/9013438513373","gid://shopify/Product/9013850374365","gid://shopify/Product/9014034661597","gid://shopify/Product/9014034759901","gid://shopify/Product/9014034890973","gid://shopify/Product/9014035022045","gid://shopify/Product/9014013460701"]
