item.title: Médéric Turay
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848525021 Médéric Turay gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640896155869 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452057166045","gid://shopify/Product/9452057198813","gid://shopify/Product/9452057231581","gid://shopify/Product/9452057264349","gid://shopify/Product/9452057362653","gid://shopify/Product/9013439758557","gid://shopify/Product/9013456535773"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Visionary, thoughtful as much as intuitive, Mederic Turay uses his talents to participate in raising awareness by telling the most beautiful as well as the hardest stories. This multidisciplinary storyteller lives his art as a privilege and uses a plurality of techniques to create entities, sometimes figurative, sometimes abstract, which become the protagonists of his graphic stories. \\n \\nHis style and the themes he deals with reflect his cosmopolitan life journey and his West African origins. Descendent of a royal family of the Akan people in present-day Côte d'Ivoire, Mederic only got to know his country of origin as a teenager when he returned from the United States where he grew up. \\n \\nHis cultural mix which explains his constant quest for balance in duality, influences the way he builds his works. Trained in Fine Arts, he easily got rid of stylistic constraints by drawing from the material and the process which \\nallow him to best express his point. This is how he combines his talent for music and writing with his passion for painting and sculpture, multiplying albums and first artistic prizes. \\n \\nThe maturity and humility he acquired through travel and meetings with other recognized artists of his generation and the previous one allowed him to focus on the visual arts and to assert his unique style. \\n \\nExcerpt from Melrose Gallery"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452057166045","gid://shopify/Product/9452057198813","gid://shopify/Product/9452057231581","gid://shopify/Product/9452057264349","gid://shopify/Product/9452057362653","gid://shopify/Product/9013439758557","gid://shopify/Product/9013456535773"]

item.title: Megan Gabrielle Harris
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641820475613 Megan Gabrielle Harris 2086 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640825180381 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013423800541","gid://shopify/Product/9013423833309","gid://shopify/Product/9013423898845","gid://shopify/Product/9013424357597","gid://shopify/Product/9013424455901","gid://shopify/Product/9452102877405","gid://shopify/Product/9452102975709","gid://shopify/Product/9452103041245"] [15410,15452,15451,21614,14541,15403,21616,21618,15405] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Megan Gabrielle Harris is a multi-disciplinary artist from Sacramento, California. \\n \\nHer work is mostly comprised of drawings, paintings and photography. M.G.H.’s desire to paint began at an early age, ignited by her father Thomas Harris whose paintings covered every wall in their home and continues to be heavily influenced by her father’s work and his Escapism style. \\n \\nThe inspiration for her work comes from fashion photography, surreal landscapes and natural forms, stemming from her experiences working as a model for over ten years. Women of color are the primary focus in her work. She uses vibrant and rich color palettes in an attempt to create a light and airy atmosphere for her subjects, while depicting these female figures as independent and powerful which is the perception she has of the women in her community. \\n \\nM.G.H.’s goal as an artist is to create dreamy and sublime escapes, not only as a form of self-therapy but also to inspire anyone who views her artwork. \\n \\nShe received her B.A. in Art History from California State University, Sacramento in 2014 and is currently based in New York City."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013423800541","gid://shopify/Product/9013423833309","gid://shopify/Product/9013423898845","gid://shopify/Product/9013424357597","gid://shopify/Product/9013424455901","gid://shopify/Product/9452102877405","gid://shopify/Product/9452102975709","gid://shopify/Product/9452103041245"]

item.title: Mel Madiba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822605533 Mel Madiba 1926 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640829571293 [] [21623,21624] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phenyo Melody Madiba, better known as 'Mel Madiba', born in October 1993, in Mafikeng and grew up in Pretoria. She now lives and works intermittently between Pretoria and Johannesburg. When she finished High School, having taken Design as a subject, she went to study Interior Design at The Design School of Southern Africa. It was there where she fell in love with wood and discovered pyrography, which is the art of drawing on wood, leather, or other materials using a soldering iron. It is through this art form that she began creating works that seek to explore various aspects of who she is. \\nMadiba taps into the inner workings of her mind to conceive work that is rooted in femininity, consciousness and the full expression of oneself. She portrays an array of emotions from a black woman's lens. Her chosen subject matter is predominantly black women at different stages of their growth. She envisions a world where black beauty can be fully expressed and appreciated without the need for it to be substantiated. The artist uses expressive markings by fire, gold, and African bronze blue to illustrate that black women are naturally divine. Her career officially launched in 2019 after being dubbed a Design Indaba Emerging Creative, appearing on the TV show Hashtags Africa, and winning the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize. Madiba's work has evolved through personal experiences and she strives to improve her craft even further."}]}]} []

item.title: Melinda Matyas
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641820934365 Melinda Matyas 577 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640831307997 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035997917","gid://shopify/Product/9452036292829","gid://shopify/Product/9452036325597"] Melinda Matyas is a London-based artist whose figurative paintings explore the complexities of the human condition, psychological aspiration, and societal pressures. Her work blends abstraction and figuration to create dynamic compositions that delve into the internal world. [3243,3244,3242] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Melinda Matyas is a London-based artist originally from Romania, was born as an ethnic Hungarian in 1976 during the communist regime. Her formative years were shaped by witnessing the violent uprising that led to the fall of the regime. The mass transition from silent acceptance to a powerful desire for freedom intrigued her deeply. This experience ignited her interest in psychological mechanisms driving human aspirations, a theme that continues to influence her artistic practice. \\nIn 2009, she graduated from the University of Art and Design in Cluj-Napoca with a BA in Fine Art, Painting, before relocating to England in 2013. Her work centers on the human condition, focusing on the internal world one navigates within the context of societal expectations. She explores the tension between individual desires and the pressures of society, using color, texture, and the deconstruction of forms to achieve a balance between figuration and abstraction. Although Melinda considers herself a figurative painter, her innovative use of dynamic form-breaking often results in works that can appear abstract upon closer inspection."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035997917","gid://shopify/Product/9452036292829","gid://shopify/Product/9452036325597"]

item.title: Méné
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848557789 Méné gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640896221405 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452053725405","gid://shopify/Product/9452053758173","gid://shopify/Product/9452053790941","gid://shopify/Product/9452053856477","gid://shopify/Product/9452053922013","gid://shopify/Product/9452059197661","gid://shopify/Product/9452059230429","gid://shopify/Product/9452059263197","gid://shopify/Product/9452059295965","gid://shopify/Product/9452059328733","gid://shopify/Product/9452059361501","gid://shopify/Product/9013453029597","gid://shopify/Product/9013453095133","gid://shopify/Product/9452165923037"] Discover the art of Méné, an Ivorian artist and Professor of Fine Arts. His human-centric paintings, characterized by child-like silhouettes with profound depth, explore the complexities of human nature and emotion. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Méné (b. 1977, Ivory Coast) is a dedicated artist and Professor of Fine Arts who lives and works in his homeland. A graduate of the National Institute of Arts and Cultural Action of Abidjan, Méné has pursued his artistic path with talent and tenacity for over twenty years, presenting his works globally—from Abidjan to Paris, Luxembourg to Dakar, and Spain. Despite his international success, he remains humble and unassuming. \\nMéné's art is characterized by its focus on human beings, both individually and in groups, often accompanied by elements like a red animal, a beast with horns, the sun, or a hut. His work examines human nature in all its facets, presented in deceptively simple, child-like silhouettes that convey both the freshness of youth and the depth of adult experience. His subjects often smile or show subtle emotions, depicted affectionately in pairs or groups, highlighting the effervescence of youth and the pursuit of life's meaning."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452053725405","gid://shopify/Product/9452053758173","gid://shopify/Product/9452053790941","gid://shopify/Product/9452053856477","gid://shopify/Product/9452053922013","gid://shopify/Product/9452059197661","gid://shopify/Product/9452059230429","gid://shopify/Product/9452059263197","gid://shopify/Product/9452059295965","gid://shopify/Product/9452059328733","gid://shopify/Product/9452059361501","gid://shopify/Product/9013453029597","gid://shopify/Product/9013453095133","gid://shopify/Product/9452165923037"]

item.title: Mercy Moyo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822703837 Mercy Moyo 2197 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640831996125 [] Discover the vibrant and evocative artworks of Mercy Moyo, a Zimbabwean-born visual artist known for her collages and paintings depicting the beauty and realities of African women. Explore her exhibitions in South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and the USA. [16056,23388,23389,23390,16054,16055] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zimbabwean-born visual artist and collagist Mercy Moyo shares, “Art and creativity have always been part of my life. As a child, I would observe my grandmother weaving baskets that were the main source of livelihood for the family. Fascinated by the techniques involved in patterns, designs and her skill of making each basket unique despite similar materials and colors. Through my observation, I realized that the more she made, the more creativity emerged from the process.” \\nFrom this experience, Mercy began to draw at a very young age. Her drawings describe the world around her and tell the story of life in contemporary Africa, specifically through women figures. This narrative is prominent in her artistic practice, where her images are primarily collages, incorporating objects that complement and reinforce the depicted images. She uses various mediums, including oil, acrylics, charcoal, pencil, and recently, smoke from candles. These diverse mediums help create vibrant images of contemporary women in Zimbabwe today, expressing their lived realities, aspirations, and dreams. \\nUltimately, Mercy uses art as a fundamental element in depicting the beauty of African women, whether they come from rural or urban contexts. She emphasizes that she does not consider herself a feminist but wants to portray the real African woman—comfortable in her self-identity, wearing long skirts, with a fuller figure, and head nicely covered. \\nMercy has participated in group and solo exhibitions in South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and the United States of America. These experiences have significantly influenced her work through encounters with the lived realities of different societies. For example, the young men working in the mines of South Africa, who live underground and surface only to socialize and sleep at night, inspired her experimentation with male figures. She captures the lives of these miners using charcoals and working in hues of black and brown, reflecting the loneliness and individualism associated with their daily lives, unlike most of her works, which depict people in community dialogues and deep conversations."}]}]} []

item.title: Mercy Thokozane Minah
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822736605 Mercy Thokozane Minah 2254 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640832192733 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013459386589","gid://shopify/Product/9013459452125","gid://shopify/Product/9452155240669","gid://shopify/Product/9452155535581","gid://shopify/Product/9452155928797"] [25329,17083,25330,17084,25327] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mercy Thokozane Minah is a queer, gender-expansive, multi-disciplinary artist who is based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Their work exists across various mediums; literary, audio-visual, theatrical and visual. Mercy has had minimal formal training for their creative explorations, however being an artist has been an organic part of their life since early childhood. They learned the rigor of rehearsal and performing by participating in plays, poetry, and song performances at church from as young as age 3. Mercy’s distinctly vibrant depictions of intimacy between Black, gender and sexually self-determined peoples have been featured and exhibited across an array of platforms, including the Paris Review and Superrare’s Black*Rare showcase (curated by Linda Dounia Rebeiz)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013459386589","gid://shopify/Product/9013459452125","gid://shopify/Product/9452155240669","gid://shopify/Product/9452155535581","gid://shopify/Product/9452155928797"]

item.title: Mfundo Mbali Joseph
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822965981 Mfundo Mbali Joseph 2285 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640833503453 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013465022685"] [17406] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I create art to express myself, about how i see life during my everyday life of people come across within my community, \\n \\nComing from a poverty stricken background my work depict everyday scenes from my Surroundings, I paint traditional scenes, I sometimes ask people to pose for me to Create scene. \\n \\nI had a second love and is photography in the day I hunts the streets for intresting composition and reference materials,that I then takes home to my Studio space to portray in a realism style using oil medium on canvas, \\n \\n\"Where there is Community the is art Where there is Community the is a Story\""}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013465022685"]

item.title: Mia Chaplin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823097053 Mia Chaplin 920 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640833896669 [] [16006,16008,9990,16009,16011,16010,9988] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mia Chaplin (b.1990 South Africa) is a painter who lives and works in Cape Town. Working in oil on canvas and paper, her highly expressive works are characterised by their rich impasto surfaces and visible brushstrokes. Chaplin’s most recent works emphasize a muted colour palette of pink fleshy tones and golden highlights. Consisting of still lifes, figure studies and landscapes, her work seems to meditate on the familiar. Her loose, erratic style of painting – synonymous with that of the impressionists – is intuitive, heightening the emotionality of her pieces. They communicate a sense of estrangement; reflecting a detachment between the self and her surroundings. Her works sway between voyeurism and intimate interaction, while remaining consistently self-referential. \\n \\nSince completing her BFA at the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town in 2011, Chaplin has hosted four solo exhibitions, Mouth (2018), Under a Boiling River (2017) and Binding Forms (2016), with WHATIFTHEWORLD and most recently, Underbelly (2019), with No Man’s Art Gallery in Amsterdam. She has furthermore extended her painting practice into printmaking, hosting a mini-exhibition of monotypes from the series, The Making of a Sharp Blade (2017), in collaboration with Warren Editions, Cape Town. Chaplin has completed artist residency programmes at Cité Internationale Des Artes in the Marais district, Paris (2018), Nirox Arts Foundation in Johannesburg, South Africa (2016) and at OBRAS Foundation in Alentejo, Portugal (2015). \\n \\nSELECTED SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2019\\tUnderbelly, No Man's Art Gallery, Amsterdam \\n2018\\tMouth - WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town \\nSurface: Emerging South African Painters, Barnard Gallery, Cape Town \\nOut of Context, UJ Art Gallery, Johannesburg \\nPink, Chandler House, Cape Town \\nPaint it Black, Salon91, Cape Town \\n2014\\tCape Town Art Fair, The Pavillion, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town \\nCubicle, Infecting the City Public Arts Festival, Cape Town \\nTurbine Art Fair, Johannesburg \\nArt in Red Light #10, Art Fair, Amsterdam \\nSA Art Now, No Man’s Art Gallery, Amsterdam \\nFlorabunda, Die Voorkamer, Cape Town \\n2013\\tCape Town Art Fair, The Look Out, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town \\nIn Good Company, Irma Stern Museum, Cape Town \\nCollections and Archives, Salon 91, Cape Town \\nOne in a Million, Salon 91, Cape Town \\nI’d Rather Be Swimming, Salon 91, Cape Town \\n2012\\tImpression: Sunset, Salon 91, Cape Town \\n2010\\tFirst Edition, These Four Walls Gallery, Cape Town"}]}]} []

item.title: Micha Serraf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641826373853 Micha Serraf 1893 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640834191581 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013380415709", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380481245", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380546781", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380612317", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380645085", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380677853", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380776157", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380808925"] [13278,14148,14147,13276,13279,13277,13275,13281,13274] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"b. 1994 in Zimbabwe \\nBAFA from Michaelis School of Fine Art, UCT \\n \\nMy practice is centred around rewriting the trauma of displacement with the imagined memory of celebration, homage and childlike wonder. In pursuit of memory, identity and a place to call home, my work is grounded in a nostalgia of personal and ancestral experience, of what never was, and of what could have been. Caught in an entanglement between ancestral history and utopic optimism. My work is often informed by memories I have from when I was a child in Zimbabwe and my endeavour to understand the deep nostalgia I feel toward the seemingly unfamiliar. To push a more celebratory narrative that is fuelled by the unshakable belief in an abundance, where the often-imposed political narrative takes second seat to that of our lived experience."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013380415709","gid://shopify/Product/9013380481245","gid://shopify/Product/9013380546781","gid://shopify/Product/9013380612317","gid://shopify/Product/9013380645085","gid://shopify/Product/9013380677853","gid://shopify/Product/9013380776157","gid://shopify/Product/9013380808925","gid://shopify/Product/9013401288925","gid://shopify/Product/9013401354461"]

item.title: Michael Badger
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823686877 Michael Badger 2547 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640835043549 [] [20588,20589,20590] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Badger (b. 1992, Accra, Ghana) is an artist proficient in traditional and digital mediums, crafting surrealistic pieces. Michael’s art delves into the realms of suppressed inner worlds, fears, and dreams, navigating the challenges of growing up and seeking direction in a society marked by increasingly rigid conservative ideals and gender norms. Michael Badger’s works have been exhibited at a group exhibition with Immerse Ghana, Accra (2023), In Relation To Light, Accra (2023), Celebrate Her: A Tribute To Women And Nonbinary Artists, Accra (2023). Michael has had work featured on products from renowned makeup artist Pat Mcgrath (2017-2018) and won a competition for an eco-friendly red carpet dress in collaboration with Vivienne Westwood and Red Carpet Green Dress, worn at the Oscars in 2013. They have a Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Fashion Design from SCAD Atlanta."}]}]} []

item.title: Michael Gah
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823883485 Michael Gah 1811 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640836059357 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013375926493","gid://shopify/Product/9452059459805","gid://shopify/Product/9452059492573","gid://shopify/Product/9452128108765","gid://shopify/Product/9452128141533","gid://shopify/Product/9452128174301","gid://shopify/Product/9452256264413","gid://shopify/Product/9452256297181","gid://shopify/Product/9452256395485","gid://shopify/Product/9452256428253","gid://shopify/Product/9452256526557","gid://shopify/Product/9452256723165"] [17477,17476,24062,24063,24064,17472,12931] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Accra born-and-based, contemporary artist Michael Gah is one of Ghana’s most exciting contemporary portraitists. His medium is equally intriguing – fashioning larger-than-life and hyper coloured figurative works using strips of endemic fabrics, the hugely colourful and patterned textiles that are intertwined with the very heart of womanhood in the modern African context. His pieces are a challenge – to social norms for women in Africa and indeed to contemporary art and figurative work; working with fabric and collaging has long been the realm of crafters and his potent portraits are frank in their delivery. \\n \\nGah cites not only his mother, but all modern African women, as his inspiration – his faceless (though no less personality-laden) subjects defy traditional ‘African expectations’. They are represented as thoroughly modern muses engaged in social and even romantic activities, that answer only to their own whims and certainly not to the stifling belief systems thrust upon them for eons. The poses are provocative in that they are a far cry from the head and shoulders ‘African Woman’ figurative work, so commonplace on the continent in 20th century art. Gah’s work also references social media and the modern day importance of Instagram reality and camera facing messaging. \\n \\nThe power in Gah’s portraits lies in the intentional tension between past and present and a suggestion that eradication of repressive expectations is inevitable and crucial. The use of traditional fabrics insists on the viewer's mindfulness about outdated norms, while still appreciating the gifts and weight of the past. \\n \\nCOUNTRY • GHANA"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013375926493","gid://shopify/Product/9452059459805","gid://shopify/Product/9452059492573","gid://shopify/Product/9452128108765","gid://shopify/Product/9452128141533","gid://shopify/Product/9452128174301","gid://shopify/Product/9452256264413","gid://shopify/Product/9452256297181","gid://shopify/Product/9452256395485","gid://shopify/Product/9452256428253","gid://shopify/Product/9452256526557","gid://shopify/Product/9452256723165"]

item.title: Michael MacGarry
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641824145629 Michael MacGarry gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640837697757 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355512029", "gid://shopify/Product/9013355577565", "gid://shopify/Product/9013355610333", "gid://shopify/Product/9013355643101", "gid://shopify/Product/9452121948381", "gid://shopify/Product/9452121981149", "gid://shopify/Product/9452211437789", "gid://shopify/Product/9452211667165", "gid://shopify/Product/9452211798237", "gid://shopify/Product/9452211962077", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212060381", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212125917", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212355293", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212486365", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212650205", "gid://shopify/Product/9452212814045", "gid://shopify/Product/9452213010653"] Michael MacGarry is a multi-award-winning South African artist and filmmaker whose diverse practice spans sculpture, photography, installation, and film. With exhibitions at Tate Modern, Guggenheim Bilbao, and Kiasma Museum, his work delves into the intersections of politics, identity, and contemporary life. A recipient of the Standard Bank Young Artist Award, MacGarry is known for his exploration of marginalized narratives and the political landscapes of Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael MacGarry is a distinguished South African artist and filmmaker, celebrated for his political and poetic exploration of contemporary life. His work spans a diverse range of media, including sculpture, photography, installation, and film, addressing the complex tensions between marginalized and dominant narratives. MacGarry's art reflect the ever-evolving landscapes of identity, power, and history, particularly in the context of post-colonial Africa. \\n \\nWith a Master's Degree in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand, MacGarry is currently a Ph.D. candidate in the History of Art. MacGarry is a fellow of the Gordon Institute of Performing and Creative Arts (GIPCA) at the University of Cape Town and a recipient of the Standard Bank Young Artist Award 2010. \\n \\n \\nHis extensive body of work has earned him international recognition, with exhibitions at renowned institutions such as Tate Modern, Guggenheim Bilbao, and the Kiasma Museum. His diverse artistic practice has also extended to film, with several award-winning short films that have been featured in over 30 international film festivals. He is a recipient of an El Ray Award - Excellence in Narrative Short Filmmaking (Barcelona Film Festival 2015), a finalist for the Huysmans Young African Filmmaker Award 2015 (Belgium) as well as Jury Awards from 19th VideoBrasil (Sao Paulo), K3 Internationales Film Festival (Austria) and 13th International Festival Signes de Nuit (Paris). \\n \\nSELECTED SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n 2017: Show No Pain, Wits Art Museum, Johannesburg. \\n 2015: There’s an Animal Inside. \\n 2013: As Above, So Below, Centre for Democracy, Cape Town. \\n 2012: The Other Half, Stevenson, Cape Town. \\n 2011: Entertainment, Stevenson, Johannesburg. \\n 2010: END GAME, Standard Bank Young Artist Award 2010 (Visual Arts) Monument Gallery, Grahamstown. \\n 2010: This is your world in which we grow, and we will grow to hate you, Stevenson, Johannesburg. \\n 2008: When enough people start saying the same thing, Art Extra, Johannesburg \\n 2004: Or Until the World Improves, The Premises Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n \\nSELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n 2017: Utopia/Dystopia, MAAT, Lisbon, Portugal \\n 2015: Bronze, Steel & Stone, Everard Read, Johannesburg \\n 2015: The Film Will Always Be You, TATE Modern, London \\n 2015: FNB Joburg Art Fair \\n 2015: Making Africa. A Continent of Contemporary Design, curated by Okwui Enwezor and Amelie Klein Vitra Design Museum, Weil am Rhein, Germany Guggenheim Bilbao, Spain \\n 2015: Africa: Architecture, Culture, Identity, curated by Mathias Ussing Seeberg Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, Humlebaek, Denmark \\n 2015: The Johannesburg Pavilion, During the 56th la Biennale di Venezia,Venice, Italy \\n 2015: Africa Salon, Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, USA \\n 2014: Half-­Devil Half-­Child, Blank Projects, Cape Town \\n 2014: Pop Goes the Revolution,The New Church, Cape Town \\n 2013: 'MINE' – MC2a – MIGRATIONS CULTURELLES \\n 2013: Aquitaine Afriques, Bordeaux, France \\n 2012: Impakt Festival 2012 \\n 2012: CBKU, Utrecht, The Netherlands \\n 2012: Making Way: Contemporary Art from South Africa and China, Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg \\n 2011: Johannesburg Contested Terrains, Tate Modern, London \\n 2011: ARS 11, Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art Helsinki, Finland \\n 2010: Ampersand, Damiler Art Collection, Berlin \\n 2010: Life Less Ordinary: Performance and display in South African art, Ffotogallery, Cardiff, U.K. \\n 2009: Life Less Ordinary: Performance and display in South African art, Djanogly Gallery, Nottingham \\n 2009: Why Not?, Kuckei + Kuckei, Berlin, Germany \\n \\nAWARDS: \\n \\nEl Ray Award -­? item.title: Michael Taylor
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641825947869 Michael Taylor 347 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640840319197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452036948189","gid://shopify/Product/9452051038429","gid://shopify/Product/9013461549277","gid://shopify/Product/9013461647581","gid://shopify/Product/9452108218589","gid://shopify/Product/9452127322333","gid://shopify/Product/9452127387869","gid://shopify/Product/9452127420637","gid://shopify/Product/9452127453405"] [15067,15007,24036,15064,4159,24038,24039,22417,15065,17150,17151,24037] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Taylor, born in Johannesburg is a South African artist living and working in Cape Town. Taylor produces works in painting, drawing, printmaking and ceramics. He has to date had 9 solo exhibition of which his recent Trophies was at Whatiftheworld Gallery, based in Cape Town; the gallery also represents Taylor. \\n \\nMichael has a story to tell, make that a few, and through his work in the monotype technique, his characters and settings materialise in humourous acts, satirized scenarios and of course at the beach – a sucker for a ‘Tropiitone’ sunset is Michael. To comparatively sketch it out he arrives with a suitcase of stuff (well, not figuratively) and ready and open to the element of chance. Taylor has the illustrator in him and that means the suitcase is tightly packed and as he decides to unpack so too does a composition. It helps that the nature of Michael’s work has much to do with editing/selecting and layering – in terms of making monotypes he is able think of the final image as a succession of colour planes, negative areas waiting to be filled and at least the possibilities of adding to or taking away from existing flat planes. He is a consummate professional in his sensibility and approach, well suited to collaboration in the print studio and, has developed from initial projects. Michael Taylor knows what will work and what will ‘fail’ due to his being comfortable with the medium as he says, “let the medium do what it wants to do.” \\n \\n– Sara-Aimee Verity"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452036948189","gid://shopify/Product/9452051038429","gid://shopify/Product/9013461549277","gid://shopify/Product/9013461647581","gid://shopify/Product/9452108218589","gid://shopify/Product/9452127322333","gid://shopify/Product/9452127387869","gid://shopify/Product/9452127420637","gid://shopify/Product/9452127453405"]

item.title: Michele Mathison
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641826406621 Michele Mathison 2541 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640842776797 [] Michele Mathison, a South African artist, explores themes of identity and transformation in his contemporary sculptures and installations. With works featured at the Venice Biennale, Zeitz MOCAA, and in major collections, Mathison’s art has gained international recognition. His large-scale public sculptures and exhibitions at venues like Frieze Sculpture and Whatiftheworld Gallery showcase his dynamic approach to contemporary art. [23803] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michele Mathison (b. 1977, South Africa, raised in Harare, Zimbabwe) is a prominent contemporary artist whose work explores themes of identity, transformation, and the relationship between the human form and its environment. He earned his BFA from Michaelis School of Fine Arts at the University of Cape Town, South Africa. His art has been widely recognized, with recent acquisitions by thCeline Art Project curated by Hedi Slimane for Celine Shanghai, Taipei, and Hangzhou. \\nMathison’s work has been showcased in notable solo exhibitions such as CIVILIAN (2023) and Over and Over (2021) at Whatiftheworld Gallery in Cape Town, as well as Dissolution (2018) and Uproot (2016) at Tyburn Gallery in London. His work also played a significant role in the Zimbabwean pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale and was featured in the inaugural exhibition at the Zeitz MOCAA in 2017. In 2021, Mathison completed a series of three large-scale public sculptures for North-West University, further establishing his impact in public art. His major installation works include Parallax at Frieze Sculpture in London (2018) and Angular Mass at the V&A Waterfront and Zeitz MOCAA in Cape Town (2017). \\nMathison’s work is part of prominent collections, including the Norval Foundation’s Homestead collection, the Zeitz MOCAA permanent collection, and the Leridon Collection, among others. His art has been featured in prestigious international exhibitions and art fairs, such as Artissima, Miart, 1:54 London, and Cape Town Art Fair. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Michelle Loukidis
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829126365 Michelle Loukidis 1868 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640843727069 [23720] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michelle Loukidis received her photographic training at TUT in Tshwane. She worked as a commercial photographer for over 10 years. However, her keen interests in photographic development led her to education where she has trained and mentored young photographers from all over Africa for over 20 years. In 2018 she founded a small woman based photographic art school, Through The Lens Collective in Johannesburg, South Africa . A fine artist herself, she has exhibited her photographs in solo and group exhibitions. Michelle prefers working in film using medium format cameras, where she feels a certain amount of the magic of photography is still retained. She works and lives in Johannesburg."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014056026333"]

item.title: Michelle Viljoen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829159133 Michelle Viljoen 2600 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640844316893 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452097470685", "gid://shopify/Product/9452097568989"] Michelle Viljoen [21172,21174,21173] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Her body of work attempts to capture the honesty, vulnerability, and raw beauty of moments that emerge when individuals enter a state of ‘otherness’ and aims to incite answers to the questions that the subjects’ expressions and demeanour pose, and by doing so, invites the viewer to step into a state of otherness as well. \\n \\nMichelle further abstracts these moments, ideas and themes that emerge from her photography into her paintings and drawings. \\n \\nShe is also the founder and creative director of Studio Co, a specialised design studio and consultancy who works with brands across the globe."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452097470685","gid://shopify/Product/9452097536221","gid://shopify/Product/9452097568989"]

item.title: Mika Revell
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829322973 Mika Revell 2455 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640845332701 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452083151069","gid://shopify/Product/9452083183837"] Mika Revell [19455,19453] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mika Revell (b. 1985, Sydney, Australia) is a Chinese-American multimedia artist. Her work delves into the complex relationship between symbols of power and commodified objects, contrasting the ominous and alluring. Using pink auto-pigments and polished finishes, she investigates processes of manufacturing and labor. These objects interrogate the global supply chain of resources and human life. Revell explores how commodification has shaped our culture and desires. She addresses themes of power, war, and wealth is both beautiful and unsettling. She received her MFA in Sculpture from Central Saint Martin’s, London, and international residencies in Riyadh, Tokyo, and Los Angeles."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452083151069","gid://shopify/Product/9452083183837"]

item.title: Mikhael Subotzky
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829355741 Mikhael Subotzky 274 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640845824221 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035571933"] [351] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mikhael Subotzky was born in 1981 in Cape Town, South Africa, and is currently based in Johannesburg. Subotzky’s film, video and photographic works are concerned with the structures of narrative and representation, as well as the relationship between social storytelling and the formal contingencies of image-making. \\n \\nSubotzky’s first body of photographic work, Die Vier Hoeke (The Four Corners), was an in-depth study of the South African penal system. Umjiegwana (The Outside) and Beaufort West extended this investigation to the relationship between everyday life in post-apartheid South Africa and the historical, spatial, and institutional structures of control. Beaufort West (Chris Boot, 2008) was Subotzky’s first monograph and the series was included in the exhibition New Photography 2008: Josephine Meckseper and Mikhael Subotzky at the Museum of Modern Art (New York, 2008). The exhibition Retinal Shift was produced by Subotzky on the occasion of the Standard Bank Young Artist Award 2012 and toured South Africa’s major museums. Retinal Shift includes two large photographic and video installations that critically engage with the artist’s own ambivalence towards the processes of representation and image construction. Retinal Shift (Steidl, 2012) was published to accompany the exhibition. \\n \\nRetinal Shift also includes Subotzky’s first major film installation, Moses and Griffiths 2012, which uses four screens to narrate the contrasting and conflicting institutional and personal histories of two seventy-year-old tour guides in the small South African town of Grahamstown. Moses and Griffiths has subsequently been exhibited at Palais de Tokyo (Paris, 2013) Yale Art Gallery (New Haven, 2014) and Art Unlimited (Basel, 2014). A third monograph, Ponte City (Steidl, 2014) is the product of a six-year collaboration with the British artist Patrick Waterhouse. This project focuses a single 54-story building that dominates the Johannesburg skyline. The building is cast as the central character in a myriad of interweaving narratives that, through photographs, commissioned texts, historical documents, and urban myths, chart the convoluted histories of both the building and Johannesburg itself. The Ponte City exhibition, which consists of a single installation of thousands of photographs and documents, has been exhibited at the Scottish National Portrait Gallery (Edinburgh, 2014), FoMU (Antwerp, 2014) and Le Bal (Paris, 2014). Excerpts from the series have been shown at the Liverpool (2012) and Lubumbashi (2013) Biennales, as well as the South African National Gallery (Cape Town, 2010). Ponte City has won the 2015 Deutsche Borse Photography Prize. \\n \\nShow ‘n Tell was initiated while on residency at the Musée MAC/VAL (Paris, 2013). This body of work looks to the relationship between images, the various instruments of their construction, and both the politics and physiology of their reception. Pixel Interface, a multi-component video installation from this body of work was included in All The World’s Futures, the main exhibition curated by Okwui Enwezor at the 56th Venice Biennale. WYE, Subotzky’s first fictional film installation, was commissioned by the Sherman Contemporary Art Foundation (Sydney) and premiered there in March 2016. Yellow Bile (or Work in Progress), his first exhibition of paintings and performance, took place at Maitland Institute in September 2017."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035571933"]

item.title: Mikhail Samuel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829421277 Mikhail Samuel gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640846446813 {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mikhail Samuel is a South African photographer, writer, and filmmaker, whose works explore identity, memory, philosophy, representation, and space through analog media. Samuel is best known for his study of South Africa’s complex racial, gender, and cultural divisions, which he unpacks through film photography. Samuel focuses on societal observations that blur the lines between the imagined and conscious realities, and which have been brought to life in his recent film, An Ode To \\nYouth: Joburg Nights (2021). His work has been exhibited internationally with his photography series in Information is Currency debuting in Germany at the 8th Photo Triennial alongside An Ode To Youth: Joburg Nights, which screened at SAUFF. \\n \\nSamuel’s contribution to film extended beyond his practice with his collaborative project, Cult Film, which saw the artist work with Troye Shannon on the establishment of a film community through a boutique film lab. Cult Film was a project that encouraged artists to experiment with analog media and provided bespoke development services in Johannesburg."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014005563613","gid://shopify/Product/9014005596381","gid://shopify/Product/9014006153437","gid://shopify/Product/9014034956509","gid://shopify/Product/9013289648349"]

item.title: Mikiyas Sintayehu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829814493 Mikiyas Sintayehu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640847200477 [] Mikiyas Sintayehu {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mikiyas Sintayehu was born in 1998 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. He is a painter whose work explores the complex landscape of human emotions and experiences. Through the use of vibrant colors and subtle textures, he captures a wide range of feelings and the depths of our shared humanity. His intimate depictions offer glimpses into moments of vulnerability, joy, and sorrow, reflecting the raw essence of what it means to be human. Mikiyas' art serves as a mirror for empathy, encouraging viewers to reflect on and embrace the rich emotions that shape our collective experience. \\n \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Mikhailia Petersen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829388509 Mikhailia Petersen 2181 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640847003869 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013989671133"] [21250,21254,21247,21248,21252,21249,20397,21251,21246,20398,21253] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mikhailia Petersen is an independent, multi-faceted creative, living and working in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nWorking through the medium of photography, Petersen is skilled in the fields of styling, creative direction and as a stills producer, cultivating a layered means of engaging with projects and work. \\nOften working in portraiture, Mikhailia aims to capture her subjects in a truthful and celebratory manner, portraying those individuals she shoots through narrative-based story-telling, as opposed to isolated and essentializing single images. \\nHer practice lends itself towards the emotive, harnessing elements of history, culture and the lived archive of those who surround her and the individuals she works with. Deeply interested in the post-colonial landscape of Cape Town, her work seeks to re-address the way POC and LGBTQIA+ people are framed within this context through hardship and oppression. Instead her photographs highlight the beauty and strength of people. \\nThe work she has produced has been described as theatrical and heavily inspired by a documentary-themed approach. Working with a community of creatives, also based in Cape Town, her practice is multi-disciplinary as she incorporates local crafts, fashion, and various skills within shoot production to create her photographic stories. \\nPetersen’s work has been published in various reputable South African and international publications, including THE FACE, NATAAL Magazine, NiCotiNe and Doek!Lit. Her work has been exhibited locally at , The Reservoir, THK Gallery, Ebony Gallery and AVA Gallery, and internationally at the V&A Museum X Guap x We are Soul show in London. Notable campaigns she has worked for include PUMA."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013949137117","gid://shopify/Product/9013949169885","gid://shopify/Product/9013989671133"]

item.title: Minenkulu Ngoyi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641829945565 Minenkulu Ngoyi 2251 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650732617949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082004189","gid://shopify/Product/9452082102493","gid://shopify/Product/9452123160797"] Minenkulu Nqoyi [19417,19324] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Minenkulu Ngoyi (b.1987) in Johannesburg,South Africa, graduated from Artist Proof Studio in 2011 and now practices printmaking at DGI (Danger Gevaar Ingozi) studio at Arts On Main at Maboneng, Johannesburg. \\n \\nHe has been involved in several group exhibitions both locally and internationally with museums, galleries and art fairs such as the Johannesburg Art Gallery, Wits Art Museum, Latitudes Art Fair Luigi Di Sarro to mention a few. \\n \\nIn 2015 he was invited to be a seasonal lecturer at the University of Witwatersrand for the second year Fine Art division where he ran a printmaking, book-binding and publication making program alongside collective partner artist Issac Zavale who he co-founded Alphabet Zoo with - A Johannesburg based street-culture zine that invites collaboration with artists from across all disciplines."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082004189","gid://shopify/Product/9452082102493","gid://shopify/Product/9452123160797"]

item.title: Miska Mohmmed
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641830895837 Miska Mohmmed 2224 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640851296477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013457354973","gid://shopify/Product/9452115099869"] [16953,16481,23177,16477,16474] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Miska was born in 1995, in Omdurman, Sudan. Miska Mohmmed works predominantly in oils and acrylics combining material experimentation with an exploration of the sensual experience of landscape. \\nMiska trained as a painter for a long time, practiced painting “en plein air” guided by her experience of nature, atmosphere, and the movement and bustle of crowded spaces. Miska renders landscape which remains the focus of her painting practice as a semi-abstract series of sweeping horizontal lines whose direction, colour, and varying density approximate the terrains from which they are drawn. Mohmmed received in 2016 a BFA in Painting from the College of Fine and Applied Arts, Sudan University. Mohmmed has exhibited widely in Sudan, Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt, Dubai, Tunisia, New York, UK, Germany and Zanzibar. \\nShe participated at Art Dubai 2022, Dubai, UAE; Art X Lagos 2021 and 2019, Lagos, Nigeria; FNB Art Joburg, Johannesburg and Investec Cape Town Art Fair 2021, Cape Town, South Africa; the Rashid Diab Arts Centre in Khartoum, Sudan; and the French Cultural Centre in Khartoum, Sudan among others. \\nArt Collectors Carla and Pieter Schulting exhibit her artwork from September 2023 to April 2024 at Kunsthal Kade, Amersfoort, the Netherlands, for Africa Supernova, a group show with a selection of 100 artworks of their collection. \\n“Highlands of Sudan” will be her first solo show in Barcelona, Spain with OOA GALLERY from October 28th to December 3rd, 2023."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013457354973","gid://shopify/Product/9452115099869"]

His body of work includes paintings, sculptures and film, having exhibited in several prominent galleries around South Africa. \\nLourens has also directed and produced films such as DIE RIT/THE DRIVE (2009), PROGNOSE/PROGNOSIS (2008) and PA/FATHER (2006), which was screened at the Commonwealth Film Festival and was in the official selection of the African International Film Festival, Tariva, Spain. Such films can be viewed at www.prefab.co.za. \\nLourens lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452065816797","gid://shopify/Product/9452065849565","gid://shopify/Product/9452150161629"]

item.title: Mmutla Kgwangka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641833943261 Mmutla Kgwangka 2629 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640853000413 [] [23782] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mmutla Mashishi, born on August 5th, 1976, in the village of Driefontein, Limpopo, is a self-taught South African artist whose creative journey began in his youth. Raised by his grandparents while his mother worked on farms, Mashishi's passion for drawing emerged during his teenage years, despite challenges and occasional punishment for using his schoolbooks as sketchpads. Undeterred by setbacks, his love for art only grew, and he later expanded his practice to include sculpture. \\n \\nIn high school, his teachers recognized his talent and encouraged him to enter art competitions. Supported by his grandparents, who provided with art materials, and his mother, who brought home art supplies from work, Mashishi began to hone his craft. Though he aspired to study art after matriculating, he struggled academically and initially worked as a security officer between 2000 and 2001. \\n \\nA turning point in his career came when a friend introduced him to renowned sculptor Anton Smit, who invited Mashishi to showcase his work. Impressed by his talent, Smit offered him a studio space, where Mashishi worked from 2000 to 2005. Afterward, he returned to working from home but faced difficulties managing his art business. In 2006, he sought new opportunities and connected with sculptor Angus Taylor, who welcomed him into his studio until 2007. \\n \\nDetermined to pursue his own artistic vision, Mashishi began experimenting with recycled plastic, a material that had long intrigued him. Despite initial fears about its reception, he pushed forward, studying the properties and potential of what he now refers to as \"plastic clay\". Drawing on his experiences at the Anton Smit Sculpture Park, Mashishi mastered this unconventional medium, which has since become his signature material for sculpture. Today, his innovative use of plastic reflects his resilience and commitment to evolving as an artist, making his work both distinctive and meaningful in the contemporary art scene."}]}]} []

item.title: Mlondi Magubane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641833910493 Mlondi Magubane 2506 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640852836573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086755549","gid://shopify/Product/9452108611805","gid://shopify/Product/9452108775645"] [22426,25059,20118,19867] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mlondi Magubane was born in Pimville, Soweto. He describes himself as a visual practitioner. He studied photography at the Market Photo Workshop in 2019 Film & Television at Revolution Media Academy in 2022. He currently lives and works in Johannesburg. He has collaborated with music artists Mduduzi Ncube and Kunle Ayo. Magubane’s interests are in environmental portraiture, landscapes and studio product shots. \\nMost of his conceptual work focuses on subcultures and indigenous knowledge. In 2021 he photographed crafts for the Dubai Craft Show. He is a resident of Occupying The Gallery and has been part of group exhibitions that include, Bazobuya (2023) at Keys Art Mile, Johannesburg, (Le)-Lapha (2023) at SMAC Gallery, Johannesburg and more recently in ‘Bazobuya' (2024) curated by Lawrence Lemaoana, at the KZNSA Gallery in Durban, South Africa."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086755549","gid://shopify/Product/9452108611805","gid://shopify/Product/9452108775645"]

item.title: Mncedi Madolo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641833976029 Mncedi Madolo 1191 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640853262557 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452137087197", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137119965", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137152733", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137185501", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137218269", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137251037", "gid://shopify/Product/9452137283805"] Johannesburg artist and cartoonist Mncedi Madolo (WSU Fine Arts) uses painting, illustration, and found materials to critique urban South African life, advertising, and social paradoxes. [23824,24750,24749,24744,24754,24746,24747,24558,23894] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mncedi Madolo is a Johannesburg-based artist who holds a National Diploma in Fine Arts (majoring in paintings) from the Walter Sisulu University, obtained in 2014. He relocated to Johannesburg in 2017 to establish himself as a full-time artist, a move that immersed him in the complex realities of urban life. \\nObserving the daily lives of people navigating a lower middle-class existence alongside the pervasive influence of advertising media selling aspirational dreams, Madolo found rich territory for artistic exploration. His work directly engages with these paradoxes. He incorporates found materials collected from the city streets—such as magazine covers proclaiming \"black is beautiful\" and flyers offering quick solutions to personal problems—into his pieces. \\nLeveraging his skills as a skillful illustrator and freelance cartoonist for major national newspapers, Madolo often integrates cartoon sketches that critique or mock the status quo, sometimes featuring familiar brand logos in the background. Through this complex layering of found imagery, painted elements, and illustrative commentary, his work offers a nuanced perspective on contemporary Johannesburg society."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126011613","gid://shopify/Product/9452137087197","gid://shopify/Product/9452137119965","gid://shopify/Product/9452137152733","gid://shopify/Product/9452137185501","gid://shopify/Product/9452137218269","gid://shopify/Product/9452137251037","gid://shopify/Product/9452137283805"]

item.title: Modisa Tim Motsomi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641834008797 Modisa Tim Motsomi 2311 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640853590237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154683613"] Explore the work of Modisa Motsomi, a Botswana multi-disciplinary artist examining the black body and challenging notions of land sovereignty through innovative mapping techniques. Learn about his international exhibitions and academic contributions. [19918,19922,19924,19926,19931,19934,17800,19162,19937,19936,24245] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Modisa Motsomi (b. 1990, Botswana) is a multidisciplinary artist based in Francistown, Botswana. His artistic practice delves into he complex contextualizations of the black bod, examining it as both a physical location and a lived-in space. Motsomi's recent work demonstrates a unique approach to topographical mapping, where he employs fragmented techniques to reveal the visible and invisible negotiations inherent in the creation of maps. \\nMotsomi imaginatively explores the concepts of defining, naming, and claiming land, challenging conventional notions of sovereignty. His work has garnered international recognition, with exhibitions held in South Africa, Botswana, the United Kingdom, Germany, China and more. Motsomi's contributions extend beyond visual art, as he also presented papers and texts in various academic conferences. Additionally, he has participated in two international artist residencies, enriching his artistic perspective and practice. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154683613","gid://shopify/Product/9452167725277"]

In 2023 he was also selected as a Top 250 finalist for the prestigious National Portrait Award hosted by Rust-en-Vrede Gallery in Cape Town. item.title: Morgan Otagburuagu

item.title: Mosa Anita Kaiser
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641838006493 Mosa Anita Kaiser 2284 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640859062493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086821085","gid://shopify/Product/9452171002077","gid://shopify/Product/9452174115037"] [22429,19862,25054,19870,20119,25018] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mosa Anita Kaiser (b.1995) is a South African born, lens-based artist. Having studied and taken an interest in various forms of visual culture, she positions herself at the intersections of years of unfolding, conflicting and evolving ideologies of art making. Kaiser engages visual culture and visual literacy as fundamental components to how we consume the world around us and as a means to piece together our understandings and our identities. Her thematic interests include the power dynamics of the camera, socio-political positioning of women, multi-cultural intersections, internet culture and the body as a site of violence and beauty. \\nShe has exhibited her work in numerous group exhibitions both locally and online. Some notable exhibitions are Occupying The Gallery, Gallery 1 Keyes Art Mile, 2023; (in)sight, Through The Lens Collective, Victoria Yards, 2019; Counter Narratives, University of Belfast Analogue Eye, 2020; Stilled Life, Turbine Art Fair, 2020; Disclosure, SMAC Gallery, 2017 and Sasol New Signatures, Pretoria Art Museum, 2016 where she was a merit award winner."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086821085","gid://shopify/Product/9452171002077","gid://shopify/Product/9452174115037"]

item.title: Moses Zibor
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641838072029 Moses Zibor 2217 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640859226333 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013440643293","gid://shopify/Product/9013440708829","gid://shopify/Product/9013440741597","gid://shopify/Product/9013440774365","gid://shopify/Product/9013440905437","gid://shopify/Product/9013440938205","gid://shopify/Product/9452059558109","gid://shopify/Product/9452103074013","gid://shopify/Product/9452103106781"] [21620,21628,16357,21621,16362,21625,17863,21631,21619,21627,16358,16354,17872,16360,17873,21626] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born 1978, Surulere, Lagos -Nigeria. \\nLives and works in Almaty, Kazakhstan. \\n \\nMoses Zibor, born and raised in Lagos, Nigeria and based in Almaty, Kazakhstan is as enigmatic and mystical as the figures and themes he depicts in his hyper surrealist portraits. \\n \\nPrior to his birth, he recounts a story told to him by his mother, in which an elderly lady known for her prophetic prowess, informed her that she would give birth to a ‘special child with many hands’ who would have a gift for inspiring and encouraging others to dream and pursue their purpose. True to the eerie decree of the elderly woman, Moses’ otherworldly works enchants its viewers with its supernatural elements and invites us to see beyond the natural and physical world, and step into the realms of the unseen and unknown. \\n \\nWhilst the artist excelled in visual arts throughout his childhood and adolescence and later topped his class at the esteemed Yaba College of Technology, which boasts one of Nigeria’s leading art departments, he first acknowledged his innate talent for art at 7 years old, coinciding with his earliest memories of the hyper surreal dreams he had, and still continues to experience to this day. \\n \\nThe overwhelming and profound nature of these dreams, the figment of a hyperactive imagination that has transcended and endured childhood, is evident in the recurring motifs of water in the artist’s paintings. In several of his works, such as Dream Infinity, the artist’s figures are submerged and suspended in water, surrounded by aquatic creatures and motifs, such as fountains and fish. This a clear nod to the ethereal nature of his dreams in which man can survive and thrive underwater, but also to the African mysticism element of his work, which speaks to folktales and fables such as Mami Wata and the world of water spirits and black mermaids. \\nIn other works by the artist, he relays a more universal and humanist appeal to pursue one’s dreams and ambitions. \\n \\nAnother recurring motif in his paintings are footballs, as well as hexagons in the background of his work, which is also reminiscent of the classic football pattern the artist was acquainted with in the 1980’s and 90’s. In works such as, Immigrants in the USSR, Only the wise and A man and his books, the reference to football speaks squarely to the artist’s personal love of, and pursuit of football as a profession, and past time, a passion which saw him leave Nigeria for the first time for Kazakhstan, where he now hones his craft. \\n \\nThe act of leaving Nigeria for greener pastures and to chase one’s dreams, is known as ‘Jakpa’ in the Yoruba language, and loosely translates as ‘to run hard’. In the instance of the artist, his leaving Nigeria for an unknown country, culture and lifestyle, through the vehicle of football, left an indelible impact on him, which he constantly reminds us of through the football motifs in his work. \\n \\nIn the artist’s own words, in a world of chaos, confusion and conformity, he wants viewers of his work to dream, and be inspired to live a life outside of the usual and ordinary, and not accept the status quo. In his own pursuit to better understand himself, the world he lives in, and indeed the world he doesn’t want to exist in, Moses takes a leaf out of the book of modern masters such as Frida Kahlo and Salvador Dali. \\n \\nIn homage to Frida Kahlo, Moses’ works includes self portraits of himself as the muse, and the subject he is trying to know best, in a world of uncertainty and loss of self. He invites the audience to see themselves in his work, and try to figure out who they are, and who they really should be. More significantly, after a seven year hiatus from painting after his short stint as a footballer, the artist gravitated towards the freedom and spell binding nature of Salvador Dali’s surrealism work, which reignited is early love of art, and culminated in the existing style and practice he has since embraced and excelled in to date. \\n \\nEnchanting, mesmerising and mystical in composition, colour palette and style, Zibor’s works are aesthetically complex as they are technically strong, portraying an artist who has not only mastered their craft over several years, but also thoroughly researched the themes, motifs and narratives that underpins their work. \\n \\nRaphael DAPAAH \\nArt Consultant, Art writer, Art Curator \\nOOA GALLERY London"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013440643293","gid://shopify/Product/9013440708829","gid://shopify/Product/9013440741597","gid://shopify/Product/9013440774365","gid://shopify/Product/9013440905437","gid://shopify/Product/9013440938205","gid://shopify/Product/9452059558109","gid://shopify/Product/9452103074013","gid://shopify/Product/9452103106781"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641840005341 Motlhoki Nono 361 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640859554013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013357019357", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290369245", "gid://shopify/Product/9013357347037", "gid://shopify/Product/9013357510877", "gid://shopify/Product/9013357576413", "gid://shopify/Product/9013460926685", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461024989", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461156061", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461221597", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461352669", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461385437", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461483741", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461516509"] [4052,4055,17128,17140,11323,17141,17127,4048,4047,11317,11316,17142,4050,11324,4051,11325,4054,17134,17130] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Motlhoki (b. 1998 in Mabopane, Pretoria) has currently completed her Honours in Fine Art at the University of the Witwatersrand, where she graduated with five distinctions and two awards. Her studio practice is currently based in Johannesburg, where she uses video, photography and printmaking as tools to investigate the intimate and violent politics that are implicated in romantic love. She engages the ideas of consumption, domesticity and romance to perform and document the internal lives and politics of black women in love. Her practice is characterised by a valorisation, problematisation and curiosity towards black love, as well as complexities and joys of the domestic and heart spaces. She defines her practice as a decolonial and sociological enquiry into love, exploring how love manifests at the intersection of race, class and gender."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013290467549","gid://shopify/Product/9013357019357","gid://shopify/Product/9013290369245","gid://shopify/Product/9013357347037","gid://shopify/Product/9013357510877","gid://shopify/Product/9013357576413","gid://shopify/Product/9013460926685","gid://shopify/Product/9013461024989","gid://shopify/Product/9013461156061","gid://shopify/Product/9013461221597","gid://shopify/Product/9013461352669","gid://shopify/Product/9013461385437","gid://shopify/Product/9013461483741","gid://shopify/Product/9013461516509"]

Mpumelelo went on to exhibit his photographs at Social Art Award in Germany 2019, and was the 2nd prize winner for Nikon Yellow competition in 2018.He lives and works in Johannebsurg, South Africa. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452257476829","gid://shopify/Product/9452257673437"]

item.title: Mpumi Peter
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641843708125 Mpumi Peter 2006 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640860307677 Discover the vibrant art of Mpumi Peter, a South African artist whose work celebrates African heritage and embraces cultural identity. Her oil paintings, featuring African fabrics and patterns, invite viewers to find joy and contentment. Purchase her unique pieces online. [19439,19434,19437,19433,19440,19441] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mpumi Peter was born and raised in Springs, Ekurhuleni, Johannesburg. She graduated from the University of South Africa with a Bachelor's Degree in Financial Management and holds a Professional Diploma in Graphic Design and Digital Marketing. As a self-taught emerging artist, Mpumi's love and passion for art knows no bounds. Her creative journey has been shaped by her diverse educational background and her dedication to exploring various artistic mediums and techniques. \\nMpumi does not limit herself to one medium, style, or concept, as inspiration and ideas continually evolve. Her creativity is expressed in various forms, with a preference for oil paintings due to their flexibility and versatility, allowing for both thin layers and thick impasto. Recently, she has begun experimenting with 3D formats and digital artwork, embracing the current digital art movement. \\nInfluenced by her continent, surroundings, and the way Africans have embraced their blackness, Mpumi incorporates African fabrics and patterns into her artwork. Each piece she creates is a celebration of her African heritage, embracing her culture and acknowledging her worth. Her paintings are influenced by life and the quest for contentment in an age of discontentment. She aims to invoke happiness, calmness, and joy in her work, reminding viewers to celebrate their current circumstances and be patient for what is to come. \\nMpumi's work has been showcased at the Pretoria Art Museum as part of the Sasol New Signature Art Competition 2021 Exhibition. She has also participated in group exhibitions at Thomarts Gallery (The Marc) in 2019 and 2020. Her pieces reflect her journey and the resilience of the individuals in her community."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013933605085","gid://shopify/Product/9013933637853","gid://shopify/Product/9013933768925","gid://shopify/Product/9013933801693","gid://shopify/Product/9013933867229","gid://shopify/Product/9013933899997","gid://shopify/Product/9013933932765"]

item.title: Mulanga Mbedzi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641844068573 Mulanga Mbedzi 1734 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640860569821 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013865054429", "gid://shopify/Product/9013865873629"] [19202,18050,19203,18054,18052,11462,11463] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Based in Johannesburg, Mulanga Mbedzi is a self-taught visual artist who primarily employs charcoal to create representational drawings that explore healing and identity. Mulanga attained her LLB degree from the University of the Witwatersrand, and her Political and International Relations Honours degree from Rhodes University. Through her education, Mulanga attained a deeper understanding of social ills and a pressing need to alleviate them. It is with this passion for alleviating social ills that Mulanga uses her practice to delve into the root causes of many social ills which she says are encapsulated in one phrase; “hurt people hurt people.” \\n \\nAs human beings, we’re all suffering from some kind of pain and trauma, and it is from a place of suffering that we inflict harm on ourselves and each other. Mulanga’s practice is thus aimed at encouraging individuals to exercise self-reflection and awareness, in order to heal from the many hidden traumas we unknowingly suffer from to become truer, better versions of ourselves. To do this, she employs the simple medium of charcoal to create uncomplicated yet profound drawings that engage the viewer in a self-reflective conversation, where they will hopefully be inspired to look deeper within themselves and come into an awareness of parts that need attention and healing."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013360459997","gid://shopify/Product/9013360558301","gid://shopify/Product/9013836349661","gid://shopify/Product/9013836415197","gid://shopify/Product/9013836513501","gid://shopify/Product/9013864300765","gid://shopify/Product/9013865054429","gid://shopify/Product/9013865873629"]

item.title: Muofhe Manavhela

Her vibrant work communicates the experience of a young black woman navigating the modern South African landscape. \\nInspired by artists like Lady Skollie and Andy Warhol, as well as her personal experience of a 21st century black womanhood, Muofhe depicts a more nuanced perspective of the daily experiences of black women. The artist uses a variety of mediums mainly paint, printmaking and embroidery, to communicate themes of sexuality, youth, freedom, pleasure, and the domesticity of women. Her work is simultaneously fun and honest. \\nThe young artist has a promising and growing stature having shown at her debut solo exhibit ‘12 seconds’ at Bubblegum Gallery, and group shows ‘Unusual Suspects’ at African Artists Foundation, ‘Mother of Mankind’ at ADA x HOFA, and ‘The Human Experience’ at Project Space Africa – her work finds home amongst different contexts."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452085412061"]

item.title: Mzwandile Mpaka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848033501 Mzwandile Mpaka 2896 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640895467741 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098034909","gid://shopify/Product/9014098067677"] Mzwandile Mpaka is a Johannesburg-based documentary photographer specializing in analogue photography. [24637,24636] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mzwandile Mpaka, 29, was born in Soweto. He is a Johannesburg-based documentary photographer whose career began in 2016 while studying at Boston Media House. He also obtained a film and television production certificate through Umuzi and March Media, laying the foundation for a visual approach rooted in storytelling and everyday life. Between 2018 and 2021 Mpaka honed his craft through collaborative work in Johannesburg and Cape Town, developing a distinct style centred on analogue photography. \\nHis ability to capture raw, intimate moments led to his debut at the 2023 Turbine Art Fair with Morning Shadows – a project that explores early morning routines and the pursuit of dreams. In 2024, he participated in the RMB Talent Unlocked mentorship programme. His work often highlights overlooked urban narratives, offering a quiet yet powerful reflection on human experience. He continues to develop personal projects with the long-term vision of engaging with global communities through photography. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098034909","gid://shopify/Product/9014098067677"]
