item.title: Nada Baraka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848754397 Nada Baraka 2180 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640900939997 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013435924701", "gid://shopify/Product/9013435990237", "gid://shopify/Product/9013443068125", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399421149", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399355613", "gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845", "gid://shopify/Product/9013940814045"] [16457,15553,16060,15552,19933,15586,15587,15917,16061,25644,18431,15589,16454,16451,16452,16453,16455,16456,19935,15554,16458,16459] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1990, Nada Baraka is a visual artist with a BA in Communication Media Art and Fine Arts from the American University in Cairo and a master’s degree in Fine Arts from Central Saint Martins, London. \\n \\nNada Baraka makes paintings that maintain an endless, active state of flux, swaying between abstract and surreal with her evocative application and vivid colors. Baraka seeks to generate forms in new contexts as a means to challenge and deconstruct the obvious and tease meaning out of absurdity. Fluctuations of emotions triggered by various experiences build up to a narrative that eludes interpretation. \\n \\nThe core of her work is this process that seeks to narrate an experience through expressionist brushwork and surrealist methodology. A central aspect in those narratives is the concept of eruption, appearing as distorted forms, body parts, colors or layers, all bathed in a fluidity punctuated with striking detail."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013427798237","gid://shopify/Product/9013435924701","gid://shopify/Product/9013435990237","gid://shopify/Product/9013443068125","gid://shopify/Product/9013443199197","gid://shopify/Product/9013443231965","gid://shopify/Product/9013443330269","gid://shopify/Product/9013443395805","gid://shopify/Product/9013443428573","gid://shopify/Product/9013443461341","gid://shopify/Product/9013842542813","gid://shopify/Product/9013399421149","gid://shopify/Product/9013399355613","gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845","gid://shopify/Product/9013940814045","gid://shopify/Product/9133221707997","gid://shopify/Product/9133228589277"]

item.title: Nadia Ettwein
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848787165 Nadia Ettwein 1400 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640901202141 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013461811421", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461844189", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461876957", "gid://shopify/Product/9013461975261", "gid://shopify/Product/9013462073565", "gid://shopify/Product/9014031614173"] [20489,22948] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nadia Ettwein (b.1984) is a contemporary lens-based artist based in Cape Town, South Africa. Her background in Information Sciences has guided her process in photography by the systematic creation and preservation of her own stories. Nadia’s work is an introspective exploration of social issues, personal identity, and domesticity in South Africa. Through her works, she authors and witnesses the individuality and diversity of womanhood. \\nRecently named a CAP (Contemporary African Photography Award) 2023 winner, her work has been exhibited as part of the group exhibition 'Shutterland' by Lizamore and Associates in Johannesburg as well as a collective exhibition, ‘(IM)Materiality’ by Notamuseum in Lisbon. She was featured in a group exhibition ‘Everything, Everyone, Always’ by Through The Lens Collective. She resonates with the complexities of the human experience, reflecting on her own identity and abuse. Nadia continues to work on projects in analogue, digital and printed mediums. She is a Through The Lens Collective mentee."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013388837085","gid://shopify/Product/9013388869853","gid://shopify/Product/9013388902621","gid://shopify/Product/9013461811421","gid://shopify/Product/9013461844189","gid://shopify/Product/9013461876957","gid://shopify/Product/9013461975261","gid://shopify/Product/9013462073565","gid://shopify/Product/9013953757405","gid://shopify/Product/9014031614173"]

item.title: Nadine Mathenjwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848852701 Nadine Mathenjwa 1686 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640902578397 [21080] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nadine Noluthando Mathenjwa is a young woman born and raised in Gauteng South Africa. In 2021 Nadine graduated at Artistproof studio where she practiced printmaking working in different mediums such as Cyanotyp, Screenprint, Linocut and etching. With the help of Artistproof studio. Nadine’s work has been exhibited at Turbine Artfair 2022, Investec Capetown Art Fair 2022, ABSA virtual space in 2021 and her grad show “A version of us” in 2021. Nadine aspires to further her study’s in fashion She currently resides in Johannesburg producing work and entering competitions \\nin the hopes of getting her works seen worldwide. \\n \\n“My body of work focuses on the hybrid cultures that western society introduced my ancestors to, I am a young black woman navigating for an identity in a society where information on native cultures has been washed down, as most young people I find solace in fashion it has become a great part of my evolved culture, my self expression, identity and individuality. As much as my work is about paying homage to the lifestyle that my ancestors and family chose to make out of colonisation my work is also about the subcultures that the millennials and genZ have created, particularly those of fashion and luxury or ghetto fabulous lifestyle. These subcultures have become part of the movement towards changing the narrative about what it is to be young, African and cultured. \\n \\nI often use tribal patterns on the figures which are a representation of the information on ancient African beliefs and history that I unravel through watching documentaries and finding books on African spirituality, with the patterns I aim to shift the demonised notions on African spirituality and rituals.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013983477981","gid://shopify/Product/9013983576285","gid://shopify/Product/9013983674589"]

item.title: Naledi Maifala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848983773 Naledi Maifala 2141 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640906117341 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014126346461"] Naledi Maifala is a contemporary artist known for their thought-provoking works that explore themes of identity, culture, and personal narratives. Their artistic practice blends traditional and modern techniques, offering a unique perspective on South African and global artistic discourse. [25214,24225,23603,15172,15181,24230,23604,23752,15177,23601,25261,23753,15175,24226,15173,23602,24228,24229,15174,24227] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naledi Maifala is a Botswana-based contemporary expressionist painter exploring themes of stillness and contentment. Her journey with painting began in 2007 during her junior years, and in 2022, she transitioned into professional art. She has participated in several group exhibitions in Botswana, including Dikgosigadi Exhibition, Women Create Love Exhibition, and Heart Scape in Nigeria, among others. \\n \\nHer work is guided by the theme “Just as Petals Fall, Life Too Fades”—a metaphor for presence, impermanence, and the fleeting nature of life. She focuses on mind-soothing surroundings, painting domestic animals, garden flowers, sentimental objects, and serene individuals. Fascinated by the journey of inner contentment, she believes that external surroundings can also nurture this experience. With her keen photography skills, she captures moments of solitude, later translating them onto canvas with acrylic paints. Her brushstrokes balance intuition and intention, using light, texture, and colour to shape mood and storytelling. Through her work, she hopes to inspire appreciation for life’s simplicity, offering a space of meditation that alleviates the pressures of constant striving. She envisions her art as a sanctuary for spiritual, psychological, and emotional well-being."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013418721501","gid://shopify/Product/9014051635421","gid://shopify/Product/9014051668189","gid://shopify/Product/9014051733725","gid://shopify/Product/9014051799261","gid://shopify/Product/9014057402589","gid://shopify/Product/9014057435357","gid://shopify/Product/9014078308573","gid://shopify/Product/9014078341341","gid://shopify/Product/9014078406877","gid://shopify/Product/9014078472413","gid://shopify/Product/9014078537949","gid://shopify/Product/9014078603485","gid://shopify/Product/9014126346461","gid://shopify/Product/9014138306781"]

item.title: Nandipha Jantjies
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641849147613 Nandipha Jantjies 2130 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640906412253 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452055855325", "gid://shopify/Product/9452055888093", "gid://shopify/Product/9452056576221", "gid://shopify/Product/9452110610653", "gid://shopify/Product/9452110643421", "gid://shopify/Product/9452110676189"] [22774,22775,16133,16083,22773,16084] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Artist Nandipha Jantjies (b.1998) is a painter and multi-media digital artist and creator. The prolific artist is also know by the name 'Neferuda' which is a character that inspires and features prominently in her digital artworks. Jantjies was born in Bloemfontein, South Africa and later relocated to Welkom. She currently resides in the Free State where she has set up her artist studio and practice. Nandipha graduated in Studio Art and Design at CUT, South Africa. Her works symbolically traverse space and time, and mediate culture and ancestry in the contemporary. \\n'My work can also involve culture, spirituality, nature and the philosophy of what a soul is. Challenging topics like \"how one should carry themselves in terms of society, or how one's culture/traditions are constantly appropriated\" are one of the things I love putting out there, but mostly I embrace the woman's body. My signature style is inspired from the complexity (overlapping lines) of this beautiful Earth, from the traffic to marching ants to different faces you meet on a daily. All of those are complexities, in all their shades of beauty. \\nThe horns I include in my paintings represent strength, a sense of boldness, royalty and yet I create them in a way that the feeling you get once glancing on them is serene. Horns are protective. I mostly use a Nguni cow, a mountain goat or a buffalo. A bit of my culture is included within the Nguni horns, which is isiXhosa. The baSotho tradition or culture is one that I include too, I tend to play around with \" Nkgo\" an African beer pot, nonetheless my love for animals is important in my practice. My medium is, ink, acrylic paint, wool and beads on a canvas. I've recently started playing around with wool and beads on my artworks'. Nandipha Jantjies \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452055855325","gid://shopify/Product/9452055888093","gid://shopify/Product/9452056576221","gid://shopify/Product/9452110577885","gid://shopify/Product/9452110610653","gid://shopify/Product/9452110643421","gid://shopify/Product/9452110676189"]

item.title: Naledi Modupi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641849114845 Naledi Modupi 2236 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640906346717 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129157341","gid://shopify/Product/9452129190109","gid://shopify/Product/9452129222877","gid://shopify/Product/9452129255645","gid://shopify/Product/9452129288413","gid://shopify/Product/9452129321181","gid://shopify/Product/9452129386717","gid://shopify/Product/9452166906077","gid://shopify/Product/9452166938845"] [24169,16984,16983,24168,24279,24171,24278,24166,24167,24275,24170,24165,16985,24164,24277,24690,24176,24175] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naledi Tshegofatso Modupi is a multi-dimensional visual artist who has developed a powerful and \\ndistinctive style of portraiture. She is known for her versatility and skill in exploring both traditional \\nand digital art form. \\nHer portraits showcase individuality, boldness and energy expressed through \\nthe use of vibrant colours and continuous lines that define each face distinctly. These colors are also \\nsymbolic of her interest in celebrating the beauty of blackness and all the qualities associated with \\nbeing a woman. \\n \\nHer work is deeply connected to this idea; it serves as an authentic celebration for women’s \\npersonalities and selfhood. Her uplifting visual representations often celebrate what it means to be \\nblack and female by renewing appreciation for these characteristics. Ultimately, Modupi's work \\nresonates with its audience by allowing viewers to witness beauty through a lens of honor and \\nadmiration. \\nThroughout her career, the artist has had the opportunity to showcase her work in a variety of \\ndiverse cities around the world. London, Johannesburg, Chicago, Brighton, Cape Town, and Bali. By exposing her work to such an array of cities, Naledi has been able to not only expand her portfolio, \\nbut also gain a deeper understanding of the global art scene."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129157341","gid://shopify/Product/9452129190109","gid://shopify/Product/9452129222877","gid://shopify/Product/9452129255645","gid://shopify/Product/9452129288413","gid://shopify/Product/9452129321181","gid://shopify/Product/9452129386717","gid://shopify/Product/9452166906077","gid://shopify/Product/9452166938845"]

As the founder and CEO of King Nandi & Co., she leads a dynamic multimedia production collective specializing in commercial, corporate, and fashion photography. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nandipha Khemese, 33, is a photographer and the creative director and founder of multimedia production company King Nandi & Co. She creates space for others – emerging artists, voices at the margins – to rise, to be seen and to belong. \\nWhether behind the lens or beside a team, Khemese builds bridges between passion and purpose. Her work has reached global platforms, but her heart remains grounded in local soil, nurturing transformation from the inside out. Her journey is not just her own – it is one shared with collaboration, courage and care. Through every frame and every initiative, she carries community forward – one powerful story at a time."}]}]} []

item.title: Nandipha Mntambo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641849442525 Nandipha Mntambo 514 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640907886813 [] [16076,16075,16077] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nandipha Mntambo was born in Mbabane, Swaziland. In 2007, she completed a Master’s in Fine Art from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. Mntambo currently lives in Johannesburg. Mntambo is best known for her figurative cowhide sculptures which allude to the symbiotic relationship between humans and nature. \\n \\nHer work addresses ongoing debates around traditional gender roles, body politics, and identity. She works in photography, sculpture, video, and mixed media to explore the liminal boundaries between human and animal, femininity and masculinity, attraction and repulsion, life and death. \\n \\nNotable solo exhibitions include Transience at Stevenson (Johannesburg: 2014); Nandipha Mntambo at Andréhn-Schiptjenko (Stockholm, Sweden: 2013) and Faena, a travelling exhibition showcased at the Grahamstown National Arts Festival, the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Art Museum in Port Elizabeth, and at Iziko South African National Gallery in Cape Town (2011). \\n \\nMntambo’s participation in group shows include Regarding Africa: Contemporary Art and Afro-Futurism at Tel Aviv Museum of Art (2017); the 12th Edition of Dak’Art, the African Art Biennale in (Dakar, Senegal: 2016); Disguise: Masks and Global African Art at Seattle Art Museum (Seattle, USA: 2015); What Remains is Tomorrow for the South African Pavilion (56th Venice Biennale: 2015); The Divine Comedy: Heaven, Purgatory and Hell Revisited by Contemporary African Artists (Museum für Moderne Kunst (MMK), Frankfurt/Main, Germany: 2014), Nandipha Mntambo at the FNB Joburg Art Fair (Johannesburg: 2013) and the 3rd Moscow International Biennale for Young Art (Moscow, Russia: 2012). \\n \\nShe has been shortlisted for the AIMIA | AGO Photography Prize in Canada (2014), was a Civitella Ranieri Fellow (2013), received the Standard Bank Young Artist Award for Visual Art (2011) and the Wits/BHP Billiton Fellowship (2010)."}]}]} []

item.title: Nanna Venter

She holds a MA in Media Studies and a PhD in ICT4D from the University of Cape Town, she recently completed her post-doctoral tenure at the department of Applied Design at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology. \\nShe has created design and illustration work for Apple Music, Nike, Microsoft, Speedo, Square Enix and Mr Price, among many others."}]}]} []

item.title: Nano Le Face
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641851080925 Nano Le Face 1835 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640908673245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014012051677", "gid://shopify/Product/9014012084445", "gid://shopify/Product/9014012117213", "gid://shopify/Product/9014044491997", "gid://shopify/Product/9014044524765"] Discover the satirical and visually striking works of South African artist Nano Le Face. His vibrant, mixed-media art pieces critique consumerism and pop culture. Explore and purchase unique, original artworks online, reflecting the beauty, humor, and complexity of contemporary life. [22273,17223,22270,22309,22269,22311,22308,22271,17267,17266,18526,23412,23413,22272,22310,18248,22312] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ntwanano Shilubana (b. 1999), better known as Nano Le Face or simply Nano, is a self-taught visual artist based in Pretoria, South Africa. Nano studied Film Arts at the Open Window Institute in Pretoria and at AFDA in Johannesburg before committing entirely to fine art. Through a suite of Post-Pop drawings, Nano Le Face employs humour and satire to mock and critique our obsession with consumerism, fame, and self-image. \\nNano work is distinguished by sharp-witted prose and acerbic characterization offering a biting critique of contemporary culture. Nano began his artistic practice during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period that prompted individuals to observe one another through screens, turning their attention inward. Initially gaining traction on Instagram, Nano developed a dedicated base of collectors. His works quickly attracted attention from prominent figures in the art world, leading to numerous exhibitions and fairs, including the Turbine Art Fair and RMB Latitudes Art Fair. \\nWorking primarily in mixed media on paper, Nano's creations borrow freely from popular culture, editorial photography, and luxury brand advertisements. His imagery is flattened into vivid lines and striking colours palettes, presenting scenes that seem like bite-sized snippets from a satirical cartoon. Through a combination of coloured pencils and wax crayons, Nano crafts playful yet deeply critical works that draw viewers into a world of glamour and melodrama. \\nNano’s art often features enigmatic characters and scenes, allowing viewers to interpret and imagine their own narratives. His characters, such as the recurring \"Bettys and Veronicas,\" embody a mixture of distant glamour and relatable human traits, reinforcing the satirical nature of his work. \\nNano’s recent works continue to delve into themes of pop culture, hyper-consumerism, and social media vanity. He remains fascinated by the glamorized yet surreal nature of celebrity culture, capturing its essence in his satirical and often provocative drawings. Through his evolving artistic practice, Nano Le Face offers a mirror to society’s obsessions and invites viewers to engage with his biting critiques. \\nNano’s distinctive voice and artistic style ensure that his works are not only visually captivating but also intellectually stimulating, providing a fresh perspective on the complexities of modern life."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013843362013","gid://shopify/Product/9014011953373","gid://shopify/Product/9014011986141","gid://shopify/Product/9014012051677","gid://shopify/Product/9014012084445","gid://shopify/Product/9014012117213","gid://shopify/Product/9014044491997","gid://shopify/Product/9014044524765"]

item.title: Natalie Paneng
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641852391645 Natalie Paneng gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640912408797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452093014237","gid://shopify/Product/9452123291869"] Natalie Paneng, a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist, combines her theatre background and digital skills to create imaginative digital art and new media. She has exhibited widely, including at Galerie EIGEN + ART in Leipzig, and has participated in several artist residencies and digital art festivals. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natalie Paneng (b. 1996) is a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist whose innovative work spans digital art, new media, and performance. She earned her BA in Dramatic Arts from the University of Witwatersrand in 2018, winning Leon Gluckman Prize. Combining her theatre background with self-taught digital skills, Paneng describes herself as a world-builder, creating and archiving imagined realities through digital art. \\nPaneng has exhibited her work with esteemed institutions such as TMRW Gallery, The National Arts Festival, Blank Projects, Michaelis School of Fine Art, BKHz, Javett UP, Galerie Eigen Art Leipzig, and Mutek. Her first solo exhibition, 'Maze,' was presented internationally at Galerie EIGEN + ART in Leipzig, Germany. She has also participated in prominent artist residencies, including Bubblegum Future 76 Residency, Floating Reverie, Fak’ugesi Digital Innovation Artist Residency, and The Centre of A Less Good Idea’s So Academy’s ‘Thinking in Cardboard’ scenographers mentorship. \\nIn addition to her exhibitions, Paneng has published creative research through Ellipses Journal and Artist Research Africa and was a 202 Fellow with the Institute of Creative Arts and UCT. Recent exhibitions include Galerie Eigen + Art in Leipzig (2023), Stevenson Gallery in Johannesburg (2023), FCA Ghana (2023), Standard Bank Gallery in Johannesburg (2022), Galerie Konerpark in Berlin (2023), and The Centre For A Less Good Idea in Johannesburg (2023). She has also participated in digital art festivals such as MUTEK Montreal, KIKK Festival, Fak’ugesi Festival, and IDFA. In 2023, Paneng was awarded the Special Jury Prize for her use of creative technology at the International Documentary Festival of Amsterdam."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452093014237","gid://shopify/Product/9452123291869"]

item.title: Natasha Evans
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855045853 Natasha Evans 351 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640914211037 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014045245661"] [21540,21543,21542,21541] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natasha (b. 1978) in Zimbabwe in and raised from a young age in Zambia, the birthplace of both her parents. In her early twenties Natasha studied at The Arts Institute at Bournemouth where she earned a bachelor's degree with honors in Illustration. Natasha works as a full time artist from her home studio in Lusaka, Zambia. Natasha has taken part in multiple group exhibitions and last year November she showed a collection of work in her fifth solo exhibition. Internationally Natasha travelled to Paris to exhibit a calabash vessel body of work, representing Zambia. \\nNatasha prepares new work for an upcoming show at the end of this year. Natasha creates contemporary mixed media works that see fluid shifts and overlaps in abstraction and figuration. Her work is realized on traditional media using paper and canvas and has editions in print. Her use of less traditional media includes the organic vessel the calabash, cement, earth, textile and found materials that are sculptural in nature. She makes use of tangible and non- tangible elements like, transferred photographic image, light, shadow, sculpted paper, automatic drawing, building, stacking, repetition, concealing, revealing and mark making. Natasha extracts resources from the physical (earth), cultural and social environments she (we) connect to in both the past and present. \\nShe goes deeper by often fragmenting texts and uses metaphor and symbolism to tell stories that she finds being Africa. Exploring selfhood, womanhood, dark and light, strength and fragility, presence and absence. In her work, Natasha quests to understand our edges, our deep cavities as well as our dreams and our lightness; the duality of being inside and outside simultaneously."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013999042781","gid://shopify/Product/9013972861149","gid://shopify/Product/9013999108317","gid://shopify/Product/9013999141085","gid://shopify/Product/9014045245661"]

item.title: Natnael Ashebir

Throughout his latest body of work, Natnael merges form in a meditative exploration of layers of life and inwardness. He works across a variety media including painting, digital art, drawing and photography. His work has been exhibited in Ethiopia, Kenya and Nigeria. item.title: Ncaoto Thama (Kuru Art Project)
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855668445 Ncaoto Thama (Kuru Art Project) gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915259613 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131451101"] Discover the vibrant work of Ncaoto Thama, a member of the Kuru Art Project Collective, showcasing cultural heritage and creative storytelling through immersive visual art. View artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Kuru Art Project is located in the village of D'kar, Western Botswana. The project was established in 1991 as part of the larger Kuru Development Trust. The artists are Naro and Dcui San, who have lived in and around D'kar since the early 1960's. Formally a nomadic people, hunting and food gathering from the veld remain significant cultural activities, but increasing westernisation means that this is not a sustainable lifestyle anymore. \\nMyths, legends and events of a bygone era are readily told by elders, but the less fortunate can only try to imagine life as it once was. Yet they all converge on a theme characterised by a mythical connection with animals and objects of their ancient past, while continuing their lives in a world that demands completely different skills to survive. \\nToday, there are 18 artists actively participating in the project. The artists work in a variety of media and techniques, which include oil on canvas, different printmaking techniques, and embroidery. \\nThey draw inspiration from stories told by their ancestors, and their expansive knowledge about the plants and animals from the Kalahari. For them, their art is a way to convey their identity and unique ways of life to the rest of the world. The Kuru artists’ work is known for its spontaneity. Often, the process is preferred over the product—their love for making and creating forms an intricate part of their culture. Bright colours and naive animal and plant forms signify the work of these artists. Their body of work is internationally acclaimed and has been exhibited in over fifteen countries abroad and in Africa over the years. \\nIn her own words, Ncaotoe says, “I do not really know what art is”, says Ncaotoe. “I just do it and I find I like it.” Ncaotoe joined the Kuru Art Project in the beginning of 2010. She loves the Kalahari bush passionately. She lived previously in the settlement of Rooibrak on the very edge of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve. Since Ncaotoe joined the project, she has made beautiful paintings and linocuts that tell of her love and knowledge of the Kalahari. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131451101"]

item.title: Ncg'abe (Nxabe) Tase
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855701213 Ncg'abe (Nxabe) Tase gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915357917 [] Explore the evocative oil paintings of Ncg’abe Tãse, a Botswana-born artist and founding member of the Kuru Art Project. Her work blends traditional San motifs with contemporary expressions, preserving and celebrating indigenous heritage. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1955, Botswana artist Ncg’abe is one of the last remaining original Kuru artists in the Kuru Art Project today. \\nShe joined the Kuru Art Project in 1992 together with her close friend Cg’ose Ntcox’o. Apart from visual art, Ncg’abe is a keen traditional dancer and musician, and she and Xgaiga, her husband, are founder members of the Nharo Giraffe Dance Group. \\n \\nAlthough she also makes beautiful linoleum prints, etchings and lithographs, Ncg’abe prefers to work with oil paint on canvas. The large-scale canvasses give her more freedom and directness, which is difficult to get with printmaking techniques. \\nShe loves to portray strange combinations of plants, birds, and other creatures like snakes and insects. The leaves, twigs, and creatures in her art sometimes form abstract patterns with great appeal. \\nShe also depicts beadwork patterns and the patterns on the shaved skin aprons that form part of the traditional attire of her San people, which she remembers her grandmothers having made many years ago."}]}]} []

item.title: Ndaya Ilunga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855832285 Ndaya Ilunga 2885 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916013277 [] Discover the powerful and expressive work of Ndaya Ilunga, a contemporary African artist featured on Latitudes Online. Explore original artworks and collect now. [24549] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Johannesburg to Congolese parents, Ndaya Ilunga, 29, began her artistic journey in her mother’s studio at the Bag Factory. She explored painting, sculpture and storytelling from a young age, later studying Fine Arts at the University of Johannesburg. In her third year, she was awarded a German Archdiocese exposure trip to Stuttgart, where she deepened her interest in surrealist and Renaissance art. \\nIlunga’s work is rooted in her exploration of a displaced refugee identity, merging Afrofuturist and surrealist elements into a unique visual language. She completed an Ampersand Foundation residency in Manhattan, New York, and interned at the Goodman Gallery, where her interest in the collective consciousness, blackness and the human condition evolved. \\nShe has exhibited at the UJ Art Gallery, The Viewing Room Art Gallery and Art & About. She was a finalist for the 2024 Nando’s Vusa Awards and participated in the RMB Talent Unlocked programme. She was awarded the 2024/2025 Bag Factory Young Womxn Studio Bursary supported by South African artist Sam Nlengethwa and has a studio at the Bag Factory in Fordsburg. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Ndlovukazi Ngilande
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641856225501 Ndlovukazi Ngilande 2630 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916144349 [] [21644] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ndlovukazi Ngilande's work is a celebration of women, honoring their beauty, strength, and vital roles within society. Her art is driven by a deep desire to pay tribute to the significance of the isicholo—a traditional Zulu hat worn by married women—and to ensure its appreciation endures for future generations \\nRooted in her heritage and inspired by the rich cultural history around her, Ngilande's pieces reflect a deep fascination with African art. She strives to honour her ancestors by blending traditional techniques with modern elements, creating works that bridge the gap between the past and the present. Her art serves as a homage to the artistic legacy that came before her, while also bringing it into the contemporary sphere. \\nNgilande's vision is for every married woman to own an isicholo sculpture, not only as a beautiful piece of art but also as a symbol of her marital status, proudly displayed in her home. Through her work, she seeks to preserve and celebrate this powerful cultural icon, ensuring it remains a meaningful part of African tradition for generations to come."}]}]} []

item.title: Neil Badenhorst
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857208541 Neil Badenhorst 1049 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917160157 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452076073181","gid://shopify/Product/9452076204253","gid://shopify/Product/9452076400861","gid://shopify/Product/9452110250205","gid://shopify/Product/9452110282973"] [22693,22710,19245,22711,19246,19247,22689] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neil Badenhorst (b. 1995) is an artist and illustrator based in Pretoria. He completed his Undergraduate and Honours degrees in Visual Communication with a major in Illustration at the Open Window, graduating in 2017 and 2018 respectively. Badenhorst began his Masters in Illustration in 2019, exploring ritual spaces and crisis heterotopias in illustrated fantasy books. Badenhorst has been pursuing a career as an independent artist since his early days at University and has also worked as a freelance illustrator and designer, as well as a lecturer, since then. Badenhorst’s ultimate goal as a creative is to be a ‘jack of all trades, master of none’. Through formally taught in digital design and illustration, Badenhorst’s artistic practice extends into painting, collage, and more recently digital and traditional installation art. His practice is largely concerned with themes such as liminality, multi-layered space and experience, queer themes, ritual process and imaginary worlds. Badenhorst’s creative process relies heavily on intuition, and his dreamscapes are a desperate attempt to map out the eternally expanding internal landscape, and recollection of memories from other worlds and universes. Badenhorst's master's exhibition, between worlds, explores these themes in practice. The exhibition centers around fragments of a narrative I have been piecing together for most of my life, from recorded dreams and daydreams. The exhibition consists of illustrated pieces that tell stories about things I ‘remember’ in the otherworld. The gallery space ultimately becomes both a ritual space (a liminal space between this world and our own), but also becomes the book of sorts; as one must move through the space to follow and piece together the narrative. The narrative, and world, the pieces centre around were never exactly an intentional creation on my part. It developed naturally from dreams and my imagination, piecing itself together. Thus artmaking, here, became a deeply personal ritual process where I am almost desperately clinging to the memories of my life in the otherworld I encounter when asleep or daydreaming; and it is these stories and spaces that allow me to reflect and make better sense of my experiences within the ‘real’ world."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452076073181","gid://shopify/Product/9452076204253","gid://shopify/Product/9452076400861","gid://shopify/Product/9452110250205","gid://shopify/Product/9452110282973"]

item.title: Neill Wright
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857143005 Neill Wright 662 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917749981 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452124930269"] [23761,23762] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neill Wright is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. His satirical work braves the world of social commentary in a bold, colourful and humorous manner. Wright explores various mediums, such as sculpture, printmaking and painting as modes of expression, drawing inspiration from the interconnected worlds of media, popular culture, politics and societal interactions in an attempt to create panoramic views of current issues, hardships, complexities and paradoxes present within South African and to some extent African society as a whole. Through highlighting the absurdities of a collectively experienced ‘everyday’, his work subverts the tragic, placing the viewer in a space where they are confronted by opposing feelings: the melancholic reality and the ironic hilarity of his compositions. \\n \\nBIOGRAPHY \\n \\nIn 2007, Neill graduated with distinction for the degree of Bachelor of Arts in Fine Art (Honours), at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, where he was co-awarded the Simon Gerson Prize for an outstanding body of work. In 2009, he graduated with a Postgraduate Diploma in Fine Art, majoring in printmaking. In 2013, Wright was named one of the ten emerging South African artists to watch by The Times, and he has exhibited in a number of group and solo shows as well as at numerous South African and International Art fairs. His works are housed in private collections in Europe, the United States, Australia and South Africa. \\n \\n \\nSOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2018 \\n \\nBuzzard Head, Everard Read Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nWilderness, CIRCA on Jellicoe, Johannesburg \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nThe Atrophy and the Ecstasy, Sulger-Buel Lovell, Cape Town \\n \\n2013 \\n \\nThe Hilarity of Reality, Circa on Jellicoe, Johannesburg \\n \\nSpectacular but Empty, The Lovell Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\n2011 \\n \\nProtect Your Roots, Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, Cape Town \\n \\n \\n \\nSELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2017 \\n \\nSpectrum, CIRCA, Johanneburg \\n \\nOff the wall: A group sculpture exhibition, Everard Read Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nBronze Steel Stone, Everard Read & Circa, Johannesburg \\n \\n2014 \\n \\nLiberation un(masked), Sulger-Buel Lovell, London \\n \\n2013-14 \\n \\nSummer of Sculpture, Mount Nelson Hotel, Everard Read, Cape Town \\n \\n2013 \\n \\nWhack! Gallery In Toto, Johannesburg \\n \\n2011 \\n \\nSummer Salon, Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, Cape Town \\n \\nTLG Competition Winners, The Lovell Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\nWinter Salon, Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, Cape Town \\n \\n2010 \\n \\nOut Of Africa, Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, Cape Town \\n \\n \\n \\nSELECTED ART FAIRS \\n \\n \\n \\n2019 \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read booth \\n \\n2018 \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read booth \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read booth \\n \\nCape Town Art Fair, CTICC, Cape Town \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nTurbine Art Fair, Sulger-Buel Lovell, Johannesburg \\n \\n2014 \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Lovell Urban booth, Johannesburg \\n \\nTurbine Art Fair, Lovell Contemporary, Johannesburg \\n \\nCape Town Art Fair, Salon91 Contemporary, Cape Town \\n \\n2013 \\n \\nArt For Me, Lovell Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\nSydney Contemporary, Australia \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Lovell Gallery booth, Johannesburg \\n \\nTurbine Hall Art fair, Lovell Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\nStandard Bank National Arts Festival, Grahamstown \\n \\n2012 \\n \\nFNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read booth, Johannesburg"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452124930269"]

item.title: Nel Erasmus
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857994973 Nel Erasmus 1019 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917848285 [] [4981,25534] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nel Erasmus (born 1928 in Bethal, Transvaal Province, South Africa) is a South African artist. Erasmus obtained a BA in Fine Art at Wits and a NATC at The Witwatersrand Technical College in the early 1950’s. After teaching in art in Johannesburg and London, she settled in France in 1953, studying at the Academie Ranson, Ecole des Beaux Arts and the Sorbonne. Her first solo exhibition was in South Africa in 1957 and she is one of the earliest abstract artists of South Africa. Erasmus has produced thirty solo exhibitions, taken part in more than seventy group exhibitions and her writing has been widely published. Although Erasmus was never a ‘popular’ painter, her work received much critical acclaim and she was the only South African artist to be included in Michel Seuphor’s 1964 survey of abstraction, Abstract Painting: 50 Years of Accomplishment. \\n \\nNel Erasmus was an early proponent of Abstract Art in South Africa – both as a practice and a principle. Erasmus also influenced the South African art scene as director of the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG) (1966–1977). \\n \\nNel Erasmus worked at the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG) from 1957 as Professional Officer until her retirement as Director in 1977. She has contributed to the acquisition of artworks to public and corporate (especially Sanlam and Sasol) collections in South Africa, in particular the international modern and contemporary collection at the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG). \\n \\nErasmus’ notorious acquisition in 1973, the year Picasso died, of Pablo Picasso’s Tête d’Arlequin (1971) was made possible by funding from The Friends of the Museum organization. The acquisition of this painting of a clown met with resistance from conservative, censored, isolated, apartheid South Africa, “No normal person would like this painting”, and provoked Erasmus to write a paper about why the acquisition was made. \\n \\nNel Erasmus is in her 80s and still paints daily. The most recent exhibitions she has participated in were solo exhibitions in 2009 in the Dawid Ras Art Gallery (Johannesburg) and in 2015 in the Dawid Ras Gallery (Cape Town), and since then various group exhibitions. \\n \\n \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Nelson Makamo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857831133 Nelson Makamo 557 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640919650525 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452127551709", "gid://shopify/Product/9452127617245"] [19981,7389,24040,24044,24047,24048,24049,19957,19958,19959,19979,19963,19967,19971,19976,19982,19984] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nelson Makamo is a Johannesburg-based artist born in Limpopo, South Africa, where he dedicates his art to amplifying the voices of African children. Over a career spanning sixteen years, Makamo has risen as one of the world's most sought-after, young visual artists. His diverse portfolio includes, but is not limited to acrylic, print, watercolor, and charcoal drawings, with a keen focus on storytelling through candid portraits of children, capturing the resilience and beauty inherent in the human spirit. \\nTrained at the Artist Proof Studios in Johannesburg, Makamo's artistic journey began with three years of studying printmaking, providing a solid foundation. Continuing to evolve, he experimented with various materials, eventually finding his signature medium in charcoal. Makamo's unconventional work ethic embraces creative spontaneity, steering clear of detailed plans in his artistic process. Influenced by artists like Dumile Feni, Picasso, and Van Gogh, Makamo's globally acclaimed collections have graced exhibitions in South Africa, the USA, France, Italy, the Netherlands, England, and Scotland. His artwork challenges stereotypes in depicting African children, finding a place in prestigious collections worldwide. \\nBeyond the canvas, Makamo's impact extends to mainstream recognition, including an appearance on 'The Daily Show with Trevor Noah' and gracing the cover of Time magazine. Celebrated for creating a platform for young African artists to communicate through their art, Makamo's portraits exude strong emotions, reflecting the conviction, prowess, and determination of young Africans. His mixed-media style and unique mark-making technique distinguish him as a trailblazer in contemporary visual art, reshaping global perceptions of what it means to be an African child."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452127486173","gid://shopify/Product/9452127518941","gid://shopify/Product/9452127551709","gid://shopify/Product/9452127617245"]

Explore original artworks that blend painting, photography, and storytelling. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neo Matloga was born in 1993 in Mamaila, Limpopo, South Africa, and is currently based between Mamaila and Amsterdam. He studied Visual Art at the University of Johannesburg, and completed a residency at De Ateliers with a focus on painting. Matloga won the 2021 ABN AMRO Art award and the 2018 Koninklijke Prijs voor Vrije Schilderkunst. \\nSolo exhibitions include Mokete, MOU Projects, Hong Kong, China (2024); along came my eyes, Hermitage Amsterdam (2022), my hero is always next to me, Stroom Den Haag, the Hague (2021); Neo Matloga, S.M.A.K, Ghent (2021); Neo to Love, Fries Museum, Leeuwarden (2019) and Good Morning Midnight, De Ateliers, Amsterdam (2018) in addition to Stevenson (2020 – 23). \\nGroup exhibitions include Circulate: Photography Beyond Frames, Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam, the Netherlands (2024); Insistent Presence: Contemporary African Art from the Chazen Collection at Chazen Museum of Art, Wisconsin, USA (2023); Africa Supernova at Kunsthal KAde, Amersfoort, the Netherlands (2023); CODA Paper Art 2023 at CODA Museum, Apeldoorn, the Netherlands (2023); Brave New World: 16 painters for the 21st Century at Museum Fundatie, Zwolle (2023); When We See Us: A Century of Black Figuration in Painting, Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art, Cape Town, South Africa (2022), Kunstmuseum Basel, Switzerland (2023), BOZAR, Belgium (2025); We just want to be closer at Marta Herford Museum for Art and Galerie der Stadt Backnang, Germany (2022); HI-STORYTELLING at Sfeir-Semler, Hamburg, Germany (2021); ofte vojagantoj at Wilford X, Belgium (2019); Still Here Tomorrow To High Five You Yesterday at Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2019); Winter Sun at Stevenson, Amsterdam (2019); De Volkskrant Beeldende Kunst Prijs at Stedelijk Museum, Schiedam (2019); BIG AND PLENTY at Foundation AVL Mundo, Rotterdam (2019); About Face at Stevenson, Cape Town (2018); Koninklijke Prijs voor Vrije Schilderkunst at Koninklijk Paleis, Amsterdam (2018); Tell Freedom, 15 South African artists at Kunsthal KAdE, Amersfoort (2018); LET'S SEE, WHERE WERE WE, IN THE PIT OF DESPAIR at De Ateliers, Amsterdam (2017); Post It’s at South African Constitutional Court, Johannesburg (2016);Time Line at The Bag Factory, Johannesburg (2015); South African and Chinese exchange at Workers Museum, Johannesburg (2015) and South African New Voices at Washington Printmakers Gallery, Washington DC. \\n \\nHe has taken up residencies at Foundation AVL Mundo, Rotterdam (2019); Thami Mnyele Foundation, Amsterdam (2018); Zeitz MOCAA, Segera, Laikipia, Kenya (2018) and The Bag Factory, Johannesburg (2015).Matloga was nominated for De Volkskrant Beeldende Kunstprijs in 2019, and was among the artists shortlisted for the 2015 Taxi Art Award."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452274909405"]

item.title: Neo Matome
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858060509 Neo Matome 2870 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640919945437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131483869","gid://shopify/Product/9452131516637","gid://shopify/Product/9452131549405"] [24242,24243,24241] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neo Matome is a Motswana artist (b.1967, Johannesburg, South Africa). Neo works in various media, which include drawing, painting, installation and photography. She also incorporates the use of textiles in her practice. \\nGender, culture and socio?political issues inform her expression. Identity, belonging, parity and issues of equity – be it to land, education, health, economic or social opportunity are issues she addresses in her artworks but mainly from a gender perspective. She is interested in the intersection between culture, perception and power relations. \\nNeo has won prizes, with the most recent one being the prestigious 2024 National Arts Festival Best in Mentorship Award (Visual Arts) at the Gaborone International Conference Centre, awarded by the His Excellency the President Dr Mokgweetsi Masisi. Neo has participated in national, regional and international exhibitions including art workshops in Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia and Mozambique and a residency at the Vermont Studio Centre, Johnson, Vermont, USA, with her artworks represented in private and public collections locally and abroad. She is also an arts activist who has served in various roles to promote the visual arts in Botswana. \\nMs. Matome is one of Botswana’s key proponents in the official establishment of a formal Creative Industry economic segment of government, and a key contributor to the emerging contemporary art scene in Botswana since the mid-90’s. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452131483869","gid://shopify/Product/9452131516637","gid://shopify/Product/9452131549405"]

item.title: Nessi Penman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858191581 Nessi Penman 2558 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920273117 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154028253", "gid://shopify/Product/9452158419165", "gid://shopify/Product/9452181979357", "gid://shopify/Product/9452182634717", "gid://shopify/Product/9452182831325"] [20866,25578,25575,25577,25579,20904,21304] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nessi Penman is a contemporary impressionist impasto painter creating works which invite the viewer into the natural world of flowers and lush landscapes. \\n \\n'My desire when I paint is to create works which instill within the viewer a deeper sense of calm and appreciation for nature and the paradise we live in. My objective is to draw people into my artworks so that they can find the creative spirit within themselves. I believe that we are all artists - may not be in paint or clay or charcoal, but we have the power to create beauty in our own environments and share that with others. \\n \\nI cannot say for sure where my love for oil painting came from, but one of my earliest memories were when my mother would take me to the art store once a month on her payday and she would buy me 'paint-by-numbers' and I would fall in love with the smell of those little tubs of paint and the distinct smell of the linseed oil contained therein - every time. \\n \\n Growing up in South Africa, the African landscape and its rich colours embedded themselves within my spirit. Irma Stern, Vincent van Gogh and Claude Monet are the three artists whose work I resonate with the most. I love their use of texture, emotion and dominant brush strokes. \\n \\nIt makes you feel like you are observing a painting - not a photograph. Your eyes dance across the canvas trying to understand what the artist did and what they were seeing and feeling. As a self-taught artist, I have been guided by my intuition, the medium and the artwork itself. It is my personal experience that I am only a conduit - the artwork creates itself through me. \\n \\n I had the privilege of meeting Pino Daeni and Howard Behrens - contemporary masters who have inspired me in both genre and technique. \\n \\nI have a passionate love for nature and animals. My deepest desire is that I use my talent to bring the viewer closer to experiencing flora and fauna within their own homes - a relief from the concrete jungle we live in. \\n \\n Since the digital economy has afforded artists an opportunity to communicate directly with collectors, I revel in hearing from you and love building relationships with every single person who has one of my works.’ \\n \\n \\n \\nEXHIBITIONS \\n \\nGroup exhibition – Young Blood, Cape Town, South Africa, 2024 \\n \\nGroup exhibition - Flagstaff Gallery, Devonport Auckland, New Zealand 2022"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154028253","gid://shopify/Product/9452158419165","gid://shopify/Product/9452181979357","gid://shopify/Product/9452182372573","gid://shopify/Product/9452182634717","gid://shopify/Product/9452182831325","gid://shopify/Product/9452182962397"]

item.title: Ngoma KaMphahlele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858257117 Ngoma KaMphahlele gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920436957 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452109136093","gid://shopify/Product/9452109168861","gid://shopify/Product/9452109201629"] Explore the profound works of Ngoma KaMphahlele, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through vibrant compositions and rich cultural narratives, KaMphahlele’s art explores themes of heritage, identity, and social commentary, creating visually captivating and thought-provoking pieces. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ngoma KaMphahlele is a visual artist who uses photography to explore various themes, such as fashion, jazz, and the architecture of Johannesburg, migration, and home (the sense of belonging). \\nNgoma's artistic journey has been deeply influenced by the diverse cultural landscapes of South Africa. In 2018, KaMphahlele graduated from the Market Photo Workshop with an Advanced Certificate in the advanced photography program. \\nInspired by the vibrant fashion scene and the timeless art form of jazz, Ngoma started capturing the essence of both through his lens. His visionary photography not only showcased the beauty and intricacies of fashion but also captured the soulful essence of the jazz appropriators in their gatherings. This unique combination of fashion and jazz became a prominent feature in Ngoma's work, offering a mesmerizing blend of visual aesthetics and musical narratives. In 2023, he developed and exhibited a body of work titled \"JazzLand,\" which further solidified his reputation as a remarkable artist. \\nFurthermore, KaMphahlele has always been fascinated by the architecture of Johannesburg, a city that reflects the history, growth, and transformation of South Africa. By capturing the city's iconic buildings and structures, KaMphahlele aimed to shed light on the intersecting stories of urban development, cultural heritage, and personal experiences. Migration, home, and a sense of belonging are recurring themes in KaMphahlele’s body of work. Drawing on his own experiences and the stories of others, he examines the complex feelings and challenges faced by individuals who have left their familiar homes in search of new beginnings. Through his photography, KaMphahlele invites viewers to contemplate the notions of identity, roots, and the profound yearning for a place to call home. \\nThroughout the years, Ngoma KaMphahlele has participated in various exhibitions, showcasing his exceptional talent and thought-provoking work. Additionally, KaMphahlele received the prestigious Thami Mnyele Award in 2018, winning the Ekurhuleni prize. \\nCurrently, KaMphahlele is part of artists under the banner of occupying the gallery under the guidance and mentorship of esteemed artists Mary Sibande and Lawrence Lemaoana. This influential and nurturing artistic environment allows KaMphahlele to further refine his craft, experiment with new techniques, and continue to push the boundaries of his artistic vision."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452109136093","gid://shopify/Product/9452109168861","gid://shopify/Product/9452109201629"]

item.title: Ngozi Lebogang Chukura
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858289885 Ngozi Lebogang Chukura 2343 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920994013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088492253"] [20358,18375] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ngozi Lebogang Chukura is a multidisciplinary Nigerian/Motswana artist based in Botswana. She holds a BAFA from the Michaelis School of Fine Art and has participated in several group shows, including Surprize Surprize, the Joburg Fringe and the FNB Art Joburg fair. Her solo exhibition, 'The Shadow Journals' was held at the Alliance Francais in Gaborone in 2012. Chukura is an ardent feminist, and her poetry, short stories and op-eds have been published in Botswana Women Write, New African Woman Magazine, Galdem.com and the Stanford Journal of African Studies. \\n“I have been interested in the intersection between femme identities, nature and spirituality. I am also an avid consumer of contemporary popular media and culture.” The result has been a series of hybrid, pop-femme-flora subjects on paper and canvas, that document her exploration of contemporary feminisms and evidence her process of ‘writing’ contemporary mythologies. \\nHer fascination with nature-based religions and indigenous spiritualities has also allowed her explore the idea of contemporary myth-making that centers femme figures and imbues them with power. Her newer work does this quite literally by playing with scale and multiple mediums including thread and beads. \\n“With my work, I am investigating symbols and energies that come from ‘Where the Stories Live’, a nameless, ageless place that speaks directly to our imaginations when we hear, look, create meaning. We are in an ephemeral continuum. What is ancient and sacred was once contemporary and secular.” \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088492253"]

item.title: Nhlanhla Nhlapho
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858322653 Nhlanhla Nhlapho 638 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640922042589 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452127912157","gid://shopify/Product/9452127944925","gid://shopify/Product/9452127977693","gid://shopify/Product/9452128010461"] [3064,3062,3060,3061,24057,24060,24059,3063] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nhlanhla Nhlapo (b. 1988, Frankfurt, Free State, South Africa) studied fine arts degree four years programme at Tshwane University of Technology specializing in painting and has been teaching painting there since 2013. Nhlapo’s practice takes Dutch masters’ techniques and 17th century Dutch landscape painting as a point of departure, situating it in the South African landscape and his hometown of Frankfurt in particular and populating it with images from his family albums. The works engage both with the nature and cultural context of depiction in art history as well as the unspoken and unacknowledged politics of trauma within carried through landscape and implicit trauma of colonization, loss and confrontation between modernity and tradition in family photographs. Through many personal and day to day conflicts growing up in rural Free State and later moving to Gauteng and City Life, Nhlapo endeavors to create a personal narrative with this body of work, a symbolic longing to re-connect to the Land of his Ancestors; His reference to the Dutch Baroque Interior paintings reflects the firsthand experience of both his late grandmother and mother being Domestic workers and the hardship he experienced with their absence in his formative years during Apartheid. Nhalapo was awarded the 2018 Unisa Academic Portrait Commission of Chairperson Mr Simelane and the 2018 Artist residency at Lacreusette in France Boussac with Louis Jansen van Vurren. His first solo exhibition was with Lizamore Associates in 2019."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452127912157","gid://shopify/Product/9452127944925","gid://shopify/Product/9452127977693","gid://shopify/Product/9452128010461"]

item.title: Nic Bladen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862090973 Nic Bladen 659 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640922697949 [] [24103,24104,24106] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South African artist Nic Bladen has become known for his extraordinary botanical sculptures, which demonstrate the technique he pioneered of casting entire plants in bronze and sterling silver. Born in 1974 in Pretoria, Bladen trained in the field of dental technology, a discipline that requires incredible precision and attention to detail. After working for eight years making gold and porcelain crowns in various dental laboratories in South Africa and the UK, Bladen developed an interest in sculpture and began working at the Bronze Age Foundry, learning large-scale bronze casting as well as all aspects of metalwork. Knowledge of the two seemingly different fields of dental technology and bronze casting precipitated Bladen's experimentations in 2001: casting flowers and leaves. In marrying the micro and macro disciplines, he pioneered a way of developing perfect castings of organic matter. His way of preserving/fossilizing plants and flowers involves a method known as 'lost wax casting' (or cire perdue) and it involves creating moulds from actual organic material, and then transforming these into once-off sculptures of entire plants. \\n \\nNic's first solo exhibition, Peninsula, held at Everard Read, Cape Town in 2013, focused on the richness of botanical diversity that surrounds the artist's Simon’s Town studio, which is situated within the heart of the Cape Floral Kingdom, the smallest yet richest of the world's six floral kingdoms. For this show, concessions from landowners on the peninsula enabled Bladen to harvest such rarities as a Blue disa and the endemic Serruria villosa, amongst others. \\n \\nIn 2015, Nic worked as an Artist in Residence at Tswalu Kalahari, a private game reserve in South Africa's Northern Cape Province. The sculptures that he created during this time, a depiction of iconic, beautiful and strange Kalahari desert plants and trees, formed his second solo exhibition: Kalahari: A season at Tswalu, held at Everard Read, Johannesburg, in October 2015. \\n \\nThe title of Nic’s third exhibition ‘even in this unfavourable dry season’ is attributed to William J. Burchell, an early Cape botanist, in about 1810. Referencing the floral abundance and diversity encountered even during severe drought, this body of work depicts the tenacity of Cape Flora to tolerate this dryness, and the splendour with which it does so. \\n \\nNic’s fourth solo exhibition ‘Botanical Studies in Bronze and Silver’ was held at Everard Read London in May 2018 and introduced his unique cast botanicals to a while new audience. In January 2020, Nic’s fifth solo exhibition ‘Proteaceae’, was held at Everard Read Cape Town and focused on this spectacular and diverse plant family. \\nNic is currently preparing for his next solo exhibition, scheduled for February 2021, at Everard Read London. \\nNic's unique works can be found in the Standard Bank Art Collection, Ellerman House Cape Town, BMW and Oppenheimer Collections, as well as in many other prestigious private collections, both locally and abroad. \\n \\nSolo Exhibitions \\n2021 Upcoming solo, Everard Read, London, UK \\n2020 Arid, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2020 Proteaceae, Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2018 Botanical Studies in Bronze and Silver, Everard Read, London, UK \\n2017 Even at this unfavourable dry season, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2016 New Works, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2015 Kalahari: A season at Tswalu, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2013 Peninsula, Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions \\n2019 Masterpiece Art Fair London, Everard Read booth, London, UK \\n2018 FNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read CIRCA booth, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2017 Off the wall: A group sculpture exhibition, Everard Read Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2014 Exact Imagination: 300 years of botanically inspired art in South Africa. Curated by Cyril Coetzee. The Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nDesign Miami/Basel 2014, Southern Guild Collection, Basel, Switzerland \\n2012 Conversation Series, with Astrid Dahl, Jane Eppel and Katherine Glenday, Amaridian Gallery, New York, USA \\nSOFA (International Exposition of Sculpture Objects and Functional Art), with Amaridian Gallery, New York, USA \\n2011 Rare, joint show with Lisa Strachan at Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\nNatural Selection, joint show with Jane Eppel at Rust en Vrede Gallery, Durbanville, South Africa \\n2010 SOFA (International Exposition of Sculpture Objects and Functional Art), Amaridian Gallery, Chicago, USA \\n2009 Realisme, Art Fair, Amsterdam, Netherlands \\n2008 Group Exhibition at KZNSA Gallery, Durban, South Africa \\n2007 Greenhouse, group exhibition at Bell-Roberts Gallery, Lourensford, South Africa"}]}]} []

item.title: Nick Muzik
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641859895517 Nick Muzik 2636 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640929349853 [] [22324] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nick Mužík is a seasoned commercial and editorial photographer with over 15 years of experience, specializing in sports, fitness, and adventure lifestyle imagery. His background in sports and calm approach allow him to capture authentic, powerful images, even in high-pressure situations. \\n \\nNick’s passion for photography began at age eight, inspired by his father. After university, he pursued photography full-time in 2008, combining his love for the outdoors with his work. While running and cycling are his main focus, he also shoots alternative sports like surfing, sailing, and motorsports. \\n \\nMemorable assignments include the 400km Ultra Gobi in China and the Cape Epic, where he captured the action while riding on the back of a motorbike. Nick’s aspirations include covering events like the Dakar Rally and South Africa's Skyrun. Inspired by photographers such as Kelvin Trautman and Simon Bruty, he continually pushes himself to create impactful work."}]}]} []

[24648,24650,24651,24649,24647,24646] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicky Newman, 57, completed a Journalism and Media degree at Rhodes University as well as an honours in Psychology in the 1980s. She has had the privilege of attending the Maurits Binger Film Institute in Amsterdam and the Berlinale Talent Campus and, more recently, participating in the RMB Talent Unlocked mentorship programme in 2021. \\n Newman started making documentary films and has had a long and fertile career in this medium on camera and as an editor, producer and director. She also lectured at numerous educational institutions. \\nLooking for a quieter medium, Newman revived her love for stills photography and after being placed in various competitions and having her images published, she now sells fine art prints of her photography from galleries and shops in Cape Town. \\nShe is currently working on a book on her series A Place of Water, featuring images from the Sea Point Pavilion public swimming pool. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098362589","gid://shopify/Product/9014098395357","gid://shopify/Product/9014098428125","gid://shopify/Product/9014098460893","gid://shopify/Product/9014098493661","gid://shopify/Product/9014098526429"]

[22364] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicole Clare Fraser (b. 1989) is a Cape Town-based image maker and artist whose work focuses on built structures, interior spaces, and objects that evoke human presence, absence, loneliness, and tenderness. Her passion for photography ignited in high school, where she developed a deep appreciation for silver gelatin hand prints through darkroom work. This foundational interest led her to further her studies at Michaelis School of Fine Art, where she earned hr BAFA in 2012 and MFA in 2022. \\nIn addition to her personal artistic practice, Nicole is a photography lecturer specializing in darkroom techniques and printing. She has taught at various secondary and tertiary institutions in Cape Town and has enhanced her expertise through workshops with master printer Dennis Da Silva in Johannesburg. \\nNicole's solo exhibitions include \"Making Space: Traces of Absence, Stillness and the In-Between in Public Spaces\" (2021), which was re-exhibited at Daor Contemporary in 2023, \"untitled (façade)\" (2020), \"a quiet place | a collection of hand-printed silver gelatin prints\" (2018), and \"Garrisons\" (2012)."}]}]} []

item.title: Nindya Bucktowar
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862844637 Nindya Bucktowar 2090 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640935346397 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013431501021", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431533789", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431599325", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431632093", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431664861", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431828701", "gid://shopify/Product/9013431861469"] [15856,15860,15606,15614,15615,15592] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nindya Bucktowar (b. 1988 Mauritius) graduated with a Bachelor in Architectural Studies at Nelson Mandela University in 2013. She runs her own multidisciplinary design practice and ceramic business. She is the co-founder and co-director of Kalki Ceramics, Studio Kalki, NT Design Studio and Leather Studio. Bucktowar previously lectured at the Architectural Department of the University of KwaZulu-Natal (2019-2021) \\nAt the beginning of 2021 Bucktowar was selected for the RMB Talent Unlocked programme in association with Everard Read and Strauss & co, where she exhibited her work at Circa Gallery in Johannesburg. Following this her work was acquired by FirstRand art collection. \\nBucktowar held her first solo exhibition at the KZNSA Gallery in August 2021. She has also exhibited on notable group shows, including Bordeaux Art and Design (France), Galerie Revel (Paris), SCENORAMA KZN (Project by Gabi Ngcobo & JAVETT UP), CloutSA (CT), Spier Arts Academy (CT), Union House (CT), Spier Wine Farm (CT), Always Welcome (CT), Nirox (JHB), the Melrose Gallery (JHB), Ceramics Southern Africa (CT & JHB), Kim Sacks Gallery (JHB), KZNSA Gallery (KZN), Tamasa Gallery (KZN), African Art Centre (KZN), Tatham Art Gallery (PMB), 100% Design SA (Decorex) and Latitudes Art Fair 2023 (JHB)(KZNSA gallery). \\nShe has undertaken various collaborative projects with Nando’s, CloutSA, Mr Price Home (Artist COLAB), Redbull, Durban Art Gallery, internationally acclaimed interior designers and South African Network Cities. \\nShe attended artist residencies at Imiso Ceramics (CT)(March-May 2022) and Hillford Pottery (Lindsay Scott). Awards includes Ndebele Premier Award, Ceramic Southern Africa (First Prize), DBR: Design Build Research, 2017 (First Prize) \\nIn December 2022, Nikhil Tricam and Nindya Bucktowar were announced as the winner of Nandos Hot Young Designer competition, led by Clout SA. They are currently working on various national and international art and design project, represented by Tracy Lynch, Clout SA."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013427896541","gid://shopify/Product/9013427962077","gid://shopify/Product/9013428486365","gid://shopify/Product/9013428551901","gid://shopify/Product/9013428617437","gid://shopify/Product/9013431501021","gid://shopify/Product/9013431533789","gid://shopify/Product/9013431599325","gid://shopify/Product/9013431632093","gid://shopify/Product/9013431664861","gid://shopify/Product/9013431828701","gid://shopify/Product/9013431861469","gid://shopify/Product/9013842280669"]

item.title: Nkabinde Mpendulo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863041245 Nkabinde Mpendulo 2864 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640935477469 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452147900637", "gid://shopify/Product/9452148064477", "gid://shopify/Product/9452148195549"] Discover the captivating work of Nkabinde Mpendulo, a South African artist exploring themes of identity, memory, and cultural expression through evocative visual forms. Explore available artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [25144,25145,25146,25147,25143] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Kwa-Zulu Natal, in March 2003, Nkabinde Mpendulo is a Johannesburg-based artist working across various mediums to explore systemic and epistemic violence in contemporary civilization. Nkabinde approaches this concept by looking at how institutionalized education and industrialization undermine relationships between humans, land, and language in the form of urbanization. In this way, Nkabinde comments on the remnants of Western oppressive powers over the “primitive nations” or the “Other”. \\nNkabinde completed his primary and secondary education in rural Kwa-Zulu Natal and began his tertiary education at BAT Center. He holds a bachelor’s degree in visual arts from the University of Johannesburg, obtained in 2024. Nkabinde participated in various group shows, including a painting exhibition in Fox Wood House in JHB in 2022; a printmaking show with the Pretoria Association of Art in 2023; the UJ Visual Art 3rd year grad show, and the UJ FADA show at the University of Johannesburg in 2024."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452147900637","gid://shopify/Product/9452148064477","gid://shopify/Product/9452148195549","gid://shopify/Product/9452148326621","gid://shopify/Product/9452148457693"]

item.title: Noa Hall
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864024285 Noa Hall 2822 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640936624349 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452121456861"] Discover the work of Noa Hall, a South African visual artist exploring the relationship between images and the human body through multimedia, photography, and performance. Featured graduate from the University of the Witwatersrand. [23710] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Noa Hall is a South African artist, she was born in 2000 in the city of Johannesburg. After graduating with an honours degree in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand in 2023 she, along with some fellow graduates, founded the artist colllective and studio space House of Special Things where she continues to practice and collaborate. \\nHer work employs a range of mediums and techniques, traversing between video art, painting, some printmaking and installation building. Hall enjoys creating large-scale experiential artworks. Her painting practice consists of a curiosity around the graphic mark. \\nShe draws inspiration from the versatility of image within social media, cartoons, the internet, manga, comic books, posters and images confronted in everyday life. She conceives of her work as claustrophobic mind-maps or orientation devices. Surfaces \\nonto which she can measures different objects and representations against one another externally from herself. \\nShe is interested in the predicament of inhabiting a body that is bound within space, located amongst many other objects and beings - embedded within varying systems, biological, interpersonal, social, technological, cybernetic and environmental. She uses her \\nwork as a way to investigate and study this experience. Her work therefore often deals with space, proximity, intimacy and suffering."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452121456861"]

item.title: Nobukho Nqaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864057053 Nobukho Nqaba 587 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640937050333 [] [16045,16046,16047] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nobukho Nqaba was born in Butterworth located in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. At the age six, she and her family moved to Grabouw in the Western Cape and later attended Luhlaza High School in Cape Town. She is a graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town(UCT) where she majored in photography and was mentored by Svea Josephy and Jean Brundrit (2012). In 2012, she was awarded the Tierney Fellowship and was the recipient of reGeneration3, a photography focused initiative by the Musee de l’Elysee. Nqaba holds a Post Graduate Certificate in Education Visual Art and Theory from the UCT (2013). \\n \\nShe has embarked on several teaching endeavours through her role as Visual Art and Digital Photography Educator at the Peter Clarke Art Centre. Nqaba is currently a Lecturer of Photography at the Red & Yellow Creative School of Business. \\n \\nNobukho Nqaba graduated from the Michaelis school of Fine Art (Cape Town, South Africa) and was the 2012 Tierney Fellowship recipient. In 2015 she was one of only two photographers from Africa selected for reGeneration3 – a travelling exhibition and publication. Nqaba has exhibited in a number of international exhibitions, including Photo Lagos (2015) and Duro Olowu’s Making and Unmaking exhibition at Camden Arts Centre, London (2016). \\n \\nNqaba has exhibited widely including at the SOLAR Festival (Brazil: 2018); FITE Festival of Textiles: Clermont Ferrand (France: 2018); Africa Africa (Milan, Italy: 2018); GETOXOPHOTO (Spain: 2017); China Afrika (Germany: 2017); Also Known As Africa: Contemporary Art and Design Fair (France: 2016); Making & Unmaking: An exhibition at the Camden Art Centre (U.K.: 2016); reGeneration3 (UK, USA, Mexico and Switzerland: 2015-16); Designing Africa 3.0 (Spain: 2016), LagosPhoto Festival (Nigeria: 2015) and Against Time, Bamako Encounters (Bamako, Mali: 2015)."}]}]} []

item.title: Nola Ayoola
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864515805 Nola Ayoola 2510 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640937214173 [] [19991,19990,19992] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nola Ayoola (b. 1992) is a multidisciplinary artist whose works are her visual journal. \\n \\nThrough sculptures, portraiture, woven and cut out abstract compositions they encapsulate the philosophy that ‘you cannot understand what you cannot pull apart’. Her works are an observation of her heritage and its profound impact on her identity by storytelling through varying lenses in which she sees and imagines, while connecting to and interpreting objects. \\n \\nNola’s work is both theoretically and physically layered as a core voice, it's a study of dismantling and assembling, while telling stories of interconnection and the synchronisation between the past, present and what is to come. She describes her work as reticulations of the state of dreams and experiences. \\nHighlighting the varying complexities of identity, she is heavily triggered by hyper- sensory processing of sensitivity and synesthesia - naturally connecting sounds, colours and emotions to each other, it allows her to capture essence. \\n \\nNola’s visual languages pay homage to traditional African craftsmanship practices, - hand dyed indigo to carved block printing and weaving. The process of hand printing layers (an ode to Yoruba carving techniques and traditional Adire textiles) holds equal importance to the subjects. \\n \\nWhilst constructing/ deconstructing; her works celebrate representation and shared narratives. She is nurturing recurring themes of her interpretations of womanhood, social constructs of gender, human interaction with communities and environments, Yoruba tradition, spirituality, individualism, auras and the seen/ unseen."}]}]} []
