item.title: Paul Senyol
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641884831965 Paul Senyol gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640964575453 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452266979549"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"PAUL SENYOL is an abstract painter who reflects the details of everyday life, paired down to an empathy with colour, line and form. His work is a crafted response to his wonderings through various spaces. The colours and textures of urban and natural environments inform his spontaneous practice in the studio where every material he uses – acrylics, pastels, ink, pencils and spray paint - is chosen for the particular mark it can contribute to a finished composition. Senyol has been studying art and the mark since his fascination with skateboarding magazines as a teenager in Cape Town. Skateboarding emerged as a gateway to early creative works on the street and remains an important part of Senyol’s experience of urban spaces. He makes regular visits to the public library to source graphics, album covers, magazine layouts and illustrations. Senyol’s unique visual language is founded on the inevitable change and flux in environments. His works are testament to the translation of experiences into form."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452266979549"]

item.title: Pauline Mazibuko
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641884143837 Pauline Mazibuko 2368 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640965918941 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452064178397"] [18792] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Pauline Mazibuko's (b. 1972) work deals mainly with women and children and the everyday struggles they go through. She grew up in a community where being a woman was viewed as being less than perfect; witnessing a lot of female and children abuse as a norm in the community. \\n \\nMazibuko was raised by both my parents, her father showed respect and love to her mother. And in turn, taught him how not to be treated badly by anyone. Mazinuko's parents taught her self-respect and to never accept less than what one deserves. Makibuko's home became a sanctuary when all you see around you is heartache. Most, if not all Mazibuko's works, are a recollection of what she saw and experienced in her youth, of how she imagined the women/children felt. Her work also reflects their need to be seen and heard, their reason to go on another day amidst the heartache and pain they experienced daily. Mazibuko depicts how these mothers and children always found a way to smile, love, and be free. \\n \\n\"The world should see that it doesn't take much for someone to love, laugh and cry. Small things that may seem non-important to you, mean the world to someone else.\" says Maibuko."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452064178397"]

item.title: Pebofatso Mokoena
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641885192413 Pebofatso Mokoena 398 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640966443229 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013328019677","gid://shopify/Product/9013947072733","gid://shopify/Product/9013947105501","gid://shopify/Product/9013947138269"] [8148,14566,14567,20257,14569,20258,20259] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Pebofatso Mokoena was born in Alberton in August 1993, 8 months before South Africa’s first democratic elections. He completed his high school career at Bracken High School in 2011 acquiring both a distinction in Visual Art and the Design School Art Trophy. In 2014 he completed his NDip (Visual Art) at the University of Johannesburg. Mokoena has participated in a number of competitions and curated exhibitions including Thami Mnyele Fine Art Awards, Diptych, That Art Fair 2015, Fresh Produce in 2014, Inner Nature in Cape Town, Fortunes Remixed, and South African Voices: A New Generation of Printmakers in Washington DC. \\n \\nMokoena’s interest lies in the entangled organisations of how organic and man-made geographies shape multiple environments. Through interdisciplinary practices which include, primarily, painting and printmaking – but not limited to drawing and film and the use of online platforms, Pebofatso uses his own personal narratives and a consistent application of experimental enquiry as tools to make sense of the chaotic integratedness of the current world he lives in. \\n \\nMokoena’s work orbits in between critical discourses across the spheres of visual art architecture, global culture, and aesthetics. These interests at times open and bridge gaps in his own understanding of the importance of being alive in a world that, in theory, in becoming smaller and smaller. \\n \\nPebofatso Mokoena’s work lies in the Springs Art Library Collection, the South African Embassy Art Collection (in Washington, D.C.), the Smithsonian Museum of African Art in Washington DC, and other private collections. \\n \\n_ \\n \\nPebofatso Mokoena first collaborated with the team at David Krut Workshop (DKW) in the production of a hard-ground etching in 2018. It was titled Statistical Weakness and later shown at the 2019 iterations of Fine Art Print Fair (hosted at Parktown Girls), Turbine Art Fair and LATITUDES Art Fair. The collaboration built on the relationship Mokoena established as an intern at David Krut Projects (DKP) in 2016. \\n \\nIn 2019, he was commissioned among four other artists to do a multi-colour silkscreen print for LATITUDES Art Fair as part of their VIP Package. The resulting print ¾ Progress on the Edge of Play was completed in collaboration with silkscreen expert printer Roxy Kaczmarek from DKW and displayed prominently at LATITUDES. \\n \\nSolo Exhibitions \\n \\n2020 – Internal Probes – David Krut Projects, Johannesburg \\n \\n2018 - Inside Jobs - Bag Factory, Johannesburg \\n \\n2017 - The Pebofatso Experience - Hazard Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions \\n \\n2020 – ARCOLisboa – First Floor Gallery - Harare \\n \\n2019 - Songs of Sankofa - First Floor Gallery - Harare \\n \\n2018 - Open Studio - Nazdik Precinct - Tehran, Iran \\n \\n2018 - ArtNext Art Fair - Hong Kong \\n \\n2017 - Disclosure - SMAC gallery Johannesburg \\n \\n2017 - Atomic Peace - Bag Factory Johannesburg \\n \\n2016 - POST-ITS - Constitutional Hill Johannesburg \\n \\n2016 - Between South Africa and Iran - NoMans Gallery - Tehran \\n \\n2016 - Beasts of No Nation - Hazard Gallery - Johannesburg \\n \\n2015 - 30|30 - Springs Art Gallery - Johannesburg \\n \\n2014 - South African Voices: A New Generation of Print makers - Washington DC \\n \\n2014 - Shared Inheritance - The Cosmopolitan Johannesburg \\n \\n2013 - Diptych: presented by Assemblage - Johannesburg \\n \\n2013 - 2014 Fortunes Remixed - Port Elizabeth, Johannesburg, Cape Town \\n \\n \\n \\nSelected Residencies \\n \\n2019 - First Sol o residency - First Floor Gallery - Zimbabwe \\n \\n2018 - artist-in-residence - Bag Factory - Johannesburg \\n \\n2018 - Artist-in- Residence - KOOSHK Tehran - Iran \\n \\n2017 - Artist-in- Residence - Nirox Foundation \\n \\n \\n \\nAwards \\n \\n2019 - Emergi ng Pai nters Competi ti on Fi nali st \\n \\n2019 - JP Mor gan/ Arts and Cul t ur e Tr ust Abadali Arti sts’ co-creati on programme \\n \\n2015 - Assemblage/African Arts Trust Studio Bursary"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013328019677","gid://shopify/Product/9013947072733","gid://shopify/Product/9013947105501","gid://shopify/Product/9013947138269"]

item.title: Peter Eastman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641885552861 Peter Eastman 2623 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640967262429 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154061021","gid://shopify/Product/9452156092637","gid://shopify/Product/9452266717405"] [25356,25355] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Peter Eastman (b. 1976) is a British-South Africa contemporary painter renowned for his experimental approach to painting. Based in Cape Town, Eastman works across a variety of mediums and techniques, employing substrates like aluminum and materials such as chrome, enamel, resin, wax, graphite, and oil paint. His process involves reworking, scraping, and incising the surface of his pieces to create paintings that balance representation and abstraction. \\nKnow for his bold use of base colours, Eastman's work often appear mono- or duo-chromatic, featuring subtle lines and shapes articulated by thin ridges of paint or resin, adding dimension and complexity. Eastman's work is profoundly influenced by his surroundings—his lived interiors, cityscapes, family photographs, and landscapes familiar to him. His unique process disassembles and re-configures these images, producing new compositions that evoke a dreamlike familiarity, subtly blending memory and mood. As an artist rooted in the physicality of painting, Eastman’s work retains an authentic painterly quality, transcending the digital distortions and re-configurations prevalent in the age of technology. \\nEastman has been featured in numerous solo and group exhibitions, with his work shown at prominent galleries such as Barnard Gallery, SMAC Gallery, and Everard Read. He has also been recognized in various art fairs, including the Cape Town Art Fair and the FNB Joburg Art Fair. His paintings have attracted international attention, with his pieces being offered at auction and achieving notable prices, including a record sale of \"Riverbank I\" at Aspire Art Auctions in 2019. \\nThrough series such as Deep Chine, which explores a remote South African forest landscape, Eastman continues to evolve his practice, drawing on the natural world and his personal history to inform his ever-changing body of work."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452154061021","gid://shopify/Product/9452156092637","gid://shopify/Product/9452266717405"]

item.title: Phanuel Shivambu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641886208221 Phanuel Shivambu 2848 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640974635229 [] Discover Phanuel Shivambu, a self?taught South African artist from Limpopo, based at Asisebenze Art Atelier in Johannesburg. His multidisciplinary practice explores urban identity, spirituality, and inner city life. View his works and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [23942] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phanuel Shivambu is a self-taught artist born 1979 in the village of Mapapila, in Malamulele, Limpopo. It was while attending Nghunghunyani Secodary School that he discovered his artistic side. \\nWhile fascinated and inspired by ideas from philosophy and spirituality, his work continues to explore and express the ideas he thinks are interesting to explore."}]}]} []

item.title: Phila Hillie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641886372061 Phila Hillie 1425 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640974733533 [16768,16767] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phila Hillie is an architecture graduate, artist and illustrator from South Africa. She comes from a family that has been involved in politics and this has influenced her interest in space and history within the African context. \\n \\nHillie’s artwork is an exploration of women, culture/tradition and space through the use of form and color. Her aim is to portray women, their stories and how all these stories are not monolithic. The idea is to simplify the subjects and themes without extracting their beauty and presence. Phila is interested in creating spaces in which women feel safe and can explore themselves without the pressure and standards that society often projects on to them. Culture/tradition in a modern context and how we can maintain a relationship with it is also a recurring theme in her work. \\n \\nHillie’s art is influenced by the years she spent studying architecture at the University of Cape Town, her experience as a young, black African woman and her Xhosa heritage. She also briefly lived in India during high school through an exchange program she took part in. Whilst she is still exploring her artistic style, she is drawn to a simple style that makes use of bold colour palettes."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013452341469","gid://shopify/Product/9013452439773"]

item.title: Philippa Allen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641886470365 Philippa Allen 1687 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640975716573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013433204957", "gid://shopify/Product/9013433303261"] [18357,15994,15990,17951,17952,16682,18358,15993,15988,18359] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Philippa Allen (b. 1969, SA) lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. Studied BA Fine Art at the University of Stellenbosch, (1990-93.) \\n \\nPhilippa Allen uses the landscapes that surround her home as reference and inspiration for the pictures that she draws. “I am surrounded by very beautiful scenes. In these landscapes I try to show the beauty, imagine the destruction and absence of nature and glorify the steadfastness of the environment.” \\n \\nShe has participated in group and solo shows since 2003. The most recent notable solo shows being Evoking Place at Sisonke Gallery, Cape Town in June 2023 and Ghostscapes at the AVA Gallery in Cape Town, November 2020. Some of her artworks were selected for the Ninety One Collection 2021, a showing of South African artists at their head office in London. \\n \\nShe plays with the surface of roughly rendered charcoal and panpastel drawings or manipulated charcoal scenes on top of acrylic layering to convey the different environmental themes that she is dwelling on. Some of the ways in which she does this is by erasing lines, taking from the drawn landscape or by pulling lines through the images. The gestures and disruption on the surface of the artworks are there to alter the scene and to challenge the viewer to examine it. She also explores the links between our mental health, wellbeing and nature. \\n \\n“Humans strive for meaning and validation in life and, in the pursuit of that quest, sometimes miss the simple reflections of meaning and belonging that are presented to us by our local natural landscapes. We also sometimes choose to ignore the fact that these landscapes are often under threat.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013433204957","gid://shopify/Product/9013433303261","gid://shopify/Product/9013449752797"]

item.title: Phillemon Hlungwani
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641886732509 Phillemon Hlungwani 341 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640976437469 [] [24102] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phillemon Hlungwani is recognised as one of the most accomplished contemporary artists now working in South Africa. Known predominantly for his large-scale charcoal drawings depicting scenes from rural life and formal and informal settlements, his work is rooted deeply in a sense of community and the traditional values that endure there. Many of his recent drawings include proverbs in his first language – xiTsonga – as ­titles. These proverbs are often difficult to translate into English but they communicate an essential moral idea – showing how members of a particular community are either sustaining or betraying the values of the people living there. The people are inseparable from their environment, although his more recent images have introduced colour into the clothing of his protagonists to help them stand out in all their vibrancy and humanity. \\n \\nThe scenes he depicts are usually full of motion and life – the characters bursting with thoughts, opinions and yearnings, which are communicated further through the arcs and lines that weave the different parts of each drawing together. Everything is connected. There is no distinction between the internal or the external, the animate or inanimate, the material or the spiritual. As a boy, Hlungwani used to herd goats and cattle and look after chickens – and this relationship with the animal world is often present in his work. Trees were also a source of shade and food – both for animals and people – as well as providing places for community debates, ceremonies and prayer. \\n \\nSometimes, as in the work entitled Vutlarhi bya lava kulu ka hina (The Wisdom of the Old People), trees embody and stand for the human – carrying in their roots and leaves and fruit all that has passed beneath them. Hlungwani is suggesting throughout his work that people who live in the simplest places with few possessions can still lead good, dignified lives and remain happy. They may have places to go and things to do, but they know who they are – where they have come from and where they are going."}]}]} []

He studied Professional Printmaking at Artist Proof Studio from 2007 to 2009. His works are part of several notable collections, including ARUP (Melrose Arch Johannesburg), Bus Rapid Transit Stations (Johannesburg), and Sonke Gender Justice Network (Johannesburg). Mabote currently lives and works in Protea Glen, Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa."}]}]} []

item.title: Phumulani Ntuli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641890599133 Phumulani Ntuli 393 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640978993373 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355348189", "gid://shopify/Product/9013397323997", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008250589", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008283357", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008316125", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008348893", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008381661", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008414429"] Phumulani Ntuli (b. 1986, Soweto) is an acclaimed multidisciplinary artist whose work spans artistic research, sculpture, video installations, and performative practices. His art critically engages with archives, surveillance, and historical narratives, striving to illuminate history's gaps and silences. Ntuli's practice invites viewers to reconsider historical and contemporary narratives, drawing connections between personal heritage and sociopolitical issues. [22037,11001,22044,22040,22038,22039,22041,22042,22043,22034,22035,22036,14030] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phumulani Ntuli (b. 1986, Soweto) is an acclaimed multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans artistic research, sculpture, video installations, and performative practices. His work critically engages with notions of archives, surveillance, and historical narratives, striving to illuminate history's gaps, silences, and remnants. Ntuli holds a Masters in Fine Arts - Art Public Sphere from ECAV in Switzerland, where he was awarded the Prix-excellence for his ongoing research project Permutations of an Event \\nNtuli's artistic process is characterized by a convergence of documentation, image, and visual engagement, creating spaces that challenge viewers to reconsider historical and contemporary narratives. He consistently engages diverse audiences, drawing connections between personal heritage and broader sociopolitical issues, particularly within the context of decoloniality. \\nHis career includes notable exhibitions and performances, such as the 2016 Kampala Biennale in Uganda curated by Elise Atangana, the Bone Performance Festival in Bern, Switzerland, and the Act Festival in Geneva, Basel, Sierra, and Zurich. Ntuli has also participated in residencies at the Fondazione Pisteletto in Italy and the Alps Art Academy in Switzerland. \\n \\nIn his own words, Ntuli explores the collision between reality and fantasy, using this intersection to investigate memory and its fragmented, unreliable nature. His recent solo work, \"Kunanela iphuzu emafini / Echoes of the Point Cloud,\" debuted at the FNB Art Joburg Fair in 2023, incorporating mixed media collages and unique works on paper. The project delves into South African motion picture history, merging it with contemporary data and artificial intelligence to re-contextualize past narratives within a changing socio-political landscape. \\nNtuli's practice often employs collage techniques, both digital and manual, to create 'pseudo-reality' that challenges preconceptions and invites alternative perspectives. His work, deeply rooted in his South African experience, is both personal and powerfully political, aiming to observe, analyze, reflect, and bring people together. \\nImage credit: Sublime Photography and Design"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013310980317","gid://shopify/Product/9013355348189","gid://shopify/Product/9013397323997","gid://shopify/Product/9014008250589","gid://shopify/Product/9014008283357","gid://shopify/Product/9014008316125","gid://shopify/Product/9014008348893","gid://shopify/Product/9014008381661","gid://shopify/Product/9014008414429"]

item.title: Phumzile Buthelezi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641892237533 Phumzile Buthelezi 611 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640979091677 [] [25418,3152,25419,24120,25420,24121] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phumzile Buthelezi (b. 1976) is a fine artist that graduated at Artist Proof Studio with print making. Her work extends the qualities of nature; as beautiful, life-giving, and a formidable force which also examples female energy of strength, beauty and nurturing qualities – exhibiting the feminine not as an idolization and mystical far-fetched concept but as a real force that shapes us and our and understanding of the world and ourselves related to the world. The works are templates of wisdom, that offer a reflection with the maternal relationships in our lives. \\nShe is currently working on multiple projects, including a sculpture/illustration exhibition with Candice Berman and exhibited work in the 2020 Turbine Art Fair amongst many others. Her most recent exhibition is Ambiguous with MMArthouse which opened on the 15th of August 2020."}]}]} []

item.title: Puleng Mongale
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641897906397 Puleng Mongale 364 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640984465629 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013327790301"] [8145,4065,4073,4074,21492,4064,4063,21493,21495,4071,4070,4069] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Puleng Mongale (b. 1991) is a contemporary visual artist based in Durban, South Africa, specialising in photography and digital media. Since the inception of her art practice, Mongale has used her creative expression to probe into her subconscious to process and articulate her lived experiences. \\nOver the years, her artistic journey has evolved into a reflective exploration of themes that resonate with her as a young African woman in South Africa. Mongale’s work explores themes related to spirituality, belonging, identity, and womanhood. \\nMongale’s work has been shown in multiple group exhibitions including Africa Foto Fair, Abidjan (2023); Abadali Group Show, Johannesburg (2022); The Fold Group Show, London (2021); Beyond Group Show, Cologne (2021); Terrains of Possibility at the Rele Gallery in Lagos (2021); Heaven on Earth, an online solo exhibition with Doyle Wham x Latitudes (2021); and Ambiguous, a group exhibition with mmArthouse (2020). \\nIn an ever-evolving society, art serves as Mongale's resistance, a tool to define her narrative on her terms."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013327790301","gid://shopify/Product/9013361115357"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641898627293 Purnaa Deb gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640984662237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452258001117"] Explore the evocative artwork of Purnaa Deb, a contemporary artist known for her deeply introspective and culturally rich pieces. Her work delves into themes of identity, memory, and human experience, using intricate compositions and dynamic textures. Discover and collect her original creations on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Purnaa Deb grew up in Kolkata, India, and completed her academic art education (under- and post-graduate degrees) in Printmaking from the faculty of Visual Art, Rabindra Bharati University, India. \\nPurnaa has been awarded Gold Medal for her BFA in 2010; and a Certificate of Merit at the annual exhibition of MFA in 2012. Purnaa also received a Fellowship in Printmaking Department at the National Lalit Kala Academy of the Government of India for the year 2014-2015. \\nBesides participating in several group exhibitions and community-based art activities, Purnaa has been working as an art educator and engaged in different schools and institutions, teaching different methods of arts and creative practice using interactive communicating tools. The artist moved to Johannesburg, South Africa in 2015 and worked as an intern at David Krut Projects, Johannesburg, where she received the professional printmaking studio experience that elevated her overall technical knowledge. Purnaa also worked as a printmaking teacher at Artist Proof Studios, Johannesburg from 2017, providing basic understanding and training in different printmaking technics to the students. \\nPurnaa is committed to her printmaking practice and has participated in several group shows and art fairs as a fellow member of The Printing girls since 2018. Her artworks have been acquired for international collections and one of her pieces featured in the comic magazine published by the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in 2015. In 2021 Purnaa was awarded the Printmaking Residency with the National Arts Festival in Grahamstown/ Makhanda."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452258001117"]

item.title: QAQAMBILE Beading Collective
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641899348189 QAQAMBILE Beading Collective gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985120989 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Cape Town-based beading, art and crafts collective Qaqambile and run by women crafters, artists and maker are the masterminds informing premiere artworks that feature beading by leading artists from across South Africa. \\nFor the exhibition 'Embodying Her, 2023' the women have for first time in their history as a collective the women feature artworks made by themselves and that brings to life their own life stories through beading. \\nThe master-beaders of Cape Town partnered with iconic artist and visual activist Zanele Muholi to collborate on the production of several works in the series, and produced beautiful beaded-paintings of their own - works that powerfully convey their journey of economic striving towards independence as women."}]}]} []

item.title: Queezy Babaz
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641900200157 Queezy Babaz 2633 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985448669 [] [21709,21700,21712,21703,21698,21702,21707,21708,21711,21710,21704] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Queezy Babaz (b. 1992) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans fine art, fashion, and performance. Through mediums such as printmaking, videography, drag performances, and DJ sets, Queezy constructs immersive worlds that blend fantasy with radical social commentary. Their work challenges and redefines the experiences of being queer and coloured in South Africa, deconstructing notions of masculinity, sexuality, and the body. Themes of gender norms and identity politics are central to their practice, where artistic craftsmanship meets authenticity to create pieces that are visually captivating and socially provocative. \\n \\nQueezy's interactive artworks foster spaces of protest, empowerment, and celebration, disrupting normative narrative. Trained in pottery, painting, sculpture, and graphic design at Belgravia Art School, Queezy later earned a BTech in Fashion Design with a distinction in specialized clothing technology from Cape Peninsula University of Technology. Their performances have been featured at institutions such a Gallery MOMO, Zeitz MOCAA, AVA Gallery, World Art Gallery, and Norval Foundation, while her work has gained international recognition in publications including I-D Magazine, New York Times, NATAAL, Paper Magazine, and Vogue Italia. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Rachel Seidu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641901871325 Rachel Seidu 2747 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986464477 Discover the powerful visual storytelling of Rachel Seidu, a contemporary photographer and artist featured on Latitudes Online. [22993] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rachel Seidu (b.1997) is a Lagos-based photographer and filmmaker whose work delves into the intimate and emotional aspects of human experience. \\n With a focus on capturing personal narratives, Seidu uses both conceptual and documentary techniques to create portraits that resonate with simplicity and depth. Her images invite viewers into the interior lives of her subjects, emphasizing authenticity and raw emotion, often exploring themes of identity, freedom, renewal, and self-expression. \\nHer photography serves as a meditation on identity, healing, and connection. Seidu’s work is marked by its quiet, affective power, engaging deeply with the emotions and stories of her subjects. \\nIn 2021, Seidu photographed the cover of the Booker Prize-shortlisted novel We Need New Names by NoViolet Bulawayo. She was shortlisted for the James Barnor Prize and Yaa Asantewaa Prize. In 2023, she collaborated with Yves Saint Laurent for a fanzine and exhibition at the Saint Laurent Rive Droite stores in Paris and Los Angeles. Additionally, she was selected for the Tremplin Jeunes Talents at the Planches Contact Photography Festival and residency in Deauville, France \\nHer exhibitions include Festival Planches contact (2024, Deauville), Freedom Multitudes (2024, Houston), YSL Rive Droite (2023, Paris/LA), Awa nibi (2023, Lagos/Hamburg), and Let’s Take a Moment (2022, Lagos). Seidu is a member of Black Women Photographers and the African Photojournalism Database."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014033613021"]

item.title: Ramarutha Makoba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902657757 Ramarutha Makoba 329 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986693853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052552925","gid://shopify/Product/9014052585693"] Explore the impactful artwork of Ramarutha Makoba, a South African artist known for using trees as metaphors for growth, knowledge, and community. His prints explore themes of personal and societal development. Makoba’s work has been exhibited internationally, and he plays an active role in art education and outreach through various community projects. [23623,23624] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ramarutha Makoba (b. 1984, Soweto, Johannesburg) is a talented artist who began his artistic journey at the age of 13 when he began attending art classes at a local community center. He refined his skills through workshops at the Johannesburg Art Gallery and completed a two-year course at FUBA (Federated Union of Black Artists). Makoba joined Artist Proof Studio in 2004, earning certificates of excellence in his first twp years, and completed his third year of professional printmaking in 2007. \\nMakoba’s artwork often uses trees as a metaphor for family and community life. He believes trees symbolize growth, knowledge, and productivity. The roots represent one's origins, while the stem and branches signify growth and success. His art reflects how communities come together for shade, support, and problem-solving under the tree, with the goal of inspiring individuals to relate to his work and bring about positive change in the world. \\nMakoba’s works have been displayed in numerous exhibitions, including the District Six 50th Commemoration Print Exchange (2016), solo exhibitions like “Change The World” (2016) at Art Room, and group shows at David Krut Art Gallery and Lizamore & Associates. Besides his practice as a full-time artist, Makoba is deeply involved in education and community outreach, facilitating art programs through the Artist Proof Studio’s ‘Artist in Arks’ and the Little Artists School Project in Berea."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052552925","gid://shopify/Product/9014052585693"]

item.title: Raymond Fuyana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903247581 Raymond Fuyana 332 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987775197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052716765","gid://shopify/Product/9014052749533","gid://shopify/Product/9014052847837"] [23626,23629,23627] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Raymond Fuyana was born in 1995 in Zimbabwe. He moved to South Africa, Johannesburg in 2009 seeking a good deaf school, where he attended St Vincent School for the Deaf in Rosebank. Fuyana joined the Saturday Youth Portfolio Development at Artist Proof Studio in 2015 as he was still in school. While at St Vincent he worked with artists at the Bag Factory for a year. \\nFuyana participated in the Strauss and Co. commission called Pierneef Interpreted in 2017. He made beautiful watercolour monoprints which were exhibited alongside Strauss and Co.’s collection of Pierneef original works at Turbine Art Fair. In 2018 he won the 1st prize in the printmaking category for the Strauss and Co. Irma Stern still life competition. The work was exhibited and sold out the Turbine Art Fair. This was followed by a wonderful article in the Sowetan on his journey as an artist. He plans to enroll for the 4th Year internship programme in 2019 to further his studies at Artist Proof Studio. \\n“My work is influenced by the Surrealism. I create a world of different perspectives. As a deaf person, my experience of the world and the hearing community can be seen in the work I make. I create dreamlike landscapes to express my feelings and mood. The spaces I creates can be viewed upside down and right up. In this body of work, I have used elements of classical architecture fused with African landscapes. The emoticon adds a contemporary element of how we communicate emotions using technology. I focus on capturing the confusion and communication breakdown I experiences daily. The crow plays an important role in my work because it represents me in these spaces. I am able to interpret noise and emotions by creating busy and strange spaces.” \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052716765","gid://shopify/Product/9014052749533","gid://shopify/Product/9014052847837"]

item.title: Rebaone Finger
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903345885 Rebaone Finger 2941 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640988004573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452155764957"] Rebaone Finger (b. 2001) is a South African multimedia sculptor. Her art dissects black identity, feminism, and consumerism, using the 'Cheese Girl' concept to explore opulence and contrasting realities. [25332,25623] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rebaone Finger (b. 2001) is a multimedia sculpture artist born in Bloemfontein and raised in Pretoria and Johannesburg. A graduate of Michaelis, her incisive practice is deeply engaged with the multifaceted politics or being, exploring themes such as silent rage, rest, freedom, luxury, black consumerism, social media, food, politics, naming cultures, blackness, and black feminism. \\nFinger's work critiques societal dynamics by adopting the South African use of food as a naming culture, reflecting the experience of living between worlds of access and lack. Central to her artistic commentary is the concept of 'Cheese Girl', a distinctively South African term denoting class privilege and social distinction. Finger re-imagines \"Cheese Girl\" as an articulation of blackness as opulence, wealth, and luxury. Her sculptures actualize this notion by merging Instagram-inspired tropes and symbols of perceived opulence with images and objects that embody contrasting realities, capturing the term's fluid and inherently complex nature."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452155764957"]

item.title: Reef Sithole
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903444189 Reef Sithole 1899 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640988365021 [] [14113] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I’m a fine artist from Johannesburg. My style of work is contemporary neo-expressionism infused with pop art and surrealism, pulling strong references from my rough-yet-unique upbringing in Soweto. The dichotomy of what Soweto is, is largely what inspires my work till today. I also produce a wide scope of multimedia visual art, exploring nuanced digital design themes, techniques and usage of soundscapes. Eventually enrolled at the prestigious National School of The Arts, by the tender age of 8, I was already engaged in art classes by my parents. With the inherent ability for draughtsmanship, art was always encouraged as an avenue away from the hotbed for drugs and violence which exists in Soweto. My accumulating gallery experience includes Artist Residency with The Fourth (2021), Death Row Dinner (2021), Fede group exhibition (2022) and Cape Town Art Fair (2022) My work is essentially an amalgamation of niche techniques, such as stitching, infused to create a completely new style. It feels extremely inspired; like a proposition for a new way of painting. And within this work, you can see the influence of legendary artists such as Basquiat, Bacon, Matisse & Warhol, and more. I’m a punk at heart, and that’s what resonates through my paintings. I experiment in digital design and soundscapes, unlocking two alternative career paths as a reputable graphic designer."}]}]} []

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903542493 Refiloe Namise 2615 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640988463325 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452100681949","gid://shopify/Product/9452100747485","gid://shopify/Product/9452100780253","gid://shopify/Product/9452100878557"] Refiloe Namise [21447,21446,21410,21411,21433,21434,21436,21407,21408,21409,21435,21437,21438,21439,21440,21441,21442,21443,21444,21445] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Refiloe Namise a Johannesburg-based artist who completed her MFA in Creative Research and Practice (2022) and a BA in Fine Art (2016) at the University of the Witwatersrand. \\n \\nNamise’s work explores the making and preserving of a place: Alexandra. Through various sites in Alex, her work re-members and re-articulates particular moments and histories. These engagements develop ways of writing, recording, storing and sharing social knowledge, heritage and culture. Though much of these concerns are reflected in the present configurations of Alex, a deepened understanding of its existence as a place often demands a return to its past. \\n \\nHer work is multi-disciplinary, incorporating image, text, sound, video and performance. Namise grapples with the notions of return, re-membering and re-articulation through poetic gestures in which she re- enacts historical moments."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452100681949","gid://shopify/Product/9452100747485","gid://shopify/Product/9452100780253","gid://shopify/Product/9452100878557"]

item.title: Regina Bardavid
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903706333 Regina Bardavid 436 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640989544669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013460041949", "gid://shopify/Product/9013460074717"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Regi Bardavid was born in Alexandria Egypt and has travelled extensively, living in Italy, Zimbabwe, Zaire and South Africa. She has remained firmly rooted in the ‘abstract’ throughout her career which spans more than four decades. Her inspiration comes from the act of play, “releasing the Self of all obligations and constrictions of upbringing.” \\n \\nMy artistic journey can be best described as a voyage through imaginary landscapes, where vibrant hues and non-figurative forms converge to evoke emotions and stir the imagination. Each painting is a spontaneous exploration, a dance of intuition, and a dialogue between myself and the canvas. Inspiration also emerges from the patterns left by coffee remnants, a ritual I adopted from my time in Egypt. These diverse stimuli ignite my creativity, leading me to seek surprise and discovery in my work. \\n \\nMeditation plays a crucial role in my practice, helping me enter a state of flow where paintings unfold organically. I embrace the notion of the Zone, where the act of creation feels effortless, allowing the artwork to manifest itself. \\n \\nDespite studying art history extensively, I ultimately returned to my roots in abstract expressionism, finding solace in its freedom of expression."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013460041949","gid://shopify/Product/9013460074717","gid://shopify/Product/9013853651165","gid://shopify/Product/9013853716701","gid://shopify/Product/9013853749469"]

item.title: Rémy Samuz
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641911931101 Rémy Samuz gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641017069789 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013439791325"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1982 in Cotonou (Benin) \\nLives and works in Benin \\n \\nThe playful dimension of creation often fades to the benefit, if I may say so, of the essential effort of the artist in the gestation of their work! \\n \\nArt is, for many artists, an outlet for their existential anguish, to the point that the notion of pleasure in creation is too often hidden in favor of a more ethereal, more intellectual dimension, which sees the creator giving birth to their works in pain and agony. \\n \\nRémy Ama SOSSOUVI, a native of Cotonou, now at the age of 40, has become a contemporary Beninese artist recognized both in his country and abroad. Since childhood he has always enjoyed manipulating materials, braiding, weaving and making miniature sculptures and, in so doing, bringing a variety of characters to life. \\n \\nThis passion, bizarre in the eyes of those around him, for whom things relating to art escape them, has long lead him to be considered a child \"not like the others”, one who spent his time having fun. He chose as his artist name, probably reluctantly, what within his family he was called, \"Rémy s’amuse\" (Remi’s having fun)! \\n \\nSAMUZ ’s professional training in general mechanics from 2001 to 2006 led him to become a Master Machinist, a position he held until 2008. Far from taking him away from his passion, this training taught him, on the contrary, to further master his favourite material which is metal. \\n \\nA machinist is a worker or craftsman who mechanizes and produces parts by removing material until obtaining defined shapes and dimensions, through the use of cutting, lathe or milling tools. In the case of a lathe, it is the tool that moves over the piece, while in the case of a milling machine it is the opposite. \\n \\nHowever, in 2003, Rémy’s decision was made, he would continue to \"have fun\" and make a career as an artist, even if he tried to demonstrate his seriousness to those close to him by continuing his apprenticeship and entering the world of work. Then in 2009, he took the plunge and trained for three years in fine art in the studio of the famous Beninese painter and sculptor Dominique ZINKPÈ. ZINKPÈ works with a variety of materials, however metal is not one of them, but he was able to guide and channel his disciple and give him the foundations for a career as an artist. And with what success! \\n \\nSpecialized books affirm that precise and methodical, the machinist is particularly skilled in carrying out calculations as well as having a fundamental quality, that of visualizing shapes in space, to meet production objectives. Rémy SAMUZ has been able to combine these different qualities as a technician with his sense of observation to the benefit of his creation. \\n \\nHe tells us that as a child he was fascinated by the ballet of weavers (a common passerine bird in West Africa) building their nests. From selecting the twigs, to weaving them into a shape that offers both comfort and safety, weavers offer an exceptional example of technique and creativity that earned them their common name. \\n \\nRémy SAMUZ quickly perfected a way of weaving wire that allowed him to create works, sometimes quite large, in which he combines rigidity and lightness with unusual dexterity. But there is also the sense of volume, transparencies and the expressions of the faces as, without exception, the artist only creates human figures. \\nThe artist goes far beyond that apparent lightness, that \"fun\" that has made him famous. His language allows him to express himself on the problems of society with which humanity, and especially that which surrounds him, is confronted. \\n \\nInviting contemplation and reflection, Rémy’s work, in lightness and transparency, nonetheless sharply evokes the troubles of our time, but always with an optimistic perspective that reflects the artist’s way of seeing the world. \\n \\nHis themes start from meditation, the necessary entry into oneself to achieve unity and sharing a common vision of things and beings in a constant desire to move the world forward. \\n \\nDignity, humility, but also moments of joy, all the movements of life are approached on very different scales, from the very large to the very small, in a dazzle of spidery wires. But his interventions are not limited to his artistic production. An activist committed to social phenomena, SAMUZ uses all kinds of media to spread his messages. \\n \\nHis white van is known throughout Cotonou having carried out an active campaign in favor of the prevention of the spread of COVID, or more recently for encouraging his fellow citizens to go and discover the exhibition, \"Art of Benin of yesterday and today: from Restitution to Revelation”, that took place from May to July 2022. \\n \\nIt was not for him just a simple incitement to go see works of art, including his own, but rather a true civic act to encourage the population to embrace their artistic production, famous for centuries and really work to claim their identity. \\n \\nRémy SAMUZ started exhibiting in 2013 in Benin, of course, but also very quickly in other countries and continents (France, Brazil, Senegal, etc.). Shortly thereafter he was “seen” by the VALLOIS Gallery in Paris which is very involved in the Beninese art world and which continues to promote his work. A famous and recognized artist, Rémy SAMUZ notably won the Gold Medal in the sculpture category during the Francophone Games in Abidjan in 2017. \\nWe wish him a long time to continue having fun to our delight! \\n \\nSylvain Sankalé \\nArt Critic \\nDakar, Senegal \\nJanuary 2023"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013439791325"]

item.title: Renée Rossouw
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641904066781 Renée Rossouw gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640990200029 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"RENEE ROSSOUW (b. 1985) is an artist, designer and architect based in Cape Town. Graphic, bold and colourful, Rossouw’s artworks are informed by a vast personal library of shapes and patterns – observed, recorded, transformed and abstracted over the years and stored in sketchbooks, on walls and inside plastic boxes. After obtaining a master’s degree in architecture in 2009, Rossouw was one of 13 students selected for the prestigious master’s programme in product design at European Design Labs, Madrid under director Jaime Hayon. Highlights include collaborations with IKEA in 2017 and 2019, participation in the Venice Biennale, Milan Saloni di Mobile, Madrid Art Fair, Moscow Design Week, Design Indaba; selection as 100% Design South Africa’s Feature Designer and recipient of the Best Product Design award in 2015. She is also a lecturer at UCT’s School of Architecture and has delivered talks at Design Indaba and Madrid Design Net Conference. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Reneilwe Mathibe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903968477 Reneilwe Mathibe 2065 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640990134493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052946141", "gid://shopify/Product/9014126248157", "gid://shopify/Product/9014126280925"] [25212,23631,25213,25417,22414,25416] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Reneilwe (Rene) Mathibe is a painter and writer living and working in Johannesburg. \\n \\nShe was born in 1989 in the North West Province, South Africa. She completed her Technology in the Visual Arts degree at the University of Johannesburg with Painting as a major. She currently works as Drawing and Visual Literacy Facilitator at Artist Proof Studio. Recent group exhibitions include Coming of Age: 21 years of Artist Proof and Images of Women. She was involved in a mural painting at the new Steve Biko Museum in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. \\n \\nHer work focuses on, and examines, themes such as sexuality and the pain felt by most lesbians owing to discrimination and hate. In her work this pain or discomfort is juxtaposed with soft and sensitive flesh."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014016442589","gid://shopify/Product/9014052946141","gid://shopify/Product/9014126248157","gid://shopify/Product/9014126280925","gid://shopify/Product/9133226098909","gid://shopify/Product/9133233275101"]

item.title: REWA
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641904165085 REWA gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986136797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452040749277","gid://shopify/Product/9452040814813","gid://shopify/Product/9452105859293","gid://shopify/Product/9452105892061"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"There’s an unmistakable air of confidence and self assuredness that radiates from the eyes of the muses, REWA masterfully captures on her canvases. Their gazes both invite you in like an old friend, yet still intimidate enough to keep you at bay, in the knowledge that the viewer is not entirely worthy of their presence. \\nRegality is the phrase best used to describe REWA’s work. Not in the gaudy sense that imposes its will, or shines so brightly one is forced to turn away - but in the quiet, subdued manner that commands respect and holds your attention effortlessly. \\nREWA’s bold figurative portraits are by all accounts an extension of the artist herself. A melting pot of varying influences, cultures, and experiences that have shaped and moulded a person that is as comfortable haggling the price of lace fabric in the heart of the hustle and bustle of Onitsha market, as they are blitzing through the high end boutiques of London and Paris. \\n??Born and raised between Nigeria and England, REWA’s hybrid upbringing greatly informs her work, and indeed perfectly depicts the sensation that is the modern ‘afropolitan’ woman. Forward thinking, progressive, uninhibited, and self-aware, yet still rooted, albeit loosely, in the expectations, duty and responsibility that tradition and ancient customs dictate.?? \\nIn REWA’s case, that tradition and ancient custom is that of the Igbo people of South-East Nigeria, who are often described as Nigeria’s most industrious and enterprising, as well as their most independent of thought and practice. The ancient value system and custom of the Igbo people and their fierce independence is evidenced in the themes REWA unpacks in her portraits, seen through a contemporary lens. Essential themes such as the importance of coming of age, engagement, marriage and playing one’s part in their community and Igbo society at large are fundamental to REWA, and seamlessly blend the old with the modern; adapted, but never compromised to suit the times. \\nWhat stands REWA apart from most contemporary artists today, is that she transcends the title of artist, and is all but in name, a historian, and chronicler of the evolution of her ethnic group, nation and continent in real time. Through her work, we witness firsthand the assertion and confidence of women; their ability to code switch, and dip effortlessly between the West and the African continent whilst retaining their essence, and above all else the liberty of having options, and not being restricted by the confines of patriarchy and perpetually subject to the male gaze as art history is all too often guilty of. \\nBeyond being aesthetically captivating, REWA’s work is intellectually stimulating, thought provoking and educational. Although working through the medium of acrylic paints, it is well within reason and justified to liken the importance of her practise to that of fellow compatriots and creative greats, Chinua Achebe and Chimamanda Ngozie Ndichie, whose work, like REWA’s has put an illuminating spotlight on both past and contemporary Nigerian society; its inhabitants and their worldview. \\nREWA eceived a BSc. in Physiology and Pharmacology from University College London (UCL). Never having received formal art training, she is self-taught and developed her innate talent from a very early age. She finds that her spirit is moved by what she refers to as \"depicted sentience\" and through the celebration of the female form and bright, vivid colours. \\n“My subject matter is woman, I celebrate her in many forms. I use traditional materials, ink, acrylic paints and brush on paper or on canvas, to capture an essence, making the paint assemble and the ink announce.” - Rewa. \\nREWA’s work was featured at the Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts (MoCADA) in Brooklyn, New York, at the Zeitz MOCAA Museum, Cape Town, South Africa, at the Contemporary Art Centre New Orleans (CACNO), New Orleans, USA and at the Nigerian National Museum, Lagos, Nigeria."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452040749277","gid://shopify/Product/9452040814813","gid://shopify/Product/9452105859293","gid://shopify/Product/9452105892061"]

[23932] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Richard Witikani is a contemporary artist. Richard Witikani is a Zimbabwean male artist born in 1967. Richard Witikani is an older, established artist from Zimbabwe who focuses on timeless landscapes of \\nhome. His main themes revolve around the power of land and belonging. Witikani's artistic practice primarily involves landscape painting, characterized by a traditional and timeless stylistic approach. \\nRichard Witikani’s first verified exhibition was Post Election Selection at Gallery Delta in Harare in 2000, and the most recent exhibition was When We See Us at Palais des Beaux-Arts (BOZAR) in Brussels in 2025. Richard Witikani is most frequently exhibited in Zimbabwe, but also had exhibitions in South Africa, Germany and elsewhere. Witikani has at least no solo shows but 39 group shows over the last 25 years (for more information, see exhibitions). A notable show was When We See Us at Palais des Beaux-Arts \\n(BOZAR) in Brussels in 2025. Other notable exhibitions were at Kunstmuseum Basel - Gegenwart in Basel and Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa - MOCAA in Cape Town. Richard Witikani has been \\nexhibited with Helen Lieros and Greg Shaw. \\nRichard Witikani is ranked among the Top 100,000 globally, and among the Top 100 in Zimbabwe. Witikani’s best rank was in 2025, the artist’s rank has improved over the last 3 years, with the most dramatic change in 2009. For a complete illustration of the artist’s career since 2000, please see the \\ncareer chart on the analytics page."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126798045"]

item.title: Rick Baloyi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641906983133 Rick Baloyi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640996327645 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452134957277","gid://shopify/Product/9452134990045"] Rick Baloyi {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I grew up at Tshivhuyuni village in Limpopo. My work is inspired by the culture and traditions in my home village but most importantly, by my family, the people that raised me. \\nI completed my BA in Visual Art at the University of Johannesburg in 2023 and am now currently awaiting graduation and my certificate award in May. \\nDuring the past few years I’ve been honing my skills and knowledge; now my art is recognized both nationally and internationally. \\nThroughout my career, I have participated in several art exhibitions and engaged in different types of art opportunities. \\nIn 2019 I was selected to be part of the 2019 Talent Unlocked program which included mentorship and culminated in an exhibition at RMB|Turbine art Fair. Later in 2019 I received a scholarship award from Nedbank in collaboration with Arts And Culture Trust and DALRO, Which also included an exhibition at the Market Theatre with other finalists from different departments. \\nIn 2020 I was invited to take part as an ALUMNI for Talent Unlocked at Turbine Art Fair. During the same year I also exhibited my works at Lizamore & Associates Gallery in a summer exhibition titled: OF THEE I SING, and another summer group exhibition at RK Contemporary titled: No Holds Bared. \\nIn 2022 I was invited/commissioned by Nedbank and Arts and Culture Trust to make an artwork for the Nedbank international Polo event at Inanda with 3 other artists the exhibition was titled #NewNobility. During the same year, Nedbank also commissioned me and other artists to design artworks for their rebranding campaign. \\nI took part in the 2022 Turbine Art Fair with Lizamore & Associates Gallery and also took part in a group exhibition with Mashumi Arts Project. \\nIn 2023 I took part in the Woordfees Festival exhibition and auction titled: Bubble, organised by Lizamore and Associates gallery in collaboration with Strauss & Co. This was held in Stellenbosch at the City Hall. \\nAs of 2024 I have participated in a group exhibition titled 'What is home to you?' which took place at the Fireststation in Rosebamk and was also facilitated by Lizamore and Associates, this exhibition included prolific artist Mashudu Nevhutalu and upcoming artist Vanessa Tembane."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452134957277","gid://shopify/Product/9452134990045"]

item.title: Ricky Ayanda Dyaloyi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641906950365 Ricky Ayanda Dyaloyi 1418 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640996589789 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013464301789","gid://shopify/Product/9013464334557","gid://shopify/Product/9013464400093","gid://shopify/Product/9013464432861","gid://shopify/Product/9013464465629","gid://shopify/Product/9013464498397"] [17347,17349,17352,17355,17357,17360] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"RICKY AYANDA DYALOYI (1974 - ) \\n \\nRicky Dyaloyi paints in a sophisticated, restrained palette. His images are more than simple snapshots of township life as they explore the various predicaments of contemporary African society, specifically as he observes it in his community. Using materials that often reflect and echo his surroundings, he is fond of working on rough, untreated canvas, occasionally mixing his paint with sand and dust. \\n \\nFrom his early childhood days in Gugulethu, Cape Town, Dyaloyi, has shown an interest in art. During the 1990s Dyaloyi was a participant in the Thupelo programme. The ideas, experiences and techniques that he was exposed to in this shared working space would have a far-reaching influence on his work. Dyaloyi has participated in numerous group exhibitions in South Africa and abroad, notably 10?- Celebrating Ten Years of Democracy at the South African National Gallery, Cape Town in 2004. 2015 saw the latest of his more than nine solo exhibitions, Shaman of The Everyday?at Everard Read, Cape Town. \\n \\nArtworks by Dyaloyi are included in various collections in South Africa and abroad including the Hollard Art Collection, Iziko South African National Gallery, The Leeu Art Collection, Old Mutual Art Collection, OMAM Art Collection, Santam Art Collection, Sanlam Art Collection, Spier Art Collection, and the Van den Ende Collection, Netherlands."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013464301789","gid://shopify/Product/9013464334557","gid://shopify/Product/9013464400093","gid://shopify/Product/9013464432861","gid://shopify/Product/9013464465629","gid://shopify/Product/9013464498397"]

item.title: Riley Axon

Their talent and vision were recognized when they were voted one of the Design Indaba Emerging Creatives of 2023. That same year, Riley held a successful solo showcase at Decorex Johannesburg, where their thought-provoking pieces left a lasting impression on attendees. \\nRiley’s work has also been featured in various group exhibitions with esteemed galleries in Johannesburg and Cape Town, further solidifying their reputation as an emerging force in the art world. item.title: Rirhandzu Makhubele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641908293853 Rirhandzu Makhubele 1286 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650755096797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169920733","gid://shopify/Product/9452170051805"] [21264,21266,21263,21265] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rirhandzu Makhubele's work deals with matters that she experience subconsciously and spontaneously. She relive her upbringing memories, trying to understand how one occurrence relates to the next, leading to the person she is today. She investigate how every decision she has made was pre-ordained and how I’m obliged to become the person she is in terms of culture, religion, and politics. Hence, she base her work on how her past, culture, religion, and politics affect her spirituality. \\nRirhandzu makes her sculptures using the ceramic process. She use clay because of its relationship with the soil and nature. Biblically, humankind is made from clay. Her Ceramics become living pieces when using clay, as each portrait is different from the next. The works’ individualism resembles emotional and spiritual experiences in everyday life. The portraits are extremely large and invite the viewer to experience what she felt as an artist and what she depict in the works. Rirhandzu use charcoal clay that becomes black when fired. She is very interested in the transition from clay form to solid form, which is why she chose ceramics as her art-making medium."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169920733","gid://shopify/Product/9452170051805"]

item.title: Robyn Field

Featured in Allow Me to Introduce You To… and Unity Gallery founder. [23706] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Robyn Field has spent many years on the Joburg arts scene, chiefly as owner and curator of Unity Gallery, from 2003-2013, where she worked with emerging artists to develop their careers When Robyn and her husband closed Unity Gallery in 2013 she started painting full time, emerging with bright and beautifully absurd work that digs into the often crazy heart of South African (and global) society. Robyn’s work hangs in a range of private and corporate collections, including the \\nJDA (Joburg Development Agency), #NetworkBBDO, the Global Credit Rating Company, T-systems SA, and Golder and Associates. She has held five solo exhibitions through the years, and she has participated at Turbine Art Fair (2017 and 2019), Melrose Gallery’s sculptX (2019) and the Biennial Neodvisnih (2021)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452121325789"]

item.title: Roger Ballen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641909047517 Roger Ballen 923 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641003995357 [] [23681,23682,23683] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Roger Ballen was born in New York and moved to Johannesburg in 1982, where he currently lives and works. \\n \\nHe is one of the most influential and important photographic artists of the 21st century; his photographs span over forty years. Ballen’s strange and extreme works confront the viewer and challenge them to come with him on a journey into their own minds as he explores the deeper recesses of his own. \\n \\nHis contribution has not been limited to stills photography. Ballen has been the creator of many acclaimed and exhibited short films that dovetail with his photographic series’. The collaborative film I Fink You Freeky, created for the cult band Die Antwoord in 2012, has garnered over 125-million hits on YouTube. \\n \\nRoger Ballen’s work is included in more than forty prestigious museum collections, among which Tate Britain, London; Victoria and Albert Museum, London; Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam; Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam; Museum of Modern Art, New York; Musee de l’Elysee, Lausanne; and Maison Europeene de la Photographie, Paris, to name a few. \\n \\nHis first photography book, Boyhood was published in the late 1970s, followed by Dorps in 1986, Platteland in 1994 and Outland in 2001, among others. His most recent series, Asylum of the Birds was published by Thames & Hudson in March 2014. Among his many awards, he was the winner of the Rencontres d'Alres in 2002 and the Art Directors Club Award in 2006. His I Fink U Freeky video won the award for best video at the Portuguese festival Short Vila do Conde International Film Festival in 2012."}]}]} []

item.title: Roger Brown
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641909113053 Roger Brown 2937 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641004323037 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452150882525","gid://shopify/Product/9452150915293","gid://shopify/Product/9452150948061","gid://shopify/Product/9452150980829","gid://shopify/Product/9452151013597"] Discover Roger Brown, an acclaimed oil painter from Zimbabwe. His art beautifully captures African wildlife, landscapes, and disappearing village life, reflecting a deep connection to the continent's spirit. Explore his captivating works and journey through the heart of Africa. [25293,25291,25290,25292,25289] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Roger Brown (b. 1986 in Zimbabwe) is a passionate oil painter best known for his evocative portrayals of African wildlife and rural village life. Roger's deep-rooted connection to Africa’s landscapes, wildlife, and cultures has profoundly shaped his artistic vision. \\n \\nFrom an early age, his creativity was nurtured by his parents—both avid artists. For a few years, Roger grew up on a wildlife reserve near South Africa’s Kruger National Park, where he was constantly surrounded by nature. School holidays spent exploring Zimbabwe’s Hwange and Matusadona National Parks further deepened his love for the natural world. It was during this time that his talent began to be recognized—he received several awards for his art in primary school and quickly gained a reputation as a promising young artist. \\n \\nAt the age of 13, Roger moved to Botswana, and later settled in Kasane’s Elephant Valley—a region known for its rich wildlife. When he was 15, he sold his first oil painting, a pivotal moment that set him firmly on the path of becoming a professional artist. In 2005, he held his first solo exhibition at Chobe Chilwero Lodge, and in 2010, he was honored with the \"Best Upcoming Artist\" award from the Thapong Visual Arts Centre in Gaborone. \\n \\nToday, Roger continues to work primarily in oils on stretched canvas, developing a style that blends realism with expressive storytelling. His work captures not just the physical beauty of Africa’s animals, landscapes, and people, but also the emotional depth and cultural richness they embody. He is particularly drawn to scenes of traditional village life—everyday activities that are increasingly overlooked or forgotten in the modern world. \\n \\nThrough his art, he seeks to preserve these moments and offer viewers a window into the authentic heart of Africa. Roger's paintings have found homes with collectors around the world. He currently lives and paints in Maun, Botswana—a town often called the gateway to the Okavango Delta. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452150882525","gid://shopify/Product/9452150915293","gid://shopify/Product/9452150948061","gid://shopify/Product/9452150980829","gid://shopify/Product/9452151013597"]

item.title: Ronél de Jager
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641909997789 Ronél de Jager gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641010090205 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452260491485","gid://shopify/Product/9452260557021","gid://shopify/Product/9452260589789"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ronél de Jager was born in Johannesburg, South Africa (1985) where she currently lives and works. An award-winning multidisciplinary artist, De Jager moves between painting, sculpture and installation. Her work shifts between concepts of time, environmental concerns and personal narratives as microcosms of broader social issues. \\n \\nThrough an abiding interest in translating photographic and video imagery into ambiguous, suggestive paint marks, De Jager explores liminal states. In her work, transience is the constant, change is the leitmotif, both conceptually and formally. Her works demonstrate the continuous transformation to which every form is subjected and reflect on the eternal process of becoming and of passing away. The through-line is that this change, this mutability renders moments, memories and sensations in a permanent state of flux, forever slipping away. The act of painting the ineffable is a process of trying to understand that which resists understanding. It is in this fertile ground that De Jager’s work exists. \\nDe Jager presented her latest solo exhibition, ‘Still Here’ at Kalashnikovv Gallery in Braamfontein Johannesburg in June 2022; the show delved deeper into ideas that the artist had been mulling over during Covid-19 and the lockdowns: gender roles, our position as subjects in the digital age, and limits of emotional range in the flattening reality of social \\nmedia. The work on the show took as its central image the bouquet, enlarged and isolated on each canvas. However, the rendering of these floral arrangements is anything but traditional. As Ashraf Jamal wrote, “De Jager’s blurred, filigreed canvases evoke the ornamental, then erase it […]To my mind, it suggests an artwork that is more impressionistic than realistic, the art of someone drawn to miasmas – visualised worlds that quake and \\ntremble in the face of certainty.” \\nRepresented by Kalashnikovv Gallery since 2022; Art Fairs includes Cape Town Art Fair 2022, Turbine Art Fair (2021 and 2022) and more recently a special focus on her work at the FNB Art Joburg in 2022. \\nSelected group show participations includes: Reshape Future Art Histories (2022) presented by Latitudes Online; Thread(ed) Interlacing Womxn in the 21 st Century (2021) curated by Adéle Adendorff and Georgia Glass; Winter Group Show presented by Kalashnikovv Gallery (2021); Verf/Paint curated by Johan Myburg (2021); In Conversation with Colour Symphony hosted by Rupert Museum (2021); The Pandemic Project, an interdisciplinary \\nproject hosted by the University of Johannesburg (2020); Lost and Found hosted by Bag factory Artist’s Studios (2019) and New Romantics curated by Mary Corrigall and hosted by Barnard Gallery in Cape Town (2018). In January 2020, De Jager concluded a four-month residency at Bag Factory Artist’s Studios in Newtown, Johannesburg. \\nAdditionally, collaborative projects includes a glass beaded work 'All that Glitters... is Glass' (2022) in collaboration with Cape Town based 'Qaqambile Bead Studio'. In 2019 she has collaborated with Eswatini based 'Ngwenya Glass' on her 'Citizen of Glass' sculpture project. Collective project exhibitions include ‘MYOPIA’ and ‘Sacred & Profane’, both in 2017. Prior to this she has been a regular finalist in National Art Competitions; ABSA L’Atelier (2008, 2013 and 2015), Sasol New Signatures (in 2008, 2010 and 2014) and the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards (in 2011 to 2016). De Jager is also a recipient of the MTN Foundation Award (2003). \\nDe Jager’s exhibition ‘Broeigrond: Fertile Ground for Golden Regrets’ secured her the 2017 KKNK Kanna Award which saw her work foray into the 3-dimensional and have moved her practice into creating environments for her work. This installation was acquired by the Hollard Art Collection (2017) and permanently installed at The Pines in Parktown, \\nJohannesburg. Further installations of her 'Citizen of Glass' sculpture series have been commissioned by First Rand Limited, (housed at Merchant Place, Sandton). She has also completed commissions for Nando’s UK and Edgars & VMLYR in 2020. \\nHer works are included in a significant number of public and private collections, locally and abroad, including ABSA, First Rand Limited, Hollard SA & Australia, Rand Merchant Rank, Sasol, Telkom, Spier Arts Trust, Nando’s International and the permanent collection of the South African National Library."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452260491485","gid://shopify/Product/9452260557021","gid://shopify/Product/9452260589789"]

item.title: Ronelle Pienaar Jenkin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641909440733 Ronelle Pienaar Jenkin 667 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641006158045 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037243101"] [5122] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ronelle Pienaar Jenkin is a visual artist and a freelance graphic designer who has been active in the industry since her 2007 graduation from Vega Brand Communications School. Jenkin worked at Lemon for many years before going freelance, and still regularly collaborates with the brand in an artistic and design capacity. \\nSouth African born, she currently resides in New Zealand where she continues to apply her exceptionally discerning eye to her various projects. The narratives in Jenkin’s work centre on psychology – our thoughts, behaviour, ways of being in the world and the congruence between these things. Themes such as ridicule, humour, pride, sanctimony, obscenity and irreverence all feature strongly in her work and this interest is explored mainly through portrait and still life. Her preferred media and modes of expression include inks, watercolours and oils."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037243101"]

item.title: Ros Koch
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641910227165 Ros Koch 1727 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641010450653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013382578397"] [13539,13504,13505,13541] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ros Koch (b.1975) is a British-born artist who came to South Africa in 1998. Her artwork reflects her diverse interests and passions, as well as her journey in life. She is an immigrant, adventurer and mother of three children, and these experiences inform her work. Using various mediums, her work explores themes of home, identity, and a sense of belonging. Her style ranges from realism to impressionistic and she enjoys giving her audience the chance to weave their own story into the narrative behind her drawings and paintings. \\n \\nShe studied law both in the UK and South Africa, developing her artisticcareer in parallel. Since becoming a professional artist, Ros has presented three solo shows, taken part in multiple group shows and her work hangs in both corporate and private collections globally. She lives, and works, in Stellenbosch with her husband, three children, and other animals. \\n \\nSELECT EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2021 Life in Lockdown MOK Gallery, Stellenbosch \\n \\nThe Cubists Liebrecht Gallery, Somerset West \\n \\nThe Pack Painted Wolf Wines, Simondium \\n \\nWalls Liebrecht Gallery, Somerset West \\n \\n2019 To see the light Hofmeyr Hall, Stellenbosch \\n \\n40 Stones National Arts Festival, Grahamstown \\n \\n2018 Ubuncwanwe SA Missionary Museum, Cape Town \\n \\n \\n \\nColour Run Crust Cafe, Cape Town \\n \\n2017 Appellation Averys Cellar, Bristol, UK \\n \\nFreshly Brought Arts Festival Wellington \\n \\n \\n \\n2016 Faces and Figures Bright Street Gallery, Somerset West \\n \\nThe Art Assembly Ghetto Art Gallery, Stellenbosch \\n \\nBly PJ Olivier Art Centre, Stellenbosch \\n \\n2015 Dash Tank Gallery, Stellenbosch \\n \\n2013 In at the deep end The Studio at 6 Robbertsz Street"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013382545629","gid://shopify/Product/9013382578397","gid://shopify/Product/9013382643933","gid://shopify/Product/9013383889117","gid://shopify/Product/9013383987421"]

item.title: Ruan Jooste
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641910522077 Ruan Jooste gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641012285661 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452227199197","gid://shopify/Product/9452227363037","gid://shopify/Product/9452227526877"] Discover the compelling works of Ruan Jooste, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through striking compositions and innovative techniques, Jooste’s art explores themes of modern life, emotion, and abstract forms, offering a unique perspective on the human experience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I was born in 1988 in Nigel, Gauteng, South Africa. As a digital painter, I held my first solo exhibition in Cape Town in 2021, which was well-received. My work has been featured on the Sunday Times Lifestyle cover and in Art Times magazine. I have exhibited in Cape Town, Paris AKAA Art Fair, and New York. \\nMy art is part of the RMB collection and has appeared in a Strauss & Co. auction. These opportunities have allowed me to connect with a global audience, and I am grateful for the support of art enthusiasts worldwide. \\nMy work blends luxury fashion elements with South African brand iconography, evoking nostalgia and shared memories. I aim to highlight our commonalities as South Africans, envisioning my subjects as part of a united tribe of courage, positivity, and joy. My fictional portraits, influenced by Magic Realism with an urban twist, exude charm, sass, and attitude. They convey pride, freedom, and self-love, crafting a real-world context around imagined characters. Combining classic portraiture with modern 'selfie' culture, my compositions reflect self-assurance and playfulness. I invite you into a world where old meets new, imagination knows no bounds, and the human experience is celebrated."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452227199197","gid://shopify/Product/9452227363037","gid://shopify/Product/9452227526877"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641910816989 Rudolf Seibeb gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641013072093 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226150621"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rudolf Seibeb (b.1964, Namibia) was born and grew up in Okahandja. Early in life he tried a few trades but always came back to some form of art, an inherited talent he couldn't ignore. Originally Seibeb was self-taught until a stranger introduced him to the John Muafangeyo Art Centre where he then studied in the 1990s. Rudolf Seibeb paints mainly in conventional materials, acrylic on canvas. In some of his mixed media works he integrates found objects. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226150621"]
