item.title: Ryan Enslin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641911079133 Ryan Enslin 2235 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641015922909 [23011] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\\nRyan Enslin is a Pietermartizburg-born, Joburg-based photographer and travel writer. Qualifying as a Chartered Accountant in the early 2000s, he soon came to understand that storytelling flowed in his veins. A self-taught photographer, aided by the odd course to hone his skillset, Ryan is happiest when lensing a scene that speaks to the storytelling nature of his soul. \\n \\nRyan photographs his subjects using prime lenses, preferring to physically frame the scene using the placement of his body to ensure a more detailed level of engagement with the subject. This approach delivers frames which are personal and evocative, as he translates the initial internal connection to a subject into the physical manifestation of the final photograph. \\n \\nIn his first exhibition Reflections from the custodian of moments, Ryan invites the viewer to look through the lens with him and consider his take on everyday occurrences. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014034596061"]

[25042,25045,25043,25044] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sadiq Ajibola Williams (b. 1981 in London, United Kingdom) is a multidisciplinary artist currently based in Lagos, Nigeria. Educated with a Bachelor's in Architecture & Design from Kingston University, William's creative practice is deeply rooted in the rich tapestry of Yoruba culture, tradition, and mythology, seamlessly integrated with the principles drawn from East Asian martial arts. \\nThis distinctive and compelling blend of influences permeates every facet of his work, culminating in a captivating fusion of art forms that articulate the essence of modern Africanism. A highly regarded artist, Sadiq was a finalist in the 2016 National Art Competition in \\nNigeria, and a 2012 UK Creative Pioneer Finalist. His artworks have been widely exhibited in numerous local and international venues."}]}]} []

item.title: Sahlah Davids
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641912619229 Sahlah Davids 1056 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641025130717 [19393,5249,19391,5483,20081,5478,19392,5482,20080] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sahlah Davids was born in 1998 in Cape Town. \\nDelving into the mediums of textiles and beadwork, mixed media artist Sahlah Davids, uses her heritage and strong affiliation to the realm of religious politics to sow the seeds of her creativity. Since completing her bachelor’s degree in Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2020, Sahlah has pursued the intricacies of religion and politics within the field of art and their relationship as one. Thereafter furthering the search for connection between these elements and the curation of pieces that embody it. Through this plight began the creation of the foundation that her work is built on today. \\nDavids has described her methods of creation as the product of the blended learning and trades of the Cape Muslim community specifically the elders within her family. It is within the domestic, traditional and religious spaces that Sahlah draws on the skills of her lineage, the history of their struggles and ultimately the embodiment of their spirituality. \\nArtist Statement: \\nMy art journey with the interest in art practice as a method of enquiry. Socio-political issues within a South African context are deeply embedded in the everyday. This provided a lens though which I saw my maternal grandmother, a seamstress, highly skilled in her field and began sewing as a way to generate income for her family during the height of apartheid. Similarly, my paternal grandfather was a tailor who too followed this profession to aid his family due to the unjust educational system. This profession of tailors, seamstresses and artisans are shared professions within the Cape Muslim “Cape Malay” community. I began to question why. My practice presents an affiliation to the realm and intertwined nature of religion and politics within a South African context. I draw on skills of my heritage and lineage, the history of their struggles through the generations, and ultimately the embodiment of their spirituality. \\nThis practice and profession as a quiet act of protest against inequality. I hope to stitch these questions, emotions and memories through the assemblage of my embellished pieces. The power of making and learning through adversity is what inspires me to create a visual archive that hopes to share this story."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013931016413","gid://shopify/Product/9013931344093","gid://shopify/Product/9013942452445","gid://shopify/Product/9013942485213"]

item.title: Sam Clark
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641915011293 Sam Clark gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641025884381 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452170838237","gid://shopify/Product/9452170969309"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sam Clark is a versatile action and adventure photographer based in Cape Town, South Africa. With a career that began as a staff photographer at Independent Newspapers, Sam left behind a stable job to pursue his passion for travel and photography in Europe. Over the past four years, he has spent every European summer capturing dynamic, unplanned moments across a variety of scenes, including mountain biking and behind-the-scenes work for commercials. \\n \\nKnown for his ability to access hard-to-reach spots in mountain bike races like the Absa Cape Epic, Sam has built a reputation for capturing the raw energy and untold stories behind the action. His photography is inspired by the high standards of printed magazines overseas and the work of fellow photographers like Davy van Laer. \\n \\nSam’s approach focuses on storytelling through a single shot, emphasizing the authenticity of natural light, timing, and the environment. Whether it’s the grit of a skateboarding scene or the intensity of a race, his photos reflect the challenges and triumphs of the moment"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452170838237","gid://shopify/Product/9452170969309"]

item.title: Sam Kentridge
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641915207901 Sam Kentridge 2020 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641026048221 Explore the thought-provoking art of Sam Kentridge, a Johannesburg-based artist blending fragmented text, collage, and narrative to explore themes of loneliness, hope, and the absurdities of everyday life. Shop original works and limited editions today. [22974,22980,22976,18261,22983,18259,22975,14278,22973,22981,22979,22990,14277,22971,22972,22984,18260,22987,22978,22991,22989,22988,22982,22986,22977,18252,22985] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sam Kentridge (born 1992) is a Johannesburg based artist whose practice centres \\naround words. He is interested in fragmented text, unintentionally funny phrases, \\nand collage as a way of encountering a world that refuses to cohere. \\nWhile studying Film and English at the University of Cape Town (2012-2015), Sam developed a passion for playing with narrative and language, making some cringey short films that are safely hidden somewhere in a folder within a folder within a folder on a hard drive that he currently does not know the location of. \\nDuring this time he was drawn to second hand book stores and began collecting odd pedagogical texts (with titles such as 'Yoga for Business Executives’, ‘The American Way of Death’, and ‘The Rubbing Eases Pain Book’). He developed a process of cutting out phrases and images from these texts and glueing them back together in new and angsty ways. \\nAfter drinking too many energy drinks on the sets of student films and developing a bad case of cognitive vertigo from the lofty language of literary analysis, Sam pursued a career in education. Working as a high school English and History teacher (2017-2021) deepened his fascination and frustration with the way in which history is narrated and the scary power language has in constructing our worlds. \\nIn 2022 Sam left teaching to pursue the twin practices of making art and managing his anxiety (which at times can feel like contradictory goals). He has participated in group shows with the Johannesburg based gallery, the gallery, and had works on display at the Turbine Art Fair in 2022, and the Latitudes Art Fair in 2023. \\nHe is interested in exploring themes including loneliness, hope, middle class ennui, and the pain of biting the inside of your cheek so that the inside of your cheek becomes slightly swollen and then you bite that same spot only moments later and now your ham and cheese sandwich tastes of blood."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014032433373","gid://shopify/Product/9014032498909","gid://shopify/Product/9014032564445","gid://shopify/Product/9014032597213","gid://shopify/Product/9014032629981","gid://shopify/Product/9014032695517","gid://shopify/Product/9014032728285","gid://shopify/Product/9014032761053","gid://shopify/Product/9014032826589","gid://shopify/Product/9014032859357","gid://shopify/Product/9014032892125","gid://shopify/Product/9014032957661","gid://shopify/Product/9014032990429","gid://shopify/Product/9014033121501","gid://shopify/Product/9014033154269","gid://shopify/Product/9014033285341","gid://shopify/Product/9014033350877","gid://shopify/Product/9014033383645","gid://shopify/Product/9014033481949","gid://shopify/Product/9014033514717","gid://shopify/Product/9014033547485"]

item.title: Samantha Impumelelo Maseko
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641913241821 Samantha Impumelelo Maseko 2207 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641026179293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082135261","gid://shopify/Product/9452082168029","gid://shopify/Product/9452126961885"] [23938,19325,19419,19418] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Samantha Maseko is an Artist Proof Studio graduate whose work wrestles with themes of \\nblack femininity. \\n“At the end of the day, black bodies are political...” – Amy Sherald \\nHer works embody the African American painter’s words, as she unearths and challenges \\naspects of blackness clothed in the female form - whether by interrogating hair, colourism or \\nthe sexualisation of the black body. \\nMaseko’s practice oscillates between the mediums of printmaking, mixed media and painting \\nto communicate her chosen message. There is a single constant present throughout her \\nmany themes and mediums, and that is a need to present blackness as aesthetically pleasing. \\nThis desire to bind representations of the black figure is no doubt a result of her love for \\nfashion. \\nWhile a piece such as Optical Façade I appears to be interrogating the duality of emotions \\nattached to natural hair in the black community, alluded to in the depictions of a polarised \\nmirroring of herself wearing a head wrap and with an afro. Even within the palpable \\nuncertainty that exists in these works, Maseko binds elements of beauty to her \\nrepresentations of blackness. \\nThis is evident in her use of make-up alongside traditional media such as collage and \\nwatercolour. The companion piece Optical Façade II, echoes its sister piece in an expected \\nprint medium; this linocut work, however, does surprise, as the viewer isn’t merely presented \\n \\nwith a monochrome copy of the first piece, but with a crown-like element of elaborate floral- \\nlike arrangements of herself. This suggests that she dresses herself in the beauty of her own \\n \\nskin.In works such as her acrylic and oil painting on canvas, Hear no evil, highlight Maseko’s \\nintention to entangle positivity to images of black people. In this instance she does so through \\nher depiction of styled black hair, keeping in her thematic use of wearing black hair in its \\nnatural state and it being seen as one’s “crowning glory”. In this work it is evident how she \\nteases out the curls of her subject’s hair, moulding their hair styles into crowns. \\nMaseko’s fondness for fashion as a mode of presenting black positivity or pride can also be \\nseen in paintings such as Rebellion and Sense of self, which are depictions of black subjects \\neach wearing afros and clad in aristocratic finery. The aim of these works is to frame the black \\nexperience within a reality devoid of the weighted negativity of past realities of the black \\nexperience. \\nThese are reimagining’s of a past that could have been and which may have been able to bring \\nabout a brighter present. In these examples we are confronted by Maseko’s desire to elevate \\nreality, not just reproduce it. \\nThe entirety of the Amy Serald quote reads: “At the end of the day, black bodies are political, \\nbut there has to be some relief from that otherwise we can never evolve as a people.” These \\nimaginings of a lighter past evident in Maseko’s work strut in step with this sentiment as she \\npresents alternatives to the flood of negative narratives perpetuated through mass media of \\nthe black aesthetic."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452082135261","gid://shopify/Product/9452082168029","gid://shopify/Product/9452126961885"]

item.title: Sam Nhlengethwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641915273437 Sam Nhlengethwa 510 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641026146525 [3559,18588,18589,3555,18592,3563,3562,3557,18590,3561,14768,3565,24774,14767,3556,3564,18591,25528] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sam Nhlengethwa is one of South Africa's foremost artists. Born in 1955, he studied at Rorke's Drift and the Johannesburg Art Foundation. He was awarded the Standard Bank Young Artist of the Year award in 1994, the year South Africa held its first democratic elections and freedom was won for all its people. He has exhibited all over the world from Senegal to New York and Cologne. His work is largely figurative and he explores themes that are close to his heart such as jazz, human interactions and the physical space of contemporary Africa. In his prints and paintings, Sam Nhlengethwa uses overlays of techniques such as collage painting, drawing and photography. His fine sense of colour and form lend an abstract quality to his work. \\n \\nHe has been included in many contemporary South African art publications and his work can be found in leading South African and International collections. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013843820765","gid://shopify/Product/9013843853533","gid://shopify/Product/9013843886301","gid://shopify/Product/9013843919069","gid://shopify/Product/9013843984605","gid://shopify/Product/9014102556893","gid://shopify/Product/9134148944093"]

item.title: Samira Saidi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641914159325 Samira Saidi 2346 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641026277597 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062965981"] [18440] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Samira Saidi is a Ghanaian-Austrian woman of colour whose practice aims to study and shift the sociological structures of race and belonging and explores the duality of intersectional identities through the body. \\nAfter completing her Bachelor’s Degree at the Royal Academy of Art, The Hague, Saidi began using photography and writing as the main mediums through which to bring her ideas into reality. In recent years, she has expanded her practice to include documentary photography, photojournalism, and performance art. Together, she uses these disciplines to create multimedia projects that seek to spark critical conversation around socio-economic topics. Saidi is currently studying Applied Human Rights at the University of Applied Arts Vienna."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062671069","gid://shopify/Product/9452062965981"]

[20690,20695,20691,21918,20694,13845,22449,20858,22720,15394,5579] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Samkelo Matomela (b. 1996, eThekwini, KwaZulu-Natal) is a South African artist whose love for art flourished after moving to Soweto. After completing matric, he initially studied Town and Regional Planning before pursuing his passion for art at Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, where he trained as a printmaker. The transition to Soweto, where he moved at the age of 14, exposed him to new languages and cultures, significantly influencing his artistic journey. \\nThis diverse community inspired him to create work reflecting the struggles and resilience of individuals in these neighborhoods. The butterfly motif symbolizes hope and overcoming circumstances, reinforcing the message that transformation is always possible. \\nSamkelo's art is inspired by both internal and external experiences, exploring vulnerabilities as a man navigating life and emotions. By applying thick layers of paint and using the impasto technique, he conveys the depth of these feelings. His portraits and figures often lack facial details, allowing viewers to see themselves in the work and engage on a deeper level. He primarily focuses on portraiture and semi-nude figures, believing these to be our most intimate states. \\nThe butterfly in Samkelo's work represents hope and change. This motif recurs throughout his art as a symbol of transformation and resilience. The hood in his work serves as an antidote and a symbol that people can turn to in various circumstances. His work captures the struggles of teenagers, the impact of unemployment on youth, and the overall resilience of individuals in his community."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013394637021","gid://shopify/Product/9013423603933","gid://shopify/Product/9013961621725","gid://shopify/Product/9013961720029","gid://shopify/Product/9013961818333","gid://shopify/Product/9013961916637","gid://shopify/Product/9013971222749","gid://shopify/Product/9014006186205","gid://shopify/Product/9014017818845","gid://shopify/Product/9014024831197"]

item.title: Samson Mnisi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641914749149 Samson Mnisi 883 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641027621085 [23895] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Samson Mnisi was born in 1971 in Lesotho. He studied Fine Art and photography at FUBA Academy. Since completing his studies he has participated in many group and solo exhibitions, both locally and internationally. \\nHis art is a symbolic language of an abstract thought. Using patterns, lines, symbols and colour Mnisi explores and articulates his understanding of a ‘South African expression’. The recurring graphic symbols in his works signify visual codes of universal language representing peace, divergence, crossroads and eternal cycles. He sees himself as part of the timeless tradition of celebrating the human godliness from the first rock paintings, to the present time and beyond. \\nSometimes also known as Rain Maker which refers to his last name - Mnisi - which translates to ‘they make it rain’. Using art as alchemy, his creativity is enacted through intuitive gestures, colours and forms across textured surfaces. In this way, Mnisi explores different cosmic dimensions across his paintings and offers them for viewers to delve into and find clues and keys that will take them into their own journeys."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126044381"]

item.title: Sandile Radebe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641915699421 Sandile Radebe 525 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641030930653 [] [21647,18788,21649,21650] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sandile Radebe’s main area of interest is art practice in both public and private spaces. Radebe explores these spaces through stimulating a new reading of graffiti and more broadly, the way language works to help construct our realities. He visualises graffiti in abstract sculptural forms instead of alphabetical lettering. The viewer is encouraged to think about graffiti and indeed language, in a new way. Radebe says that his aim is to develop a new graffiti language devoid of stigma. \\n \\nBased in Johannesburg, Radebe completed a BAFA (Honours) in 2006 at Wits School of the Arts and in 2009 studied for a PGDA in Arts and Cultural Management at the same institution. A solo exhibition, A Walk in the City, was held in 2014 at the National School of the Arts. He has participated in various group exhibitions with the most recent being Cubicle Series, Everard Read, Cape Town (2018). Radebe has been involved in several public interventions and has executed a number of commissions. He has been involved in curating and his artwork is included in private collections locally and abroad."}]}]} []

item.title: Sanell Aggenbach
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641915994333 Sanell Aggenbach 668 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641033879773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452128895197", "gid://shopify/Product/9452128927965", "gid://shopify/Product/9452129026269", "gid://shopify/Product/9452129059037"] [24088,24083,24085,24087,24084] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sanell Aggenbach’s (b. 1975 Cape Town, South Africa) work deals primarily with the intersection of history and private narratives by considering the process of recall and interpretation. \\nHer work displays an accomplished virtuosity as she moves comfortably between the various disciplines of painting, printmaking and sculpture. Since 2003, Aggenbach has focused mainly on subverted feminine tropes and feminist themes. \\nIn her most recent solo exhibition, Bend to Her Will, she subtly and mischievously reframed the hobbyist art of flower arranging by appropriating the traditionally masculine art of Japanese Ikebana. Her sculptural work, primarily in bronze, parody Western masterpieces from Michelangelo, Henry Moore, and Warhol to Pierneef and take a refreshing look at these pivotal references from a woman’s perspective. \\nAggenbach currently lives and works in Woodstock, Cape Town. Her explorative work has secured her many achievements including winning the Absa L’Atelier Award in 2003. Her work is represented in numerous public and private collections, including Sasol, ABSA, Spier, SABC, Red Bull (Austria), the South African National Gallery, 21C Museum in Kentucky (USA) and Anglo Gold. \\n“My earlier works relied heavily on processing found imagery, rethinking associations and creating new fictions. These works were often an amalgamation of historic references with private narratives and forms part of a process of investigating pathologies and deconstructing the past. My primary intention is to construct subtle paradoxes by introducing a quite humour, either formally or materially.” - Sanell Aggenbach"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452128862429","gid://shopify/Product/9452128895197","gid://shopify/Product/9452128927965","gid://shopify/Product/9452129026269","gid://shopify/Product/9452129059037"]

item.title: Sarah Ballam
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641916551389 Sarah Ballam 363 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641037746397 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046450909","gid://shopify/Product/9452046483677"] [13515,13514] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Colour startles in the new work. Dynamic, even confrontational, these paintings challenge our commonplace expectations of colour and shape. Local colour – the colour an object “owns” – has been replaced with saturated colour, more rooted in intuition than observation. Although embedded in the figurative, these works lean into more abstract realms. The tension between form and dissolution, between the need to structure composition and render dissipation, is what draws us in and holds our attention. Ballam references celebratory images of women by great modernists – Matisse’s dancers and Picasso’s women running on the beach. These are reworkings of artists who are key pillars of the male modernist canon. Are the Ballam paintings a homage, a challenge, or both? The roots in art history go back further, into classical friezes of Antiquity and their traditional themes like the Three Graces. Ballam’s entranced figures recall to mind the Pompeian mystery cults of which only fragments of murals remain. The American art critic Harold Rosenberg famously stated that “… the canvas is an arena in which to act.” Large canvases make unusual physical demands on a painter. The large canvas is likely to be the recipient of bolder, emphatic gestures, trapping and holding the energy and emotion of a painter. Ballam’s paintings are arrived at through a succession of applications, broad swathes laid in with large brushes and palette knives, then drawn into with incisive fluid line. Each painting is the result of a perilous voyage, a tightrope walk into the unknown that requires considerable poise. And counterpoise."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046450909","gid://shopify/Product/9452046483677"]

item.title: Sarah Biggs
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641916780765 Sarah Biggs 653 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641038500061 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037275869"] [5169] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sarah Biggs (b. 1990, Ixopo, South Africa) received her BFA from Michaelis School of Fine Art (UCT) in 2013 and currently lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\n \\nWorking primarily with oils on canvas and sized paper, Biggs applies her paint in thinned down layers of translucent colour, allowing her fluid marks and surfaces to shift and settle organically over time. Her work is characterised by an ongoing interest in the relationship between her painterly subjects and the natural world, tracing encounters beyond just the physical and the visual, but also the ways in which other senses, real and imagined, are woven into our experience of our surroundings. Through painting, Biggs finds ”a way of seeing in which there is space for the invisible forces that move the world\" (Allende, 1991). \\n \\nHer work is characterised by an ongoing interest in the relationship between her painterly subjects and the natural world, tracing encounters beyond just the visual, but also the ways in which other senses, real and imagined, are woven into our experience of our surroundings. Through painting, Biggs finds \"a way of seeing in which there is space for the invisible forces that move the world. \\n \\nBiggs applies her paint in thinned down layers of translucent colour, allowing her fluid marks and surfaces to shift and settle organically over time. Her scapes often sit on the edge between figurative landscape and abstracted colour field, seeking to capture the constantly shifting nature of the outside world as one moves through it. Painting exists as a threshold between these realities; a portal to the world to which her figures belong. \\n \\nSarah graduated from Michaelis School of Fine Art in 2013 and has since exhibited on a number of local group shows and fairs. She has held three solo shows at the Barnard Gallery in Cape Town. 'Further Afield' was presented in 2015, followed in 2017 by 'Waiting for rain', and most recently, 'Gathering dust' in 2019. \\n \\nIn 2015 she was awarded the TASA Emerging Artist Award. Presented by the Turbine Art Fair and the Sylt Foundation, this award took the form of a one-month residency at the Foundation’s headquarters on the island of Sylt, Germany and a one-month residency at the Künstlerhäuser Worpswede, Germany. \\n \\nSelected group exhibitions include Ocular (131 A Gallery, 2020, Wildflowers (Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, 2019), New Romantics (Barnard Gallery, 2018), A Piece of Work (David Krut Projects, Johannesburg, 2017), Fluid: Perspectives in Paint (Barnard Gallery, 2017), Surface: Emerging Painters (Barnard Gallery, 2015), Distance, a two-person exhibition (Salon91 Contemporary Art Collection, 2014), and Do-it, a project curated by Hans-Ulrich Obrist (Michaelis Galleries, 2014). Her work was presented by Barnard Gallery at the Cape Town Art Fair (2015-2020) and AKAA (Also Known As Africa) in Paris (2017, 2018), and in 2016 she had a solo booth at the Turbine Art Fair. \\n \\n1 Isabel Allende, ‘The Shaman and the Infidel’ (1991)"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037275869"]

item.title: Sarafina Naisula
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641916518621 Sarafina Naisula gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641037287645 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013463515357","gid://shopify/Product/9013463548125","gid://shopify/Product/9013463580893"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sarafina Naisula (b. 1999) a rising contemporary artist of Tanzanian and Dutch \\nheritage is deeply influenced by the rich storytelling traditions of her homeland. \\nHer artistic journey began there, fueled by a passion for creative expression \\nnurtured by the vivid narratives of her roots. \\n \\nEducated at the University Of Arts in London, Sarafina work has been showcased \\nin the Netherlands and South Africa, resonating with diverse audiences. Central \\nto Sarafina’s artistic mission is the exploration of human identity, with particular \\nemphasis on the female experience within the African diaspora. \\nSarafina sees art as a powerful catalyst for challenging preconceptions, sparking \\ndialogue, and evoking emotions. Her work is a call of action, a catalyst for change, \\nand a mirror reflecting society’s unspoken and uncomfortable truths. \\nHer current body of work delves into the harsh realities of sexual abuse, \\nhighlighting the erosion of individual identity often linked to such trauma. \\nUtilizing silhouettes she emphasizes society’s tendency to reduce complex \\nstories to mere statistics and bodies, obscuring the profound narratives beneath \\nthe surface. \\n \\nSarafina’s diverse mediums convey multi-layered messages, aiming to dismantle \\nthe walls of indifference, urging society to recognize that these stories are not \\ndistant, but intimately woven into our daily lives. Her aim is to bridge the gap \\nbetween familiarity and awareness, fostering compassion, insight, and equality. \\nUltimately, Sarafina’s art serves as a call to engage, a plea to acknowledge the \\nworth of every individual and their unique story. She aspires to inspire change, \\none piece at a time, and to awaken society to the interconnected narratives that \\ndefine us all."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013463515357","gid://shopify/Product/9013463548125","gid://shopify/Product/9013463580893"]

[22033,21403,22030,23400,22028,21417,21418,22027,22026,22031,22029,22032] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sarah Jayne Fell (b. 1986) is a Cape Town-based artist whose primary medium is painting. Her work delves into personal myths through expressionism and process art, celebrating the interplay of her two muses: colour and light. The subject matter is both personal and universal, reflecting the human condition and her personal experiences. Drawing on images and ideas from dreams and journaling, she engages in freestyle painting or digital collage, culminating in poetry. \\nFell's artwork ultimately reflects a personal process that is both cathartic and autobiographical. Her artistic journey began in her mother's ceramic studio in rural KwaZulu-Natal, sparking a lifelong passion for art. She was awarded the matric art prize at Durban Girls' College in 2003 for practical art. She furthered her education in creative writing, media & communications, philosophy, and English literature, fulfilling her love for broader arts and culture. In 2008, she moved to Cape Town to become the editor of One Small Seed magazine, later specializing in digital media and communications, and running a content studio since 2014. \\nAs a counterpoint to the digital world, Sarah has continuously produced art in various mediums, including painting, drawing, collage, mixed media, digital art, and ceramics. She has attended art classes, painting workshops, live figure drawing, and process art groups at Ruth Prowse, Bright Studio, and A Star. Sarah has participated in group exhibitions at the KZNSA, with ANON. Pop Up, and the Zeitz MOCAA (At Home, 2021). She now paints from her home art studio in Kommetjie, Cape Town."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013994815709","gid://shopify/Product/9013995307229","gid://shopify/Product/9013995339997","gid://shopify/Product/9014007857373","gid://shopify/Product/9014007922909","gid://shopify/Product/9014007955677","gid://shopify/Product/9014007988445","gid://shopify/Product/9014008021213","gid://shopify/Product/9014008053981","gid://shopify/Product/9014044164317"]

item.title: Senzeni Marasela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641919860957 Senzeni Marasela gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641043382493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452271698141", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271730909", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271796445", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271829213", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271861981", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271894749", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271960285", "gid://shopify/Product/9452271993053", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272058589", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272091357", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272124125", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272156893", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272189661", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272222429", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272255197", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272287965", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272320733", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272353501", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272386269", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272451805", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272484573", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272550109", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272582877", "gid://shopify/Product/9452272648413"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Two words would describe Senzeni Mthwakazi Marasela: headstrong and uncompromising. Impatient with labels and pigeon-holing, Marasela uses photography, photocopy transfers, silkscreening and handicraft to explore collective and personal memory. Her choice of ‘raw’ (unprocessed) fabrics like calico, set against the highly worked quality of lace have, for her, strong ties to colonialism. The labour-intensive process of handstitching is her way of inscribing herself into this past she wishes to explore, as well as attempting to elevate her chosen imagery into a realm of the cherished and respected. Although deeply political, Marasela’s work bespeaks an ambivalent atitude towards past atrocities from which she was protected and guarded. Her sense of place as a black woman educated at a Catholic school in a white Afrikaans suburb gives her work an edge rarely encountered. In her own words: ” I believe that by revisiting the past, by giving myself a place in it, I’ll be able to forgive myself for my indifference.” (‘Democracy’s Images’ catalogue; interview conducted by Rory Bester) \\nAn immediate concern is altering the profile of black women artists in this country. Marasela is acutely aware of the absence of black women in decision-making positions in the realm of arts and culture, and while acknowledging the importance of artists like Noria Mabasa and Mmakgabo Helen Sebidi, feels they have not ‘developed’ their language effectively or critically: black women artists need a contemporary language with which to speak about traditional content, and to move away from the association with ‘craft’. Marasela cites Tracey Rose and Moshekwa Langa as examples of ‘black’ artists whose work avoids easy categorisation. \\nArtist’s statement: \\n“Artists have an important role to play in telling stories about our turbulent history, especially when so many of the sincere gestures which make up this history have been cut down and mutilated. Hector Peterson is a good example. Up until 1976 young people hadn’t really been seen at the forefront of political struggle, especially in images that so vividly depicted the slaughter of innocence. A lot of people don’t really comprehend the significance of the events around 16th June 1976, especially the extent to which it marked the catalyst of events that were to bring down a regime. Stompie Seipei is another important example. He got caught up in a series of events that he didn’t fully understand. The way Stompie lived and died was and still is a burden to so many people. History is making him elusive to memory. These are just two examples of children who have become the victims of political ideologies. It is these emasculated ideologies that I try to grapple with as a woman and as a black artist.” \\n– Senzeni Marasela"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452271698141","gid://shopify/Product/9452271730909","gid://shopify/Product/9452271763677","gid://shopify/Product/9452271796445","gid://shopify/Product/9452271829213","gid://shopify/Product/9452271861981","gid://shopify/Product/9452271894749","gid://shopify/Product/9452271960285","gid://shopify/Product/9452271993053","gid://shopify/Product/9452272058589","gid://shopify/Product/9452272091357","gid://shopify/Product/9452272124125","gid://shopify/Product/9452272156893","gid://shopify/Product/9452272189661","gid://shopify/Product/9452272222429","gid://shopify/Product/9452272255197","gid://shopify/Product/9452272287965","gid://shopify/Product/9452272320733","gid://shopify/Product/9452272353501","gid://shopify/Product/9452272386269","gid://shopify/Product/9452272451805","gid://shopify/Product/9452272484573","gid://shopify/Product/9452272550109","gid://shopify/Product/9452272582877","gid://shopify/Product/9452272648413"]

item.title: Sepideh Mehraban
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641920483549 Sepideh Mehraban 538 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641043677405 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359345885", "gid://shopify/Product/9452042911965", "gid://shopify/Product/9452060999901", "gid://shopify/Product/9452260163805", "gid://shopify/Product/9452270321885"] [11457,9981,9980,18047,18049,11425,18048,3287,3288] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sepideh Mehraban uses primed and raw canvases and allows paint to seep through the material, capturing fragile moments and embodying the ephemeral nature of remembrance. Farsi text adds a graffiti protest to the official histories she contests. Mehraban questions the notion of ‘truth’ in history and offers her art as a further interpretation of others’ chronicles. Her deeply introspective work explores memory and its link to personal histories in contemporary Iran. \\n \\nNow living in Cape Town, but born in Tehran, Iran, Mehraban has two Masters degrees in Fine Art from the Alzahra University in Tehran and the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town, South Africa. She has lectured in the Painting Departments at Michaelis and Stellenbosch Universities, worked as a curator, set designer and collaborated on puppeteering projects. She is a PhD candidate at the University of Stellenbosch. Participating in over 40 group exhibitions, her latest one was The Female Line, SMAC Gallery (2019) and her most recent of three solo exhibitions being Until The Lions Have Their Own Historians, The History Of The Hunt Will Always Glorify The Hunter, SMITH Studio, Cape Town (2019). Mehraban’s work is held in a number of private and corporate collections globally."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359345885","gid://shopify/Product/9452042911965","gid://shopify/Product/9452060999901","gid://shopify/Product/9452260163805","gid://shopify/Product/9452260262109","gid://shopify/Product/9452270321885"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641920516317 Serai Lobelo 2892 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641044725981 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098329821"] Discover the compelling work of Serai Lobelo, a South African artist whose practice explores identity, heritage, and visual storytelling through vibrant mediums. Explore available artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [24625,24645] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Serai Lobelo, 42, was born in the then Bophuthatswana “homeland”. He is a multidisciplinary artist and creative director based in Johannesburg. He studied multimedia design at Tshwane University of Technology and works at the intersection of Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS), African luxury and speculative art. \\nA descendant of the Basarwa – the first people of southern Africa – Lobelo explores cultural memory, materiality and ancestral presence through painting, digital media and immersive installations. His practice blends traditional craftsmanship with contemporary technology, drawing on Basarwa rock art, Afro-Surrealist cinema, Setswana praise poetry and user interface/user experience (UI/UX) principles. Central to his work is the digitisation of oral traditions into an audiovisual lexicon that preserves and honours IKS. \\nHe is the founder of Ditoro Studios, a platform for storytelling and cultural reclamation. Lobelo’s work has been exhibited at Kalashnikovv Gallery, Norwest Gallery of Art in Detroit, RMB Talent Unlocked and TEDx Johannesburg, and featured in Wanted Online and Al-Tiba9 Art Magazine (Issue 17), affirming his voice in contemporary art discourse. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098329821"]

item.title: Sethembile Msezane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641921761501 Sethembile Msezane 2182 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641049477341 [15603,15604,15602,15578,15605,15579,15580,15577] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sethembile Msezane b.. 1991 in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa. She lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\n \\nShe was awarded a Masters in Fine Arts in 2017 from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town. Using interdisciplinary practice encompassing photography, painting, live works/embodiments, film, sculpture and installation. \\n \\nMsezane creates commanding works heavy with spiritual and political symbolism. The artist explores issues around spirituality, commemoration and African knowledge systems. She processes her dreams as a medium through a lens of the plurality of existence across space and time, asking questions about the remembrance of ancestry. Part of her work has examined the processes of mythmaking which are used to construct history, calling attention to the absence of the black female body in both the narratives and physical spaces of historical commemoration. \\n \\nMsezane participated in the 14th edition of PhotoIreland, she has participated in the13th Bamako Encounters African Biennale of Photography (2022), she completed a residency at Central Saint Martins, London (2022), she participated in the 14th Dak’art Biennale (2022), she was a UEA Global Talent Fellow hosted by the Sainsbury Research Unit and Sainsbury Centre (2021). She was Mellon Artist Residency Fellow in partnership with Gallery of the University of Stellenbosch and the English Department (2020), she is a National Institute for Human Social Sciences Award nominee (2020), OkayAfrica 100 women 2018 Honoree. Msezane was a TEDGlobal Speaker in Arusha, Tanzania (2017). Msezane is the first recipient of the Rising Light award at the Mbokodo Awards (2016). \\n \\nMsezane’s work has been widely exhibited across South Africa and internationally and was included in various exhibitions and museums that include the Zeitz MOCAA (Cape Town), as well as that of the Iziko South African National Gallery (Cape Town), The Royal Ontario Museum (Canada), Oscar Niemeyer Museum (Brazil) and more."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013427372253","gid://shopify/Product/9013427405021","gid://shopify/Product/9013427470557","gid://shopify/Product/9013427634397","gid://shopify/Product/9013428093149","gid://shopify/Product/9013428158685","gid://shopify/Product/9013428388061"]

item.title: Setlamorago Mashilo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641921827037 Setlamorago Mashilo 639 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641049706717 [] [3067,3072,3069,3071,3068,3065,3066] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Setlamorago Mashilo is a trained visual artist who lives and works in Pretoria. He graduated High School in 2005 and his development as an artist was profoundly influenced by his introduction to postmodern theory and his Sepedi upbringing. Mashilo works in various media including drawing, sculpture and printmaking. \\n \\n“I employ the use of 'dika le diema' (Sepedi Proverbs and Idioms) which incorporate objects, images, stories and songs inherited from my collective Sepedi upbringing. As a result, I unpack my own spiritual and psychological connections with these established systems of thought or ideologies and how they still condition our contemporary lives – the very same systems created by previous generations to secure our being and give them what we/they seek from life. What takes place in my work is a strange monologue – recited, sung – scenes and acts that are eerily fateful and transcendent, stories that resonate individually and collectively about our sense of loss, nostalgia and inherited memories and the future. My work becomes one form of me talking about how the values of our societies are deeply encoded in these stories and how that extrapolates into the communities we grow up in.” \\n \\nSelected Group/Solo Exhibitions \\n \\n \\n2013 \\n \\nPPC Young Sculptor Awards, Pretoria Artist Association \\n \\n2014 \\n \\nFresh Produce, Turbine Art Fair \\n \\n2014 \\n \\nContemporary Totem Poles (Cool Capital Biennale) \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nLandlords & Trespassers, Turbine Art Fair \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nEmerging Artists, Shanghai Art Fair \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nCapital Present, Fried Contemporary \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nThe Spiritual in the Material”, Lizamore & Associates \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nFETISH, Albany Museum \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nWhen You Come Back, Art on Paper Miami \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nNew Voices, Lizamore & Associates \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nAfrican Equations, Lizamore & Associates \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nInstallation Art Fair, New York \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nTokyo International Art Fair \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nPerforming Wo/Man, North-West University Gallery \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nBodulo, Rotterdam International Art Fair \\n \\n2016 \\n \\nAmandla! item.title: Shakil Solanki
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641922023645 Shakil Solanki 290 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641051803869 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013327331549", "gid://shopify/Product/9013378744541", "gid://shopify/Product/9013378810077", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380284637", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380350173"] [8118,13158,8150,13157,13268,13269,22725,22726] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Shakil Solanki (b. 1998) was born in Cape Town, South Africa. He has recently completed his undergraduate degree at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, and is currently based in Cape Town, practising as an artist. Solanki majored in the medium of printmaking during his third and fourth years of study. On completion of his degree in 2019, he was awarded the Simon Gerson Award, as well as the Katrine Harries Print Cabinet Award, for excellent achievement in the printmaking medium. Since 2018, he has taken part in several group shows, along with many silkscreen-printing jobs, and a residency at the South Atlantic Press in 2020. \\nSolanki interrogates dynamics of intimacy, using the space of a secret garden to explore dualities of tenderness, desire and violence. His experiences as a queer brown man remain central to his practice, with classical Eastern art standing as a prominent source of inspiration. This vernacular is repurposed, encompassing homoerotic dialogues to evoke lush, dreamlike lands, which remain both romantic and discomforting at once. The trope of a secret garden is used as a liminal space, where contrasting emotions of trauma and longing exist hand-in-hand with moments of stillness, using the theme of intimacy as a point of convergence to explore its many dynamics, evoked within many shades of the colour blue."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013327331549","gid://shopify/Product/9013378744541","gid://shopify/Product/9013378810077","gid://shopify/Product/9013380284637","gid://shopify/Product/9013380350173","gid://shopify/Product/9013835170013"]

item.title: Shamilla Aasha
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641922842845 Shamilla Aasha 2145 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641054228701 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088066269"] [20320,20321,20322,20323,20326,20328,15199] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born 1977 Hwange, Zimbabwe. Lives and works in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe \\nShamilla Aasha is a practicing artist and teacher of art and design. After many years of working in painting and mixed media, in 2018 Aasha re-engage with her love of textiles through exploration of her multi-cultural background as a Shona and Indian woman living in Matabeleland region of Zimbabwe. Developing complex works addressing issues related to merging cultures and traditional practices and how they influence identity, spirituality and social status for herself and other women in her community. \\nAasha’s works defy attempts at categorisation, incorporating weaving, tapestry as well as engaging with the idea and history of painting. They emerge as soft sculptures, wall-hangings made from found objects as well abstract embroideries. She describes them as sacred objects, a fitting metaphor for her narratives. This metaphor is further expanded on, as she uses sewing patterns, fabric and stitching. This process allows her to create new patterns from the old and with each layer creating a palmistry language. \\nShamilla has participated in numerous exhibitions locally regionally and internationally. She is currently part of an ongoing, regional collaborative project, which is interrogating the participation of women in land redistribution in Southern Africa. In addition to artistic practice, Shamilla also continues to nurture creativity minds through her trust-Asha Children’s Trust, an organisation devoted to creating safe spaces for young creatives grow and thrive outside the formal education sector."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452088066269"]

item.title: Sharday Swanepoel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641923137757 Sharday Swanepoel 2687 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641054654685 Discover the evocative work of Sharday Swanepoel, a self-taught photographic artist from Kommetjie, South Africa. Combining digital and analogue photography, Swanepoel's images capture the essence of childhood wonder and domestic life, offering a nostalgic glimpse into the realities of motherhood. [22468] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sharday Swanepoel (b. 1986, Durban) is a visionary South African photographic artist who resides in he small coastal village of Kommetjie, just outside Cape Town. Raised in Durban, Sharday's journey with photography began at a young age, capturing momens of her family anf friends. With a degree in Architectural Studies, her deep understanding of light and space soon led her to the world of photography, where she discovered her passion for sculpting with light. \\nAs a self-taught artist, Sharday's work delves into the juxtaposition of childhood wonder and mundane domestic life, revealing the uncensored realities of motherhood through intimate and evocative imagery. Her photographs combine digital and analogue techniques, reminiscent of the timeless family photo album, and evoke a sense of nostalgia and melancholy. Themes of social issues, personal identity, and memory are intricately woven into her work, exploring the notion of \"this too shall pass,\" a sentiment often experienced by mothers navigating the challenges of raising children. \\nSharday's artistry has earned her recognition within the photographic community, with her work being showcased in various group exhibitions. Notable exhibitions include the 2023 Portrait Show hosted by Through The Lens Collective and 'The Wildest Most Beautiful Ugly,' hosted by Too Tired Project and Open Studio Kommetjie in 2023. As a stay-at-home mother of four, Sharday's photography serves as a means of documenting and preserving her own stories, as well as those of others, creating a powerful narrative that resonates with many. \\nSharday Swanepoel's work is an introspective exploration of the human experience, capturing the beauty and complexity of life's fleeting moments through her lens."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014018474205"]

item.title: Sharlene Khan
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641923170525 Sharlene Khan 591 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641055703261 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359313117","gid://shopify/Product/9452042879197","gid://shopify/Product/9452095832285","gid://shopify/Product/9452095897821","gid://shopify/Product/9452095930589","gid://shopify/Product/9452153209053","gid://shopify/Product/9452153307357","gid://shopify/Product/9452153438429","gid://shopify/Product/9452153503965","gid://shopify/Product/9452153831645","gid://shopify/Product/9452155699421","gid://shopify/Product/9452155830493","gid://shopify/Product/9452156059869"] [25351,25349,25348,25350,25324,25322,25352,25346,25347,21115,21116,21117,25323] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sharlene Khan is a South African visual artist whose multi-media works focus on the socio-political realities of a post-apartheid society and the intersectionality of race-gender-class. She was a recipient of the Rockefeller Bellagio Visual Arts residency (2009), the Canon Collins/Commonwealth Scholarship (2011), the African Humanities Post-doctoral Fellowship (2017), the National Institute for Humanities and Social Sciences Award for Visual Arts (2018) and was runner-up winner in the Videokunst Preis Bremen video art award (2015). She has published three books on her artwork: What I look like, What I feel like (2009), I Make Art (2017) and When the moon waxes red... (2018). She is co-convenor of the annual African Feminisms (Afems) Conference, runs the Art on our Mind Research Project, the Decolonial AestheSis Creative Lab, and the bi-weekly Black Feminist Killjoy Reading Group. Her writings on contemporary visual arts appears in journals, books, art catalogues and magazines including Art South Africa, Artthrob, Springerin, Manifesta, Contemporary-And, The Conversation Africa, Imbizo: International Journal of African Literary and African Studies, Journal of African Cultural Studies and Agenda. She holds a PhD (Arts) from Goldsmiths, University of London and is currently Associate Professor at the Department of Fine Arts, Wits School of the Arts, Wits University, Johannesburg. You can read more about her practice here and here. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359313117","gid://shopify/Product/9452042879197","gid://shopify/Product/9452095832285","gid://shopify/Product/9452095897821","gid://shopify/Product/9452095930589","gid://shopify/Product/9452153209053","gid://shopify/Product/9452153307357","gid://shopify/Product/9452153438429","gid://shopify/Product/9452153503965","gid://shopify/Product/9452153831645","gid://shopify/Product/9452155699421","gid://shopify/Product/9452155830493","gid://shopify/Product/9452156059869"]

Explore her journey and cultural insights captured through her lens. [23003] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Shayma Idris (b. 1986, Saudi Arabia), is a documentary and street photographer. A native of Sudan, she grew up in Khartoum and earned a Bachelor of Dental Surgery. In 2013, she moved to Cairo to pursue her postgraduate degree. It was in the alleys of Old Cairo that she discovered her passion for capturing sceneries with her phone camera. \\nIn 2014, she joined a photojournalist initiative to create the EverydayCairo online photo project and participated in numerous national photography exhibitions. Shayma returned to Sudan in 2017 and started the EverydayKhartoum project, continuing to exhibit her work nationally. Due to economic difficulties, she moved to Saudi Arabia, where she lived in a small town with colleagues from 10 different nationalities, gaining insight into diverse cultures. In 2023, Shayma relocated to Spain to continue her life journey in a new continent, with a memory full of images that encapsulate her experiences."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014034170077"]

[22369] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sibonelo Chiliza (b. 1979, Mtwalume, Port Sheptsone) is a renowned botanical artist known for his exceptional focus and artistic skill. His early artistic endeavors included making intricate wire cars and clay sculptures. Chiliza studied Textile Design and Technology at Durban University of Technology, where his talent was recognized by artist and mentor Jean Powell. In 2004, he interned at the Durban Botanical Garden and later at the National Herbarium under botanical artist Gillian Condy. His work with the African Plants Initiative included managing the SANBI Pretoria art collection. \\n \\nChiliza's botanical art captures the freshness and colour of plants, ofen using Lyra pencils. His meticulous approach involves drawing from live plants to scale. He has contributed illustration to several books and participated in numerous exhibitions, including the SANBI Kirstenbosch Biennales, where he has won multiple awards. Chiliza's serene presence and dedication to his craft make his work both inspiring and technically precise."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015000797"]

View works like Girl with Blue Headband on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sibusiso Makhunga's innocent paintings display a yearning barely articulated. Either one values the artist's innocence - the work's purity - or, if doubtful and ironic, one might prematurely declare - NO. What we witness when looking at Makhunga's paintings is a yearning for honesty, a sensitivity to the unsung - the often forgotten truth of black life. \\n Njabulo Ndebele described this hidden truth superbly when he contrasted the Spectacular with the Ordinary - Black Life as the spectalurisation of abjection-pain-horror instead of a quiet incidental poetry. Sibusiso Makhunga has chosen to explore the latter."}]}]} []

[23414,23415,24414,24410,23188,24412,24416] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sichumile Adam (b. 2001) is an emerging visual artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. She recently graduated with an honours degree in Fine Arts from the University of Witwatersrand. As a multi-disciplinary artist, Sichumile works primarily with acrylic paint, fabric, and glass beads. Her work uniquely combines contemporary African American and South African imagery to create a landscape that resonates with women across the Black diaspora. \\nThrough curated posing, Sichumile uses the figures in her painting to celebrate and explore womanhood, drawing from both personal and collective experiences as a Black woman. The use of beads and fabric in artwork further celebrates her cultural heritage, adding texture and dimensions to her creations. \\nThis approach also enhances the viewing experience, encouraging viewers to engage with her painting up close and explore the intricate beading styles and techniques. “I enjoy using my art to explore the dynamic social cultures that women share globally, but from a South African context, ” says Sichumile."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452115460317","gid://shopify/Product/9452232802525","gid://shopify/Product/9452246794461"]

[20961,20958,22243,22242,20960,22245,25653,25652,20962,22244,25654,20959] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Silindokuhle Shandu (b. 1998) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work intricately weaves together themes influenced by her upbringing in a small mining town and her diverse experiences across urban, suburban, and rural South Africa. Raised in Empangeni, KwaZulu-Natal, and eMalahleni, Mpumalanga, Shandu's artistic journey reflects the complex interplay between womanhood, human existence, industrial landscapes, and the contrasting worlds she has encountered. \\nShandu completed her diploma in Fashion Design and Technology at Tshwane University of Technology in Pretoria. item.title: Simon Venter
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928544477 Simon Venter 1407 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641063567581 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014053961949", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054027485", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054060253", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054093021", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054125789", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054158557", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054256861", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054289629", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054322397", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054355165", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054420701"] Discover Simon Venter, a multidisciplinary artist who integrates traditional fine arts with emerging technologies like AI. His work explores creativity's evolving dynamics, engaging with themes of history, identity, and the meaning of life. [23665,23669,23661,23659,23304,23673,23300,23299,23658,23579,23670,23671,23760,23578,23580,23672,23662,23664] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simon Venteris a multidisciplinary artist who bridges traditional fine arts with emerging technologies to explore creativity in the digital age. With a foundation in classical oil painting, Venter incorporates artificial intelligence into his work, creating a dialogue between human ingenuity and machine-driven processes. This interplay critically examines how technology redefines creative boundaries, focusing on the tension between human agency and AI’s transformative presence in artistic production. \\nCentral to Venter's work is an engagement with archetypal themes and existential questions. Drawing from global traditions and cultural memory, his art weaves together symbols and narratives that speak to the timeless human pursuit of meaning and individuality. By juxtaposing traditional techniques with AI-generated elements, Venter addresses fundamental questions about the essence of creativity and the ways technology mediates our connection to history, identity, and the meaning of life. \\nVenter's projects often highlight critical themes, such as the myths surrounding AI’s perceived autonomy and intelligence, while challenging its status as a colonizing force in contemporary culture. His recent works include explorations of still life, existential symbolism, and architectural motifs, serving as metaphors for humanity’s complex relationship with technology. \\nA graduate of a Master’s program in Creative Media and Production, and a 'self-taught' artist, Venter has exhibited work both locally and internationally. His practice is deeply influenced by his South African heritage, rich in oral storytelling and visual traditions, which he combines with European art historical references to create a globally resonant dialogue. Venter’s art is a testament to the enduring relevance of traditional artistic techniques as a critical lens for understanding the rapid technological shifts shaping the 21st century, making him a compelling voice in contemporary art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014041084125","gid://shopify/Product/9014041116893","gid://shopify/Product/9014041182429","gid://shopify/Product/9014041215197","gid://shopify/Product/9014041247965","gid://shopify/Product/9014041313501","gid://shopify/Product/9014050455773","gid://shopify/Product/9014050521309","gid://shopify/Product/9013864300765","gid://shopify/Product/9014053961949","gid://shopify/Product/9014054027485","gid://shopify/Product/9014054060253","gid://shopify/Product/9014054093021","gid://shopify/Product/9014054125789","gid://shopify/Product/9014054158557","gid://shopify/Product/9014054191325","gid://shopify/Product/9014054256861","gid://shopify/Product/9014054289629","gid://shopify/Product/9014054322397","gid://shopify/Product/9014054355165","gid://shopify/Product/9014054420701","gid://shopify/Product/9014057730269"]

item.title: Simone Brewster
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641926742237 Simone Brewster 2760 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641064288477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452114739421","gid://shopify/Product/9452114772189","gid://shopify/Product/9452114804957","gid://shopify/Product/9452114870493","gid://shopify/Product/9452114903261"] Discover the art and fashion of Simone Brewster, a London-based artist and designer blending Caribbean roots with contemporary aesthetics. Her vibrant works celebrate Black female narratives, exploring identity through abstraction, rhythmic forms, and the fusion of ethnic and Western influences. [23164,23162,23161,23160] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Art and Fashion Experience \\nSimone Brewster (born 1983, London) is an artist, designer, and educator. A Bartlett School of Architecture graduate (2003) with a Masters in Design Products from the Royal College of Art (2007), Brewster boldly infuses her Caribbean roots into her work, celebrating Black female narratives through vibrant colors and rhythmic forms. Based in London, she explores craft, balancing beauty, functionality, and a fusion of “ethnic” and “western” influences. \\nIn painting, Brewster uses abstraction to delve into identity, expressing the hidden complexities of our internal landscapes. Her works transcend figurative art, inviting viewers to interpret layered shapes that reflect multifaceted identities. \\nIn fashion, she frames design as a reflection of emotion and self-discovery. Through colors and forms, she highlights the power of fashion to celebrate individuality and the \"beautiful messiness\" of identity, merging art and self-expression beyond aesthetics."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452114739421","gid://shopify/Product/9452114772189","gid://shopify/Product/9452114804957","gid://shopify/Product/9452114870493","gid://shopify/Product/9452114903261"]

item.title: Simone Verfaille
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641927233757 Simone Verfaille 2250 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641065435357 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013988950237", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004744413", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004809949", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004842717", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004875485", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004941021", "gid://shopify/Product/9014005006557", "gid://shopify/Product/9014030106845"] [21800,21798,21803,21804,21799,21801,21208] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simone Verfaille (b. 1995, Cape Town, South Africa) creates through the folds and layers of her life. After earning her BA(Hons) Fine Art from Stellenbosch University in 2018, she had a break from the art world, before returning in 2023 with renewed passion and perspective. \\n \\nTo Simone, art is not merely a product but a process that extends beyond the canvas. It mirrors the way we experience, navigate, and embrace life's ever-evolving nature. She believes that life, in all its facets, is best captured through the intricate layers that compose it. In all her work, she strives to capture the depth and richness of life, whether it be the present moment or memories. Each layer of paint represents a distinct memory, a fragment of time, or a moment of existence. To Simone, layers hold the power to create depth and dimensionality. Through layering, she’s able to process the multitude of narratives that shape our and her existence, both weaving together the personal and the universal. \\n \\nHer works become a captivating interplay of colors, forms, and textures, where she hopes to capture the folds and layers of her own sense of self, life and expression. Simone uses her artistic expression not only as a medium for self-discovery but also as a means to find her voice and articulate the profound beauty and complexity of the world."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013988950237","gid://shopify/Product/9014004744413","gid://shopify/Product/9014004809949","gid://shopify/Product/9014004842717","gid://shopify/Product/9014004875485","gid://shopify/Product/9014004941021","gid://shopify/Product/9014005006557","gid://shopify/Product/9014030106845","gid://shopify/Product/9013994815709","gid://shopify/Product/9013338210525","gid://shopify/Product/9013899329757"]

item.title: Simphiwe Julia Thabede
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928741085 Simphiwe Julia Thabede 1646 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641065992413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452047696093", "gid://shopify/Product/9452047761629"] [13635,13636,13637] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simphiwe Julia Thabede born 1999 is from Katlehong, the East of Johannesburg. \\nSimphiwe is a female visual artist working with the medium of photography and collage. \\nShe draws her inspiration from various artists such as; Pamela Tulizo, Ogorogile Nong \\nand Frida Orupabo to name a few. Simphiwe’s work is influenced by the everyday life \\nencounters and contemporary visual culture, Thabede completed the Foundation and \\nIntermediate Courses in Photography at The Market Photo Workshop in Newtown, \\nJohannesburg.Currently Thabede is completing the Advanced course at Through The \\nLens Collective, Simphiwe strongly believes that every individual has a story to tell and \\nfor her the camera is more than just a device for creating images but it is a tool for \\ncommunicating and creating dialogues with the self and the outside world."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452047696093","gid://shopify/Product/9452047761629","gid://shopify/Product/9452047827165"]

item.title: Sinalo Ngcaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928872157 Sinalo Ngcaba 1685 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641067630813 [11873,11617] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"My name is Sinalo Ngcaba, I'm a 27 year old visual artist from East London and Bizana but now based in Johannesburg. I'm self taught in technique but learnt about the industry when I was doing a year of design in advertising at Umuzi Academy. I'm always updating my style and trying new things with different mediums such as oil pastels, ink, digital and paint. \\n \\nI am a creative. I am a storyteller. I am an artist. In my art I explore the intersections of black joy, black pop culture, womanhood and human rights issues in a contemporary world. As creatives it's our duty to evoke emotions that can change the world for the better, to record and document stories of the current world we live in. I believe There's more to life than just breathing. \\n \\nI am grateful to have worked with brands and people such as Piano People UK, Nike, Aperol Spritz, Gauteng Dept. of Sports, Arts & Culture, Amref International, Comedy Central Africa and NATIVE Mag, Sindiso Khumalo and Bam Marley."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013362000093"]

item.title: Sipho Mpongo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929724125 Sipho Mpongo 374 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641069891805 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452036784349"] Sipho Mpongo, a South African photographer born in Nqamakwe, Eastern Cape, and raised in Langa, Cape Town, is known for his powerful visual stories documenting the "Born Free Generation" and advancing human rights. Currently studying at the Michaelis School of Fine Art. [3950,22360] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sipho Mpongo's (b. 1993, Eastern Cape) photographic journey began with IIiso Labantu, a local mentorship program, which propelled him into his career. Mpongo completed a full-time course at The Cape Town School of Photography. In 2014, he embarked on a four-month tour around South Africa with photographers Wikus de Wet and Sean Meterlerkamp, as part of the Twenty Journey project, documenting the \"Born Free Generation\" 20 years after apartheid. \\n \\nA member of the lliso Labantu photography collective, Mpongo is currently studying at the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town. In 2015, the Magnum Foundation recognized Mpongo as one of their Human Rights Fellows, providing scholarships and training for photographers from the Global South. Through this fellowship, he attended NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts in New York City, where he developed strategies for creating powerful visual stories to advance human rights."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452036784349"]

item.title: Siphokazi Mlangeni
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929461981 Siphokazi Mlangeni 2602 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641070088413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452097601757","gid://shopify/Product/9452097634525","gid://shopify/Product/9452097667293","gid://shopify/Product/9452097700061"] Siphokazi Mlangeni [21186,21190,21188,21415,21191,21189] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I Siphokazi Mlangeni was born on June 12, 2001, in Bergville KwaZulu \\nNatal. I later moved with my family to Johannesburg, Gauteng where I \\nattended primary school and later interchanged high schools between \\nKwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng. \\nThe passion I have for art developed during my early years of high school \\nwhen I taught myself how to draw. Upon studying BA Visual Arts at the \\nUniversity of KwaZulu-Natal I was introduced to the ceramics medium \\nwhich I felt more drawn to as I continuously worked with it. I realised that I \\nenjoyed working with the medium as it allows me to feel the clay, and to \\nmanipulate it into any form I may desire. \\nThe inspiration behind my work is the feminine body, particularly the vulva, and the positive and negative notions that society associates with it. As a young woman my experiences with my body and where I stand in society are also inspirational to my work. The series titled Ukuzihlola (2023) which is a part of the Decurex Exhibition was created for the purpose of my honours research at UKZN titled; State of the Vulva: Themes of virginity and female sexuality in the works of Suzanne Santoro, Lady Skollie, and Siphokazi Mlangeni. This body of work was informed by the themes of virginity and female sexuality, where I translated collected information into visual depictions to be consumed as art. \\nThese art pieces reflect on the descriptions extracted from my sources describing the changes that occur on a woman’s body upon losing her virginity. These changes include sagging breasts, stretchmarks on the waist and behind the legs, and any signs of cellulitis or loosening of the skin on the lower parts of the body. I took some of these descriptions and added them as textures on my vases with an attempt to embrace these changes as normal. The titles of the art works derive from the word intombi, describing a virgin girl in Zulu. \\nMy research and my works do not pose as a challenge, an agreement, or disagreement to the cultural practice of virginity testing. It is more of an inquiry on the practice, its notions, and the value that society holds against women through their bodies. \\nIn the process of creating these pieces as an artist, I felt more like an examiner looking into the vulvas and choosing which ones I viewed as “virgins” and “non-virgins” as I gave them characteristics that forced me to question how I feel about the practice as a woman who has never been exposed to it. I hold dear the idea of an individual examining her own virginity, both literally and metaphorically, something like self-reflecting, seeking to perceive yourself from your perception. This idea creates a feeling of acceptance and comfort in one’s skin, shadowing feelings of shame, hate, and other negative self-imagery that stem from women viewing themselves through the lens of society. \\nI appreciate how clay allows me to feel the work as I make it. Like my interpretation of Ukuzihlola, I feel and see parts of myself through the process of making art and from that I choose how to respond to the negative views of society associated with female sexuality."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452097601757","gid://shopify/Product/9452097634525","gid://shopify/Product/9452097667293","gid://shopify/Product/9452097700061"]

item.title: Sitaara Stodel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929953501 Sitaara Stodel 2021 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641071333597 ["gid://shopify/Product/9133212074205", "gid://shopify/Product/9133233930461", "gid://shopify/Product/9133233963229", "gid://shopify/Product/9133234028765"] Discover the evocative art of Sitaara Stodel, a Cape Town-based contemporary artist working across photography, collage, video, and printmaking. Her work, shaped by a lifetime of frequent relocations, reconstructs memories through found family photographs. Purchase her distinctive pieces online. [22290,22292,19249,19250,19251,22293,19253,19248,19254,25518,25519] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sitaara Stodel (b.1991) is a Cape Town-based contemporary artist whose practice spans photography, collage, video, and printmaking. Her unique artistic perspective is deeply influenced by a lifetime of frequent relocations, having moved house forty times. This transient lifestyle profoundly shapes her work, where she often reconstructs personal and collective memories through found family photographs sourced from antique stores and markets. \\nStodel's pieces are marked by her meticulous process of tearing, cutting, and reassembling these photographs, often using gold thread to symbolize the preciousness of memory. Her collages depict domestic scenes, integrating her ideals of home—complete with fresh flowers, framed artworks, houses with sea views, and shiny cars. \\nAfter graduating from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2014, Stodel received the prestigious Tierney Fellowship. She has since exhibited her work in numerous Cape Town galleries, including Zeitz MOCAA, SMAC Gallery, Smith Gallery, Gallery MOMO, and Everard Read. Stodel also contributes to the Michaelis photographic department as the technical officer of photography, utilizing her extensive knowledge of analogue photographic methods to influence her varied approaches to image-making"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013898608861","gid://shopify/Product/9013899329757","gid://shopify/Product/9013900181725","gid://shopify/Product/9013900935389","gid://shopify/Product/9013901787357","gid://shopify/Product/9013902573789","gid://shopify/Product/9133212074205","gid://shopify/Product/9133213188317","gid://shopify/Product/9133231636701","gid://shopify/Product/9133233930461","gid://shopify/Product/9133233963229","gid://shopify/Product/9133234028765"]
