item.title: Sizwe Khoza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931755741 Sizwe Khoza 327 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073332445 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013330182365", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330247901", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330346205", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330411741", "gid://shopify/Product/9014052978909"] [4211,4210,8706,8707,22400,19706,8709,8708,8705,4214,8715,4212,4213] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Khoza was born in Mozambique towards the end of the Civil War and moved to South Africa with his family in 1995. He matriculated in 2010 from Nkumbulo Comprehensive School and during his matric year he attended Saturday classes at Artist Proof Studio. Thereafter, he studied printmaking for three years and graduated in 2012. In 2013 he was awarded a residency through Artist Proof Studio at William Humphrey Art Gallery (WHAG) in Kimberley under the mentorship of the late Dumisani Mabaso. Khoza was then offered an internship at Artist Proof Studio in 2014 as a facilitator in Printmaking for first and second year students attending full time and chose to be a full-time artist from 2016. Twice a year Khoza travels to Mozambique to take photographs and sketch people and upon return creates new works inspired by his visit home. Khoza specializes in painting, monotype and combined printmaking techniques. In 2017 he was commissioned by Rand Merchant Bank Holdings to create an artwork for their boardroom. He donates two artworks a year to auction initiatives that raise money for education and continues to have exhibitions and shows around the country. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013330182365","gid://shopify/Product/9013330247901","gid://shopify/Product/9013330346205","gid://shopify/Product/9013330411741","gid://shopify/Product/9013330477277","gid://shopify/Product/9013330542813","gid://shopify/Product/9013330575581","gid://shopify/Product/9013330608349","gid://shopify/Product/9013330641117","gid://shopify/Product/9013330706653","gid://shopify/Product/9013330739421","gid://shopify/Product/9013937832157","gid://shopify/Product/9014015951069","gid://shopify/Product/9014052978909"]

item.title: Sizwe Nyanga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931821277 Sizwe Nyanga 2253 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073463517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013845459165","gid://shopify/Product/9013845491933","gid://shopify/Product/9013845524701","gid://shopify/Product/9013845557469"] [18716,18717,18714,18715] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Nyanga, an artist and community activist, merges creativity and social impact. Hailing from Vosloorus (South Africa), he sees art as a transformative force, blending research, education, and culture to reshape society's outlook through his photographs, paintings, drawings and multi-medium installations. \\nEducated at Umuzi.org in Multimedia, he has delved into the digital art space for over a decade, crafting a unique artistic voice. In 2018, his daring expedition backpacking from Johannesburg to Malawi with only R1300 a tent and a camera, captured in \"Mayendo Abwino\" (Photo-Essay), revealed his narrative through powerful imagery. This year, Sizwe exhibited twice in Bonn, Germany, leaving an indelible mark. \\nFirstly, with \"the holy trinity,\" presenting \"Please Don't Pinch\", at Alanus Hochschule für Kunst und Gesellschaft and later, an artist-in-residency project called \"Homeless in The Global Village\" at the Kunst Museum Bonn. \\nSizwe's art transcends borders, reflecting his dedication to preserving culture, fostering creativity, and creating conversation through his stories and photographs. His journey showcases art's transformative potential and its ability to shape a better tomorrow. Now, he expands his artistic horizon into music, film, and performing arts as mediums to convey his evolving ideas."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013845459165","gid://shopify/Product/9013845491933","gid://shopify/Product/9013845524701","gid://shopify/Product/9013845557469"]

item.title: Sizwe Sama
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931952349 Sizwe Sama 2223 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073758429 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452040290525", "gid://shopify/Product/9452057788637"] [16719,18312,16685,18303,16690,18304,18305,18310,16686,16687,18311,18308,18318] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Sama (b.1986) is a self-taught visual artist from Kwa-Zulu Natal, who learnt about art from his local library in Pietermaritzburg and from visiting the Tatham Art Gallery. The fabrics he uses in his tapestries are sometimes recycled from his own closet, or acquired for their specific visual impact and cultural references. The imitation tartans and Kente cloths used in these works draw attention to the intercultural translation of visual languages, and the ease with which cultural forms are appropriated and cross-pollinated in a globalised world. \\n \\nFor Sama, this plurality is always proudly celebrated. He sees his work as a tribute to the LGBTQI+ community, as calls to freedom and self-expression, just as art-making has allowed him to express his own queer identity. \\n \\nAs much as his work is a highly visible outward celebration of queer personhood, it is also deeply rooted in his personal experiences and memories. Sama learned sewing by hand from his mother, a seamstress who raised him and his brother alone, and who mended their clothes in particular ways. \\n \\nSama has exhibited in multiple group shows with Guns & Rain and had his first solo with the gallery in 2022. He has also recently shown work at Galerie Christophe Person in Paris, and at the KZNSA Gallery in Durban, as well as at Duende Art Projects in Antwerp, Belgium, MOV’ART in \\n \\nLisbon, Portugal, and by Africa First/Gordon Gallery in Tel Aviv, Israel. His work already sits in multiple international and local collections, including the AMAWAL (Spain), ARAK (Qatar) and Africa First (Israel) Collections."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452040290525","gid://shopify/Product/9452057788637","gid://shopify/Product/9452057854173"]

item.title: Sma Rajoale Kumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932443869 Sma Rajoale Kumalo 599 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641075396829 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035703005","gid://shopify/Product/9452035735773"] Sma Rajoale Kumalo, based in uMlazi, KZN, creates ritualistic video, installation, and photographic art that challenges cultural and religious norms, focusing on post-colonial trauma and queer identity in the context of African heritage. [3094,3095] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sma Rajoale Kumalo is a multidisciplinary artist based in uMlazi, KwaZulu-Natal, who uses video, installation, and photography to document his ritual performances. Raised in a strict Christian household by his paternal grandmother, who rejected Zulu traditions, Kumalo was also influenced by his grandfather, who embraced his African Zulu/Sotho heritage and playfully called him \"Bussman\" due to his lighter skin. \\nAs a queer Black man, Kumalo’s work is deeply rooted in exploring the tension between societal expectations, such as religion and culture, which uphold heteronormative sexualities. \\nIn this 2017 exhibition, The Monkey on My Shoulder, Kumalo examines post/colonialism and psychological trauma, particularly in the context of being considered the Other. His research into historical figures like Sara Baartman and Frans Taaibosch, who were displayed as “freaks” in European colonial freak shows, alongside the work of artists like Tracey Rose and Nandipha Mntambo, informs his artistic exploration. Kumalo’s work engages with the concept of cultural contestation and resistance, focusing on how these artists challenge European colonialism by inserting their bodies into their works, as seen in pieces like Venus Baartman (2001) and The Rape of Europa (2009). \\nDrawing from their legacy, Kumalo presents his own counter-gaze, performing his identity at historical colonial sites in Durban, such as Francis Farewell Square, the Natural Science Museum at City Hall, and his former school, George Campbell School of Technology. His art challenges oppressive narratives, reflecting on the complexities of cultural identity and the effects of colonialism."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452035703005","gid://shopify/Product/9452035735773"]

item.title: Smiso Cele

Cele is currently living in Johannesburg, practicing as an artist and completing his third year of his BA in Visual Arts at the University of Johannesburg. In his latest works he’s been exploring his interest in printmaking and drawing, trying to merge the two. \\n \\nAs per Cele's prolonged desire to be an artist, he chose Visual Arts as a subject in high school (Olwandle High School). item.title: Sol
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932902621 Sol gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076150493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355282653","gid://shopify/Product/9013355774173","gid://shopify/Product/9013355872477"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sol is a first-generation Eritrean South African. Having experienced life through various lenses, she's learnt to develop a strong sense of story. \\n \\n'Understanding that despite all our differences, we're all fundamentally the same. We all want peace, love, and to feel valued and heard. Wherever you go on this planet, you will always meet people with dreams and stories they want to share. That's the secret to great storytelling. Understanding.' \\n \\nSol has worked as a producer and scriptwriter in the South African Film and Television industry for the past few years. She aspires to create co-production across the African continent and bring our uniquely African stories to the rest of the world with an emphasis on showing the beautiful capabilities and strengths that lie in African stories."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355282653","gid://shopify/Product/9013355774173","gid://shopify/Product/9013355872477"]

item.title: Solomon Geleta
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641933754589 Solomon Geleta gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076281565 [] Solomon Geleta Urgessa is an Ethiopian visual artist known for his evocative figurative paintings that delve into human emotions, identity, and societal dynamics. His work has been showcased at Post Gallery in Addis Ababa and featured in the 2024 FNB Art Joburg Fair. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Solomon Geleta Urgessa (b. 1990) is a full-time studio artist based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in painting from the Addis Ababa University Alle School of Fine Arts and Design in 2018. Following in the footsteps of his brother Asrat Urgessa and Tesfaye Urgessa (60th Venice Biennial - Ethiopia Pavilion) who graduated from the same school in 2004 and 2006, respectively Solomon also studied under the influential Ethiopian modernist artist Tadesse Mesfin. \\nSolomon focuses on capturing the essence of daily urban life within the broader community. His artwork serves as a critical commentary on the constantly evolving social and political structures. As an emerging artist, Solomon is actively developing his unique visual language, drawing inspiration from the works of his former mentor, Tadesse Mesfin, and his older brother, Tesfaye Urgessa. Solomon, who prefers oil painting because he believes it enables him to capture the nuances of the flesh effectively, portrays figures that make direct eye contact with the viewer. In his most recent collection titled \"Connections,\" the artist delves into the political and social implications of engaging with and consuming information in the realm of social media. \\nSolomon Urgessa is currently represented by Post Gallery Ethiopia, which showcased his works at the FnB Joburg 2024 Art Fair. Moreover, he has been involved in numerous exhibitions hosted by the Addis Ababa Museum, Alliance Ethio-Française, Addis Ababa City Hall, and the Sheraton Addis. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Songezo Zantsi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641933820125 Songezo Zantsi 1030 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076576477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452064932061","gid://shopify/Product/9452095340765"] [18046,18805,17484,20892,20893,18807,21076,18043,18808] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Songezo Zantsi (b. 1991) is a Cape town born and based multidisciplinary mixed media contemporary artist. He studied Art & Design at college of Cape Town, and graduated in 2017. Zantsi has worked in the design industry for two years and started his solo career in 2019. \\nIn 2019 he joined the Association For Visual Arts (AVA) Gallery on their installation crew training program which he completed in 2020, 2021 he became part of a group exhibition at Association For Visual Arts (AVA) Gallery called IDENTITY. \\nZantsi's work explores with cultures that encompasses social behaviours, ritual’s, customs, traditions, beliefs faced by different ethnic groups. The works conceptions are mostly personal experience based and multi layered referenced. \\nSongezo Zantsi is a painter and mixed-media artist who portrays African culture and traditions, particularly that of the Ciskei and Transkei people. Through his work, Zantsi questions why many of the products used in traditional ceremonies are Western objects, in turn raising questions about where and how culture and tradition are formed. He also laments the loss of pre-colonial identity."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452064932061","gid://shopify/Product/9452095340765"]

item.title: Sophia Van Wyk
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641934803165 Sophia Van Wyk 592 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641077264605 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452092981469","gid://shopify/Product/9014031155421"] Sophia van Wyk is a South African artist with a background in fine arts and furniture making. Her work blends craftsmanship with conceptual art, exploring themes of materiality, myth, and history. Her latest solo exhibition, Future Mythology, was held at Everard Read Cape Town in 2022. \n \n [23810,3273,14108,20828,22938] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sophia van Wyk is a South African artist who earned her Bachelor of Fine Arts at the University of Stellenbosch and graduated cum laude with a Master of Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg in 2015. Along with her fine art education, van Wyk holds qualifications in furniture making, with a specialization in wood machining and cabinet making. This technical skill in craftsmanship plays a significant role in her artistic practice, blending both conceptual and material elemens in her works. \\n \\nBetween 2007 and 2013, van Wyk was actively involved in community engagement workshops and artist talks, which shaped her approach to art-making and deepened her connection to both local and global art communities. Her most recent solo exhibition, Future Mythology, was held at Everard Read Cape Town in May 2022. She has also participated in numerous group exhibitions across South Africa, including at the renowned NIROX Sculpture Park, and has been awarded several prestigious residencies both locally and internationally, further enhancing her exploration of contemporary art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452092981469","gid://shopify/Product/9014031155421"]

item.title: Sophie Mahlangu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641934934237 Sophie Mahlangu 2438 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641077625053 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452157862109","gid://shopify/Product/9452157927645"] [20914] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nguni beadwork is a vibrant form of communication among Zulu and Ndebele peoples, evolving from traditional materials like bone and shells to colorful plastic beads. Renowned Zulu beadworks express intricate societal themes through their shapes and patterns. \\n \\nSouth African musician Sophie Msoziswa Mahlangu gained international recognition for her exceptional beadwork, winning the 2020 Innibos National Craft Awards in the Beading Category. Her winning entry, a pair of intricately beaded bicycles, showcased her originality and skill, inspired by her mother's craftsmanship. \\n \\nBased in Gamorwa, Mpumalanga, Mahlangu sells her beadwork through Nomhlekhabo Craft Africa, catering to both local ceremonial needs and tourist interests. She advocates for women's empowerment through craft and educates others in traditional Ndebele arts alongside Dr. Esther Mahlangu. \\n \\nMahlangu emphasizes the importance of perseverance and originality, both in her own work and in mentoring her children and students. Through her efforts, she continues to inspire and preserve the rich cultural heritage of Southern African beadwork. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452157862109","gid://shopify/Product/9452157927645"]

item.title: Sophie Smith
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935098077 Sophie Smith 2542 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078149341 Discover the evocative work of Sophie Smith, a lifestyle photographer based in Kenton on Sea, South Africa. Her images blend documentary photography with fine art, capturing the intimate dynamics between women, children, and nature, and evoking deep emotions through the magic of everyday moments. [22462,22463,22464] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sophie Smith (b. 1988) is a lifestyle photographer based in Kenton-on-Sea in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. Her creative journey is a mirror of her personal evolution, embarking on a path of introspection and healing while documenting tender moments of motherhood and her children's lives. This journey has fueled her fascination with the intimate dynamics between women, children, and nature, particularly the healing properties of water. \\nTrained as a photojournalist, Sophie practiced documentary-style photography for many years. However, it was only after having children that she began to blend documentary photography with fine art, creating images that evoke emotion rather than just capturing moments. Sophie's work is an artistic documentation of life, capturing both the big moments and the small, seemingly mundane ones, in a way that allows viewers to relive the depth and soul of those experiences. \\nSophie's philosophy revolves around the collaboration between the photographer and the subject, capturing authentic and intimate moments in the most beautiful way when the subjects feel relaxed and confident. She believes in creating a sweet spot between storytelling and art, capturing the magic that already exists within her subjects. \\nDeeply inspired by life, nature, and her children, Sophie is obsessed with light and shadow and how they dance together. Her ability to blend storytelling with art has been nurtured over the years, allowing her to see what others might not notice and turn it into magical photographs. Living near the ocean in Kenton on Sea, Sophie finds daily inspiration and a sense of freedom, but she also loves the feeling of being on the road in search of new adventures."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014018212061","gid://shopify/Product/9014018277597","gid://shopify/Product/9014018310365"]

item.title: Sotiris Moldovanos
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935196381 Sotiris Moldovanos gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078477021 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452278644957","gid://shopify/Product/9452278710493"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sotiris Moldovanos (b.1977) was born in Johannesburg and obtained a B.Tech degree in Fine Arts from the Pretoria Technikon (now known as the Tshwane University of Pretoria) in 1999. \\n \\nMoldovanos focuses on painting, with a preference for portraiture and figurative work as subject matter. These figures, while anatomically accurate, are simplified and flattened to become outlines and silhouettes. He would often hide the figures, providing clues of its existence through the use of vibrant patterns reminiscent of op art and hard-edge abstraction. \\n \\nIn his recent work, Moldovanos incorporates bold flat colours with geometric patterns to create a sense of optical illusion. He plays with positive and negative spaces and blurs the lines between subject and background. The result is a surreal illusion where the viewer experiences uncertainty. This is extended with the use of realistically painted elements that are juxtaposed with the abstract patterns, offering clues to possible varied meanings. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452278644957","gid://shopify/Product/9452278710493"]

item.title: Stacey Gillian Abe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935589597 Stacey Gillian Abe 2459 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641080246493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452081643741"] [19375] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stacey Gillian Abe (b. 1991 in Kampala, Uganda) graduated from Kyambogo University, Kampala, with a BA in Art and Industrial Design. \\nAbe is a Ugandan contemporary artist whose practice includes photography, sculpture, installation, performance, and painting. By drawing from past experiences and using her autobiography to highlight the strengths and fragilities of the female mind, her work references identity, gender, spirituality, and cultural mysticism by criticizing stereotypical depictions of black women. Each space that Gillian works in has its particular context and receives its own interpretation; highlighting self-resilience and that which can be overcome. \\nThe stereotypes she addresses in her work materialize into imagined spaces that instigate a surreal mystical feel borne of two realms, contrasting and complementing each other. The artist incorporates a metaphorical and experimental approach to her work through her interest in exploring new techniques with parallel mediums like glass and ceramics, fibers, textures, and photography. Her work draws attention to the hand-made through the method of tying together and binding, stitching, clustering, and pairing which are assembled and layered into a metaphorical concept. \\nShe has received numerous awards, and, in 2018, the artist was listed among the Forbes Africa 30 under 30 Creatives. The artist has held various artist residencies among them Urbane Künste, Dortmund (2019) and Fondation Blachère, Apt (2018). Her work has been exhibited in both Africa and abroad, at Nairobi Museum, Nairobi; Institut Francais Kinshasha, Kinshasa; Goethe institute, Nairobi and the 12th Dakar Biennale, Dakar, among others. In 2020, she participated at the 2020 Stellenbosch Trienniale, Cape Town. She lives and works in Kampala, UG. \\n\"My concepts are more or less birthed from a personal context and then blown out of proportion, shrunk, distorted or disintegrated from which possible meaning and interpretations are shifted… I personally believe we are spiritual beings and that there exists no hard and fast distinction between the spiritual and physical (or material) world and a life oriented towards an inner being.\" – Stacey Gillian Abe"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452081643741"]

item.title: Stefanie Langenhoven
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935917277 Stefanie Langenhoven gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641081393373 Discover the poetic and nature-inspired works of Stefanie Langenhoven, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through delicate textures, organic forms, and subtle color palettes, Langenhoven explores themes of memory, emotion, and the natural world. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stefanie studied at the National College of Photography in Pretoria, where she graduated with a joint best portfolio award, (2004). After her studies, she started a commercial photography studio and was represented by Shine Photographers Johannesburg. In 2008, Stefanie moved to the UK where she studied for a diploma in Transpersonal Integrative Psychotherapy at the Centre for Counseling and Psychotherapy Education in London, (2009 – 2013). In June 2015 Stefanie returned to South Africa. She has been a full-time artist since 2015. In 2022 she was awarded as one of the winners of The British Journal of Photography’s Female in focus awards. In 2023 she was awarded as a finalist in the Lensculture Black and White awards, and became a winner in the Lensculture Art photography awards 2024. \\nRecently she has also been shortlisted for British Journal of Photography Portrait of Humanity Vol 6, and BBA Prizes, her shortlisted series will be exhibited at BBA Gallery, Berlin. Her work has been Published in the book Eye Mama: Poetic Truths of Home and Motherhood by Karni Arieli (foreword by Allesia Glaviano) and featured in: The Guardian; British Journal of Photography: Brenda Magazine; Hashtagphotomag; Unvael Journal; Oath Journal; Korper Magazine; Accumen Magazine; FotoFemme United etc. She has been exhibited all around South Africa as well as in London, UK; Paris, France; Uslan, South Korea; Miami, and in New York, USA."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452112445661"]

item.title: Stephané Conradie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641936244957 Stephané Conradie gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641081819357 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stephané Conradie is a senior lecturer in printmedia at Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, South Africa. \\nAlthough primarily a trained printmaker, her artistic practice is invested in bricolage assemblages with a focus on object ontologies. Her research and practice stem from a fascination with how people arrange sentimental objects in their homes, particularly in her family member’s homes in Namibia and South Africa. Her ornate sculptures and prints examine the histories of colonialism and creolisation embedded in domestic material culture. \\nConradie holds a PhD in Visual Arts at the University of Stellenbosch, where she completed her MA in Visual Arts (Art Education). Most recently Conradie was included in Materiality (2020) an exhibition at the Iziko National Gallery, the Megalo International Print Prize 2020, Kingston, Australia and Black Luminosity (2021) curated by Gcotyelwa Mashiqa at SMAC Gallery in Stellenbosch, The vibration of things, The 15th edition of the Triennial of Small Sculpture, Fellbach, Germany (2022), (IM)MATERIALITY, Águeda Arts Center, Portugal (2022), Souvenir, a solo exhibition at Whatiftheworld, Cape Town (2022) and Find/Fuse, a two-person exhibition with Elise Thompson at Ceysson Bénétière, New York (2023) curated by Maëlle Ebelle & Francesca Pessarelli. \\nConradie’s work is held in several private and public collections namely the Leridon Collection, France, GAUTREAUX Collection, Cansas City and UNISA Art Gallery, South Africa."}]}]} []

item.title: Stephen Hobbs
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641936343261 Stephen Hobbs 505 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641082245341 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452121587933","gid://shopify/Product/9452121620701"] [23713,23714] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stephen Hobbs was born in Johannesburg in 1972. Since 1994, Johannesburg has served as a critical reference point for Hobbs’ artistic and curatorial insights into the apartheid-city-turned-African-city, with a particular interest in the impact of defensive urban planning and architecture on the behavioral aspects of city and society. Hobbs’ functions not only as a practicing studio artist and dedicated printmaker, but also as a public arts curator and advocate. Having recently relocated with his family to the Republic of Ireland, Hobbs is based between County Cork, London and Johannesburg. \\n \\nHobbs’ printmaking practice is informed by the complex, often obfuscating, visual language and urban defensive planning used to construct cities. He works predominantly in etching, linocut and monotype, and his prints serve as a distillation of his practice – public and studio-based. \\n \\nDazzle camouflage has been a key trope in Hobbs’ practice for many years – a zebra-like pattern used on gunships in the early 1900s to fragment the visual field of enemy sites in combat situations. Although dazzle patterning became obsolete after World War I, Hobbs has mined the potential that such visual deception presents for aesthetic reflection on dystopian urban environments. Since moving to Ireland, Hobbs has begun to activate a new making trajectory that began during his three-year-long research project resulting in his Permanent Culture exhibition in Cape Town in 2015, and which involved thinking in a different way about the intersections between defensive architecture, theatre and visual optics. \\n \\nHobbs graduated from Wits University with a BAFA, in 1994. He was the curator of the Market Theatre Galleries (Johannesburg) from 1994 to 2000, and Co-Director of the purpose-built Gallery Premises (2004-2008) at the Joburg Theatre. Since 2001 he has co-directed the artist collaborative and public art consultancy, The Trinity Session, and since 2004 has co-produced a range of multi-medium urban and network-focused projects with Marcus Neustetter, under the collaborative name Hobbs/Neustetter. From 2017-2019, Hobbs joined the Graduate School of Architecture at the University of Johannesburg, as Unit Leader and resident critic. Since 2002 The Trinity Session has provided consultative and turnkey services with regards to the development and procurement of various scales of public art, in most of the major metropolitan areas of South Africa."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452121587933","gid://shopify/Product/9452121620701"]

item.title: Stephen Langa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641936605405 Stephen Langa 1779 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641082409181 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013457715421", "gid://shopify/Product/9013457748189", "gid://shopify/Product/9013457780957", "gid://shopify/Product/9013457846493", "gid://shopify/Product/9013457879261"] [23933,11947,16979,16978,18912,16981,16982,16980,11948] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stephen Langa (b. 1995) is a South African Contemporary Artist from the Limpopo province. Langa currently lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\nStephen practiced art at a very young age, from drawing cartoon characters to becoming a professional artist who specializes in different mediums such as charcoal drawing, watercolor, and oil paintings. He studied Art & Design at the Tshwane North College in Pretoria. Furthermore, he studied Printmaking at Artist Proof Studios (APS). \\nHis body of work explores diverse stories of black people and experiences of those around him and personal journey of life. His work is Inspired by the Impressionism art period from the 20th Century, he researches and explores ways to capture his emotions and fuel his artworks. Inspired by profound artist such as George Pemba, Claude Monet, Gerald Sekoto and Vincent Van Gogh, my charcoal linework’s and oil paintings have become pictorial visions that has a mesmerizing effect that is inspired directly by my emotive feelings that one can immediately identify and engage with the characters portrayed in such a way one would like to know them better in person. \\nLanga's work seeks to galvanize and has intimacy of black cultural experiences, composition’s that have questions for the viewer and highlights of his own experiences of his hometown and the city as visual detailed in his journey, experiencing life in both worlds from moving to one place to another. \\n‘’There’s a lot of intimacy when I’m engaging with my practice, and how I can evolve as an artist and myself\" states Langa."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013457715421","gid://shopify/Product/9013457748189","gid://shopify/Product/9013457780957","gid://shopify/Product/9013457846493","gid://shopify/Product/9013457879261","gid://shopify/Product/9013849030877","gid://shopify/Product/9013849096413","gid://shopify/Product/9014063792349"]

item.title: Steve Maphoso
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641936965853 Steve Maphoso 2203 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641082736861 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452133843165", "gid://shopify/Product/9452133974237", "gid://shopify/Product/9452134629597", "gid://shopify/Product/9452134760669"] Meet Steve Maphoso, a Johannesburg-based, Angolan-born self-taught artist. Discover his charcoal drawings exploring memory, loss, love, and identity in contemporary life. [24481,24473,24462,24479,23830,24480,24466] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Steve Maphoso (b. 1990, Viana, Luanda, Angola) is a self-taught artist currently based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Since completing his secondary education in 2010, he has developed his artistic practice and contributed to teaching and mentorship projects, including MC Art at the State Threatre in Pretoria. Working primarily and with renewed energy in charcoal on paper, Maphoso delves into social and personal issues, drawing inspiration from memories, experiences of loss and themes of love. \\n \\nAs a contemporary African artist, he aims to express his world and reflect the complexities of daily life. He views his art as a vital reminder of identity, a way to document even small triumphs, and foster pride through navigating both failures and accomplishments. \\n \\nMaphoso has held solo exhibitions, including at Trent Gallery (2020), and participated in numerous group shows at significant venues such as the Pretoria Art Museum (2018), Turbine Art Fair (2022), Lizamore Gallery (2023), and auctions facilitated by Strauss & Co (2023). He was recognized as a finalist in the Culture Leader Arts Competition in 2019 and his work is represented in collections such as the MAD Leadership Foundation. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452133843165","gid://shopify/Product/9452133974237","gid://shopify/Product/9452134105309","gid://shopify/Product/9452134629597","gid://shopify/Product/9452134695133","gid://shopify/Product/9452134760669"]

item.title: Sthembiso Zwane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641937227997 Sthembiso Zwane 2850 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641083523293 [] Discover the evocative linocut prints of Sthembiso Zwane, a South African artist capturing the textured faces and emotional depth of elder communities. Explore award?shortlisted works and exhibitions now on Latitudes Online. [23943] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sthembiso Zwane is the assistant printmaker at Prints on Paper and a full-time artist and printmaker based in Johannesburg. His paintings and prints attempt to express a sense of humanity and the idea of hope by highlighting moods, emotions and social sensibilities. \\nThese ideas are often concentrated solely on the face of his subjects, which are often portraits of elderly men and women who have reached a ripe old age. Zwane studied printmaking at Artist Proof Studio (2009 – 2010) where he obtained a certificate. He has participated in a number of group exhibitions, including the Print Portfolio Exchange, Sasol New Signatures Competition, and Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards. \\nZwane’s captivating portraits are such that one cannot merely glance across them and assume that they are thereby known. On the contrary, we look and cannot stop looking. On the contrary Zwane’s portraits are the fretwork of a beguiling infinity. We look and cannot stop looking."}]}]} []

item.title: Strauss Louw
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641937686749 Strauss Louw 1158 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084571869 [] [18628] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Strauss Louw was born in 1992 in South Africa. In 2022, he completed a Master of Fine Arts from the University of Stellenbosch. He currently lives and works in Stellenbosch. \\nThe group shows that Louw has participated in include The Phoenix Runway, presented at Whatiftheworld in Cape Town, South Africa, and Falling Awake at The FOURTH; RESERVOIR curated both shows. Hot House, curated by Jana Terblanche at Sixty Six in London, UK, in 2022. Emphatic Whispers at SMITH Studio, Cape Town and 2k.2 ‘Untitled’ at No End Contemporary in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 2019 and Close Encounters at SMITH Studio in 2018. His work has been included in group presentations at the RMB Turbine Art Fair in 2020 and Latitudes Online in 2021. \\nAlso in 2021, Louw presented a small body of work titled Bitter-Sweet-Salt as part of his Master’s degree for the Artist Room programme at SMAC Gallery in Stellenbosch, South Africa. His first solo exhibition was Showing Skin at Whatiftheworld in Cape Town in August 2022. \\nCentral to Louw’s work is experimentation with photographic processes, namely the 19th-century salt print and silver gelatin print. He regularly combines glass, cloth and imitation gold leaf with these processes to reconfigure the original image. “I like to say that I am a languid photographer,” says Louw. “What I mean to express is that I don’t actively seek to photograph but have adopted a languorous photographic methodology, a perpetual process of photographing on the fly, so to speak. I build an archive of images captured in response to my experiences through this process.”"}]}]} []

item.title: Stuart James Arnold
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641937817821 Stuart James Arnold gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084866781 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452139872477","gid://shopify/Product/9452140069085","gid://shopify/Product/9452140265693"] Discover the captivating work of Stuart James Arnold, a South African artist exploring form, texture, and emotional depth through evocative visual storytelling. Explore his artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Stuart James Arnold (b.1960) is a visual artist from Botswana working primarily in analogue photography, with a distinctive practice merging intense technical experimentation and poetic exploration of Indigenous people, The San and other tribes within their natural landscapes. Rooted in Southern Africa, his work captures fleeting, often overlooked interactions between humans and their environments—revealing the sacred in the mundane and the ephemeral in the enduring. \\nStuart juxtaposes the profound beauty and harshness of Botswana’s landscapes with deeply personal stories of the people who remain intrinsically tied to the land despite being systematically excluded from it. \\nStuart's analogue process is meticulous and intensively hands-on. Using vintage cameras, hand-processed film, and alternative darkroom techniques, he pushes the boundaries of traditional photography. Emulsion lifts, solarizations, and intentional chemical distortions transform each image into a vibrant print—one that resists replication and celebrates the materiality of the medium. \\nHis subjects are portrayed with great respect, allowing the terrain and cultural context to speak through grain, blur, and light. \\nDriven by lifelong storytelling and the impermanence of memory, Stuart's photographs are both document and dream—archival yet experimental. His work has been exhibited in regional and international shows, resonating with audiences drawn to analogue revivalism and ecological awareness. Stuart continues to create from his darkroom in Botswana, forging a unique visual language that honours both craft and connection."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452139872477","gid://shopify/Product/9452140069085","gid://shopify/Product/9452140265693"]

{"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Johannesburg based artist, Sue Martin, has been honing her painting and printmaking skills since the 1980s when she completed a BA Fine Arts degree at the University of Natal in Pietermaritzburg. Sue writes about her recent body of work, \"My African Garden\" \\n \\nOver the past year, my studio transformed and became what I like to refer to as my ‘magic garden’. An environment of fantasy and wonder where I found myself spending hours exploring and playing. I found beauty in my artworks and the various materials that surrounded me. \\n \\nLike a garden I need light, and I allow this light to shine out of my work. Love is light. \\n \\nThis body of work is a celebration of life and its fragility. \\n \\nThis show comprises a body of new paintings, monoprints and etchings. The series of monoprints began evolving last year as a response to the death of my Mother. Her passion was her garden. Unlike the wild indigenous garden that I have surrounding my home, my mother’s garden was an English country-style garden, comprising of many exotic plants carefully pruned into compliance. She spent hours maintaining her garden, she planted in ‘beds’, along boundary walls and around the house: neat, orderly and clipped back. \\n \\nMy images of peonies, poppies and dahlias are a nostalgic reference to these past memories. Juxtaposed with images from my own indigenous garden, which is wild, unruly and left to self-seed and regenerate, as the seasons come and go. The Iris, referenced in my “Lie of the Land” series, represents a colonial, bygone era, blooming only for a short period of time. Its exotic, foreign beauty strangely out of place in the harsh highveld landscape. \\n \\nIn the “Cartographer’s Notes” series, I have worked onto the surface of found maps, which take on a more botanical theme. Plants and places that I have seen and visited, have re emerged onto the surface, in a bright and spontaneous way. The limited edition of etchings, with their sketch-like quality, denotes a field study, capturing the essence of a plant seen in nature, to be taken home and reworked in the studio. \\n \\n“But I believe above all that I wanted to build the palace of my memory, because my memory is my only homeland.” - Anselm Kiefer \\n \\nAll the prints were done in collaboration with printer Bevan de Wet at Eleven Editions. \\n"}]}]} item.title: Sulette van der Merwe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641942536413 Sulette van der Merwe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641086996701 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452083019997", "gid://shopify/Product/9452083118301", "gid://shopify/Product/9452256788701", "gid://shopify/Product/9452256854237", "gid://shopify/Product/9452256952541"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cape Town-based artist Sulette van der Merwe draws inspiration from philosophy, art history, and digital culture to create vibrant paintings and video animations. Her work delves into the concept of Heterotopia, exploring spaces with hidden layers of meaning beyond the surface. \\n \\nVan der Merwe's artistic process is a playful dance between the physical and the digital. She enjoys weaving together diverse elements like illustrations, internet imagery, and photography, fostering a dynamic conversation between traditional painting and the fleeting nature of online experiences. This results in captivating abstractions that spark the viewer's imagination. \\n \\nEducation \\n \\n2004 Dip Fine Arts. Tshwane University of Technology \\n \\n \\nSelected Exhibitions \\n \\n2024 Surreal synapse at WORLDART \\n2022: Investec Cape Town Art Fair \\n2021: Node at WORLDART \\n2020: Turbine Art Fair (online) \\n2019: Summer group show, WORLDART, Cape Town \\n2019: \"nano 1.3,\" Barnard Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452083019997","gid://shopify/Product/9452083118301","gid://shopify/Product/9452256788701","gid://shopify/Product/9452256854237","gid://shopify/Product/9452256919773","gid://shopify/Product/9452256952541"]

item.title: Sydney Kumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641943847133 Sydney Kumalo 2478 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641088995549 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452137545949"] Sydney Kumalo [24764] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\\n \\nSydney Kumalo born and grew up in Soweto, Johannesburg. He attended Polly Street Art Centre from 1948 where he studied under Cecil Skotnes. He soon became an assistant to Skotnes and later a teacher at the school. The Centre was forced to close in 1957, but reopened in a new location as the Jubilee Art Centre, where Kumalo continued to teach and mentor students. He worked on two mural commissions for churches with Skotnes and spent time in the studio of Edoardo Villa where he was exposed to the work of modernist sculptors such as Constantin Brâncu?i, Henry Moore and Marino Marini. In 1962, Kumalo had his first solo exhibition at Egon Guenther’s gallery and showed later in the 60s with Guenther’s Amadlozi Group, which included Villa, Skotnes, Cecil Sash, Giuseppe Cattaneo and later Ezrom Legae. \\n \\nKumalo was exposed to central and west African sculpture though Guenther’s extensive collection and synthesised his own style from African and Modernist precedents. His bronzes depict human and animal forms, sometimes in combination, using expressive figuration with striated and stippled surface texture. Kumalo had work on numerous local and international exhibitions including at the Grosvenor Gallery, London, in 1965 and 1967, and at the Venice and São Paulo Biennales in 1966 and 1968, respectively. His work is in the collections of the Johannesburg Art Gallery; Rembrandt van Rijn Art Foundation; Iziko South African National Gallery; University of Fort Hare; and Wits Art Museum."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452137545949"]

[25258,21144,25260,15758,21146,25259,21147,16369,25231,21145,15458] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in De-Aar in 1985, and raised across Taung (Magogong) and Mafikeng, Sylvester Falata moved to Johannesburg in 2006. he moved to Johannesburg, where he currently lives and works. His artistic journey officially began during his time at Mmabatho High School, where he pursued art as a subjects. He has maintained his commitment to art creation ever since, even as his creativity expanded into the realm of fashion. \\n \\nFalata's artworks are profoundly influenced by his extensive background in fashion, which commenced in 2005 under the mentorship of Annah Getaneh and Eric Raisina. He launched his eponymous fashion label in 2010, showcasing collections at both South African Fashion Week and internationally. This fashion sensibility is clearly visible in his art, particularly in his sophisticated use of colour, texture, and experimental approach to proportions. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013424488669","gid://shopify/Product/9013430026461","gid://shopify/Product/9013441265885","gid://shopify/Product/9013986164957","gid://shopify/Product/9013986296029","gid://shopify/Product/9013986328797","gid://shopify/Product/9013986492637","gid://shopify/Product/9014130376925","gid://shopify/Product/9014138044637","gid://shopify/Product/9014138142941","gid://shopify/Product/9014138241245"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641944305885 Tabax’ae Ntcõx’o gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641090601181 [] Explore the vibrant canvases and linocuts of Tabax’ae (Nxabe) Ntcõx’o, a San artist from Botswana’s Kuru Art Project. His works—like forest and wild-food scenes—honour ancestral narratives and celebrate Kalahari biodiversity. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tabax’ae was born (b. 1978) and grew up in D’kar, Botswana. In 2018, she made her first painting when she was persuaded to participate in a workshop to select new artists for the Kuru Art Project. She enjoyed it very much but was not very convinced that she would be able to be an artist. She has since made lovely artworks and continues to surprise herself and others. \\nTabax’ae draws her inspiration from the plants and animals endemic to the Kalahari veld, which has always been a significant part of her life. Sensitivity predominates in Tabax’ae’s work, and her unique way of conveying her subject matter lends to great originality."}]}]} []

item.title: Tafadzwa Masudi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641944928477 Tafadzwa Masudi 1124 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641091387613 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129091805","gid://shopify/Product/9452263047389","gid://shopify/Product/9452263080157","gid://shopify/Product/9452263112925","gid://shopify/Product/9452263145693","gid://shopify/Product/9452263211229","gid://shopify/Product/9452263243997","gid://shopify/Product/9452263309533","gid://shopify/Product/9452263407837"] [24089,24092,21238,24108,24097,24099,24114] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tafadzwa Masudi (b. 1988) started painting at an early age in Harare while assisting a family friend who introduced him to the visual arts. In 2010 he moved to South Africa and started working in a clothing factory until 2020 when he was laid off. He saw this as an opportunity to paint full-time and soon his work was featured in group exhibitions at galleries in and around Cape Town. 2021 is proving to be an eventful year with participation in the online versions of the Turbine Art Fair in Johannesburg and Art X Lagos in Nigeria lined up."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129091805","gid://shopify/Product/9452263047389","gid://shopify/Product/9452263080157","gid://shopify/Product/9452263112925","gid://shopify/Product/9452263145693","gid://shopify/Product/9452263211229","gid://shopify/Product/9452263243997","gid://shopify/Product/9452263309533","gid://shopify/Product/9452263407837"]

item.title: Talia Goldsmith
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641946468573 Talia Goldsmith 1994 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641097973981 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013398634717","gid://shopify/Product/9013398667485","gid://shopify/Product/9013398733021"] [14066,14064,14065] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Talia Goldsmith was born in Israel and studied art at the Kalisher school of Art. She came to South Africa in 1984 and grew up with this country. She has an inner fascination with found materials and their use, influenced by her roots (Yemen) and her life in South Africa. Talia infuses her work with unusual and unique combinations of new and recycled materials. The organic forms, texture, weaving, stitching, manipulating and human labour are influenced by her roots. She always says \"Roots are the Essence.” Her work is a story that bridges between material, religion, culture and history. Her latest body of work Sysiphus incorporates a range of materials in an unlikely combination which come together in an absurd dystopian vision of the human condition. Her focus as an artist is to comment on the human condition through means and metaphors of interrogating the human \\nform, language, spirituality and music. Talia's work forms part of collections in South Africa, Israel, Canada and New York. She has had solo exhibitions as well as group exhibitions."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013398634717","gid://shopify/Product/9013398667485","gid://shopify/Product/9013398733021"]

item.title: Talia Ramkilawan
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641946665181 Talia Ramkilawan 1897 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098105053 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045926621","gid://shopify/Product/9452159369437"] [13361,15216,25520] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Cape Town and raised by her single mother in Nelspruit, Ramkilawan returned to Cape Town in 2015 to major in sculpture at the Michaelis School of Fine Art. Her work focuses on the trauma of dislocation and displacement she felt because of her South Asian identity. However, far from allowing the pertaining ideologies surrounding such an identity to dominate her, Ramkilawan uses her artworks to speak out and become a restorative tonic for her community. \\n \\n“Attempting to find a process of healing through making led me to where I am now. I craved intimacy between what I was making and myself,” the artist explains. Her work uses portraiture to create a visual presence of the ‘Indian experience’ that disrupts linear narratives. “I place emphasis on exposing how trauma of the past resonates in the present,” she adds."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452045926621","gid://shopify/Product/9452159369437"]

item.title: Talitha Deetlefs
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641946861789 Talitha Deetlefs 2536 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098367197 [] Talitha Deetlefs [20253] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“I enjoy exploring the beauty that can be found in the interplay between contrasting forces, whether these be tangible or spiritual; the hard edge of the metal and the soft lines of the female form, smooth and textured surfaces, strength and vulnerability.’ \\n \\nTalitha Deetlefs has created a truly unique collection of art by combining her love of metalwork and the sculpted figure. \\n \\nDeetlefs has focused predominantly on the female form as her subject and she has created a collection of striking figures embodying the strength, sensuality and sensitivity of the multi-faceted feminine identity. Viewed from the angle of her own life experience, her aim is to search and explore all facets of the feminine archetype. \\n \\nShe explores the ways in which our identities as woman are formed by our personal and collective history, and how it relates to the notions of femininity expressed in modern society. Her work is inspired by mythology and the symbolic language; by the ways in which it can enrich our lives, enabling us to transcend popular culture and reveal our own beauty. \\n \\n"}]}]} []

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641947189469 Tamara Osso 243 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098793181 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013327134941","gid://shopify/Product/9013327266013","gid://shopify/Product/9013328838877","gid://shopify/Product/9013352464605"] [8404,10528] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tamara Osso’s (1983) artworks always grapple with the connection between the immediacy of performance and the physicality of painting. item.title: Tashinga Majiri
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641949155549 Tashinga Majiri 2144 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104232669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452225003741","gid://shopify/Product/9452225298653"] [15196,15197] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Painter, Zimbabwe (b. 1993) \\nTashinga Majiri graduated in 2019 with a Diploma in Fine Art from the National Gallery of Zimbabwe school of Visual Art and Design, specializing in painting and printmaking. \\nOver the past couple of years, he has been working to develop his own approach which blends painting and printmaking together, working with monotypes on canvas interlaced with painting and spray paint. \\nAs a poet he is also interested in the engagement that is possible through subtle incorporation of automatic writing in his canvases, his works float in and out of figuration and have the quality of daydreams, an escape from the here and now into art and its possibilities."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452225003741","gid://shopify/Product/9452225298653"]

item.title: Tatenda Magaisa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641951875293 Tatenda Magaisa 2503 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106165981 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086952157"] [19858,20122] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tatenda Magaisa is an artist, writer, researcher and culturalm producer from South Africa. She obtained her MAFA in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand (Johannesburg, South Africa) in 2016. Her work explores themes pertaining to global cultural interaction, Black women in popular culture, as artists and/or practitioners in Africa and the foregone conclusion of surplus labor under a culturally dominated society. Drawing strongly on prevalent visual material and assumed norms referenced from popular media and socialm media, her research is rooted in an exploration of art practiced under irreconcilable conditions. Magaisa works in painting, print, text and video. \\nTatenda Magaisa is the 2023 David Koloane Award recipient, Bag Factory Artists’ Studios; writing edition. Exhibitions and projects include ‘It wearies me; you say it wearies you’ (2024), a solo exhibition at Johannesburg Art Gallery, she is a resident of the Occupying The Gallery project (2023-), ‘Minding Our Business’(2018/2019) a podcast project by Rera Letsema in collaboration with the Visual Arts Network of South Africa, ‘Five Bhobh – Painting at the End of an Era’ (2018/2019) a group exhibition at Zeitz MOCAA and the co-curation and publication of ‘Overtime: representations, values and imagined futures of ‘classical African Art’ (2017) at the Wits Art Museum."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452086952157"]

item.title: Tawanda Mhandu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641951940829 Tawanda Mhandu 1523 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106231517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126863581"] [23934] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Zimbabwe, Mhandu describes himself as a living African artist representing unsung indigenous artists. The basis of his practice as an artist comes from creations that modern-day technology cannot replicate or surpass. These creations range from the pyramids of Giza, Mapungubwe - Great Zimbabwe and the pre-Columbus American Olmec civilisation. \\n \\nA multifaceted artist, Mhandu creates work in a variety of media, painting in oils, Acrylic, Pastels, smoke, watercolour, and charcoal. He also dabbles in sculpture using metal, stone, and mixed media. He works largely work with found material and is in the habit of upcycling with his art. \\n \\nHe also does performance art in the form of live sand art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126863581"]

item.title: Tawanda Takura
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641951973597 Tawanda Takura 370 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106362589 [] [4019,4014] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tawanda Takura (b. 1989), who trained as a shoemaker, takes apart and expertly re-assembles old shoes which carry the traces and biographies of their owners in his sculptural pieces. These new figurations carry the subtle but persistent smell of rubber and leather. Hollow, hybrid, tortured and distorted, sometimes carnivalesque, Takura’s work comments on socio-political injustice, and takes clear aim at the extractive practices of charismatic churches. \\nThe artist describes how, “at times, in earlier years, I was considered a madman, going around collecting old shoes...people would see a heap of shoes in my house”. He goes on to describe how his work has opened up conversations and dialogue with neighbours and others in his community: “People really want to say things but they don’t know how to say it. I get to speak through my work and address the things that they are facing and going through [in daily life].” \\nA laughing mermaid-devil with a scaly body of many tongues, a head of molten plastic, high-heels for a horned crown and swimming flipper for her tail. A macabre decapitated spirit-head talks to his body: split football boots trace the firmness of the human spine and back; shoulders rise up from the undersides of well-worn ballet slippers. Mai Mfundisi, the ‘lady pastor’, flourishes under her lurid fascinator, her face adorned with condom packets. \\nA shocking pair of screaming yet mute heads seem to comment on economic desperation and the erosion of basic dignities. Look closely: one of the mouths bears the New Testament’s Book of Timothy, with some of the miniscule verses underlined: “For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil for which some have strayed from the faith in their greediness and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” The lips of its nearby anguished twin are smeared with the defunct Zimbabwe dollar, millions of them - a reference to 15 years of economic turmoil and increasing deprivation. Elsewhere, no irony is lost with the same dollars being used to line the anus of a feline creature that mutates into an assaulted, cowering human torso, its head mummified with bank notes. Around its neck: the priest’s collar. \\nIf Takura’s critique of the abuses of state and church is an expression of suffering and anger, his continuous binding together of materials is also an attempt to stitch back together what is torn asunder. Takura has exhibited at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe, several times at the Joburg Art Fair (2015, 2016, 2018) and Cape Town Art Fair (2017, 2018, 2020), and in shows in Mauritius and Hong Kong. In 2019 he completed a residency with the South African Foundation for Contemporary Art and participated in a group show at Guns & Rain. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Tayhe Munsamy
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641952071901 Tayhe Munsamy 2048 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106559197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014044655837", "gid://shopify/Product/9014044688605", "gid://shopify/Product/9014044754141", "gid://shopify/Product/9014044786909"] Explore the captivating artistry of Johannesburg-born Tayhe Munsamy, who delves into themes of creation, displacement, and transformation through painting, video, performance, and digital media. Discover her unique perspective as a mixed-race woman and her exploration of the Coloured and Indian communities in South Africa. [23419,23416,23417,23418,17196,21124] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tayhe Munsamy,a Johannesburg-born artist, graduated with First-Class Honours in Fine Art and History of Art from Goldsmiths University of London in 2020. Her multidisciplinary practice encompasses painting, video, performance, and digital media, exploring themes of creation, displacement, transformation, and fantasy. \\nTayhe's work is deeply rooted in her identity as a mixed-race woman, drawing from the Coloured and Indian communities in South Africa. She masterfully combines cultural specificity and historical archives with fictional elements to craft fantastical worlds that celebrate her nuanced identity. Her artworks unravel connections, memory, time, and traditions, exploring how mythology and folklore create stories that bind us together in a world that has fragmented our ancestry. \\nIn 2021, Tayhe was selected for the RMB Talent Unlocked mentoring program and group show at Everard Read CIRCA Gallery in Johannesburg, in association with Strauss & Co South Africa. She continues to showcase her artworks in group exhibitions across South Africa and internationally. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013985247453","gid://shopify/Product/9014044655837","gid://shopify/Product/9014044688605","gid://shopify/Product/9014044754141","gid://shopify/Product/9014044786909"]

item.title: Tebogo Losaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641952858333 Tebogo Losaba gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107837149 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sometimes surviving day to day is the dream and that is alright. We can all learn a lot from those who understand the weight of this truth. I am a Soweto born artist who documents the lived experiences of ordinary people in my community of Soweto and the Johannesburg inner-city. As a street photographer, I use digital photography to reflect the vibrancy, hustle, and beauty in the everyday life of my subjects. We can easily miss the beauty in these gritty spaces, but my photography celebrates and accentuates this. Over and above reflecting the aesthetic value, my art pays homage to the fighting spirit which is innate in the communities I photograph. \\n \\nMy work has earned accolades such as being the 2019 Canon Roadshow winner in the Local Travel category and the Standard Bank Gallery-Photography in Our Mother Tongue competition winner in 2021. In August 2022, I showcased my work in a group exhibition titled ‘A Safe Space’ which I hosted with two other artists at Ellis House Art Building. \\n \\nThis year, I also got to exhibit my work during the Thami Mnyele exhibition for shortlisted artists in Ekurhuleni. I am currently working with HSRC as an artist who has been selected to exhibit in their upcoming Youth Livelihoods Virtual Museum. Another exhibition that I have been selected to showcase my work in, is the prestigious Turbine Art Fair (TAF) Paper Exhibition 2023. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Tegene Kunbi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641953972445 Tegene Kunbi 2347 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109115101 [18439,19147] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tegene Kunbi (b. 1980 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia) is an Ethiopian abstract contemporary painter whose practice deals with issues of place, politics, and the nature of abstraction. Tegene Kunbi’s practice also demonstrates his study and analysis of painting history. \\nFormally educated in the Western European and Russian academic tradition of realism, his work looks to break down notions of landscape. What he considers a rebellious act that falls in parallel to the historical understanding and function of abstraction, he looks to demonstrate a painterly and abstracted understanding of material, colour, and the notion of nostalgia to break the limitations of visual representation. \\nTegene Kunbi received his BFA from the University of Addis Ababa in 2004. He continued his education at the Universit?t der Künste Berlin. In 2022 he was awarded the Léopold Sédar Senghor prize from the President of the Republic as part of his participation in the Dakar Biennale. He has held solo exhibitions at Bode in Berlin (2023); Barbara Thumm in Berlin (2022); Primo Marella Gallery in Milan (2022); Circle Art Gallery in Nairobi (2019), among others. He has also participated in group exhibition in CH HILL in Stockholm (2021); SAVVY Contemporary in Berlin (2021); Margaret Thatcher Projects in New York (2020), and more. Tegene Kunbi currently lives and works in Berlin, Germany."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062572765"]

item.title: Tebogo Qhingana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641953153245 Tebogo Qhingana 2847 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108000989 [] Discover the evocative paintings of Tebogo Carllouis Qhingana, a South African artist from Daveyton whose work focuses on community, childhood, and resilience. Explore his award?winning artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [23941] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tebogo Carllouis Qhingana was born in Daveyton (Benoni) in 1993. He discovered his love of art during his early childhood, pursuing this passion as a self-taught artist after matriculating from Unity Secondary School in 2012. \\nAlthough he nearly abandoned his dream at one stage, he persevered in his endeavour of a professional full-time career through commissions. He hasn't looked back since and recently completed a diploma in Fine Art and Applied Arts at Tshwane University of Technology. Tebogo has participated in several group exhibitions and was one of the finalists of the 2019 Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards. \\nHis artworks talk about the realities of vulnerable children from a small township in Daveyton, outside Benoni, who have had to assume leadership from a young age. They have not been strictly guided or groomed for the role, which is reflected in his works as the children yearn for happiness, peace, love and wisdom."}]}]} []

[23126,23127,23128,23129,16766,20610,10913,23124,23130,23131,15546] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tessa Teixeira (b. 1969, Ermelo, South Africa) is a visual artist who completed a Bachelor's in Primary Education, majoring in Art, in 1991 through the University of the Witwatersrand. Her self-portrait from that time was preserved by the JCE Arts Department. \\nIn her twenties and thirties, Tessa was deeply involved in projects addressing housing access in lower-income sectors. She founded an NGO, raised funds to build two primary schools for children who were receiving tuition under trees, and worked with The Mineworkers Development Agency, the development wing of The National Union of Mineworkers, addressing rural development and economic needs in South Africa. \\nIn 2006, Tessa began to actively focus on her art practice, participating in various short art development programs in San Francisco and London in 2010 and 2011. She returned to Johannesburg at the end of 2011 and has since been developing her practice, focusing on Existential Philosophy and Ecology—Climate narratives, aligned with materiality exploration in Mixed Media, Painting, Installation, and Printmaking. \\nSince 2012, Tessa has exhibited, auctioned, and sold work for private collections in local and international group shows. Some recent exhibitions include: ‘1.5 Degrees’ in Berlin, Germany (2021), ‘What’s next for earth? - Depletion’ – MAHB, Stanford University, USA (2021), ‘Enviro Art gallery 2021’ – Dukes University, USA (2021), ‘Amref Artball Auction – pre-featured on Artsy – New York (2019), ‘Optimism’ Endless Editions Biennial in New York (2018), ‘Art of Lithography’ - The University of the Witwatersrand Museum (WAM), and a solo show - ‘Nothing stands still’ - Johannesburg Holocaust & Genocide Centre (2018)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013354430685","gid://shopify/Product/9013425635549","gid://shopify/Product/9013443526877","gid://shopify/Product/9013452275933","gid://shopify/Product/9013959164125","gid://shopify/Product/9014036922589","gid://shopify/Product/9014036955357","gid://shopify/Product/9014036988125","gid://shopify/Product/9014037086429","gid://shopify/Product/9014037119197","gid://shopify/Product/9014037250269","gid://shopify/Product/9014037283037"]

item.title: Teresa Kutala Firmino
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954070749 Teresa Kutala Firmino 670 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109311709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452056772829","gid://shopify/Product/9452138201309","gid://shopify/Product/9452138266845"] Teresa Kutala Firmino is a multimedia artist based in Johannesburg, exploring trauma, collective history, and the resilience of women in post-colonial Africa. Her work delves into themes of identity preservation, personal and collective trauma, and the complexities of living with past and present struggles. Firmino’s art uses vibrant, surreal scenes to rebuild African history and challenge the legacy of colonialism and civil conflict. [24119,24777,24778,16069,16148,16070,23791] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"We heal by retelling our stories. \\nTeresa Kutala Firmino’s work negotiates trauma both personal and collective in her everyday life. Her paintings are constructed scenes of the past and present, which are sometimes intertwined. Firmino carefully collects images from magazines, newspapers, historical documents and social media, and places them in colourful, box-like stages. This creates surreally baroque scenes which take place in tightly confined interiors, where the characters have the opportunity to re-enact their stories or construct new ones. This process allows Firmino to create alternative past, present and future narratives of Africa, thus rebuilding her own archive of African history. \\nFirmino seeks to investigate the trauma that African people in her community and beyond have experienced and continue to experience due to colonisation, civil wars and present day obstacles. Her own stories begin with the collective trauma of Pomfret. Located in the North West Province of South Africa, and the place where she was born, Pomfret is a community of former 32 Battalion soldiers and their families, many of whom settled there after the end of the South African Border War. \\nColonial rule and the trauma it induced forced many African people to cling to one another in a common cause, which was to create free and independent countries. Africans, though constantly reminded that they were seen as less than human, held on to what reminded them of their humanity: their communities and their struggles for freedom. Once they achieved a form of independence, though, many civil wars erupted, where the people who fought for the same freedom were caught in a new, raw struggle for power. These civil wars caused a second wave of trauma; suddenly the people one depended on for a sense of community and humanity now turned against each other. \\nBoth the women and men in the Pomfret community experienced these traumas – but it is the women who were subjected to further pain. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is not only experienced by people who have been through a war. Firmino affirms that the women in the community experienced a second wave of trauma: rape, abuse, accidents and torture. The women clung to what gave them a sense of security and humanity, which were their husbands and the community. Many of them experienced abuse, and some were even killed by their partners. Those who survived could not trust the community for support, because society had normalised abuse against women. \\nKutala Firmino looks at how, despite the trauma they experienced, many of these women had to continue living with their abusers. The artist interrogates what it is about the black female body and mind which, despite trauma, continues to thrive. Is she truly living, or is she in constant melancholy as she exists in the aftermath of colonialism, civil war and betrayal? Is negotiating trauma realising that your abuser is possibly part the bigger of cycle of abuse? \\nTeresa Kutala Firmino is a multimedia artist, now based in Johannesburg, working with paint, photography and performance. She is part of a collective called Kutala Chopeto, which started as an investigation into their shared history which is linked to the 32 Battalion, the soldiers who were settled in Pomfret after the Border War. \\nCV \\nCOLLECTIVE EXHIBITIONS \\n2018 \\nKutala Chopeto, The Point of Order, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2017 \\nSilences in Between, Goodman Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa \\nNirox Sculpture Winter Fair, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThe Centre for the Less Good Idea Season 1, Arts on Main, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n [South-South] Let me begin again, Goodman Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2016 \\nBoda Boda Lounge Project, South Africa \\nHybrid Culture, MB Studio, Pretoria, South Africa \\nSELECTED GROUP & SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n2021 \\nARCOLisboa, Everard Read, Lisbon, Portugal. \\n2020 \\nBlack Melancholy, solo booth, Investec Cape Town Art Fair, with Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\nStaring Straight to the Future, digital group exhibition, Everard Read, South Africa \\n2019 \\nTaxidermy of the Future, group show, Luanda Museum of Natural History, Angola \\nPseudo Restitution, solo, World Art, Cape Town, South Africa \\nThe War at Home, solo, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nTurbine Art Fair, with World Art, Johannesburg , South Africa \\nInvestec Cape Town Art Fair, with Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2018 \\nEmergence, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nMasters solo show: Pomfret Community Stories, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThou Art Women, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThe People’s Exchange, IDC Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nNow and Then, Trent Gallery, Pretoria, South Africa \\nProtagonist: Artists in Response to Sexual Violence, Studio Fracture, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2015 \\n14/15 exhibition, The Point of Order, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2014 \\nThe African Utopia Lecture Series, University of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nRESIDENCIES \\n2020 \\nFynbosch Residency, Franschhoek, South Africa"}]}]}
