item.title: Thabo Skhosana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954496733 Thabo Skhosana 2340 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641110556893 [22403] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in the East Rand in 1996, Thabo Skhosana has always had a love for art particularly drawing from an early age. He was inspired by the animation and comic books that his father would give to him. He studied graphic design at Rosebank collage and subsequently joined the Artist Proof Studio. He completed his third year in 2019. \\n \\nSkhosana has been part of a number of joint exhibitions with the Artist Proof Studio which include, Strauss & Co at Turbine Art Fair 2018/19, The Legacy exhibition 2019, and JoburgArt Fair 2019, TAF 2022, Art Joburg 2022 to name a few. When Thabo isn’t printing artwork he is either busy with a beat, producing music with friends or working on his ongoing comic book series, that one day he hopes to publish. Having learned many different printing mediums, he has focused on of linocut, etching and combination printing with colour. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014016016605","gid://shopify/Product/9014016049373"]

item.title: Thamsanqa Kiti
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954791645 Thamsanqa Kiti 2555 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111638237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452091244765"] Thamsanqa Kiti [20776] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thamsanqa 'Thami' Eddie Kiti was born in 1968 in Machabini, a village near Queenstown in the Eastern Cape. He has lived in Khayelitsha since his early youth. \\nIn the late 1980s and 90s, Thamsanqa Kiti attended Community Arts Project (CAP) at St Philips in Woodstock, and took classes in carving, drawing, painting and print making under Mario Sickle, Lucy Alexander, Lionel Davis, Lovell Friedman and Sipho Hlati. \\nWorking mainly as a carver, Thamsanqa Kiti has had his work included on various exhibitions including: ‘Thami Kiti and Wanini Hill’ at the UCT Irma Stern Museum in 1995; ‘Engaging the Shadows’, Robben Island, 1997; ‘Homecoming’, Gug’Sthebe, Langa, 2001; ‘Against the Grain’, 2013, Iziko South African National Gallery curated by Mario Pissarra; ‘my whole body changed into something else’, Stevenson gallery, 2021 curated by Sisipho Ngodwana and Sinazo Chiya; and ‘Seeds of the Fig’ an exhibition curated by RESERVOIR in collaboration with Whatiftheworld for Krone in Tulbagh, 2023. He participated in the Thapong International Artists Workshop in Gaborone in 1996 as well as a number of workshops in Cape Town and Pretoria. Thamsanqa Kiti worked for the Handspring Puppet Company from 2008-2011, and has produced a number of his own unique articulated and puppet animals. In 2017, he was the winner of the Craft Award for his carved initiation staffs for the Innibos Laeveld Nasionale Kunstefees in Mbombela. He was commissioned to create a large temporary public sculpture, a mosaic hybrid figure of a bride, Umakhoti, for an outdoor exhibition, ‘Reflections’, in Stellenbosch in 2015; a staff with a leopard, Ingwe Izidla Ngamabala, for the UCT Vice-Chancellor’s annual Award for Transformation in 2019; and a carved broom with a bird as part of Jane Alexander’s installation Infirmary, 2014, 2019. He has artwork in the Robben Island Collection, the collection of William Humphreys Art Gallery in Kimberley, the Community Arts Project Collection at the University of the Western Cape, and numerous private collections. \\nThamsanqa Kiti’s works make direct reference to Xhosa culture, particularly birth, initiation, marriage and death in relation to the earth. They sometimes combine hybrid forms, particularly human and goat features, and other animals that hold cultural significance such as Inqaqa (civet) and Inganda (serval). His most recent work includes carved and decorated staffs with mounted animal figures that often refer to initiation, and individual animals composed of multiple types of wood, some with elaborate inlay."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452091244765"]

item.title: Thami Nonceba Dwanya
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954758877 Thami Nonceba Dwanya 2913 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111539933 [] Discover the vibrant and thought-provoking work of Thami Nonceba Dwanya, a South African artist exploring identity, culture, and social narratives. Explore their artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [24812,24811,24809] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nonceba Thami Dwanya (b. 2000, Pretoria). Nonceba is a young, black female artist who explores and utilises art to understand unconfronted parts of herself. Excelling in fine arts/ multidisciplinary portraiture she unpacks layers of understanding using paint and drawing mediums, charcoal and ink. \\nMotho ke motho ka batho. \\nAlthough one’s experience is personal to themselves it is not singular, as it is shared in a space with and amongst equal and opposite singular experiences. \\nSelf understanding is “the awareness of and ability to elaborate/explain that which is considered a being which distinguishes from others, especially considered as the object of introspection or reflexive action”. This abstract idea has been the topic of my work, expressed in the form of portraiture which looks at others and self for and from both others and self. Life is an experience that is personal to both the experience, but is just as personal to the those \\naround the experience as it is to the experience. In simple terms, self doesn’t and can’t exist without others. \\nLooking beyond the simplicities of the face, my practice uses colour, and texture to unpack reflection of myself in others and the perspective of others through the subject. Through layers of paint, drawing mediums, collaging, texture and colour this is a complex relationship which I unpack in my work. Silhouettes play a vital role in the visual respesenstion of presence and absence simultaneously, thus using silhouettes of existing objects or co-subjects allow me to highlight the absence and presence of others in the understanding of self, prioritising and emphasising balance/coexistence as the basis for one’s relationship with themselves. \\n"}]}]} []

item.title: Thania Petersen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955676381 Thania Petersen 2348 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641114063069 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062703837","gid://shopify/Product/9452081545437","gid://shopify/Product/9452081578205"] [18441,19148,19373,19374] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thania Petersen (b. 1980, Cape Town) is a multi-disciplinary artist who uses photography, performance and installation to address the intricacies and complexities of her identity in contemporary South Africa. \\nPetersen’s reference points sit largely in Islam and in creating awareness about its religious, cultural and traditional practices. She attempts to unpack contemporary trends of Islamophobia through her analysis of the continuing impact of colonialism, European and American imperialism, and the increasing influence of right-wing ideologies. Threads in her work include the history of colonialist imperialism in Africa, Asia and the Middle East, as well as the social and cultural impact of westernised consumer culture. Her work is also informed by her Cape Malay heritage, and the practice of Sufi Islamic religious ceremonies. Petersen studied at Central Saint Martin’s College of Art in London. \\nShe has held solo exhibitions at WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town, the AVA, Cape Town and at the Everard Read Gallery, Cape Town. She has participated in numerous group exhibitions both locally and abroad. Recent exhibitions include ZAMUNDA FOREVER?????, Nicodim, Los Angeles (2023, solo); ??Galeria Nicodim, Bucharest: 10 Years, Galeria Nicodim, Bucharest (2023); 18th Venice Architecture Biennale (2023); Indigo Waves and other Stories, SAAVY Contemporary, Berlin (2023); Indigo Waves and other Stories, Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2022–2023); Artists’ Film International (traveling), Whitechapel, London, Istanbul Modern, Istanbul, Ballroom Marfa, Marfa, and others (2022); Can We Sing Together, Old Friend?, 32 Bis, Tunis (2022, solo); Triennale Kleinplastic Fellbach: The Vibration of Things, Alte Kelter Fellbach, Fellbach (2022); Where Do I Begin, Stevenson, Cape Town (2022); KASSARAM, Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2021, solo); Indian Ocean Craft Triennial: Curiosity and the Rituals of the Everyday, Fremantle, Australia (2021); Self-Addressed, curated by Kehinde Wiley, Jeffrey Deitch, Los Angeles (2021); Un.e Air.e de Famille, Musée d’art et d’histoire Paul Eluard, Saint-Denis (2021); Between Land and a Raised Foot, National Arts Festival, Grahamstown, South Africa (2019, solo); Radical Love, Ford Foundation, New York (2019); and IQRA, WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town (2019, solo). Her work is collected by the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington, D.C.; Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA), Cape Town; IZIKO South African Museum, Cape Town; Pérez Art Museum, Miami; and many others."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062703837","gid://shopify/Product/9452081545437","gid://shopify/Product/9452081578205"]

item.title: Thato Makatu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955807453 Thato Makatu 2837 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641114423517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014104522973", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104555741"] Discover the evocative prints of Thato Makatu, a South African artist whose work explores memory, home, and identity through thoughtful printmaking and curatorial inquiry. Explore their practice on Latitudes Online. [23861,24839,24840,23882] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thato Makatu (b. 2000 Oslo) is a South African artist/cultural producer in training and printmaker from Boksburg. Makatu completed their Honours in Curatorship at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (UCT). Born in Norway and having moved across the world several times during their childhood, their artistic work is concerned with working through notions of home and stability through the physical aspects of domestic spaces. \\nThey Engage with questions of how these spaces interact with evocations of memory and formation of identity.Because of their dislocated upbringing, Thato has used their art to work through howthe home is constructed both physically and socially. Focusing on how the domestic space interacts with our memories, and how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time, the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people. Through their Hons in Curatorship, they have become increasingly interested inhow homemaking practices exist culturally, and how the family can be a way to navigate research and access cultural identity in the home. \\nThato's work thinks through how the domestic space interacts with our memories, how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time and the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014060843229","gid://shopify/Product/9014061301981","gid://shopify/Product/9014104522973","gid://shopify/Product/9014104555741"]

item.title: Thato Toeba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641956823261 Thato Toeba 1170 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641124843741 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013318516957"] [7498] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thato Toeba is a Lesotho artist and legal scholar currently called flattendacurve (b.1990, Maseru). She shares visuals of continuing thoughts on personhood, politics, propaganda, nationality, globalisation, law and culture. Her work is influenced by her suspicion of formal things (culture law, politics, institutions,) as sober, objective, neutral tools in resolving growing crises of being here in the world today. She speculates on the intrusion of formal things in the emancipated joy of life, womb to tomb and fantasises about some kind of sweet chaos to be master in a less theorised life. \\nShe is a LLD candidate at UWC."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013318516957"]

item.title: Thato Tlatsi

She uses her work to explore themes related to chaos, death, sexuality and mental health. \\nIn 2022, Tlatsi received her Bachelors in Fine Arts from the University of Johannesburg and currently resides in Roodepoort."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845","gid://shopify/Product/9013425373405","gid://shopify/Product/9013425406173","gid://shopify/Product/9013425471709","gid://shopify/Product/9013425537245","gid://shopify/Product/9013425602781","gid://shopify/Product/9013439856861","gid://shopify/Product/9013991047389","gid://shopify/Product/9013992095965","gid://shopify/Product/9013993111773","gid://shopify/Product/9013995503837","gid://shopify/Product/9013995536605","gid://shopify/Product/9014025584861"]

item.title: Thebe Phetogo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641956921565 Thebe Phetogo 1119 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641125073117 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452120834269","gid://shopify/Product/9452120867037","gid://shopify/Product/9452129681629","gid://shopify/Product/9452129845469","gid://shopify/Product/9452130369757"] Thebe Phetogo is a Botswana-born artist known for blending figurative and abstract landscape painting. His work addresses themes of race, Setswana geography, mythology, and indigenous knowledge systems, reflecting on how personal positionality shapes the world we create. [24191,24210,24199,23597,23598] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thebe Phetogo (b. 1993, Botswana) is an artist whose work blends figurative and abstract landscapes painting to explore themes of race, Setswana geography, and indigenous knowledge. Drawing inspiration from sacred caves and African mythology, his art reflects on the concept of origins and personal identity, offering a unique perspective on how individual experiences shape our understanding of the world. \\nThrough his work, Phetogo seeks to make visible the distinct “world-version” he carries. As the artist himself states, “Each of us ‘makes’ the world. In other words, it is our positionality that allows us to imagine each of our own immediate worlds. In my work, I endeavour to make visible the specific ‘world-version’ I carry.”"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452120834269","gid://shopify/Product/9452120867037","gid://shopify/Product/9452129681629","gid://shopify/Product/9452129845469","gid://shopify/Product/9452130369757"]

item.title: Themba Khumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963278557 Themba Khumalo 330 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641126547677 [19691,19692] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Benedict Khumalo was born on 16 February 1987 in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa. He graduated from Artist Proof Studio in printmaking, where he obtained a Design Foundation Certificate. He went on to do a professional printmaking development course under the sponsorship of Pinpoint One, at Artist Proof Studio in 2009 where he was an intern in the silkscreen unit and special project team. Khumalo is interested in exploring different mediums, such as charcoal drawings and painting. \\nKhumalo’ work is inspired by everyday day life. His visuals are stimulated by events he witnesses daily in the city such as everyday struggles, prospects and desires. He documents his interaction with the city as both an outsider and a city dweller. This dual tension is evident in his work; as he takes note of people who have come to the city in seek of the unknown. This is reflective in his work through his intense dark mark-marking and subtle texture of clouds, which evoke specific moods and emotions. \\nKhumalo’s work explores the dangers of Johannesburg while reflecting its beauty through its architecture and cityscape. Khumalo identifies in his work the importance of family and how they play an important role in one’s life. Although he hardly depicts human figures in his work, he uses pylons, cranes, and electric wires to represent movement, energy, and unity: portraying how electricity connects us all. Thus, informing his audience of his relationship with people, exploring feelings of connectivity and isolation within the city. \\nHe has been involved in number of group exhibitions, commissions and special projects; such as painting murals in the Eastern Cape and being invited to exhibit in a group show at Isolate del Cinema festival in Rome, Italy. He has exhibited widely and been on various residencies internationally since 2016. Khumalo works as an independent artist."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013937733853","gid://shopify/Product/9013937799389"]

item.title: Themba Shabalala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963442397 Themba Shabalala 1349 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641127497949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126929117"] [23937] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Shabalala is a contemporary South African artist born in 1994. A totem award winner in 2015 and currently based in Johannesburg in an art community called August House, Themba Shabalala’s formal discipline lies in printmaking. He is predominantly engaged with fire and wood as a medium. He is currently exploring the concept of self-image, which is a reflection of his upbringing and his battle with an absent father figure. His work shows how he chooses to carry traits his mother has given him instead and how he learns to overlook his father’s physical absence. His work has been featured in several group exhibitions and has also been auctioned. Shabalala was one of 9 artists selected in Africa for the prestigious World Art Print in France."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126929117"]

Inspired by his background in Analytical Chemistry, Themba's work explores human connections and the need for recognition and belonging. Recently featured in the “My First Love” exhibition. [16948,25298,25296,23121,16371,16944,25297,23122,16947,13866] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Sibeko (b. 1994, Johannesburg) is a self-taught artist who studied Analytical Chemistry at the University of Johannesburg. Inspired by his studies, which focus on the bonding between atoms and elements, Themba translates this concept into his art practice to explore human connections. Influenced by the people around him, his work is a contemplative study of the unknown possibilities of entering new scenarios, situations, relationships, and territories in people's lives. \\nThe removal of facial features in his art signifies the need for recognition, approval, and a sense of belonging. Themba's work also questions authentic human interactions by removing the stigmas attached to human connections, reminding everyone that we are humans first. His work was recently featured in a group exhibition titled “My First Love.” \\nInspired by people around me, my work is a contemplative study of the unknown possibilities of walking into new scenarios, situations, relationships and territories in peoples lives. Removal of facial features signifies the need for recognition, approval and sense of belonging. \\n \\nMy work also questions authentic human interactions by removing all the stigmas attached to human connections, reminding everyone that we are humans first. My work has recently been featured In a group exhibition titled “My first love”."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013394866397","gid://shopify/Product/9013441298653","gid://shopify/Product/9013457092829","gid://shopify/Product/9013457158365","gid://shopify/Product/9013457223901","gid://shopify/Product/9013457256669","gid://shopify/Product/9014036791517","gid://shopify/Product/9014036857053","gid://shopify/Product/9132522078429","gid://shopify/Product/9133222527197","gid://shopify/Product/9133222723805"]

item.title: Thembi Mthembu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641964753117 Thembi Mthembu 1680 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641131790557 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013356626141","gid://shopify/Product/9013356757213","gid://shopify/Product/9013356822749","gid://shopify/Product/9013356855517","gid://shopify/Product/9013356921053"] [11307,11306,11304,11308,11302] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1992 in eNseleni, Kwazulu Natal, Thembi Mthembu is a multi-disciplinary artist who lives and works in Durban. She completed her Bachelors of Technology in photography at the Durban University of Technology in 2017. \\n \\nThembi has participated in a number of notable local and international group exhibitions. Being part of the Pride and Loss collaborative exhibition, curated by Prof. Zanele Muholi at the Jenkins Johnson Gallery in Brooklyn, New York in 2018, is a particular highlight in her career to date. Thembi is also a member of visual arts collectives in Durban, Amasosha Art Movement. Thembi’s artistic practice spans a variety of different disciplines and mediums. \\n \\nHer work explores the notions and politics surrounding ‘the body’, with her often using her own body as a site for her artistic exploration of these themes. Although initially trained as a photographer, she now explores various artistic mediums such as paint and Digital art."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013356626141","gid://shopify/Product/9013356757213","gid://shopify/Product/9013356822749","gid://shopify/Product/9013356855517","gid://shopify/Product/9013356921053"]

item.title: Thembinkosi Hlatshwayo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641964196061 Thembinkosi Hlatshwayo 1945 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641132282077 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452047892701", "gid://shopify/Product/9452047958237", "gid://shopify/Product/9452048023773", "gid://shopify/Product/9013397356765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013397389533"] [13639,23711,13640,14031,13638,14032] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thembinkosi Hlatshwayo uses the shebeen run by his parents as a studio in which to investigate themes of first-hand generational trauma, violence, and memory. He joined Of Soul and Joy Photography initiative in 2016. In 2018 he completed a year course in the Advance Programme in Photography at the Market Photo Workshop. \\nHlatshwayo’s first Slaghuis series won him the 2019 CAP Prize for Contemporary African Photography in Basel, Switzerland. His work has appeared in NICE Magazine 3rd Edition and group exhibitions at Fotomuseum Winterthur, IAF Basel Festival, and Johannesburg’s Turbine Art Fair. Thembinkosi Hlatshwayo is the Gisèle Wulfsohn Mentorship in Photography Recipient for 2019 and Slaghuis II is his first solo exhibition. \\nMoments in solitude allow Hlatshwayo quietness to process the noise, and the trauma, allowing for healing through the images he makes."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452047892701","gid://shopify/Product/9452047958237","gid://shopify/Product/9452048023773","gid://shopify/Product/9013397356765","gid://shopify/Product/9013397389533","gid://shopify/Product/9452121522397"]

item.title: Thenjiwe Niki Nkosi

View available exhibitions and works on Latitudes Online. [25600,25601,24539,24540,24541,25598,25599] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1980 in New York, Thenjiwe Niki Nkosi currently lives and works in Johannesburg. \\nNkosi obtained her BA from Harvard University (2004) and her MFA from the School of Visual Arts in New York (2008). She divides her time between studio work, performance, and navigating the field of art as social practice. Her work investigates the lived consequences of imperial histories and the personal dimensions of political identities, collectivity, and futurity, among other concepts. \\nArena V by the artist was exhibited as a site-specific mural and installation in the lobby of the Hammer Museum (2024). Nkosi presented, in collaboration with East Side Projects, the multimedia work Equations for a Body at Rest, across public spaces in Birmingham as part of the 2022 Commonwealth Games. Her solo exhibitions include Stadium, Stevenson, Amsterdam (2023); Landings, Stevenson, Cape Town (2022); Gymnasium, Stevenson, Johannesburg (2020); Gymnasium, The Africa Center, New York (2019); and The Beginning of Stories (Part 1 of Many), Seed Space/ Tri-Star Arts, Nashville, Tennessee (2017). \\nNotable group exhibitions include Movements, Museum Hilversum, the Netherlands (2024); In Terms of Sports, New Taipei City Art Museum, Taiwan (2024); Power Plays, Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburg, USA (2024);Thinking Historically in the Present, the 15th Sharjah Biennial, UAE (2023); Resistance Training: Arts, Sports, and Civil Rights, the Broad Museum of Art, Michigan State University (2023); Fix Your Pony, Naughton Gallery at Queen’s University, Belfast (2023); CHAMPS, Granville Centre Art Gallery, Cumberland (2023); Don’t Ask Me Where I’m From, Orlando Museum of Art, Florida (2023); THE GYM, Soho Studios, Vienna (2022); When We See Us: A Century of Black Figuration in Painting, Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa, Cape Town (2022) and Kunstmuseum Basel, Switzerland (2024); New Formations, deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum, Massachusetts, USA (2022); How to Make a Country, FRAC Poitou-Charentes, Angoulême, France (2021); Mixed Company, Norval Foundation, Cape Town (2021); Don’t Ask Me Where I’m From, Aga Khan Museum, Toronto (2020); NIEPODLEG?E, Women, Independence and National Discourse, Museum of Modern Art, Warsaw (2018); and Art Afrique, Le Nouvel Atelier, Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris (2017), among others. \\nShe has participated in residencies including the Pala Lab (2018); XXVIIes Ateliers Internationaux, FRAC des Pays de la Loire, France (2013); VAIVEM, Sao Paulo, Brazil (2013); Vanilla Facts, Berlin (2012); Cruces International, Montevideo, Uruguay (2011); and the Bag Factory Artist Residency (2009). \\nShe has received grants from Pro-Helvetia (2019); Goethe-Institut (2018, 2010); National Arts Council of South Africa (2015, 2009); Virginia Wellington Cabot Foundation (2008); and fellowships, including the School of Visual Arts Alumni Award Fellowship (2006); Pforzheimer Foundation Public Service Fellowship (2006); and Mellon Mays Undergraduate Fellowship (2002). \\nNkosi is the recipient of the Helgaard Steyn Prize in Painting (2023); the Tollman Award for the Visual Arts (2019) and Philippe Wamba Prize in African Studies (2004) \\n \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452136005853","gid://shopify/Product/9452136038621","gid://shopify/Product/9452136071389","gid://shopify/Product/9452153012445","gid://shopify/Product/9452185387229"]

View his artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [24454] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Theophelus Rikhotso (b. 1990) is a Tshwane based multi-disciplinary artist who works in sculpture, painting and drawing. \\nHis inspiration to become an artist came from his uncle who was a self-taught artist. \\nIn 2019 he completed a B-Tech diploma in Fine and Applied Arts at Tshwane University of Technology, majoring in sculpture. \\nRikhotso freely uses symbols and metaphors, in particular the shovel, which symbolizes strength, and the pied crow, which he identifies as a personal totem that functions a guide through this journey. item.title: Thuli Lubisi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966031069 Thuli Lubisi 852 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641139654877 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013296496861", "gid://shopify/Product/9013296595165"] [22396,4349,4347,23721,4348] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thuli Lubisi, a Johannesburg based visual artist and printmaker, was born in 1993 in Atteridgeville, Pretoria. In 2011 Lubisi completed her matric at P.J Simelane Secondary School and in 2013 she obtained a Computer Literacy certificate at Birnam Business College. Thuli then went on to study Visual art at Funda Art Centre in Diepkloof, Soweto during 2015. \\n \\nDuring 2016, Lubisi enrolled at Artist Proof Studio for a printmaking programme and, upon graduating, she began an internship at the Studios Education unit, assisting as a printmaking facilitator. \\n \\nSince 2017, Lubisi has been involved in various printmaking and mural projects as well as being part of group exhibitions such as the Joburg and Turbine Art fairs with Artist Proof Studio, in collaboration with Cartier and Strauss & Co respectively. In 2019 Lubisi was one of the artists commissioned by The Trinity Session to make artworks to be installed at the Leonardo Building; in addition Lubisi’s artworks have also been commissioned by the Bidvest bank SA and the HSBC bank. \\n \\nArtist Statement \\n \\nMy work is a celebration of African heritage and embraces our diversity. I combine patterns that derive from fabrics/textiles that are associated with different cultural groups, to make them hybrids. No pattern dominates or overpowers the other (suggesting cohesion); they create shapes that are a metaphor for a new landscape that is free from its historical, political and cultural constraints. \\n \\n‘Segregated’ and ‘Apart’ represent the new norm which has been created by this pandemic. The lives that we were accustomed to have been interrupted; because we’re separated from each other and there is now a void. As we slowly resume more normality I’m hoping that, with our differences, we can and will be able to form stronger and cohesive relations and keep the bonds that we have formed ‘intact’. \\n"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013296496861","gid://shopify/Product/9013296595165","gid://shopify/Product/9014015819997","gid://shopify/Product/9014056059101"]

He has been influenced by his time spent under the tutelage of artists Sfiso KaMkame and Thami Jali. Mthiyane has experience in children’s theatre with the Madcap’s Educational Theatre Company, after which he had his first solo exhibition at the Flat Gallery in Durban. Mthiyane’s artistic flare stems from his creative combination of painting and poetry. He has exhibited for Alliance Françoise and Resolution Gallery in Johannesburg. In 2015 he had a solo exhibition titled “Whetin dey happen Lagos/ Jozi” at Mzansi Gallery Johannesburg South Africa. He was represented by Art Eye Gallery and had his solo show titled “Soul Songs: The shape of my head.” \\nWhenever Mthiyane paints he plays a lot of jazz in the background and that also fuels his thought process. His works are more about personal expression and the channelling of innate creative forces than they are stylistically reflexive engagements with the discourse of art history. “The works are only premeditated up to maybe the first gesture. After that to complete them, it’s something completely different\", he says."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013397487837","gid://shopify/Product/9013397520605"]

Since graduating, he has dedicated himself to a rigorous studio practice, developing a distinctive and expressive artistic voice. \\n \\nMesfin's work is deeply influenced by key modern art movements, skillfully blending the structural innovations of Cubism and the bold colours of Fauvism with an overarching love for expressionism and figurative art. item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966588125 Tinyiko Makwakwa 2199 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641141260509 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014061138141", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104129757", "gid://shopify/Product/9133224755421"] Discover the work of Tinyiko Makwakwa, a South African artist exploring personal and cultural identity through bold, expressive forms. [23870,24824,23875,21099,21097,23871,25463,25461,25464,25462] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tinyiko Makwakwa (b. 1984) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose process-driven studio practice is a deep investigation into African indigenous science and realities. Working primarily with textiles, she creates layered compositions of vibrant colour using ochre, glass beads, and stitch embroidery on umbaco, a fabric used in traditional Xhosa attire. \\n \\nAt the heart of Makwakwa’s work is the exploration of cultural materiality as a form of language. Her practice is centered on what she terms \"Matrilineal Methodologies\"—rituals and spiritual practices that promote circularity and link generations. She champions ancestral knowledge systems as a valid science in and of itself, examining how these indigenous perspectives and lived experiences build and sustain cultures over time. \\n \\nThrough a visual language of curvilinear abstract shapes and forms, Makwakwa explores the interwoven narratives between her materials, the landscape, and her artistic process. Her work seeks to create a seamless blend between the physical and the spiritual, functioning as a continued, natural synthesis of tradition and contemporary expression."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013984526557","gid://shopify/Product/9013984755933","gid://shopify/Product/9014061138141","gid://shopify/Product/9014104129757","gid://shopify/Product/9133224165597","gid://shopify/Product/9133224132829","gid://shopify/Product/9133224755421"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641968193757 Treasure Mlima gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641150697693 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452090491101","gid://shopify/Product/9452090753245"] Treasure Mlima, a self-taught South African artist born in 1999, explores identity and space through his mixed media art. Using digital manipulation, wood carving, and painting, Mlima's ethereal works reflect his journey of self-discovery and new identities from an African perspective. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Treasure Mlima (b. 1999, Durban, South Africa) is a self-taught mixed media artist exploring themes of identity, space, and the African experience through his distinctive art. Raised between visual arts education in high school and self-driven learning via the internet, Mlima's journey of self-discovery is rooted in both trial and error and spiritual exploration. His ethereal work features untypical spaces against blank backgrounds, symbolizing a quest for answers and new identities. \\nMlima's creative process includes the digital manipulation of found images, which he then carves into wood and paints with oil-based and acrylic inks. This technique results in 2D prints that deal with space and identity from an African perspective. \\nMlima plans to work on a lifelong series titled \"Honing,\" which will explore various mediums in a non-linear fashion. His art reflects his journey of rebellion against traditional art principles, using unorthodox techniques to capture the essence of his thoughts and emotions. Mlima considers himself a cultural practitioner with the duty to reveal hidden realities and suggest alternative ones using neutral symbolism. \\nHis art is for anyone who sees value in it, and private collectors hold pieces of his work, continuing his legacy. Mlima's commitment to sharing a part of himself through his art ensures that his creations will make sense and be treasured long after he is gone"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452090491101","gid://shopify/Product/9452090753245"]

[22778] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Turiya Magadlela is a highly acclaimed South African artist whose work skillfully balances politically charged narratives with a refined and powerful aesthetic sensibility. Using unconventional materials such as pantyhose, correctional service uniforms, and textiles, she creates abstract compositions that explore themes of gender, sexuality, and the complex social and political histories of South Africa, particularly those relating to women's bodies and incarceration. \\nAs acclaimed artist Sue Williamson once observed in ArtReview, Magadlela's \"blocks of fabric in brilliant scarlet, pinks and oranges suggest an exuberant celebration of womanhood, a refusal to allow oneself to be downtrodden.\" This potent combination of material and meaning earned her the prestigious FNB Art Prize in 2015, an award judged by influential curators Bisi Silva and Koyo Kouoh. \\nA graduate of the renowned Rijksakademie in Amsterdam (2003–2004), Magadlela has a significant exhibition history. She held a major solo exhibition at the Johannesburg Art Gallery in 2015 and has participated in numerous high-profile international group shows, including Blue Black, curated by Glenn Ligon at the Pulitzer Arts Foundation (2017), Blackness in Abstraction at Pace Gallery (2016), and The Past is Present at Jack Shainman Gallery (2017)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452060770525","gid://shopify/Product/9452110545117","gid://shopify/Product/9452155044061","gid://shopify/Product/9452155338973"]

item.title: Tyrrel Thaysen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970421981 Tyrrel Thaysen 1146 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641161969885 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037963997","gid://shopify/Product/9452039078109"] Discover the work of South African artist Tyrrel Thaysen. His mixed-media assemblages and portraits explore heritage, self, and spirituality, with work featured at the Zeitz MOCAA. [6012,6095,12869,17918] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tyrrel Thaysen (b. 1969) is a mixed-media, multidisciplinary artist from Belvedere, Knysna, whose work is deeply rooted in his heritage as a descendant of farmworkers in apartheid South Africa. Now based in Cape Town, Thaysen's art is a profound exploration of the self, examining the cyclical patterns of thought and behavior that arise from personal history and coping mechanisms. He frequently represents his family in his work, finding solace and a foundational peace in spirituality. \\n \\nThaysen creates complex assemblages, layering materials with an inspiration drawn from Hollywood fashion and celebrity lifestyles. This unexpected juxtaposition stems from an upbringing where a pristine physical appearance was emphasized as a key to success. His portraiture reflects this internal narrative; the figures appear to have weathered numerous life events, emerging wiser and more capable. \\n \\nA graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art with a diploma in Fine Art and a major in sculpture, Thaysen's talent was recognized early when he won a national drawing competition at the AVA Gallery. His career is marked by prestigious awards, including the Montague White bursary and the Vermont Studio Center Triangle Arts Residency fellowship. He has been a frequent participant in Thupelo workshops worldwide, a three-time finalist at the Brett Kebble Art Awards, and an artist-in-residence at Greatmore Studios. \\n \\nThaysen has held two solo exhibitions at the AVA Gallery and currently has work on loan at the Zeitz MOCAA Museum. He is represented in corporate and private collections both in South Africa and internationally and has worked as a freelance visual artist for the Spier Arts Trust for over seventeen years."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452037963997","gid://shopify/Product/9452039078109"]

item.title: Tzung Hui Lauren Lee
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970454749 Tzung Hui Lauren Lee gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641162264797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452056903901"] Discover Tzung Hui Lauren Lee, a South African Chinese artist whose installation work, blending calligraphy and sculpture, explores diaspora, identity, and decolonizing the self. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tzung Hui Lauren Lee (b. 1998) is a multimedia South African Chinese artist based in Johannesburg. A recent graduate of the Wits School of Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand with a BA in Fine Arts, Lee has quickly established a unique and compelling artistic voice. Her practice is primarily installation-based, emerging from a multi-layered process that incorporates digital spaces, hand-made paper, sculpture, and calligraphy. \\nA core element of Lee's work is the translation of two-dimensional markings, such as her personal writings and calligraphic forms, into three-dimensional, immersive environments. [7255,7254,7256,7257,7260,7261,7264,7265,7268,7269,7270,7271,7266,7267,7262,7263,7258,7259,7253] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"Umseme Uyakhuluma: A celestial conversation” is a collaborative and experimental body of work that delves into the profound connectivity and duality between the physical and spiritual realms. The project explores the multifaceted nature of communication across these different planes of existence. The title, which translates to “The Straw Mat Speaks,” pays homage to one of Africa's most ancient and sustainable methods of recording information on grass mats. \\n \\nAt its core, the project reinterprets Bantu symbol writing—an ideographic system that evolved into a form of steganography, or coded language, used to convey sacred messages. This tradition is preserved today in cultures like the Ndebele, where it is known as “Umgwalo.” The artists draw a parallel between this coded script and the historical and divine significance of cowry shells in African spirituality, treating them as sacred messengers from the unseen world. \\n \\n“Umseme Uyakhuluma” serves as a powerful metaphor, urging viewers to contemplate the evolution of communication—what it has been, what it is today, and what it might become. By weaving together the spiritual symbolism of cowry shells and “umgwalo,” the work gives form to previously overlooked methods of dialogue. Ultimately, the project acts as a modern-day letter exchanged between African artists, recorded in digital mediums yet transcending space and time, much like the enduring legacies of the artifacts it honors."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452034719965","gid://shopify/Product/9452034752733","gid://shopify/Product/9452034785501","gid://shopify/Product/9452151767261","gid://shopify/Product/9452151800029","gid://shopify/Product/9452151832797","gid://shopify/Product/9452151865565","gid://shopify/Product/9452151898333","gid://shopify/Product/9452151931101","gid://shopify/Product/9452151963869","gid://shopify/Product/9452151996637","gid://shopify/Product/9452152062173","gid://shopify/Product/9452152094941","gid://shopify/Product/9452152193245","gid://shopify/Product/9452152226013","gid://shopify/Product/9452152291549","gid://shopify/Product/9452152324317","gid://shopify/Product/9452152357085","gid://shopify/Product/9452162351325","gid://shopify/Product/9452162384093","gid://shopify/Product/9452162449629","gid://shopify/Product/9452162547933","gid://shopify/Product/9452162580701","gid://shopify/Product/9452162613469","gid://shopify/Product/9452162646237","gid://shopify/Product/9452162711773","gid://shopify/Product/9452162744541","gid://shopify/Product/9452162810077","gid://shopify/Product/9452162842845","gid://shopify/Product/9452162908381","gid://shopify/Product/9452162941149","gid://shopify/Product/9452162973917","gid://shopify/Product/9452163006685"]

[9099,16150] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South African artist Usha Seejarim (b. 1974) is widely recognized for her thoughtful and inventive transformation of everyday domestic items into compelling works of art. She holds a B-Tech Degree in Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg (1999) and a Master’s Degree in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand (2008). \\nSeejarim has an extensive history of solo exhibitions, both locally and internationally. Her work has been showcased at major art fairs such as the Investec Cape Town Art Fair and featured in prominent institutions including the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG), the Durban Art Gallery, and NWU Gallery."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452056838365"]

[24620,25412,24618,3612,25414,25413,25411,24619] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vanessa Tembane is a South African artist of Mozambican heritage, currently based in Johannesburg. She holds a master’s degree in Fine Arts and is an acclaimed artist, having received the prestigious Ampersand Fellowship in 2018, among other awards. \\n \\nWorking primarily in collage and digital print media, Tembane’s art is a deep exploration of how her mother's narratives have influenced her own identity and sense of belonging. She creates strange and beautiful hybridized composites by merging her photographs taken in South Africa with those of her Mozambican relatives. These collages are further enriched with photographic cut-outs of capulanas—vibrant fabrics given to her by her grandmother and aunts during visits to Mozambique. \\n \\nThrough this process, Tembane’s work becomes a powerful means of telling stories about her origins and what is, for her, an alternative “home” culture. Her art enables her to identify with her mother’s country by constructing new, imagined memories, ultimately forging a unique and personal sense of belonging."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452172640477"]

item.title: Veryan Edwards
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971241181 Veryan Edwards 2397 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641169440989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169494749","gid://shopify/Product/9452169527517","gid://shopify/Product/9452169560285"] Veryan Edwards is a Botswana-based artist and the founder of the Thapong Visual Art Centre. [19001,19008,18999,19000,18984,19007] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Veryan Edwards (b. 1949, Hong Kong) is a pivotal figure in the development of contemporary art in Botswana, recognized both for her artistic practice and her foundational work as an arts organizer. Based in Gaborone, she holds a Master’s Degree in Fine Art from Rhodes University, South Africa, and has exhibited her own work extensively across Africa, the USA, and Europe since 1979, including numerous Triangle Network workshops. \\n \\nA visionary organizer, Edwards initiated and coordinated the first international artists' workshop in Botswana in 1989, based on the Triangle model from New York. Her efforts were instrumental in creating a vibrant, international artistic dialogue within the country. In 1995, she initiated the idea for a visual arts centre in Gaborone, which led to the establishment of the highly influential Thapong Visual Art Centre in 1999. Edwards served as its founding Director and as Chairperson of its Trust until 2003. \\n \\nEdwards' own artwork spans various genres and mediums, from abstract to semi-figurative. She describes her practice as a continual investigation of reality, informed by her readings in lay-person's quantum physics, spiritual texts, and the vast beauty of the Kalahari. Her work often features an ambiguity of space, inviting viewers to bring their own perceptions to complete the meaning."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452169494749","gid://shopify/Product/9452169527517","gid://shopify/Product/9452169560285"]

item.title: Vivien Kohler
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971896541 Vivien Kohler 391 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641172783325 [] Vivien Kohler is a South African artist who explores themes of urban identity, decay, and transcendence. Discover his work inspired by the liminality of the South African city. [4351,4353,4352] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vivien Kohler (b. 1976) is a Johannesburg-based artist, originally from Cape Town. He holds a National Diploma in Fine Art from the Ruth Prowse School of Art and Design and is an acclaimed, award-winning artist, having received the Thami Mnyele Sculpture Merit Award, among others. His work is housed in prominent private and public collections throughout South Africa. \\n \\nKohler's work is a profound investigation into the unique liminality of the South African city and the ability of the human spirit to transcend what he terms ‘conceptual decay’. He is fascinated by how individuals and communities flourish and bloom from circumstances of enormous complexity. His practice is driven by a need to restructure the \"residue\" of this urban chaos, finding meaning, positivity, and history in the cracks of the city. \\n \\nThrough his art, Kohler explores the perpetual process of change and the striving to move from deficiency to authenticity. Using the metaphor of a chrysalis, he views his works as representations of the traces we leave behind as we change form. Each piece is a vital aspect of a shifting persona, collectively redefining the identity of people in this complex place called home."}]}]} []

item.title: Vusi Khumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972027613 Vusi Khumalo 555 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641199915229 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452044878045","gid://shopify/Product/9452044910813","gid://shopify/Product/9452044976349","gid://shopify/Product/9452045009117","gid://shopify/Product/9452045041885","gid://shopify/Product/9452045074653","gid://shopify/Product/9013378449629"] Vusi Khumalo is a South African artist who creates startlingly realistic collages of landscapes and informal settlements, shaped by his history in political exile. Discover his unique work. [11607,11610,11613,11615,11614] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vusi Khumalo (b. 1951) is a celebrated South African artist whose life and work are deeply intertwined with the country's political history. A long-standing member of the African National Congress, Khumalo left apartheid South Africa in 1986 for ANC camps in Zambia and Tanzania. It was in the Dakawa Camp, Tanzania, that he first had the opportunity to fully explore his artistic talents, initially training and later teaching textile printing, art, and design. \\n \\nAfter being repatriated in 1992, Khumalo continued his work as an educator at the re-established Dakawa Art and Craft Community Centre in Grahamstown. His efforts earned him a scholarship to the Konstfack National Art College in Stockholm, Sweden. In 1996, he dedicated himself full-time to his own art, seeking a medium that could powerfully render the South African landscape and its burgeoning squatter communities. \\n \\nFinding oil painting insufficient for the intense realism he wanted to evoke, Khumalo developed his signature collage technique. By meticulously reconstructing these informal settlements, his startlingly real works challenge viewers to look beyond media facades of squalor and crime, humanising the residents and environments of these complex communities. Now working as a full-time artist in the Eastern Cape, Khumalo has exhibited extensively in South Africa and internationally, with a long history of solo and group shows at Everard Read Gallery and in London, China, and Sweden."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452044878045","gid://shopify/Product/9452044910813","gid://shopify/Product/9452044976349","gid://shopify/Product/9452045009117","gid://shopify/Product/9452045041885","gid://shopify/Product/9452045074653","gid://shopify/Product/9013378449629"]

item.title: Walter Battiss
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641973436637 Walter Battiss 302 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203585245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452125978845","gid://shopify/Product/9452153766109"] Discover the work of Walter Battiss, a pioneering South African modern artist. His dynamic style was influenced by Picasso, Ndebele art, and more. Founder of the Walter Battiss Museum. [23892,20282,4280,4277,25529] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Walter Battiss (1906-1982) was one of South Africa's most significant and innovative modern artists, known for his lifelong dedication to art education and his dynamic evolution of style. A founding member of the New Group, Battiss was a revered art educator for over 30 years. His early realistic painting style transformed following travels in Europe and pivotal meetings with figures like Abbé Henri Breuil, Pablo Picasso, and Gino Severini, leading to a more symbolic and hieratic approach. \\n \\nThroughout his career, Battiss seamlessly absorbed and reinterpreted a wide range of influences. His work saw the introduction of calligraphic forms, the abstract influence of Ndebele bead work, experiments with coloured woodcuts, and later, the use of palette-knife techniques with graffito. His extensive travels to the Middle East and Greece further expanded his visual language, introducing Pre-Islamic and island-inspired motifs into his creative thinking. \\n \\nA pioneer in South African printmaking, Battiss championed the medium of serigraphy (silkscreen), culminating in his organisation of the country's first exhibition of serigraphs in 1970. His immense contribution to South African art is immortalized in the Walter Battiss Museum in his hometown of Somerset East. His work continues to be celebrated for its intellectual curiosity, vibrant energy, and unique synthesis of global and local influences."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452125978845","gid://shopify/Product/9452153766109"]

item.title: Walter Oltmann

[20128,20129,20131,18571,18572,18573,18574,18948,22399,20127,368,18575,20132,20133,369,22413] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Walter Oltmann (b. 1960) is a celebrated South African artist renowned for his mastery of line in both two and three dimensions. He holds a BA in Fine Arts from the University of Natal (1981) and an MA in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (1985). His unique aesthetic is deeply influenced by his migratory childhood across remote areas of KwaZulu-Natal, which exposed him to the region's rich craft traditions. \\n \\nOltmann’s practice is primarily divided into intricate drawings (using pencil, ink, and bleach) and delicate wire sculptures. A conceptual and visual thread runs through all of his work, seamlessly connecting the drawn line to the sculpted wire form. This exploration extends into his printmaking, as seen in his work with The Artists’ Press. Reflecting on this process, Oltmann notes how \"the thread of the pencil line moves into wire which moves into polymer plate.\" He successfully found a way to translate the \"delicacy of lace and wire work\" into print media, a discovery he describes as both unexpected and welcome. \\n \\nThrough his meticulous and innovative approach, Oltmann continues to explore the boundaries between drawing, sculpture, and printmaking."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013843394781","gid://shopify/Product/9013843427549","gid://shopify/Product/9013843460317","gid://shopify/Product/9013843525853","gid://shopify/Product/9013843558621","gid://shopify/Product/9013850243293","gid://shopify/Product/9013943992541","gid://shopify/Product/9013944025309","gid://shopify/Product/9013944123613","gid://shopify/Product/9013944189149","gid://shopify/Product/9013944254685","gid://shopify/Product/9014015918301","gid://shopify/Product/9014016377053"]

[23913] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wayne Barker, born in Pretoria, South Africa, in 1963, is a fine artist based in Komatipoort. He rose to prominence in the late ‘80s, at the height of the political unrest during apartheid. He remains one of the most prolific and influential artists to have emerged from the country. \\nHe works in various mediums, including but not limited to painting, printmaking, sculpture, video, performance and installation. In addition to collaborations with other artists, Barker has collaborated with the Qubeka Beadwork Studio based in Cape Town, South Africa, to realize large-scale glass beadworks. Major concerns have included the legacy of colonialism in South Africa, issues of land and contestation – as evidenced in works referencing the paintings of JH Pierneef – issues around race, reconciliation and accountability as well as a sensitivity to humanist concerns that border on the poetic. \\nHis works have influenced contemporary art practice in South Africa, with several of his contemporaries and younger artists citing his work as turning points in perspective and practice."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452126372061"]

item.title: Wendy Vincent
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641977172189 Wendy Vincent 2471 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641211810013 [] Discover the work of Wendy Vincent, a master painter and a pioneer of stone lithography in South Africa. [19506,19510,19496,19529,19497,19511,19495,19508,19513,19522,19526] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wendy Vincent is a celebrated South African master painter and printmaker, distinguished as a pioneer in the field of stone and lithography within the country. Her artistic journey began in her childhood on a farm, where she developed a profound connection with nature, drawing and planting from the age of ten. This lifelong passion is the central theme of her paintings. \\n \\nEducated between 1958 and 1971 at the Durban and Witwatersrand Technikons, Vincent later continued her training in the international art hubs of New York and Paris. Her work has achieved global recognition, with exhibitions across South Africa, Europe, Australia, and the UK. In the United States, her art is part of significant public collections, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the New York Public Library, and the South African Embassy Collection in Washington, D.C. Her importance in the national canon is cemented by her inclusion in seminal publications like Esmé Berman’s Art and the Artists of South Africa. \\n \\nFor the past two and a half decades, Vincent has largely retreated from the public art scene. In a creative partnership with her life partner, artist Geoffrey Armstrong, she has dedicated herself to another form of artmaking: the creation of a sprawling indigenous rock garden, continuing to work with the natural world that has always inspired her."}]}]} []

Explore his powerful, site-specific projects that confront prejudice and explore themes of exile, memory, and healing. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wezile Mgibe is an acclaimed South African art practitioner whose interdisciplinary work encompasses performance, film, and installation to drive social change. His practice is centered on confronting societal prejudices and advocating against inequality, creating platforms for critical self-reflection in often unwelcoming spaces. In recognition of his impactful work, Mgibe is a recipient of the prestigious 2019 David Koloane Award and a 2020 Arts & Culture Trust Award. \\nA core element of Mgibe's practice involves developing continuous, site-specific series that interrogate the dynamics of place and culture. He powerfully uses his own body as a primary tool to reveal forgotten ways of existence and to facilitate a process of internal healing. A recurring visual motif is his body covered in bandages, a striking image that evokes the dual sensation of remembering home while simultaneously carrying a profound sense of exile. \\nMgibe's work has been exhibited at prominent institutions both locally and internationally, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, Norval Foundation, FNB Art Joburg, the Centre for Applied Human Rights (UK), and Hangar Online (Portugal). He has an extensive history of residencies and workshops, and is currently a permanent artist at the Bag Factory studios in Johannesburg."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452062376157"]

[376,377,378,24061] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Willem Boshoff stands as one of South Africa's most important and intellectually rigorous contemporary artists, with a career marked by national and international exhibitions. Born in Vanderbijlpark, his early exposure to his father's carpentry work instilled a deep appreciation and technical expertise for working with wood, a skill that has influenced his artistic practice profoundly. \\nWhile renowned for his mastery of various materials including stone, paper, and sand, Boshoff is most celebrated for his conceptual installations. These large-scale works are frequently based on a deep exploration of language, dictionaries, and the boundaries of knowledge. His art often challenges viewers to reconsider established power structures and the ways in which information is organized and withheld. \\nBoshoff's practice is supported by a distinguished academic career spanning over two decades. After training as a teacher, he earned a diploma in fine art and a master's degree in sculpture. His commitment to research is evident in his study trips across Europe and his extensive work in academia. In recognition of his immense contribution to the arts, he was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of Johannesburg in 2008."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452128043229"]

item.title: Wim Botha
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641980514525 Wim Botha gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215381725 [] Explore the striking works of Wim Botha, a renowned South African artist featured on Latitudes Online. Known for his sculptures and mixed media works, Botha's art engages with themes of memory, identity, and the complexities of post-apartheid South Africa, offering a deep reflection on contemporary issues. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wim Botha (b.1974) is a leading South African contemporary artist best-known for his sculptural works. He graduated with a degree in visual art from the University of Pretoria in 1996. \\nA defining feature of Botha’s practice is the diverse and often unconventional media he employs – from carved books, marble, bronze and wood, to oil paint and ink. Famously, in 2004, Botha created a replica of Michelangelo’s Pietà out of maize meal. \\nThe mediums Botha uses are very much intertwined with his objective to explore history, religion, status and power through an art historical lens. Botha’s reinterpretations of baroque and renaissance figures in his unique armoury of materials sees them transformed, blurred and reconstructed, subverting their original meaning. \\nBotha has been recognised with a number of honours and awards including, in 2013 the Helgaard Steyn Prize for sculpture, in 2005 the Standard Bank Young Artist Award, and in 2003 he was the first recipient of the prestigious Tollman Award. In 2013 his work was included in the South African pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale, and in 2018 a major solo exhibition of the artist’s work, Heliostat, was shown at Norval Foundation, Cape Town. His work is included in a number of important collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery as well as the Spier Art Collection."}]}]} []

item.title: Wim Legrand
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641981268189 Wim Legrand gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215447261 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452263440605"] Discover the playful and paradoxical art of Wim Legrand (b. 1978). Explore his unique blend of painting, cartoons, and pop culture with art historical references, creating peculiar allegorical narratives that comment on our postmodern world. See his exhibition history, including numerous solo shows at 99 Loop Gallery in Cape Town. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wim Legrand (b. 1978) is a contemporary artist who offers a playful yet poignant take on the paradoxical strangeness of everyday reality. His work serves as a commentary on the postmodern condition, where individuals are often victims of a relentless barrage of information and news feeds. Legrand has a unique ability to transform mundane and forgettable objects into central figures within peculiar allegorical narratives. \\nIn his art, the past blurs with the present and fact intertwines with fiction, creating scenes set in a liminal zone that resembles the unfettered \"now\" of a dream. Meanings remain tantalizingly out of reach, continually open to the viewer's interpretation. Legrand masterfully combines painting with drawing, infusing his work with elements of cartoons and pop culture. These contemporary references are overlaid onto an art historical atmosphere, drawing from North European history painting and Surrealist traditions. \\nWim Legrand has established a significant presence in both Europe and South Africa, with solo shows in Belgium and numerous exhibitions in Cape Town, particularly at the 99 Loop Gallery, which has hosted several of his solo shows including 'The Parafix' (2020) and 'Twilight of the Vanities' (2019). He has also participated in major art fairs such as the RMB Turbine Art Fair and the Cape Town Art Fair."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452263440605"]

item.title: Wole Lagunju
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641983496413 Wole Lagunju 927 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215873245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452117262557","gid://shopify/Product/9452117295325","gid://shopify/Product/9452117360861","gid://shopify/Product/9452117393629","gid://shopify/Product/9452117491933"] Discover the works of Wole Lagunju, an award-winning Nigerian artist based in North Carolina, USA. His art blends traditional Yoruba textile motifs with contemporary techniques to explore identity, spirituality, and multiculturalism. [23378,23373,23374,23381] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wole Lagunju is a distinguished artist and 1986 graduate of Fine Arts and Graphic Design from the University of Ife, now Obafemi Awolowo University, Nigeria. Currently residing in North Carolina, USA, Lagunju has showcased his work in numerous esteemed public and private exhibitions. His accolades include the Phillip Ravenhill Fellowship awarded by UCLA in 2006 and the Pollock-Krasner Foundation award in 2009. \\nLagunju’s artistic inspiration draws from traditional Yoruba women textile designers, particularly those involved in the indigenous indigo tie and dye industry (Adire), which is a significant part of Nigerian heritage. By integrating Adire motifs, his work explores themes of human character, spirituality, and the interplay between physical and metaphysical realms. \\nAs an artist navigating different cultures in a globalized era, Lagunju employs these motifs to delve into the concept of multiculturalism. His drip technique with inks echoes the vibrancy of indigo dyeing, merging spontaneity with a meticulously calculated artistic process. This synthesis allows Lagunju to address profound questions of identity and purpose as a contemporary African artist."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452117262557","gid://shopify/Product/9452117295325","gid://shopify/Product/9452117360861","gid://shopify/Product/9452117393629","gid://shopify/Product/9452117491933"]

item.title: Wopko Jensma
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641983791325 Wopko Jensma 890 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641217446109 [] Explore the life and work of Wopko Jensma (1939-1993), a white South African artist and poet who used his craft to challenge the injustices of apartheid. Discover his powerful poetry, including "Once and Now," his significant contributions to the art world, and the mystery surrounding his disappearance. [4577,4809] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wopko Jensma born in Middelburg, Cape Town, on July 26, 1939, was a prominent white South African artist and poet who became a vocal critic of the apartheid regime. Educated at the University of Potchefstroom and the University of Pretoria, where he majored in sculpture, Jensma's creative endeavors were deeply intertwined with his political convictions. His work, which includes the poignant poem Once and Now, openly addressed the systemic racism experienced by Black South Africans, particularly the exploitation of young domestic workers. \\n \\nJensma's artistic expression was not confined to a single medium; he was also an editor for Gerwe Magazine and a translator. His extensive travels and work experience in Swaziland, Botswana, and Mozambique, including a teaching position at the Serowe Art School in Botswana, broadened his perspective and influenced his work. As a privileged white artist, he used his platform to give voice to the oppressed, and his poetry is often interpreted as a reflection of his personal struggles with the South African government's discriminatory policies. In a tragic and enigmatic end to a life of creative resistance, Wopko Jensma disappeared without a trace after August 1993."}]}]} []

item.title: Xanthe Somers
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641987789021 Xanthe Somers 1118 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223246045 [] Explore the work of Zimbabwean ceramic artist Xanthe Somers, whose playful and political sculptures challenge colonial aesthetics. Her work is held in the V&A Museum. [24858,24866,24867,24862] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xanthe Somers (b. 1992) is a Zimbabwean artist whose ceramic sculptures are a vibrant and critical examination of the politics of aesthetics in a post-colonial context. Born and raised in Harare, Somers graduated from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2015. She was subsequently awarded a grant to study at Goldsmiths, University of London, where she completed an MA in Postcolonial Culture and Global Policy with distinction in 2020. \\nHer practice is profoundly informed by how Zimbabwe's colonial history continues to manipulate and shape aesthetic values. Through her work, Somers reimagines everyday life and explores what she terms the \"subtle treason of objects.\" Employing a distinct visual language characterized by a sense of play, bright colours, a mocking tone, and exaggerated shapes, she actively challenges prevailing ideas of normalcy, beauty, and refinement. \\nHer sculptures serve as a powerful critique of the Christian-Colonial gaze that remains fixed upon southern Africa. Somers' work is held in numerous private and public collections, including the prestigious Victoria and Albert Museum in London."}]}]} []

item.title: Xavier Briel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641988083933 Xavier Briel 2639 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223639261 [] Xavier Briel is a South African adventure sports photographer who captures the raw energy of trail running and endurance events by shooting on the move. [22329] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xavier Briel, born and raised in Pretoria, moved to Cape Town in 2010, inspired by its stunning landscapes. Initially a draughtsman and IT professional, he discovered his passion for photography while exploring South Africa’s outdoors. In 2016, Xavier left his job to pursue photography full-time, focusing on capturing the raw energy of adventure sports, especially trail running. \\n \\nHis big break came when his work at PUFfeR 2016 led to opportunities with Ultra-Trail Cape Town and other major events. Known for his ability to run long distances with a camera, Xavier’s work is defined by his belief that great stories come from pushing beyond comfort zones. \\n \\nWith dreams of shooting in Africa’s most remote locations, Xavier aims to link adventure photography with conservation, showcasing the continent’s beauty and challenges through his lens. Inspired by local talents like Kelvin Trautman and Craig Kolesky, he continues to push his creative and physical boundaries."}]}]} []

item.title: Xhanti Zwelendaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641990246621 Xhanti Zwelendaba 1891 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225015517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013394669789", "gid://shopify/Product/9013397979357"] Explore the work of Xhanti Zwelendaba, a South African artist interrogating Xhosa culture, colonialism, and identity through sculpture, printmaking, and performance. [20764,20761,20762,18426,20763,13860,14051] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xhanti Zwelendaba is a South African multi-disciplinary artist whose practice spans sculpting, printmaking, installation, performance, and video art. His work confronts the complex tensions between traditional Xhosa culture and the contemporary forces of capitalism and nationalism, all while interrogating the enduring legacies of colonialism and apartheid. This exploration is deeply informed by his own experience of navigating and balancing these often-conflicting cultural paradigms. \\nEach of Zwelendaba's works is a testament to his commitment to questioning both his personal identity and the collective identities of Black people in South Africa. By employing diverse materials and collaborative processes, he allows each idea to unfold with unique nuance. His practice is overtly situated within a decolonial framework, constantly pushing the boundaries of art-making from the African continent within a contemporary art sphere that remains largely dominated by Western European traditions. \\nZwelendaba's career has been marked by numerous significant achievements. He was featured as the Artist of the Year at the Turbine Art Fair in 2021 and has participated in major art fairs, including Investec Cape Town Art Fair and FNB Art Johannesburg. His work has been shown in solo and group exhibitions such as Chamber of Mines (2016), Familial Threads (2019), and Tongues (2021). He has completed prestigious residencies at NIROX (2017) and the Leipzig International Art Programme in Germany (2022)."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013394669789","gid://shopify/Product/9013397979357","gid://shopify/Product/9013842346205","gid://shopify/Product/9013962604765","gid://shopify/Product/9013962703069","gid://shopify/Product/9013962866909","gid://shopify/Product/9013962997981"]

item.title: Yakno Abasi Ene
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641992376541 Yakno Abasi Ene 1927 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641227309277 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046876893","gid://shopify/Product/9452062539997","gid://shopify/Product/9452096291037"] [21011,21209,21046,21010,21013,21120] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yakno-Abasi Ene is an abstract realism artist based in Lagos Nigeria. \\nYakno-Abasi's artistic journey, delves into the profound realms of sisterhood, women's empowerment, and the divine feminine. Shaped by the nurturing bonds within my predominantly female family, her work aims to illuminate the varied roles of women and address the challenges they navigate. Each creation is a testament to her idealistic vision of societal development, capturing the essence of unity and strength inherent in sisterhood. Empowerment, a recurring theme, resonates through her art, advocating for the elevation of women in all facets of life. \\nThe divine feminine, a source of inspiration, lends a spiritual and transcendent dimension to her work, celebrating the inherent grace and power within every woman. Through diverse mediums, her art mirrors the dynamic interplay of surroundings, personal experiences, and an ever-evolving imagination. As I navigate this continuous learning journey as an emerging artist, her central goal remains to educate, heal, and inspire, contributing to a more inclusive and equitable world by spotlighting the beauty and resilience of women."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452046876893","gid://shopify/Product/9452062539997","gid://shopify/Product/9452096291037"]

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641993392349 Yannis Davy Guibinga 1259 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641227342045 [] Discover the work of Gabonese photographer Yannis Davy Guibinga, who explores and celebrates the diverse identities of Africa and its diaspora through stunning visual narratives. [14795,14796,14797] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yannis Davy Guibinga (b.1995) is a celebrated photographer and master storyteller from Libreville, Gabon. His work is a vibrant and essential exploration of the diverse identities and cultures found across Africa and its global diaspora. \\n \\nGuibinga uses his lens not merely to document but to celebrate this rich multiplicity. His primary mission is to actively counter the singular, often reductive narratives that have historically been associated with the African continent. Through a powerful combination of narrative depth and an incisive eye for composition and colour, he creates images that are both visually stunning and conceptually profound. \\n \\nThis unique and compelling vision has enabled Guibinga to build an extensive and remarkable portfolio, leading to prestigious collaborations with world-renowned brands such as Apple and Nikon, solidifying his status as a significant voice in contemporary photography."}]}]} []

[23013] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yassmin Forte (b. 1980, Quelimane) is a distinguished Mozambican artist, curator, and communication professional based in Maputo. With a degree in Communication Sciences from ISPU, Forte has cultivated an impressive 11-year career spanning Mozambique, Portugal, Cape Verde, and Brazil, working in both urban and rural contexts. \\n \\nPassionate about art and cultural diversity, Forte is an accomplished photographer who has presented several solo exhibitions, including 'On the Stage' and 'In Stage 1' at BCI Mediateca and 'Mulheres com Pinta' at Livraria Minerva. Her work has also been featured in numerous collective exhibitions over the last eight years. \\n \\nBeyond her artistic practice, Forte is a respected curator. She has curated significant projects such as the UN Women Photography Contest and a homage to Jorge Almeida (in collaboration with Filipe Branquinho) at the Franco-Mozambican Cultural Center. She is also committed to community development, leading photography workshops like \"Olhar da Rapariga\" and serving as a juror for various photo contests. \\n \\nHer global perspective has been further enriched through participation in three international artistic residencies: Catchupa Factory in Cape Verde, and Gineceu/Legado and Up Cycle in Maputo."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9014034694365"]

[22817,22812,22856,22823,22857,22813,22814] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yasmine Amal is a self-taught artist and political scientist with Moroccan heritage, born in Germany. [21005] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yeabsra Yemru (b. 2000) is an Ethiopian mixed-media painter and printmaker whose work is a profound exploration of the theme of \"Waiting.\" Born in Debre Birhan, Yemru’s art captures transient moments with a contemplative depth, finding beauty in what is often fleeting and forgotten. \\n \\nThrough a unique fusion of sculptural elements, rich symbolism, and masterful technique, his pieces evoke a powerful sense of nostalgia and introspection. Yemru’s work stands in quiet opposition to a world driven by haste; it serves as a contemplative invitation for the viewer to pause, reflect, and appreciate the delicate and often overlooked beauty of the present moment."}]}]} []
