item.title: Yonela Doda
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144842924253 Yonela Doda gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144843022557 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452125159645","gid://shopify/Product/9452125618397"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/134196429021 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Yonela Doda, born in 1998 is a Cape Town based collage mixed media artists. Doda work is premised on the Catharsis Theory and the deep connection she has with her physical and emotional aspect of her life as well as the things she wishes to fix within herself. Doda does this by dealing with the distortion, healing and purification of her own pain and the pain caused by others onto her. 
 Doda’s interest in looking at the fragmented and distorted body (particularly the woman body) by experimenting with collage and thread has led her to her interest in extended and prosthetic bodies as well as ritualistic and transgressive body. Doda explores and confronts the violence towards women in South Africa, how and why the body comes to matter, what the body can and is able to do as a material, bodies that she comes in contact with, how sometimes these bodies are welcome and invited and how sometimes they are not. Doda also speaks of the process of going through to get through that result in Self-Knowledge which is strongly influenced by her interest in the Catharsis theory which was first used in a psychological context by Josef Breuer. 
 Doda’s collage work is influenced by the creating of the hybrid body beyond the physical limitations of the human scale; extending and distorting the body to create new identity. Doda also uses stitching in her work(s), a way to communicate the process of healing and purification. 
 Doda’s ways of recalling her vulnerability through herself and her own experiences, it’s heavens and hell might sometimes view as violent, which in some cases is. This helps Doda not reject self but instead visit and highlight those vulnerabilities and help herself heal. Finding a home in self is one of the important subjects that Doda highlights in her works. Doda describes “ It was when I found home within myself that I realized the importance of self-love, peace and nurturing self before others”. 

EXHIBITIONS
Group exhibited at The Move Gallery, 2019.
 
And So The Stories Ran Away Exhibition at the Zeitz MOCAA, 2019 – 2020.

Winner of the Dreams Realities competition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography 2020.

Virtual Group
Exhibition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography titled Dreams Realities, 2020. 
"}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452125159645","gid://shopify/Product/9452125618397"]

item.title: Mira Jaan
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144854458589 Mira Jaan gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144854491357 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452159074525","gid://shopify/Product/9452214616285","gid://shopify/Product/9452214780125"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/174690336989 South Africa ZA {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Mira Jaan is an emerging artist born in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal and raised the majority of her youth in Cape Town, South Africa. Mira Jaan was first introduced to the art world by her father Ashram Jamal who remains a great inspiration to her. His affinity with. Bright colours which covered the walls of her childhood home, appreciation of art history and his own heritage has reflected itself in her work. Her primary medium is gouache paint on paper but she is transitioning into using more acrylic paints on canvas. Mira Jaan is inspired by the art of the past specifically of ancient India. And parts of East/South East Asia. Within her art her core concern is a blend of. Felinity and androgyny and how these factors can exist along side each other in one person. \r\n She often paints two figures mirroring each other but holding different characteristics in the same frame. For her no body is every one thing, we are all split genetically, spiritually and emotionally into multiple manifestations of ourselves. She feels as though one can become frustrated with maintaining a singular identity, unable to embrace certain an aspect of themselves as they might contradict the other. By portraying these dual manifestations in the same frame living alongside and supporting each other she hopes to create an acceptance within the viewer of all the different versions of themselves within them as as well as an acceptance. And love within herself. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452159074525","gid://shopify/Product/9452214616285","gid://shopify/Product/9452214780125"]

item.title: Zandile Makroti
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144860061917 Zandile Makroti gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144860160221 [] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169546907869 Johannesburg ZA {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Zandile (Zandi) Makroti is a multidisciplinary storyteller, qualified production designer, aspiring curator, creative director, and certified UX/UI designer based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her work is deeply rooted in personal experience, spiritual growth, and the quiet power of becoming, reflecting a journey of self-discovery through art. 
 Working across film photography, fine art materials, fabric, performance, and installation, Zandi builds visual worlds that explore womanhood, ancestry, and identity. Each piece is a fragment of her journey, a mirror of emotional, creative, and spiritual transformation. 
 She has exhibited at the Open Window Institute and Kameraz, and was nominated for the Pangolin Awards at Open Window for Best Production Design Project. Her background in production design and user experience informs a practice that is both visually immersive and emotionally resonant, bridging the disciplines of film, design, and fine art to tell stories that honour where she comes from, who she is, and who she is still becoming. 
"}]}]} []

gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144866910429 Gabrielle Kannemeyer gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144866975965 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452201312477","gid://shopify/Product/9452201443549","gid://shopify/Product/9452201574621","gid://shopify/Product/9452201705693","gid://shopify/Product/9452201836765","gid://shopify/Product/9452202000605","gid://shopify/Product/9452202131677","gid://shopify/Product/9452202262749","gid://shopify/Product/9452202361053","gid://shopify/Product/9452202459357","gid://shopify/Product/9452202557661","gid://shopify/Product/9452202655965","gid://shopify/Product/9452202819805","gid://shopify/Product/9452202950877","gid://shopify/Product/9452203081949","gid://shopify/Product/9452203180253","gid://shopify/Product/9452203344093","gid://shopify/Product/9452203507933","gid://shopify/Product/9452203671773","gid://shopify/Product/9452203868381","gid://shopify/Product/9452203999453","gid://shopify/Product/9452204196061","gid://shopify/Product/9452204327133","gid://shopify/Product/9452204458205","gid://shopify/Product/9452204622045","gid://shopify/Product/9452204785885","gid://shopify/Product/9452205015261","gid://shopify/Product/9452205179101","gid://shopify/Product/9452205375709","gid://shopify/Product/9452205539549","gid://shopify/Product/9452205703389","gid://shopify/Product/9452205834461","gid://shopify/Product/9452206063837","gid://shopify/Product/9452206260445","gid://shopify/Product/9452206391517","gid://shopify/Product/9452206588125","gid://shopify/Product/9452206751965","gid://shopify/Product/9452206948573","gid://shopify/Product/9452207112413","gid://shopify/Product/9452207767773"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169539666141 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Gabrielle Kannemeyer (1989 - ) is a photographer and visual storyteller based in District Six, Cape Town. Her work is rooted in personal history, community connections, and a deep engagement with heritage and place. With a background in fine art and a practice informed by years of visual exploration, Kannemeyer’s photography foregrounds emotionally resonant, often overlooked stories, particularly around South Africa’s equestrian traditions. These stories are deeply personal and interwoven into her own life, exploring themes of intergenerational memory, identity, erasure, and belonging. 
 She is currently pursuing a multi-year documentary project on South African horse culture, which archives the experiences of established horse communities across local showgrounds, suburbs, city spaces, valley towns, and remote corners of the country. Gabrielle highlights the close, complex bonds between individuals, families, their horses, and their culture and heritage. Through portrait photography, archival research, and active participation, her work examines representation, land, tradition, and pride within communities often overlooked in mainstream narratives. 
 SOLO EXHIBITIONS : 
 2025 
 'As Necessary as Bread', EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa 
 GROUP EXHIBITIONS : 
 2025 
 ‘Perde Mense’, Central Library, Cape Town, South Africa 
 'UNO', Ultra Violet, Cape Town, South Africa 
 'Journey Mercies', EBONY/CURATED, Cape Town, South Africa "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452201312477","gid://shopify/Product/9452201443549","gid://shopify/Product/9452201574621","gid://shopify/Product/9452201705693","gid://shopify/Product/9452201836765","gid://shopify/Product/9452202000605","gid://shopify/Product/9452202131677","gid://shopify/Product/9452202262749","gid://shopify/Product/9452202361053","gid://shopify/Product/9452202459357","gid://shopify/Product/9452202557661","gid://shopify/Product/9452202655965","gid://shopify/Product/9452202819805","gid://shopify/Product/9452202950877","gid://shopify/Product/9452203081949","gid://shopify/Product/9452203180253","gid://shopify/Product/9452203344093","gid://shopify/Product/9452203507933","gid://shopify/Product/9452203671773","gid://shopify/Product/9452203868381","gid://shopify/Product/9452203999453","gid://shopify/Product/9452204196061","gid://shopify/Product/9452204327133","gid://shopify/Product/9452204458205","gid://shopify/Product/9452204622045","gid://shopify/Product/9452204785885","gid://shopify/Product/9452205015261","gid://shopify/Product/9452205179101","gid://shopify/Product/9452205375709","gid://shopify/Product/9452205539549","gid://shopify/Product/9452205703389","gid://shopify/Product/9452205834461","gid://shopify/Product/9452206063837","gid://shopify/Product/9452206260445","gid://shopify/Product/9452206391517","gid://shopify/Product/9452206588125","gid://shopify/Product/9452206751965","gid://shopify/Product/9452206948573","gid://shopify/Product/9452207112413","gid://shopify/Product/9452207767773"]

item.title: Guy Du Toit
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144867401949 Guy Du Toit gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144867434717 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129485021"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169539174621 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" “My objects come from my immediate environment, selected for their non-heroic, open-ended meaning. Bells, for instance, may refer either to slavery or liberty. My overriding concern is that of reality and illusion; the fusing of Western and African realities is somehow reflected in this ambiguity.” 
 Guy du Toit uses a wide range of media in his sculptures, including bronze, stone, wood and steel, and draws in pen, ink and charcoal. He has exhibited extensively, both locally and internationally, and has been consistently supported by private and public collectors, institutions, academics and fellow artists. 
 Honoured with several awards, he curates and adjudicates exhibitions and lectures at a number of institutions, including Pelmama Academy in Soweto, Pretoria University, Johannesburg and Pretoria Technicons, and the Johannesburg School of Art, Ballet, Drama and Music. He gives workshops throughout South Africa and has been involved in community projects, seminars and symposia. 
 The past few years have increasingly been spent on private and public commissions and in working closely with artists and businesses, especially those involved in design, communications, architecture, advertising and entertainment. Guy currently teaches part-time at the University of Pretoria and works full-time from his new home and studio in Zwavelpoort. 

Guy du Toit’s apparent irreverence can obfuscate the fact that he is undoubtedly one of South Africa’s most accomplished sculptors. “Liberated” (as he says) by the advent of democracy in South Africa from having to concern himself and his art with the notions of identity, he has happily turned his attention to “less provincial” pursuits like revelling in form, concept and media for their own sakes. Du Toit uses the unexpected juxtaposition of bronze casts of universal, everyday found (and made-to-look-found) objects to invite his audience to invent dialogue themselves."}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452129485021"]

item.title: Ina Maria Shikongo
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144867795165 Ina Maria Shikongo gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144867827933 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226281693","gid://shopify/Product/9452226412765","gid://shopify/Product/9452226609373","gid://shopify/Product/9452226740445","gid://shopify/Product/9452226871517"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/149280784605 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Ina Maria Shikongo ((b.1979)) creates striking textile works that reflect her deep commitment to climate justice. Born in Angola as a refugee and raised in Namibia, her practice is shaped by a life of resilience, activism, and care for the planet. Her textile collages—often crafted as protest banners—are both art and advocacy, calling for a shift in humanity’s impact on the environment. 
 Having started her artistic journey in 2000, Ina’s focus on textile collage emerged from a deeply personal place, driven by a dedication to reusing materials after the loss of her aunt to gender-based violence. Her creative practice extends beyond the studio: as a climate justice organizer, educator, and movement builder, she works across local and international platforms including Fridays for Future Africa, Extinction Rebellion, and Debt for Climate. 
 Recent exhibitions include Unresolved Memories at Guns & Rain in Johannesburg (2025), Slow Burn: A Look at Contemporary Art in Stellenbosch, her solo show Echoes of Resistance at The Project Room in Windhoek (2024), FNB Art Joburg (2024) and the Africa Speaks show at Zee Gallery in Mauritius (2023). She received first prize in the Textile Art category at the Bank Windhoek Triennial in 2021. Her writing and activism have been featured internationally, including in The Climate Book edited by Greta Thunberg (Penguin, 2023). The artist also features in the documentary Temperature Rising, which tracks the climate justice work of Shikongo, Gabriel Klaasen, and Kumi Naidoo as they campaign against fossil fuel projects in Southern Africa. It focuses on grassroots activism and the fight for a just transition. 
 Ina’s art is a form of storytelling—interweaving fabric, memory, and resistance into a visual language that speaks for justice, regeneration, and hope. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226281693","gid://shopify/Product/9452226412765","gid://shopify/Product/9452226609373","gid://shopify/Product/9452226740445","gid://shopify/Product/9452226871517"]

item.title: Mapopa Hussein Manda
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144874283229 Mapopa Hussein Manda gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144874315997 [] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169546711261 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Mapopa Hussein Manda, Mapopa Hussein Manda, B.1982 in Lusaka, raised and living in Lusaka, Zambia.
Manda is an alumni of Asiko Art school that is run by the Center of Contemporary Art of Lagos, Nigeria. Manda participated in the 2015 edition that was held in Maputo, Mozambique, also going through the
apprenticeship programme at Stary Mwaba’s studio from 2006 to 2009. 
 Manda works predominantly in mixed media and has developed his own mock newspaper style and
techniques of painting that is influenced by the specificity of the Zambian political environment, colonial
experience, traditional culture, history as well as social commentary that is encompassed with satirical
humor. 
 His work is inspired by artists like Stephen Kapata, Jean-Michel Basquait, Banksy Salvador Dali,
Michelangelo and Diego Rivera. He works with manipulating text, collage and drawing, through developing
complex tableaux of political satirical humor, which become points of conversation and platforms for
investigating issues and ideas rather than delivering prescribed answers. Mapopa creates his own ‘mock
newspaper' paintings and uses these newspapers to turn real local newspaper headlines from the colonial
times to the present into mockery of Zambian politics in relation with societal development. 
"}]}]} []

item.title: Masoud KIbwana
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144874807517 Masoud KIbwana gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144874840285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226052317"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169546645725 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Masoud Kibwana, born 1988, is a painter from Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania. Kibwana received training as an artist from the Dar Youth Art (DYA) Vocational Training Center and worked under the mentorship of renowned Tanzanian painter, Max Kamundi. 
 Through a seamless blend of cubism and African figurative paintings on abstract backdrops, Kibwana’s paintings on canvas capture the beauty, culture and traditions of the East African people. His meticulous attention to detail gives life and depth to the subjects in his work. Incorporated in his art are the intricate tribal patterns that can still be seen tattooed into the faces of the Makonde people of Tanzania and Mozambique. 
 His work is characterised by movement, intertwining of subjects and colour combinations not immediately identified as African. The detailed 3D applications along the edges of the paintings, usually with white detail, give his paintings an interesting aspect. Kibwana hopes his work brings to light a dialogue regarding the challenges that have hampered development and sustainability in the Tanzanian community. 
 Kibwana has exhibited his work both locally and internationally. He has shown his work in Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda, Taiwan, China and Italy. Kibwana’s work is in the collection of The Silesian Museum in Opava in Czech Republic. He has a working studio at Nafasi Art Space in Dar Es Salaam. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452226052317"]

item.title: Nuits Balnéaires
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144904790237 Nuits Balnéaires gid://shopify/MediaImage/38144905085149 ["gid://shopify/Product/9452241092829"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/169992487133 Unknown {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Nuits Balnéaires was born and raised in Abidjan in an Akan Agni-bona and Malinké family. A multidisciplinary visual artist and poet from Côte d'Ivoire, his work is deeply rooted in tradition, culture and spirituality. \r\n He attempts to capture the multiple mechanisms that underlie time and the correlation between life and death. Nuits Balnéaires attempts to create a parallel space-time outside geographical constraints, while embracing the universality of the oceans and the way they connect worlds and universes. Nuits Balnéaires' works have been exhibited in multiple exhibitions in Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, France, Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Australia. \r\n His series ‘The Power of Alliances’ 2021, inspired by the symbols of the seven founding families of the N'zima Kôtôkô community of Grand-Bassam, was exhibited at ArtXLagos, at the 1-54 contemporary art fair at Christie's in Paris, and revealed in its complete version during his first solo exhibition in Canada, presented at the 2024 Contact Photo Festival in Toronto. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9452241092829"]

item.title: Maja Maljević
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/38154364190941 Maja Maljević gid://shopify/MediaImage/38154364223709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013396537565","gid://shopify/Product/9013396766941","gid://shopify/Product/9013396799709","gid://shopify/Product/9013398503645","gid://shopify/Product/9452122013917","gid://shopify/Product/9452270256349","gid://shopify/Product/9452270616797"] gid://shopify/Metaobject/134187286749 South Africa ZA {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":" Maja Maljević (b. 1973, Belgrade, Serbia) is a multidisciplinary artist currently living and working in Johannesburg, South Africa. After completing her Masters in Fine Art at the University of Belgrade in 1999, she relocated to South Africa in 2000 to escape political turmoil in her homeland. Since then, Maljević has been refining her unique style that merges gestural abstraction with a vibrant palette. 
 Maljević begins her creative process by 'dirtying' the canvas with bright paint, breaking the starkness of the white surface and creating a foundation her intuitive jigsaw of colours and shapes. She meticulously builds up surfaces with drips, blocks, bands, and waves of colour, seeking harmony between form, line and detail. Physical movement is integral to her method, ensuring her compositions remain dynamic and engaging. 
 Drawing inspiration from German Expressionists and modern artists like Philip Guston, Cy Twombly, and Jean-Michel Basquiat, Maljević's work reflects her diverse influences. She integrates fragments of contemporary life into her work without dictating their significance, allowing viewers to find their own meanings. Her art spans painting, printmaking, and sculpture, always striving for coherence and interplay between conflicting elements. 
 Maja Maljević’s art is a visual symphony of figurative and abstract, organic and geometric, obvious and elusive elements. Through her works, she aims to create a visual language that resonates with the viewer, much like music communicates emotion through sound. "}]}]} ["gid://shopify/Product/9013396537565","gid://shopify/Product/9013396766941","gid://shopify/Product/9013396799709","gid://shopify/Product/9013398503645","gid://shopify/Product/9452122013917","gid://shopify/Product/9452270256349","gid://shopify/Product/9452270616797"]
